title: "Extra Large" Is Too Big, But "York Lyra" Is Just Right!
abstract:
This INTERDESIGN YORK BATHROOM SHOWER CADDY, EXTRA LARGE (Satin Finish) is a wonderful shower caddy, with two big, wide, high-sided baskets for lotion and shampoo bottles, as well as lots of hooks for razors, loopas, and the like. It comes with two big suction cups, and a very useful "no slip wire clip" that goes around the shower pipe (after you hang the caddy over the pipe) to hold the caddy hanger hook in place. The "satin" finish is matte metallic gold-toned, and the entire caddy is rustproof.

However, this Extra Large model is too big for my shower stall. The vertical basket supports are 8" wide, which is about 1/2" too wide, because my shower wall has a grouted-in soap dish that gets in the way, even though the baskets are positioned far enough apart to clear the dish. Also, the extra large caddy is 26" long, which makes it hang down over the pullout shower control knob located below the shower pipe in the shower stall wall.

Happily, a very similar, but smaller INTERDESIGN YORK LYRA SHOWER CADDY is also available (see this same product page), and it fits my hard-to-fit shower stall perfectly! The lower basket is not as high-rimmed as the upper basket, but both baskets accommodate large bottles of soap, shampoo, lotion, etc. I love having even one high-rimmed basket, because it securely holds the shampoo and conditioner tubes that I was constantly knocking off my old caddy's shallow tray (usually breaking the plastic caps on impact).

The vertical supports for the smaller caddy (the York Lyra model) are 7-1/2" apart, and they fit flat against the shower wall (clearing the built-in soap dish). The wide spacing of the two shelves also provides clearance for the soap dish. The smaller model is 4" shorter than the Extra Large, so the caddy's hooks stop just above the pullout shower control knob. I ordered the York Lyra model in "silver" finish, which is matte metallic silver-toned, because silver goes better with my chrome shower fixtures. The York Lyra model is also rustproof, and also comes with two big suction cups and a "no slip wire clip" to secure the caddy hook.

Both of the two Interdesign York shower caddies on this product page are excellent. Just be sure to measure your shower area or shower stall before you order, so that you end up with the correct size for your space.

title: "Flat-Edged" Spoon Scrapes Pan Evenly, Is Great for Stirring Easily-Burned Sauces
abstract:
The square corner on this wooden spoon makes it easy to scrape the bottom of your saucepan or frying pan, and not miss spots, when you're stirring something that burns easily. I really love it for making caramel ice cream, because the caramelized sugar forms a lump and sticks to the bottom of the pan after I add cool cream. With this "flat-edged" spoon, it's easy to combine the lump and cream into a smooth caramel sauce without scorching any of the caramelized sugar.

This featherweight spoon is made of beechwood, and is beautifully shaped and balanced. It's extremely comfortable to pick up, and to hold when you're stirring a sauce or gravy. The handle has a slight curvature, unlike the traditional wooden spoon with round, ramrod-straight handle that you're likely to find at the grocery store (for example, [[ASIN:B0019R9QKI HIC Harold Import Beechwood Spoon 12-Inch]]).

Wooden spoons are not dishwasher safe: they will quickly dry out and split if washed in a dishwasher. Even if they are hand washed, they should be oiled with mineral oil from time to time, to prevent splitting and prolong their useful life. One reasonably priced mineral oil sold for this purpose is [[ASIN:B00280MY7M Snow River 7V03401 32-Ounce Wood Oil]].

title: 13 1/4" lodge cast iron skillet
abstract: So... In an effort to cook with a healthier option to non-stick cookware. This pan is supposed to be seasoned... it did have oil on it when it arrived. It says that if you properly care for the pan it will become more and more "non-stick"... after careful use, cleaning and re-seasoning after each use, it remains pretty awful to cook with. (I've used it daily for about 30 days) The other thing I find is that you will use so much more oil in the process of cooking.... so it's adding a lot more calories to the foods I cook.It may help, as other reviews have said,it would help if the bottom was smooth. I think I am going to go back to the high quality non-stick cook wear and turn the fan on as I am using them at moderate heat. This is my personal experience and it may differ from yours. I will continue to try and use my cast iron pans for high oil content cooking... but I am not going to purchase any more cast iron. My review is an honest reporting of my own personal experience and may differ from yours. I respect that and hope you can be too.

title: 2022 book was better
abstract:
This is a pricy faux leather planner. I loved the 2022 book so much that I paid for this higher priced 2023 planner. I won't be back for 2024 at the current rate of increase.

The inside of the binder is the same as last year. I could use more pages for notes but it wasn't a deal breaker. However, the cost of the planner increased while the value of the cover drastically decreased.

The 2022 planner's bookcover was flawless. The faux leather looked and felt nearly real. The cover was perfectly adhered to the cardboard hardback. My very well used planner looks to be in perfect condition a year later. It was a professionally done book that looks and feels professional in my hand. Last year, I bought the gray.

Unfortunately, this 2023 binder lacks the same quality binding. The cover feels very cheap and thin. It's not adhered to the cardboard hardback at all; so, you see ripples in the cover when it's open and closed. I'm highly disappointed with the extreme lack of quality and professionalism. This 40 dollar binder is dollar general quality. It's a bait and switch. Now that they have all the great reviews, they didn't feel compelled to maintain or improve the quality with the higher price.

Next year, I'll just go into a store to make sure I get everything I'm paying for. This should've been 1/3 the cost or less. I'm very disappointing to say the least. Note, if you are solely concerned with what's inside the planner, you should be fine. But, I need the entire planner to reflect its cost and the very thing you see 1st is annoyingly sub par and I don't have confidence in its durability as a result. I no longer have faith in the company and won't be returning for a 2024 planner.

title: 3 Hr Learning Curve
abstract:
I love this game but it's not a game to casually grab and play with just anyone. Took me about 3+ hrs to learn how to play and a few 1-2 hr play throughs before I got the hang of it and there's probably still something I'm overlooking. The game is fun and easy once you understand how to play but it's very complicated and could easily overwhelm new players. There's just a lot to keep track of. There are a lot of moments where we pause and question if there's anything we missed which makes the game feel like it's going slower.

Also, while I think they nailed some parts of the rulebook, like visually showing game setup and having an index, I think in a lot of ways the rulebook could've been done better. I frequently have to flip through several different pages to better understand one thing and I'll feel like I still didn't get an answer.

The game is supposedly designed to prevent "alpha players" but there's really no built-in defense against delta players. My current designated playmate, despite having played several games, has me hold their hand through almost every single step for their own play and requests my guidance to the point that I can't focus on my own play until they're done with theirs. When I prompt for coordination for just a small portion of my play, whether due to being a poor team player or not having the confidence with the rules, it's not reciprocated and then I'm somehow a nuisance to them for "taking forever" because I'm finally able to set up my own play. Granted, I might not have the most ideal playmate right now but hosting a game night, especially with multiple new players, currently seems like a nightmare. So with that... it's great for solo play!! Again, love the game

title: 3 shelf system
abstract: Even though the photos show the shelves with the "lip" edge down, good luck. There's only ONE way to put the shelf system together and that is with the lip edge up. A spent a horrible amount of frustration time trying to get this put together as the directions laid out - finally gave up and called "customer support." I was told, VERY SLOWLY - there is only ONE WAY the system can go together and that "MAY mean the lip edge is up." GRRRRRRRRR I don't like it. The directions show and tell you NOTHING that is useful, except to call tech support. OMG. Of course, at this price point, you're not expecting much - and I wasn't really. But I DID expect the directions to reflect the item I had in front of me. If you are DETERMINED to have this shelf, here's a couple of hints... the black clips do NOT adjoin to themselves and may pop off - the lip edge MUST be up - which definitely limits the use of these shelves - things MUST fit inside the lips... and it "suggests" a rubber mallot "may" be useful - don't try to put this together without one. I'm just going to toss this and try something better - where the lip edges go down as they should. What a mess. - OH. And there are 4 wheels... 2 regular, 2 with a "brake" switch... Don't bother... the "brake" doesn't work AT ALL. Just junk.

title: 3 tier ceramic service
abstract: The plates are ceramic. Comes with silver metal (very, very lightweight) hardware including washers for in between plates as you assemble. The outer box is pretty. Great for gift giving - so I purchased the two I needed to serve tea treats at a shower and one as a gift for the bride because the box looked like such a pretty gift. I proceeded to unpack my servers and was immediately hit with a horrible, musty, overwhelming smell...probably due to the tremendous amount of Styrofoam packing - Styrofoam is great for holding awful smells. A real mess - no to mention the mess it creates when you unpack it... it breaks and floats everywhere... To be fair, careful packing was necessary to protect the ceramic plates, but Styrofoam is so awful to get rid of in an environmentally positive way. Further, the bride I had planned on gifting a set to, is a VERY earth conscientious person. So now I am torn. I am thinking of making an additional purchase of a really nice storing box and cushioning felts for in between each plate - opening her set and giving it to her open, but clean, not smelly (was better after dishwasher) set. *PS - I DID make the additional purchase* The ceramic plates are close to the measurements given. There are pierced holes in the design of each plate in case that matters to you. They are also look "embossed" with a lacy like print that you can feel, so the plates are not perfectly smooth. The edges are scalloped. The bottoms of the plates is smooth and not embossed. The plates are warm white in color. It is going to use for my purpose, but I wish we could have packing that would be WAY more earth friendly. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: 5-disc DVD player, perfect for Couch Potatoes!
abstract: So glad to have found a DVD player with a 5-disc changer. They were almost impossible to find a few years back, but this time, I was able to find a few choices. I know everyone is streaming now, and I like to stream movies, too. But I also have certain favorites on DVD. If you want to watch a bunch of episodes of your favorite TV series, or just have some kind of movie marathon - it's great to be able to put in a bunch of DVDs and then just click the remote to change discs. Especially when I'm curled up on the couch, surrounded by dogs and the occasional cat, and don't want to get up and disturb everyone. This Sony has worked perfectly so far. It came with a remote, of course, and also included audio/video cables, the ones that have the red, yellow and white ends. Unfortunately, being an older model, it does not support HDMI input. But the picture is still very good even without that. I was really happy to find this unit, since my old one recently gave up the ghost! If you like to watch a lot of movies or TV without getting up, this DVD player is for you!!

abstract:

title: A FOR REAL bummer
abstract:
To be honest, I purchased two of these types of cats... One is this one.. the "FurReal" brand and the other was a "Joy" brand... the cats looked nearly identical, however, the other brand - $25.00 cheaper was significantly better. This one sounds horribly mechanical, jerky - almost looks like the cat is having a seizure. One eye is bright and shiny, the other is dull and scratched.... In order to get the cat out of the box I had to literally destroy the box, otherwise, it would totally be going back - in a second. I'm disappointed to say the least. Even the fur was nicer on the Joy brand! The FurReal brand also did not "go to sleep" either... it was constantly moving - (I see a LOT of batteries being used). The meow sound is very odd and fake. Honestly, if you really think you need to purchase a robo pet - try the Joy brand. It was more real and smooth in movement... the meow, still fake, was sweeter... you could actually feel the purr... and it seemed to be more interactive. It's not perfect either, but a better buy and more satisfying experience.
I always update my reviews if new info would be useful -however, not being able to return this was an expensive donation item - so unlikely there will be much more to report.:(

title: A Great Buy with Everything I Need
abstract:
I just opened this package of six hooks this morning and am so pleasantly surprised. I used hooks like this style quite a few years ago and found them totally strong enough for hanging planters, lamps, etc.

I want to hang various planters around the house and decided to go with this six-pack of hooks. There were several options out there in Amazon "world," but this particular product seemed like a good fit for me.

They arrived really fast and everything was packaged so well. Each hook came in its own little protective bag (so no issues with scratches or dings), and another larger bag held various screws, plastic plugs, toggle wings, etc. I counted everything and it was all there.

You select the hardware specific to whatever material you are screwing into (concrete, wood, drywall). My hooks will mostly go in drywall ceilings, so the "toggle wings" are my choice.

I was a little concerned about the design or pattern of this hook looking a bit too "antique" like my last one. Because I chose the white color this time, they look so much more modern and minimalist. They should blend in really well with my white ceilings. I really like the the way they look!

I also was a bit surprised and pleased that the white enamel (not matte) paint covers the hook completely…even the part that won't show. I can't imagine having trouble with rust, if that were to become an issue.

Very happy with this choice and purchase…highly recommend!

title: A Great and Necessary Cover
abstract:
Since I wanted to protect my investment in a Kindle Touch, I ordered this cover. I am glad I did. It fits my Kindle Touch perfectly. The four corner straps secure it to the cover, and there is an elastic strap at the lower end that fits around the entire case, making the Kindle impervious to attack by foreign objects in your bag, backpack, what-have-you.

I agree with others who have said the cover is a bit pricey, but if you love your Kindle Touch as much as I love mine, you will want to protect it for many years to come with this sturdy jacket.

When I purchased the cover, I wondered if the flip design would get in my way. Not to worry. I find myself so focused on what I am reading that I don't even think about it being there.

Do not expect to stand the cover up with the Kindle in it. Despite the rubber strips on each end, the cover will slide. Not good.

All things said, I recommend this cover. The first (and I hope last) time your Kindle slips out of your hand, you will be glad you have a modicum of protection if the cover is open, and a lot of protection when it is closed and secured.

title: A Not So Good Anker Product (Updated: 01/23/2018)(Updated: 02/08/2018)
abstract:
I have a six foot PowerLine cable that's just about a year old. That's twice as long as any other cable, braided, cloth, heavy duty, whatever, has lasted. Where I keep my tablet in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed puts a fairly sharp bend in cables. I've had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months. I'm replacing the six foot cable for two reasons. The six foot cable just isn't long enough, it's really close and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need but I think it's better to have the extra length. The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting. The other reason is the connector has loosened up a little which I've noticed in both my tablet and Kindle but it still works so it's a good backup cable to have around. The new cable end are very tight fitting which I'm happy with, the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of usage so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy.

Update 01/23/2018 - I bought this 10' cable based on the longevity of the company's 6' cable of the same style. My 6' cable lasted nearly a year of numerous daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet. With no discernable change in usage or handling the 10' cable is now disconnecting from the tablet at the lightest touch after less than three months. Very disappointed.

Update: 02/08/2018 - I contacted Anker about warranty support for this cable. They were very quick to respond, friendly, concerned and quickly sent me a braided upgrade cable to make up for this cable failing. Communications were never delayed, response times were generally 12 - 24 hours apart. If you get a dud Anker will stand behind their product.

title: A Tale of Three Pillows…
abstract:
When I ordered two of these TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS (One Size, Beige), one pillow turned out to be overstuffed (very fat, heavy, and rather hard), and the other turned out to be perfect (moderately flat and flexible). Both are excellent small pillows, though the fat one is more suitable for a lumbar pillow or "propping-up" pillow than a travel pillow.

Why are the two pillows so different? It's because they are NOT solid-core pillows like my wonderful [[ASIN:B07CMK551C full-size Tempur-Pedic Symphony Pillow]], which is a "100% molded viscoelastic polyurethane foam pad". Instead, the travel pillows consist of "70% shredded visco elastic polyurethane foam" and "30% visco elastic polyurethane foam pad".

My fat pillow obviously received more shredded foam during manufacture than the more flexible pillow. Because shredded foam tends to shift in pillows, I try to avoid pillows with shredded foam fill. In fact, I wouldn't have purchased the two travel pillows had I known that they weren't solid-core.

However, I like my two travel pillows pretty well--so far the fill hasn't shifted. They are good quality pillows made with Tempur-Pedic memory foam that conforms to one's body. They work for me because the small size is very good for propping up an arm or leg in bed, or for providing spot support for back, neck, or shoulders in a chair.

title: A banana slicer that seems ridiculous to own but is absolutely fabulous for certain purposes
abstract:
My colleague and I laughed when we found a link to this banana slicer on Amazon and asked each other "How hard can be it to slice a banana?" Well, about one week later I came across this exact slicer in a kitchen gadget store and knew I had to order it. Now I'm not laughing any longer, because:

- A medimum-size banana can be sliced in four passes through the gadget.
- All slices are a perfect 1/4" wide.
- If you use a dehydrator to dehydrate your own fruits, this slicer makes sure all the banana pieces are even so that they dry at the same time.
- Uniform banana slices on jello, cereal, or desserts make for great presentation when serving food.

Cleaning is easy as long as you use a brush; otherwise it can be difficult to clean the blades thoroughly. Of course, use caution when cleaning and do not leave this tool around children as they can put their fingers in the chamber and get hurt when squeezing the handles--but this is just common sense for any kitchen tool.

For a person who uses a dehydrator or just wants presentable banana slices, this is a must have. For others, it's a great conversation piece and nifty tool. For those who slice one banana every so often, don't bake or use a dehydrator or have no one to converse with, then this would be a frivolous purchase.

Personally, I love it!

title: A cinch for a strap
abstract:
Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And recheck ever so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying positions.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain (or when your hands are otherwise occupied)

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed.

5. There's a locking mechanism to hold the strap in place when you're not shooting.

6. Strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a shot (when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course)

7. This strap is built for a man, (the women's strap has a small curve for the zaftig photographer) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) regardless.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive lens
upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit nerve-wracking. (But regular straps can malfunction also)

2. Strap could have been improved with a bit more padding.

3. Strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag (but you can't have everything) For smaller bags you can detach the strap and reattach when needed in a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap when you want to use a tripod

5. No fault of the strap, but the models in the video on the product page need some instruction on how to hold a DSLR properly (LOL)

Overall, this has solved a big problem for me, as this is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap. The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top, and has a clever little bend for negotiating feminine curves.

title: A good value
abstract: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don't seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn't kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That's really my only complaint - there's nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: A pretty darn good space saving, high performance machine
abstract:
I picked up this little beauty to replace both an ancient and cranky 5-disc CD Player and a single disc DVD player. I now have breathing room in the old entertainment center, so even my antique turntable can take a creaky spin every now and again.

Seeing that I can't connect a toaster without help, I called on my trusty better half to unravel the mystery of setting it up. In non-technical language, a.k.a. plain English, this is what you need to know about this mighty machine:

1. The manual needs a lot of work. It's neither user-friendly nor idiot-proof. Ditto for the boxy silver remote.

2. It is easy to set up if you already know how to do that sort of thing. (We have component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver.)

3. It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs. With the benefit of 5.1 surround, movies like Master and Commander can literally move you, and CDs have never sounded better.

4. It is as convenient as a 5-disc CD changer as it is a 5-disc DVD player, except that when you're playing more than one CD you'll need to put it in "CD Mode" first.

5. It can easily play different types of media, such as audio Cds, MP3s, DVDs and those other mysterious formats - just put in the discs and play away.

6. The video quality is very good on a regular TV. You can set up different pre-defined picture quality modes, or customize to suit your own taste if you're a techie or a buff. If you have difficulty making up your mind, ignore this option.

7. The player is chock full of options, but you have to explore for yourself, which can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of it. Read the manual, you say? See Item 1 above.

8. There's on-screen information for MP3s and photo CDs, with different views available for the contents. (Groups/folders or entire playlists)

9. I can't comment on the progressive scan feature, since I don't have an HD or HD-ready TV - yet. (Still waiting for that lottery win)

10. It is supposed to play DVD-Audio discs, but you need 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver to play them. Unfortunately, our receiver is lacking these inputs, but then again, I am also lacking any DVD-Audio discs.

Electronics buffs will probably say that it needs a bit of "tweaking" to get it to look and sound just right, but it looks and sounds great to me. All in all a very good player, perhaps excellent when you factor in the price.

Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004

title: A top-notch laser all-in-one printer
abstract: I have had a lot of printers over the years (IBM, Epson, HP, Canon, Lexmark, etc.), and had kind of gone away from HP a bit due to their software/driver problems (when they off-shored the development/support, the quality slipped quite a bit). However, when printing Christmas cards, my Canon died, and I had been impressed with this HP model when I was helping my sister sort out hers, so I bought one (MFP M479fdw). Software seems to work reliably so far, so I think HP has addressed that somewhat, granted it is a bit rough and crude in places, but it works. And it works from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 (Big Sur), as well as from mobile (iOS). The printer hardware seems to be very good, output arrives quite fast. One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers (including some lower end HPs) is that they do not put much horsepower into the printer CPUs, and cost-reduce the hardware to the point that they are slow and do not hold up, but this version seems well designed and made. Ratings from PC Magazine, Wirecutter, etc. generally have this printer at or towards the top, I would say that is accurate. Print quality on text is excellent, graphics from web pages and similar also excellent, scans are very good (a custom flat-bed would be a tad better, but this is for an all-in-one amongst the best I have seen). For printing high-quality pictures, you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer, but this one prints OK for a laser. HP does not ship this printer with full duty cycle cartridges, but the ones they ship with will still do a decent number of pages. Control screen is touch and good sized, gets the job done. Unit is fairly heavy and large, so if you are using this on a desk, check the dimensions some. The printer is not cheap, but it has excellent print quality and appears to be very well built, so HP has come back to where it once was, at the top.

title: A very poor tablet
abstract:
This tablet computer lacks several features that were present on my older Galaxy Tab A 10.1:

1. The new tablet lacks a hard Home button. This is inconvenient because I use the tablet for running Garmin Pilot software. Having a hard Home button is easier to use while flying that the soft button.

2. On my old tablet I was able to move apps from internal storage to an SD card, thus saving internal storage space. The new tablet does not allow for moving apps to an SD card. Very disappointed.

Had I known about these problems before I bought the new tablet, I would not have purchased it.

I tried using the tablet today while flying. I use the Garmin Pilot app for navigation and flight information. The display did not show all of the information provided by the app. For example, it failed to display the "Direct To" icon. This makes the tablet almost useless when used for running the Pilot app.

This afternoon, I contacted Amazon and asked for a refund. I returned the tablet computer to a local Amazon site.

Regrettably, the tablet proved almost worthless in light of the use for which it was purchased.

title: ADS and more ADS Paying for an AD generator
abstract:
I have Echo's all throughout my house. But, as a writer, I quickly learned that recently, distraction has now become the norm with Echo Show. Pop-Up Ads show up every 5-10 seconds, disrupting my photo collection and my train of thought. And then to integrate Avatar items into responses is annoying as can be! No, I don't want to play all those games you are showing continuously. I've contacted Amazon and was told that they are paid ads and I cannot remove them or refuse them. Does it show your choice of photos all the time? No, more often than not, I get a Blue screen. So, I am no longer a fan because you see, I also have Google Nest in my home, and truth be told, they show my photo collection much sharper, the sound is better when playing music and I have found, much smarter when in need of information, and the best part... NO ADS! NO INTERRUPTIONS! NO TRYING TO SELL YOU ANYTHING. So you make your own choices, but Google also has a sense of humor. I am done with Echo Show. Warning here: Don't complain to them about the ads because they'll only send you more and faster. See Jeopardy photos.
UPDATE 12/05/22:
I had my music playing on ALL Echoes, including the ECHO SHOW 10, in a loop play, when everything stopped in mid-song, to show the Jeopardy ad!!!! Seriously?! Damn Echo Show 10 and 8, are going back while the returns are available. With my refunds, I'm buying the new larger Google Nest with NO ADS. Furious!!! This is nothing more than pure Corporate greed!!! I respected you Amazon, no more... You don't deserve respect when you go cheap and tawdry!

title: AIRPLUS 3000 sq ft
abstract: If I could rate MINUS ZERO I would. I see that this model is now "discontinued" - I must have purchased the very last POS they had. GRRRRR. It doesn't work. I need it to continuously drain out - and even though I have followed very instruction carefully - it does NOT. It just keeps filling the drain drawer. I should have know when I opened the box - the drain tube was crushed in multiple places, rendering much of the tube unusable. I had to cut it - there was just enough hose left that was un-crushed to run it. There is a pic of part of the crushed tube and the other is to prove I have it properly "plugged" inside to auto drain. My tech guy told me it is very likely wrong internally - meaning the setup inside will not allow it to auto drain. Unfortunately for me, my recycle was picked up and I do not have the packing material. I trusted it was going to work. I am attempting to get it picked up- and get a refund. Stay tuned - I will update my review if new info would be helpful. In the meantime, I should also not that the seller has NO WAY to contact them if you have a problem - other than a hotmail email address. Yeah. So I sent an email but do not expect much. It's already in the junk pile we have going. DO NOT purchase this brand under any circumstance. JUNK JUNK JUNK! As I said, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem helpful.

title: Absolutely gorgeous kettle that is supremely well-made; perfect for those with high-end tastes
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:5cb01b680d3ae41bbade0eaedaabfe62]] This is an absolutely gorgeous kettle. It is well made, solidly built, and overall a dream to use. 

POSITIVES
- It holds up to 2 quarts of water to the fill line.

- It is solidly built.

- It whistles lightly when the water has reached a rolling boil.

- The top fits securely on the kettle but requires a little extra strength to seat and remove.

- It comes with a blue potholder.

- It comes in seven wonderful colors--gray, cream, navy, perracotta (like a salmon color), marigold (yellow), sage (deep green), and mist (a light green).

NEGATIVES
- The last bit of water in the kettle gets caught under the rim unless one can center the flow through the spout. This means that I have to dry the inside with a towel for storage.

- The kettle is heavy; almost like a cast iron pot.

- It requires a potholder to use (opening of the spout, pouring, etc.) because the entire kettle gets very hot and that includes the handle and spout lever. I also would have liked a mitt potholder the color of the kettle.

In summary, I love this kettle despite its negatives. At this high price, supplying the user with a mitt potholder instead of a flat one in the color of the kettle one purchases, would elevate the purchase to the next level.  Note that I never heard of the Caraway brand before and saw this kettle in blue on the Vine program. Since ordering this through Vine would not provide me with much savings at the list price, I decided to order this when the price came down for prime day in the color I wanted. The Caraway site was cheaper that day by $4 (i.e. $176) but sort of required the purchase of insurance for $4.95. Therefore, I purchased this on Amazon for $180 plus tax, bringing this to $191.93. I still consider this pricey but this is the best made kettle I ever tried. It is right up there with Le  Creuset Dutch Ovens and almost just as heavy too. This is a kettle that I expect to last my lifetime. There are many kettles on the market that are less than $40 that also could last a lifetime but they are not as nice. I do hope it continues to meet my expectations going forward. If it fails in any way, I will lower my rating, update my review, and will most likely regret my purchase. As of now, I love this and took off one star due to the negatives.

UPDATE - I've been using this regularly for days now and I noticed that this takes longer to boil water than my other kettle and keeps the water warmer a little longer. I also noticed that if I put this on my burner that has a lower flame, the handle does not get hot when the boil is complete, so that is nice.

title: Acceptable
abstract: I work for the United States Postal Service and recently purchased the OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth speaker for use in my LLV truck on my rural mail route. The speaker performs beautifully and I wanted to protect it to, from and while at work so I purchased this case. I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker, but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route. I received the case and used it at work yesterday. The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket and the carabiner clip. I have no need for them now, but I'm sure they will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along and want to clip the case to my day pack. As for playback while in the case? Yeah, it was terribly muffled. It didn't work for me as it apparently has for others. Yet, the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work. I like how smooth the zipper is and how heavy duty/reinforced the stitching for the zipper is. The interior is not as thickly padded as I would have expected, however it does protect the speaker. I deducted one star due to the mediocre interior padding. I hope that, if the company ever revamps this case design, they beef up the padding a bit.

title: Actually installed on the outside of a sliding glass door...
abstract:
You read that correctly - I installed this on the outside of my (1985) sliding glass door. Here's why: My kid is 23, legally, and 2 intellectually. He also has seizures. Oh, he's also moderate to severely Autistic. All of my doors on this house have double cylinder (two keys required to unlock, outside and in) deadbolts. The sliding glass doors have nothing. And apparently there is no way to key lock a sliding glass door. My son is just observant enough that all the typical sliding glass door 'locks' he figured out within about a week of our moving in; and given that 3 years ago he escaped on me for literally less than 60 SECONDS and in that 60 seconds or less he had a seizure, slammed backwards on the concrete, and got not only a nasty gash on the back of his head but a near-life threatening brain bleed on the front of his brain where his brain flew forward into his skull. I'm a solo parent... not a single parent that gets every other weekend or so free, no help from family or friends or government agencies... and sometimes a girl's gotta get a bath. Or go the potty. And I do not have the money for a set of French doors. So, after more investigating than I care to admit, I figured I'd give this a try. (I had already attempted one of those track locks and for this old style sliding glass door it just didn't work.) In our situation, when I need to use the restroom or take a shower or just sleep without worry, I go out one of my locking doors, use the slide lock to impede the opening of the sliding glass door from the inside, come back in the house through the door I went out, lock everything up, and do what I gotta do. Then I can go back and unlatch the slider from outside the house and it's just out of the way. No one comes in that sliding glass door - it opens onto a screened in porch (with a concrete slab floor) - so I'm not worried about how weird it looks that I have a lock outside - lol.

Anyway, my use for this item is unconventional (they call that 'off label' in the medical field) but it sure makes my life easier and for that I am immensely happy:)

title: Affordable Coverage for Your Dot
abstract:
Here we have another case of purchasing an extended warranty being asked to provide a review but never having made use of (and hoping never to have to) the purchased coverage. The price was right but lower on SquareTrade's site (I'm signed up for the specials and such mailings so I should have been made aware of. But it's only a few dollars so its no big loss).

The plan covers up to three replacements of the covered item or the term of the warranty you purchased (two years in this case). After trying to troubleshoot your device over the phone they will make the decision to either repair or replace your item. If they decided to replace the item it's wholly their choice to either provide a new or newest model of your device or provide a refurbished model of what you have. They promise quick turn-around and cover shipping in both directions. If you do not return the defective model within in a certain time frame (I believe it's 30 days) of receiving your replacement your credit card (which you MUST have on file to file a claim) will be charged the full cost of the device when new.

I've heard nothing but good things about SquareTrade for years and almost all of the low-star reviews seem to be user's not understanding the plan or not making sure they would be covered for their purchases rather than anything to do with SquareTrade itself. While I hope I never need to use the plan it was affordable enough to make up for Amazon's fairly deplorable ninety day warranty (our refurbished PaperWhite came with a full year's coverage. A brand new Dot, like their seven and eight inch tablets (unlike their six or ten inch tablets, the Echo or Tap and their entire eReader line which all have one-year warranties) only has ninety days I don't know why. I've always trusted Amazon's electronics, I wonder at their apparent lack of faith.

But anyway. I've rambled on enough. The two years of coverage is comforting and was quite affordable. I'm happy with the purchase and honestly hope I never need to use it.

title: Affordable and effective
abstract: My husband and I bought two sets of these three years ago from Circuit City during their going out of business sale. We both travel quite a bit and were in need of decent headphones for longer flights (let's face it, the ear buds provided by the airlines just don't cut it). My husband accidentally left his set, in their pouch, in the seat back pocket on a flight last year and was in need of a replacement set for our trip to Germany last week. I was amazed by the price when I came onto Amazon to check - $29.99 was a steal compared to the $80 we spent a few years back! This headset is not the top of the line, but it is effective in canceling out the low aircraft drawl while in-flight. (They are also quite nice when you need to drown out the crying child in 23F.;)) The battery life is remarkable. I have had to change the battery on my set only twice in the three years I've owned it. The only complaint that I have, which results in the four star rating instead of five, is that after wearing the set for a few hours (i.e., Amsterdam to Houston, TX), my ears begin to ache on the outside. It is almost like the headset becomes to tight over longer periods of time. I tend not to wear earrings on airplanes, so I can rule out the possibility of pinching. Other than that slight achy feeling, these are wonderful for the casual traveler and the price simply cannot be beat!

title: Allowed me to add a 2009 TV to a 2008 laptop via HDMI
abstract:
This device connects to the VGA port and from there connects to a monitor or TV HDMI port, It WILL NOT work in the other direction, and it requires a source of 5V 1A power (any standard phone charger will work.)

It comes with a USB charging cable and a 3.5mm cable for transmitting sound. Apparently it will not send sound interlaced with the HDMI signal through the HDMI cable (that you will need to supply.) For me this is not an issue because I am using it on a legacy laptop to send video only to a legacy TV, which I am using as extended video under Windows 7. Yes, it's using some ancient gear. But that is why I rated it five stars.

Limitations: even if your TV or monitor is capable of higher resolutions this is not going to provide more than 720p from an old laptop or PC to an old monitor or TV. I know the specs say that this will go higher, but I could not get it there. Yet, going straight VGA from my T400 to my Sanyo TV it went into higher resolution as an extended screen. I am OK with the limitation because I am only using the TV as a second screen with MS Office,

On an old Windows 7 system it's truly plug and play. I had it up and running without the scant instructions in mere minutes. For me it is a perfect solution.

title: Art Deco Oscillating Fan Moves a Lot of Air, Despite Its Small Size
abstract:
This VORNADO SILVER SWAN S SMALL ROOM OSCILLATING FAN (Brushed Nickel) moves a lot of air! On the high setting, it's definitely capable of sweeping a small room (e.g., a child's bedroom, a home office), and completely circulating the room's air. Even the low setting delivers a breeze that will disturb loose papers if the fan is aimed at your office desk.

I love the minimalist "modern" design (this is actually an Art Deco design that harks back to the 1920s). Viewed from the front, the fan displays a wire cage with a silver central disc, encircled by a thin black ring. The base has a streamlined, pointy foot, and a silvery matte finish. The fan has a very small footprint (even when oscillating).

The tilt of the fan's head is adjustable, but the limited arc means the fan will be much more effective when placed somewhere off the floor. The fan oscillates, or delivers a directly-aimed air stream--just pull up or push down the stalk on top.

This is a small fan that doesn't know it's a small fan! It's a great choice for any small-to-medium-sized room where flat surface space is at a premium. And it's a Vornado, so you know that it's good quality, made to last.

title: Assembly Almost Impossible
abstract: Just got this chair yesterday. Thought, okay, other people are being whiners about the assembly. Not so. The second thing you put on is the back - and the bolts they give you will not hold it on safely. I ended up getting our own longer bolts to put the back on with so that I don't have to worry about my kid falling out when the back breaks off. I had only one part where I was able to get the bolts in without sheer misery, the bottom step of the stool. Good thing they give you extra bolts - because you end up stripping off half of them. And I still used several of my own. I do not mind the stools sliding out rather than the hidge on the old models as I also remember getting pinched on the old ones and how heavy they were. So, that will not be my complaint. But, the assembly is too painful to make this thing worth it. I still have bolts falling off that I just can't get in. The top step of the stool has one (I think the threads where I am bolting it into are all wrong) and the plastic side rails are IMPOSSIBLE as they are just not quite wide enough for where they are supposed to go, so the bolts are at an angle. Yes - I even used one of my husbands super clamps to try to get them on by squeezing the legs together. It took 3 hours of MISERY and like I said, I have a stool, it's still not all assembled. And, yes, I do know how to assemble products and use a screw driver.

title: Automatically Cooks Rice, Cream of Wheat Without Burning
abstract:
This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup yield for white rice) cooks perfect fluffy rice every time, and is a good family-sized rice cooker (enough rice for 4 persons). It has the same capacity as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], but has a hinged lid (with rubber gasket, a fancy steam vent, an exterior condensation cup, and a lid liner).

The fancy lid of this Model 37518 causes steamed foods to cook in one-third to one-half of the time required by the simpler Model 37506, but the fancy lid has NO effect on rice or cereal cooking times. The Model 37518 has a condensation cup that must be emptied, as needed, during cooking. The lid liner is a part that must be removed each time for washing. (The instructions don't explain how to remove the lid liner, but it pulls straight off the post that holds it.)

The Model 37518 allows you to set custom cooking times for Hot Cereal or Steam. This isn't really necessary, because the Model 37506 cooks both cereal and rice automatically, and steams food with the aid of a cooking timer.

Most rice cookers do a good job of cooking rice--they have a thermostat that contacts the underside of the cooking pot and turns the cooker off automatically when the water evaporates and the pot temperature rises. Some rice cookers--like this one--cook rice to greater perfection than others, but rice cookers mostly differ in their controls (ranging from simple on/off to extra-fancy multi-button digital displays), and in the quantity of their cooked rice yield.

This rice cooker is sort of in the middle, regarding both controls and yield. It will cook different kinds of rice (there is a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown or white, jasmine, basmati, etc.). It will cook different cereals and grains (barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, etc.). It will steam food (vegetables, poultry, seafood); and it will steam food and rice together.

The size of this cooker is good if you're making rice for a family of four, or if you're steaming foods for a family of two. I love it for the way it cooks fluffy rice and automatically keeps the rice warm for up to 12 hours. I also love it for cooking Cream of Wheat automatically without burning it on the bottom.

Cooking in a rice cooker takes longer than cooking on a stovetop or in a microwave. For example, 3 cups of uncooked white rice will take up to 45 minutes; 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat, up to 37 minutes. But it's easy to start the rice cooker and let it work while you're preparing the rest of your meal.

The rice cooker comes with a standard rice cup measure (about ¾ cup U.S.), a rice-rinsing/steamer insert, and a nylon spoon. The cooking pot has an excellent nonstick surface. The removable pieces are all hand washable in warm, soapy water; handwashing is very easy.

In choosing between this Model 37518 and the Model 37506, I prefer the latter (with a simple, vented glass lid, no condensation cup, longer steaming times, and no ability to set custom cooking times). Both models are very good, but sometimes simpler is better.

title: Awesome
abstract:
I had a 3 cup Black and decker Processors. It was about $10.00 cheaper then this, but didn't do a very good job of doing anything! That one could not even chop Onions very good!

I bought another 3 cup processor, not knowing there was a 4 cuper.
I returned my 3 Cup, for this 4 Cup. its just the right size, I love this one.
 I do not take out my big food processors anymore.
This is lite and easy to use. I do not leave appliances on my counter, but if you did, it does look nice.
It cleans easy, and so easy to handle.Everything clicks into place perfect.

One of the button makes this Processor go backwards, and the other one forwards.So everything gets chopped up evenly..
 It will chop fine or just a little.
This makes great Salsa,etc. not mushie.

 What I really use this little processor for is, We do not like Kale and leafy veggies like that.
When I make a soup, chile, stew, etc. I put veggies that my family does not like, and put them in the food processor, then put it in the food at the end, just to cook it.Also throw parsley in.
 Nobody has complained. They just think its part of the seasoning.I know my family is getting Healthier food.

I gave this 5 stars, but the plastic seems very thin and would crack, but it hasn't.
I do Not put this in the dishwasher.."Handwash"..
 I have had this for about a year. I bought this from Amazon..

Two Thumbs up..

title: Awful build quality.
abstract: These work great out of the box, and it IS clever how it gets packed into a soda-can sized plastic tube, but I wish they were made to a higher spec. These break within hours of getting them, and even appear used already (LED light assembly had one that was out in the tail, the antennae connection was snapped off inside, and the paint appears smeared and/or chipped). I thought maybe I had gotten a defective unit or returned item, but it turns out I got a replacement and it was SAME ISSUE. I think these are just built poorly. Its a shame because the idea of a remote controlled car the size of a hotwheels is super cool and fun! But even if you get one that works most of the way out of the box, it'll only take a few minutes of driving before the wheels start having trouble sending it into a perpetual 360 degree spin instead of going in a straight line (riding the steering button sometimes helps it go in a straight line again). I had similar issues with Pocket Racers, I thought maybe these would be better but it seems all of these tiny RC cars are just built poorly. I wish someone made good ones even if they have to cost more. Very disappointed, my son was really set on one of these.

title: BEST PURCHASE ON AMAZON I'VE EVER MADE
abstract:
My purchase of this stainless steel french press was the best purchase that I have ever made on Amazon. Not only is the product amazing, but the customer service of the manufacturing company is beyond comparison.
Looking first at the product, it's super durable, easy to clean, and makes the best coffee that I've ever had. I think my favorite part is that it keeps my coffee nice and hot until I want to pour myself a cup or two.
As I mentioned, it's really easy to clean, and that's because the parts are easily unscrewed from each other. Unfortunately, because of this I lost a little piece of it that helps the filter stay positioned before plunging it down to filter the coffee. Since I live with a bunch of pig roommates, I knew that that piece was gone for good in the mess. After propping the plunger up with various items while I was waiting for my the coffee to sit, I knew I needed to contact the company about getting a replacement piece since I loved my french press so much.
As soon as I was thinking of this, the company seemingly read my mind and sent me an email asking how I liked the product and if I needed any replacement parts. After telling them about my missing piece, they told me that they didn't have a replacement right now, but were able to send me a whole new French Press for FREE!
I can't say enough about the quality of this item, and the amazing customer service of the company. BUY this product, and you will not be disappointed!

title: Bamboo drawer dividers
abstract: I purchased these not really knowing how I was going to use them but I was hopeful. I LOVE them. They are spring loaded - press on and in - press on again and lift out. I have this wanky silverware drawer and I can't get a tray that fits. SO.... I decided to recycle the old tray and kind of make the drawer the tray. It couldn't be better for me. The picture I have included doesn't show the drawer pulled all the way out - but I have utilized the entire drawer and my forks and spoons are no longer a tangled mess - as I have placed the dividers closely together so everything stands up (except the knives - which is fine). I am just in love with how this ended up. The dividers appear to be solid bamboo. There are non-slip rubber tips on each end. The edges are a tad sharp - but so far so good. If I could change on thing - it would be ro round the edges just a tad. They are super easy to adjust. If you're thinking about something new in your silverware drawer, these are definitely worth the try. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and as always (around 25 years worth), I never have accepted ANY compensation of ANY kind for my honest opinions and experiences.

title: Bamboo recipe card holder
abstract: I am one of those people who still writes recipes that I see on social media - etc in order to save memory on my phone! I ran out of room in my older, very full holder, so I purchased this one. It appears to be bamboo, which is sustainable so I like that. There is a groove on the top of the box that will hold a recipe card if you're in to that ( I cover mine with protector films and wander around the kitchen with them) and also an interesting knob at the bottom that slides in and out of the bottom of the box. It's grooved widely and holds your phone if you're watching a media recipe. Not sure if I will ever use that - but it's interesting. This box does not come with any dividers, so you'll need to purchase those, your recipes card and protective covers if you like. It is literally just the box. Period. It fits a 4x6 card. I like it and am happy to use it. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including well over 24,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Base AND exalted.
abstract:
This is my favorite roller pen of all time. I have tried MUCH more expensive pens and refills - I still hold onto my LAMY's because I love the design - but nothing can touch the G2 0.5mm - the refill AND the pen.

I scrape the logos off with a razor blade. That's enough to make me feel okay about using this pen.

I used to use fountain pens for everything, but I got back into cycling this year and that shakes up the pen in my pocket like a paint mixer at a hardware store. So I had to go back to roller pens for when I'm mobile. I tried really hard to find a "nice" pen but the closest I came was LAMY pens that can be made to take the G2 0.5mm refills. And I still like the G2 pen better. I kinda hate the fact that my taste gravitated to the cheapest, most popular thing on the planet, but I have to either be honest and use the best thing for me, or risk becoming a hipster LOL.

I settled on the 0.5mm refill pretty early on. It writes a great line and has the best feel for me on the paper I use. I gernally buy just the refills and keep using the same pen, but I lost my last G2 on vacation and figured a 12-pack is probably a lifetime supply for me. I feel really gross about buying disposable things, but I appeal to the case that I tried everything else before I resorted to this.

I would recommend anyone to visit the local pen store and really try to find an elegant, suitable pen that will last for a lifetime - generations. If that fails, don't feel too bad about using G2 0.5mm; it really is a great - all time great - pen.

title: Base is aesthetically 4 stars, functionality is 5 (with right bulbs)
abstract: Actually it is, for me, more like 4 or 4.5 stars BUT because the issue I have is due to personal taste and not the functionality, I'll give 5 stars. I viewed this product three times before deciding which size of the exact same product to purchase - on my iPad 4, my Droid 4 phone, and on my Dell AIO/desktop. I mention this so that no one will berate me or my screen resolution for not noticing the finish (which is where my personal taste preference issue lies). The actual fixture is a great deal shinier white finish, moderate to high gloss, than what I perceived it to be (my perception was that it was a satin or even matte that was reflecting flash from the camera that captured the image). For me the finish gave the fixture a clinical feel, like the shiny white you see in hospitals or other medical facility lighting...admittedly our family has spent more than our share of time in hospitals, so it's probably just my problem (thus I gave it 5 stars). I happened to have a can of the matte white textured paint on hand, so I just gave the fixture a couple of quick, light coats and I think it looks great. The fixture, in my opinion, needed the grainy (almost like fine salt mixed in the paint) matte finish to go with the opaque glass. Easy to install (one gal with mediocre patience and one ladder, plus my 12v cordless drill [but a screwdriver would suffice]). Make sure, if using the CFL bulbs that the lumens are higher. I've noticed that some 60 watts are as low as 800-something lumens and some are as high as 1100-something lumens. The lumens-output isn't noticed by most folks, but is critical, I think.

title: Basic Check Transaction Registers for a Low Price
abstract:
People don't write checks as much as they once did. But we still have checking accounts and still have transactions, which makes the need for a check register as relevant as ever. The registers that are included when you order checks are far too few, and that is why a set of registers like these from Easy Read Register are a good idea to have.

With this set, you get ten registers. There are 26 pages and a total of 416 lines on each, which is enough to last a long time. The individual pages have the usual headers for date, description, payment, deposit, balance, etc. One extra on these registers is a column for Fee. This is not something I have seen on most checkbook registers.

The calendars on the back of each registers shows 2021, 2022, and 2023. That means, with normal usage, you should have the necessary calendars as you use these registers. If you have very few checking account transactions, it is possible that 2024 might roll around and you will still be using these registers, and that means you won't have the correct calendar. With normal usage, you should be fine.

These check registers fit into a standard checkbook. They are staple bound and made for the basic function for which they are designed. They are exactly what you expect, and the price is low, which earns this product a high rating from me.

title: Basically Jurassic Park the game
abstract:
I already like Tiny Epic games. This is probably my favorite. If you can imagine a Jurassic Park game, this is more or less the one you want. Small package, great price, endless fun. What more can you ask for?

You build parks and enclosures to house dinosaurs. The dinosaurs are hungry. If you can't feed them, they'll still eat - guess what? - your other dinosaurs! Very well made and lots of fun. If you don't like this game, maybe board games aren't your thing.

I look at this game as an example to understand how to make games well. I think anyone who likes board games has to give at least one Tiny Epic game a try, and this is the one I would recommend most.

Limited closet space? Desperate for something besides Monopoly, Risk, or Settlers of Catan? Like building games with dire consequences? Think dinosaurs are the least bit cool or interesting? Look no further.

My only minor criticism is that some might consider it complex with the different special dinosaurs and some of the rules about how and when to place dinos. Any board game is going to have a learning curve, and this one is small.

title: Beautiful and modern
abstract:
I purchased this sink to use in our newly renovated bathroom and I am very happy with it. It looks great in our gray toned and white bath, and the hardware is very modern.

One thing that is a little tricky is controlling the amount of water--it is very easy to get an excessive flow of water, and you have to adjust the control. I am used to this now, but I would recommend it for a bath that is going to be used by adults--I think kids might waste a lot of water by not controlling the flow very well.

As this is our first vessel sink, I also wondered about water splashing onto the counter, but this has not been a problem at all unless you turn the flow to super high. I also thought it might be difficult to keep spotless, but I find that it dries really well. If I am not going to use the sink for awhile, I do wipe it out after use, and I find that this is very effective, too.

I am very happy with this purchase. It was well packaged and arrived intact, as have most items we purchased from Amazon. Highly recommended.

title: Beautiful design, except...
abstract:
This table is beautiful, sturdy, of a very nice design and quality. Very well thought-out. Which is why it is incomprehensible how they overlooked the fact that the book stand simply does not fit in the slot provided. I have noticed that there is a padded buffer tape running along the inside edge of the slot. I imagine if I peeled that tape off, the book stand would probably fit. But then, I would no longer have a proper, safe support for my phone or tablet, when I want to use those... Somewhat disappointing, especially since everything else about this table is so perfect. Even the book stand itself is of a fairly nice quality.

The legs of the table are sturdy and well-built. The supporting slats that go on the bed have tips that turn up, like skis. This keeps them from getting caught in the bedclothes.

The instructions helped too, because the legs are tightly folded against the underneath of the table and I couldn't figure out how to get them open at first. I didn't want to force things and possibly break them. I checked the instructions, which said to just pull hard (use more strength). So I did.

I love the size, the colors and the materials they used. The slightly textured, leather-like surface provides a nice grip, so things stay stationary and don't tend to slide around on the table-top when you are moving around or moving the table itself around.

I also really enjoy being able to tilt the table-top. It has a narrow lip near the bottom, which keeps papers and canvases from sliding off. Genius! It also comes with a piece you can insert into the bottom slot, to keep your notebook or laptop from sliding off. But I find that is not really necessary because the narrow lip that runs from side to side at the bottom does the job anyway. I do sometimes use the additional piece mentioned to prop my tablet to a more desirable angle when I have it in its protective case.

I like having the little drawer on the underside, in which I can store pens, pencils, notes. It's strong enough to hold a cup of tea, coffee, juice. And it won't slide open when stored.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase and I would even buy at least one more of these for a friend if the price were a little bit more reasonable. I think I read some reviews that said it used to be around $55.... I paid 50% more for mine. Not so happy about that...

The table is a little heavier than expected, but with thinner materials, it probably wouldn't be as sturdy.

title: Beautiful fan
abstract:
We have had a fan in our lanai that works well but is rusty. I didn't want to spend a lot of money on a fan because it is for outside. I went to the large stores and a fan store and can't believe how expensive the larger fans are. I wanted dark brown that had an extension to hang from our really high ceiling. This has the option of 10 or 6 inch drop and the 10 inch is perfect. The remote works well as well as the transition from the old fan to the new inner spring works perfectly.
The nitty gritty of installation. It was going to cost over $100 at the box store for installation of their already expensive fan. We decided to try this fan and self installation after looking at the positive reviews. We opened the box after removing the old fan and placed all of the parts out and inventoried with the instruction sheet. All parts were there and the instructions were easy to understand and clear. We need a tall ladder and also a showered ladder for me to assist my husband. We are not handy people but with the instructions and a couple of tools it is installed. The most difficult thing is holding the unit while installing-the height made it more tricky but we got it done. It would be difficult without a tall ladder for support and 2 people.
This is a really big fan that really cools down an area. 60 inch is perfect for a large space or tall ceilings. It looks so nice and the color looks so clean compared to the previous rust fan.

title: Bedz King Twin Over Full Stairway Bunk Bed
abstract:
UPDATED REVIEW BELOW... Purchased two sets and sent to my daughter in Arizona. She recently moved into a new house and my grandsons now have their own rooms, thus the two sets. My daughter and son-in-law report that the wood looks very, very high quality and they arrived in good condition. They were very well packed. It did take them the better part of an afternoon to put the first set together, but they feel as though the second set will possibly take a little less time as they are now "experienced" in having already done the first set. I will include pics when they provide them. I will say that my 5 year old grandson was SOOOOO excited he could hardly contain himself. My daughter says that it is SO nice to have the drawers and not a ladder. I also purchased some memory foam mattresses to use with these sets (8" and my daughter reports they fit perfectly in terms of thickness). We chose these beds because there wasn't any particle board and while I haven't seen them yet in person, I think they will last as long as the boys will want to be in them. I will update with any information that might be useful. Further, I do NOT receive compensation of ANY kind for my reviews.
UPDATE: 8/2/2016..... I have now seen the beds in person. And all I can say is WOW. Honestly. These beds are the same price as the really flimsy metal beds in local stores here in Arizona... and yet THESE beds are just unbelievable quality FULL wood. The grain is simply beautiful and rich. I am SOOOO pleased with my purchase. I would definitely recommend them. My daughter reports they arrived in excellent condition via a special shipper. My daughter did say that it helps to have two people to finish the beds. While one person can easily assemble the stairs, but putting the frame together with the stairs really requires a second person. She did not feel the need to reinforce the bottom slats as another reviewer stated - but everyone should make their own decision on that. As the boys get bigger she made add slats. She also feels that they are very high quality and is very, very happy with them. My grandsons are also VERY happy with them. I purchased 8" memory foam mattresses (made in the usa) to go on the beds and that really completes the quality. These beds will last every minute as long as they boys want them and then be good enough to share along in the family. Again, I do NOT receive compensation of any kind for my reviews. And I would recommend this particular bed and seller all day long.

title: Been running for 3+ years
abstract:
I've been using this motor for just over 3 years now. I thought the price was a bit high for what it is, but it was worth every penny. The string is still holding up too, which is surprising since it's in full sun for most of the day.

The only problems I've had were with timers. I've gone through one or two digital timers that didn't work the best. One of them actually started randomly opening at night, letting a skunk in. We realized this once we went through a couple of weeks with no eggs. I set up a trail cam, and sure enough, a skunk went in the coop every night, ate the eggs, and exited before the door closed, with one of our ducks chasing it out every night.

It was a game changer once I connected a Meross Outdoor Smart Plug. I used to have to change the schedule on the digital timer ever couple of weeks or so to open near sunrise and sunset, but now I only do this a few times a year. If your smart plug app allows you to turn things on and off depending on the sun, it makes things a whole lot easier.

One last tip - don't make your door too heavy. I had an issue for a while where the door would get slightly stuck and would drop. Unfortunately our duck always had her head out the door as soon as she heard it starting to open, so she's been pinned a few times, and I'm glad it didn't kill her. I'm seeing other people use baking sheets, and that would have been a lot easier to use.

title: Best Cookware for Baking Cakes, Roasting Vegetables
abstract:
For baking, aluminum pans and sheets always produce the best results. Aluminum conducts heat very evenly, so that cakes and cookies bake uniformly and quickly, and vegetables roast fast without burning. Plain aluminum bakeware (without any nonstick coating) is also easy to clean with handwashing or a dishwasher.

The CHICAGO METALLIC 5237982 UNCOATED TEXTURED ALUMINUM ROUND CAKE BAKING PAN (9-Inch, Silver) takes aluminum bakeware to a new level, by adding a textured surface that allows better air flow, and ensures that a baked cake layer releases easily from the pan. To bake with the pan, you use your usual method of greasing (shortening, oil, cooking spray), or use parchment paper or baking mats. Afterwards the pan comes clean easily with light handwashing; you can also use the dishwasher, but the harsh dishwasher detergents will discolor the aluminum (without damaging the baking performance).

The CHICAGO METALLIC 5234613 UNCOATED TEXTURED ALUMINUM LARGE COOKIE/BAKING SHEET (13-Inch-by-18-Inch, Silver) has the same textured surface as the cake pan. It has changed the way that I prepare vegetables (e.g., zucchini, potatoes, root vegetables, eggplant, carrots), because sliced veggies roast beautifully in the oven, taking less than 10 minutes, and make terrific, healthy fries. The baking sheet is wonderful for this purpose, because of the high rim that keeps the veggies from rolling off the sheet as you put it in and take it out of the oven.

The manufacturer recommends that you avoid using sharp-edged utensils and knives with this bakeware. (I use a [[ASIN:B002MQ3SOA Zyliss Knife]] for cutting brownies and sheet cakes, and it has never damaged my coated bakeware in spite of its vicious appearance.) Also, you should avoid using scouring pads and abrasive cleaners, which is easy because you don't need them.

title: Best Sander Out There
abstract:
I've owned and tried a lot of sanders and this one is the best so far. I wanted a cordless for the convenience but found the battery that comes with the DeWalt cordless lasted only 10 - 15 minutes. Unless you have several backup batteries, which are extremely expensive, you might get one side of a shelf done before the charge runs out. But THIS sander gets the job done. Yes, I have to use an extension cord, but a small inconvenience compared to what you get. It's lightweight; in fact, I can guide the sander with one finger just to show it (I'll make a video after). It only has one setting, but that's all I need. The vacuum bag is also the best I've seen. I would say it retains 90% o the sawdust. You can see when the canister is full without a big mess. I have a huge dining room table I'm refurbishing and I get quite a lot of sawdust in the bag. I pour the sawdust into a plastic container and mix it with wood glue later to make a perfectly matching wood filler for the table or other pieces. I have also used the sander inside for about an hour when I desperately needed to get a job done and the weather wasn't permissible. Again, I'd say it retained about 90% or less, unlike other sanders. (I wouldn't advise using it inside and would always advise wearing a mask and goggles, but I had to do what I had to do and it only required a light clean-up around the area. And the vacuum bag is simple to take off, empty, and put back —a simple push and twist.

I'm so impressed with this sander, as you can tell. DeWalt is one of the pricier tools but the electric sander alone (which comes with the bag) is not that expensive at all (depending on when and where you buy it -- Amazon has the best prices so far) and is well worth spending a bit more. Plus, I get the sanding pads on Amazon for so much cheaper than at the local home improvement store. And they stay on. I'll edit this later and mention which company sells the pads. They come in multiple size grit packages (40-240, 80-350, 100-600n...) for around $10 per 20 (or 25) piece package. Though I imagine you could use any pad from a reputable company. I look at how many buyers rate a product as well as the rating. Beware of products that spout 5-stars and have under a hundred reviewers. Many of those companies sell mediocre if not poor quality products that get bad reviews. So they change their company names and have their people buy and rate the product with 5-stars. Unfortunately, many buyers fall for the 5-star rating over how many others have bought and rated it. I like to pass on this trip for those who may not have figured it out.

I digress. I've had this sander for three months now and have used it 3-4 times a week for hours at a time. I couldn't be happier. If I could give it more than five stars I would. This is one of the best items I've purchased on this site (and I have purchased WAY too much). Highly recommend.

title: Best Wear OS for true Android users, but not perfect
abstract:
I will avoid the facts that this watch is outdated at launch by its hardware (processor). That, coupled with retail and even discounted price also are out of step with the competition. These two big gripes aside. The watch is good and likely the best choice going into 2023 for pure Android Wear OS users (not looking at Apple or Tizen overlay users.)

Its not perfect and Pixel users will benefit the most when paired to this watch. Its lost most of the lag recent watches from other Wear OS brands. Has all the sensors the majority of buyers could want based on watch tech right now. It swipes, it plays well with the apps made for it. It gives you the info you ask of it. There are even a few nice 3rd part accessories now to avoid Google Gouging for proprietary bands. And there are few quirks I hope they iron out soon. Mainly, when the phone is in Bedtime Mode. Make the watch do it too, or add that Zen Mode feature to the watch also. It sucks to have animals tripping the security cameras outside dinging on my wrist and killing my sleep score. The snooze/do not disturb button on watch fails too easily and you have turn it on/off manually everytime.

As many claim, the battery sucks. Sort of. I can go up to 36+ hours on a slow day, and many others can too. It will depend on too many factors to list. But basically your popularity with notifications and thinking you need the screen always on are the biggest battery hurdles. Most can get use to touch to wake. And maybe only having text, phone, front door doorbell and one email be allowed to bother your watch with notifications. Do you really need to know what cousin Billy had at Dairy Queen when he posts the same pic/vid on Facebook, Instagram, Tic Toc and YouTube, etc. Find a nice balance of wrist information along with what sensors you need checking if you are still alive. You can start the day and track everything till the next morning when you charge it again while you shower and get the next day started. It charges quickly. And most other Wear OS watches have the same daily charge requirements. Nobody on Wear OS is winning on battery. Or Turn every setting all the way up and have a spare charger puck ready for a mid day juice. If you go that route. I suggest a quick release band to ease the removal of the watch.

So, its not up to the level or price of the Ultra Apple Watch. And if you don't care for Samsung. Your love for stock Android will eventually lead you back to this watch.
