Unless you forgo ECG sensors. The price will drop soon. Cases are minimizing the fragility of an ALL glass jelly bean design. But when comes to keeping your phone pocketed and yet still have info relayed in a useful way. Pixel Watch is the best current albeit not perfect solution for now.

title: Best bokeh for your buck
abstract:
I bought this because when you can't afford Nikon glass, you choose Sigma.

One of three (arguably) most recommended wedding lenses, the others being a 50mm f/1.4 or f/1.8 prime and a 24-70 f/2.8, my experience with this is creamy dreamy soft backgrounds with perfectly focused subjects. Please note that this is an amateur point of view, and I shoot weddings when the bride or groom asks whether I'm going to walk with my camera, because the camera takes really good pictures.

I love it for details like the decorations, cake and candles, for far off shots of the ceremony without getting in the way, and for those cool shots where the bride/groom is in focus and the groom/bride beside her/him is out of focus (but very recognizable)

What I don't like is the weight (but I can suck that up) and that you can't work the group shots without changing the lens (until I get a second camera) unless you're standing way back, which isn't always possible.

I also love it for portraits, especially of toddlers, and will be trying it next at a field hockey game, as I understand it to be aces at sports. I bought the [[ASIN:B000CDA7Y4 Sigma APO Teleconverter 2x EX DG for Nikon Mount Lenses]] which works fine with this lens, and plan to go stalking hummingbirds as soon as they discover my [[ASIN:B0019Y0YCA Aspects 153 Mini Hummzinger Hummingbird Feeder]].

If you need to shoot in low light, and prefer ambience instead of the brightness of flash, this fast lens and some ISO pumping can really do the job. (Note: I'm currently using a Nikon D7000 and hope to upgrade to a full frame in the near future)

Amanda Richards, January 2, 2013

title: Best ink cartridges for my HP Envy printer
abstract:
I only use HP printers for my work, because they have always been reliable throughout my career. I work from home full-time and my company reimburses me for my work expenses. I try, however, to get a good price on whatever I'm buying…so I keep coming back to this particular product.

I like this convenient 2-pack of black and color cartridges, since it seems to simplify my shopping. I always have backups since you never know when your ink will get used up.

I prefer a black ink laser printer for most of my work, but I do have the occasional need for color printing.

I'm sure we all find these ink and toner cartridges painfully expensive sometimes, but we do what we have to, right?

As long as I go through the proper testing and adjusting (calibration?) when I put in new ink (the printer walks me through it), it usually is a simple enough process.

The one complaint I have about inkjet print is that, when I use a highlighter on my copies, it smears my ink...even after the ink has dried. I just know not to highlight if I can help it.

I do find this a decent value and HP products have always worked well for me.

title: Better than the old ones, but still needs improvements.
abstract:
The first one we received was defective, in that it would not sync with our alarm system. Amazon sent another one and we've not had any problems with it falling off the system. If yours doesn't work like it supposed to, be sure to contact Amazon STAT. What I like about the GoControl is, I can adjust it, turn it off and on, change the temp all through my alarm app on my devices. What I don't like about it: is that it's not accompanied with a separate room sensor (like the Ecobee is). If you live in a very hot and humid area and your thermostat location is on an exterior wall like ours is in a loft, it will read the temp of the hotter wall than the colder air at center of room. It's next to Impossible to accomplish a 72° room in the heat of the summer. If you set it at 75° When it's 85° outside or hotter, The air will plummet down to 68°, lickety split because it's competing with the reading of the heat of the wall, not the coolness of the room. Grr and brr. But it is infinitely better than the old fashion thermostat that we replaced. But dear GoControl, please update this thermostat with a separate room sensor to make this more accurate for us wimps that can't take the heat nor cold like our ancestors did.
The plastic of the unit is very lightweight and seems flimsy, but it has remained intact for almost 9 months now. We rarely actually touch the unit since we control it from our app, so I don't see that we will have an issue. I was able to install this relatively easily, do you take a picture of the wires attached to your old unit first. Really old wires change color easily with age (the yellow and white look the same), so mark what they are, it'll help you to attach to your new thermostat.

title: Big Echo is better for music. Controlling a TV, reading audio books etc is where the Dot shines
abstract:
I have had my main Echo since the first days after the initial invitation to buy was sent out. I absolutely love Alexa and use her for tons of things daily. - she lives in the hallway between the living room and kitchen where we spend the most time. I added the Dot a month ago to bring the Alexa functions into our master bedroom.

The Dot is as easy to use as the big Echo and now that the two can be connected, we have music throughout the house at the same time. I also like the intercom skill so we can talk to each other across the house quickly. My one dislike is the tinny sounding small speaker n the Dot. I've grown so accustomed to the balanced, clean sound from the big Echo that the Dot sound quality was a let down with music. However, reading me the news, ordering Starbucks, reading my audio books, working as an alarm clock or intercom is smooth and works just fine. I especially like being able to control our tv with Alexa voice commands - we cut the cable cord and stream via Prime, Netflix and Hulu Live and Alexa has made searching for a specific show much more simple.

title: Big Silver-Colored Plastic Clock Set Itself to Correct Time Within 10 Minutes
abstract:
This LACROSSE TECHNOLOGY 14 INCH ATOMIC ANALOG CLOCK (WT-3144S, Silver) replaces a similar "atomic" wall clock that I purchased from Staples many years ago. That clock finally lost its ability to find a radio-broadcast time signal after being dropped once too often.

I love atomic clocks, because they never need resetting for daylight or standard time. I also love battery-powered wall clocks, because they aren't affected by frequent local electrical outages. This clock will run for a couple of years on a single AA alkaline battery! When you need to replace the battery, the clock resets itself automatically. (The battery is not included.)

This big silver clock is plastic, and looks kinda cheap; but that's forgivable because it's budget-priced (about $22 on Amazon). The face is large enough, and readable enough, that you can place it up high somewhere--and then nobody can tell what it's made of. I have mine sitting on a stand for decorative ceramic plates, on top of a bookcase, and it looks fine.

My clock was simple to set up. There is a slider for setting the time zone, and one for setting automatic Daylight Time adjustments. I inserted the battery and placed the clock near a window, facing east (because the source of the time signal is in Colorado, and I'm in California). The clock found a signal almost immediately and set itself to the correct time. (The manual says it may take up to 5 overnights to find a signal; but the clock can also be set manually if no signal can be found.)

title: Big and complex game, but also straightforward
abstract:
There was so much for me to like with this game. It has a depth few games have, with a lot of different strategies that could work due to the number of options despite the fact that a player only has 6 different options for what action to take each turn.

I've heard this described as Zoo Tycoon the board game, and it fits that. Will you try to fill your zoo with appealing animals and impress everyone that way? Or will you try to build up your conservation bonafides and get your zoo declared the best for its efforts? Or can you find a new path between the extremes?

Its definitely not easy to learn. My first game included one person who had played before, one very experienced gamer and two relatively newer gamers. The score quickly showed that the experienced players built a huge lead and turned the score into a race. The other two enjoyed the game, but both admitted that the complexity of the options had slowed their progress.

This is not for those who can get analysis paralysis, but it is a great game and I expect it to become a regular game in my rotation of what I bring to the table.

title: Bought 2 of these
abstract:
I bought 2 of these for my GF and myself. So far we both love them. They seem to be pretty well made for most of the parts being plastic. Its pretty sturdy working on it, the leather top is beautifully made and looks great. My GF gets more use out of it than get from mine so she could write a better review than me, however, the little I used it so far was a very nice experience when you just want to lay in bed and play PC games or surf the web for the day on your day off. Makes a good food table as well. lol
The only thing in the short time I've owned this I noticed with this is if your not careful something with enough weight on the front edge of this will tip it forward if there isn't any weight on the back to balance it out. I think the feet should have been just a slight bit longer by at least about 3-5 inches to make it that much more stable while using this. I seen my GF tip hers over using just her 10.1 inch Samsung tablet while watching a movie on it. Aside from this and a few minor things I didn't mention, this thing is awesome to have and use.

title: Budget Friendly Cover
abstract:
Fall 2019: I bought this because of the low price and it's a breeze to install. I'll eat my hat if it last eight years. But I just needed to keep leaves and pine needles out of my pool during the winter months. For that it works great. It is in no way a safety cover and a fallen tree branch would probably poke a hole in it.

Spring 2020 Update: After a moderate winter, the cover did the basic job of keeping debris out of the pool, But a couple wind storms ripped half a dozen grommets out of the cover and that allowed the tarp to develop long rips and worn spots. It was not salvageable for a pool cover, although I was able to cut it up in sections and use those to drag leaves to the street and cover some other smaller things... so not all was lost.

Overall, it will last only a year or two as a pool cover. But considering the price, I could buy a new one of these tarps every year for 20 years and still spend less than I would on a "real" pool cover.

Fall 2020:
Ordered a new one for this fall/winter. The only thing I would add is that the tarp's grommets cannot take very much tension. If you are going to drape this over something and lightly secure it with rope or bungee cords it will do fine. But if you need to put any tension on the tarp or pull it tight, the grommets will start to pullout within minutes.

title: Buyer Beware
abstract: We purchased this as an overflow holding tank for our rain water. We could put this close to our garden and refill it by pumping water from standard rain barrels to this barrel. Seemed to work, until we got about 25 gallons in it, then the bottom faucet started a steady drip. We drained the water and checked that all the gaskets were exactly per the instructions. One side of the gaskets are ribbed and one side it flat. Nothing in the instructions say which side goes where. Tried reversing them, filled it again. Leaks. Empty, take apart, tried O-Ring silicon, that eventually worked. We got the tank half full and had the same challenge with the top faucet. Same solution worked. Left it sit for 48 hours, then carefully went to hook up a hose to the bottom faucet. Wait, the quick connect is reversed and a standard quick connect will not flow. Found an old quick connect with no shut off inside. Hooked it up and magic... leaking again. Got the leak to stop, for now. Giving it 48 more hours. If it leaks when we try the hose this time. Empty/Disassemble and return. Waste of several hours and several gallons of rain water. If this did not leak, it would have been 5 stars across the board. BUT, a storage tank that will not hold water has no value.

title: Caramel-Colored Slipcover Installs in Minutes, Fits Large Wheeled Ottoman
abstract:
This SURE FIT STRETCH PIQUE OTTOMAN SLIPCOVER (ANTIQUE) is exactly what I was hoping for! It fits my large ottoman (23-1/2" wide x 28-1/2" long x 16" high) snugly, and stays in place.

The antique color (a light caramel) is darker than the product page photo. The fabric (94% polyester, 6% spandex) has an attractive, tiny-waffle texture that doesn't show up in the photo. It's machine washable (cold water, gentle cycle). The fabric is fairly thin, and it won't last forever, but for about $23, this is quite a nice slipcover.

It took me under 10 minutes to install the slipcover. It would have taken less than 5 minutes, but my ottoman has a dust ruffle and ball-shaped wheels that called for a little extra tucking-in.

Collapsed, the top of the slipcover (measured corner to corner) is 20" wide x 27" long. The main limitation on fit is the elastic band that goes around the bottom edge and holds the slipcover in place. According to the manufacturer, the slipcover will fit ottomans "up to 116" (measured by adding all four sides together). My ottoman adds to 106" (23-1/2 + 23-1/2 + 28-1/2 + 28-1/2), and it was close to the maximum stretch for the elastic band.

I really like the way this slipcover looks and feels! It's sleek and soft, and completely covers my ottoman's ripped flower-print covering (as well as my duct-tape repairs).

title: Carpal Tunnel Be Damned!
abstract:
I've been using these for years, and I honestly believe it's the only reason I don't have carpal tunnel problems. I use them at work and at home. There is virtually no repetitive wrist movement when using this mouse...but...after long-term heavy use, there is a lot of wear & tear on a person's thumb, which is used to click the primary mouse button. Sure, you can reverse the buttons, but imagine your hand over the top of this mouse. You'd use your index & middle finger together to roll the ball, probably, while your thumb clicks the primary button, and the secondary button is clicked with the ring finger or palm, not parts of the hand that have the most dexterity.

I'm left-handed, and have the buttons reversed, but some games & application don't recognize the reversed buttons, so the primary mouse button becomes the one I click with my ring finger or palm, and that's not good for gaming. Also, if this mouse has an alternative to a mouse wheel, I've never been able to find it, and, again, lots of games incorporate the wheel into the controls, so that's an issue for me. Eventually, the ball, which is normally smooth as silk to operate, loses its finish and begins to feel less accurate, harder to roll & rough...but that doesn't happen for years. In fact, I can't remember when I bought the one I'm here to replace. Despite the minor annoyances, which are few, this is a comfortable, sturdy mouse, and the best mouse I've found for my left hand. Plus, no carpal tunnel surgery. What's that worth?

title: Charming Design, Small Footprint, But Powerful Enough to Circulate Air Through Entire Bedroom
abstract:
I positively adore this retro-design VORNADO VFAN VINTAGE WHOLE ROOM AIR CIRCULATOR! It's small--just 14" high, 12" wide, and 7" deep--but it's powerful enough to circulate all of the air in my 420-cubic-foot master bedroom (8' high x 13-1/2' wide x 15' long). This little fan is highly functional, and the vintage dark green and antique gold coloring, along with the classic pivot-fan shape, is totally charming.

One of the best things about this fan is the unusually small footprint. The fan fits on the large side table that I use as a bedside table, with oodles of room to spare. To circulate the entire room's air, I just aim the fan upwards at the room's opposite ceiling corner, and set the speed to medium. The pivot stand holds its position, and a pleasant breeze springs up. The medium speed setting is perfect for circulating the room's air at night without creating a cold draft.

This fan is also very, very quiet, even when running at high speed. For my bedroom, I strongly prefer this little fan to its bigger, more powerful, slightly noisier cousin, the [[ASIN:B0025QKUE8 Vornado 660 Whole Room Air Circulator]], which I also own. (I'm going to move the cousin to my home office, which has a southwest-facing window and gets very hot on sunny California afternoons. For the office, I can use all the air circulation I can get!)

Another great feature of this little retro-design fan, is that it's constructed entirely of metal. Yet it doesn't weigh a ton. It's highly portable, and you can place it on a floor, table, or bookcase, and aim it wherever you please. The fan pivots and holds its position through a full 360 degrees. The fan is also made with safety in mind, because all of the moving parts are completely enclosed. The plug is an ordinary ungrounded two-prong plug (with one wide and one narrow prong). The fan can be easily taken apart for periodic cleaning--the manual gives detailed instructions.

title: Check the positive battery holder terminals
abstract:
Like many others I owned the original Radio Shack version of this 130-in-1 electronics kit decades ago. True, this Elenco version isn't very sturdy. It's light and flimsy. But the overall layout, components, and experiments you can wire together are about the same. The 159-page real paper manual that comes with it is a plus (the PDF is also available for download from Elenco's web site). Each experiment has an overview, a schematic, and wiring connection-by-numbers instructions. Many useful and educational analog circuit designs are included (plus one digital gate logic IC). No microprocessor, computer, smart phone, or software updates required. Yea!!!

OK, now the quality issues. The first experiments I correctly wired together didn't work at all. I installed two different sets of 6AA batteries (Amazon Rechargeable then Duracell Alkaline). Still nothing. I returned the first one back to Amazon, got a replacement the next day. Both had the same problem. Both had a sticker with Date Code 0119. Hmmmm, manufactured the same day, same problem. I did some basic troubleshooting to try to figure out the problem.

It turns out the design or manufacture of the battery holder is defective. There is a gap of about 1mm between the + side of each battery and terminals in the holder. Two small plastic tabs at that location prevented the battery connection from being made. My "fix" was to jam a wadded up piece of copper tape to fill the gap at each of the 6 positive battery terminals to complete the battery circuit (aluminum foil would work fine too). Hopefully Elenco will crack the whip at the Chinese factory to fix this, or they'll see a lot of returns for this very simple and silly defect. Check recent reviews to see if the problem has been fixed in newer batches from the factory.

If you don't have a voltmeter, you can construct a simple circuit to see if power from the batteries is making it to the front panel. Install the batteries and try lighting up the decimal point of the digital display by connecting: 25-121,24-119 or 25-124,24-122

Most of the experiments I've tried so far worked. But the AM radio receiver circuits are iffy. The only one I could make work was #113: Two-Transistor Radio. I used the supplied long green wire raised up high as the antenna. The signal levels seem too low to work for #112: Crystal Set Radio and #109: Operational Amplifier AM Radio.

Quality issues aside, I'm keeping it. I'm having too much fun with it. And I have great respect for the designers who created the original analog circuits that can be recreated using this kit.

title: Comfort markers
abstract:
I love this set. About 3 years ago I received a set of 10 Stabilo 88's as a free incentive with some colored pencils I ordered. The biggest challenge was keeping them! Lots of people wanted to "borrow" them.

I used them daily at work for 2 years and marveled at the seeming never ending supply of ink. I retired them to the home last year and my 3 year old granddaughter discovered them soon after. She managed to destroy three of the tips before mastering the pressure needed to make marks. Exactly the excuse I needed to purchase this set.

Of the few art supplies I took with me on a two month trip, with only two bags of luggage allowed, these were the #1 choice with my micron pens, and my derwent inktense and graphitint pencils. My pencils were rolled up in an expensive canvas pencil case and this cheap plastic rollup with the stretchy velcro closure turned out to be the better storage. So I started sneaking several of the other pencils into this case for quick trips around town. VERY satisfied.

If you get a set with busted nibs or dried out ink (as one reviewer noted) check out Amazon's return policy! It's the best!!

title: Contender for best mouse I've owned
abstract:
Contender for best mouse I've owned, going up against the Logitech g900. They are very different mice, for different people though.

PROS:
-excellent feel. the ergonomics are on point, and it's honestly a pleasure to hold. slides nicely on any surface, weight is perfect, and fatigue is zero.
-separate buttons. so tired of the trend of mice that have one piece of plastic on top, rather than individual cut out buttons. (e.g. razer deathadder) it looks nice, but feels like crap.
-the auto switch scroll mechanism. I miss it on all other mice now. my G900 has a mechanical button to switch modes, and while that is nice, it's not as incredibly satisfying and intuitive as the MX master
-beautiful. my office mates are jealous
-LONG battery life. I forget it needs to be charged after 3 weeks to a month, which is about when it starts blinking at me. (I use it 4-8 hours a day at work), and when it does charge, the charge port is in a perfect place to not impede your work.
-excellent bluetooth. I leave it on my desk at night, and when sit down with my laptop it wakes right up and immediately works. I've had some input lag issues with it, but those are few and far between, and can be fixed by flipping the switch.

Neutral:
-the side scroll wheel. It's a nice feature, but doesn't respond all that well in GIMP or chrome. it's always either too sensitive or not enough. that said, it's the best side wheel i've ever used. they must be hard to do right or something.

CONS:
-mine came with a bump in the scroll wheel, due to bad molding. normally this wouldn't be a complaint, but for a $100 mouse (at time of purchase) it better be absolutely perfect.
-back and forward buttons are tiny. you get used to them for sure, but a more conventional layout would be a lot better, and more efficient.
-the gesture control button. might as well have just omitted it. It has its uses, but it's so awkward to press (the actual button is on the seam of the plastic and the metal) that it is 99% of the time easier to just do the thing the gesture was replacing. now, if the button had been under where your thumb rests naturally, this might have been in the pros category.
-the omission of side clicks on the scroll wheel. I can see why they wouldn't on a non-gaming mouse, but I would like them just to assign controls to.

title: Cordless Flex Adds Alexa Safely to Powder Room, Needs No Accessory Shelf
abstract:
The ECHO FLEX is perfect for my powder room. It plugs directly into an electrical outlet above the vanity sink, and it doesn't require either (1) a cord, or (2) an accessory shelf to hold it out of the way (above the vanity countertop). Thus it reduces clutter around the sink; and it is safer than a regular Echo or Echo Dot in this location. (You can't accidentally knock it into a sinkful of water.)

The Echo Flex connects through the Alexa app, and does everything that the other Echo devices do. For my household, this means turning lights or tv on and off; setting timers and reminders; asking for local weather or traffic information; checking the time; asking general knowledge questions; doing math and recipe calculations; playing music; and "dropping in" on Echo devices in other rooms (using the Echos as an intercom). The speaker isn't up to audiophile standards for playing music, but it's fine for playing casual background music and for hearing the spoken word.

The Echo Flex is especially great for my husband, who is hard of hearing. When he's in the powder room now, he can hear me when I "drop in" even if the water is running. The Echo Flex is located only about a yard away. (He can't hear me when I "drop in" to a bedroom device that is located about 15 feet away.)

Setup takes about 5 minutes if you have already downloaded the Alexa app. After you plug the Echo Flex in, it advises you to open the Alexa app to complete the setup. The app takes you the rest of the way through setup.

title: Could have been wonderful. Has execution flaws.
abstract:
Update: received replacement & the second is just like the first unfortunately. So I will assume this was made by the same crafter & from the same batch as the last. Again, the paper has been pulled too tightly & ripped through the backing. It has also been cut through the first 30% of the pages at one edge. There are paint pen marking all over the journal inside & out. This one has a cut down the front where maybe they had begun to make a scoring cut in the leather & realized it was going to be too short & then just put the design over it. They did a better job of getting a deeper embossing on this one tho. The finish is worse however. This one has a weird finish almost like pumice stones where it looks kind of crackled & porous Idk if it was done on purpose as a design or not. I wish this crafter would learn to not use paint pens to mark up leather bc it ruins the product. If you try to remove the paint pen you ruin the leather. I am double bummed for having given them a second chance.
Old review:
This could have been a beautiful little hotter notebook. Unfortunately it is not. The ppl that made it decided to use metallic paint pens & permanent markers to mark all their sewing lines ruining the aesthetic. There is not a spot on either side without a blemish. I had resolved myself that if only the inside was ugly I could live with that. Lol. Bc there's a lot of that irl imo, but it turned out that both the inside & outside had imperfections behind what I was prepared to pay for & live with. As a disabled person I can generally live with a lot lol, but I spend my little bit of money on writing tools & I like them to be nice. This could have been a thing of true beauty as it reminds me of several Levenger notebooks I own. Sadly, while the idea was great the execution is lacking. I hope they will do it right next time bc it's the perfect size to throw into a purse or backpack for a short trip or even a longer jaunt if you bring paper refills. The paper quality was not what I was hoping for either & as it arrived torn & already pulling away from its base I would not have used it anyways. As it is it is a hard no for me in its current state. I hope that either the seller or amazon will do right me. Someone should definitely be doing quality inspection checks bc this would not have passed even a rudimentary one. The metallic silver paint pen was a glaring no staring me right in the face the second I opened it up. The black permanent marker while it did match the journal better was still extremely obvious & still extremely annoying to see. It's a well thought out design in my estimation just an extremely flawed execution. I hope the seller tweaks their issues & offers it in other colors bc I would totally try again.

title: Critical review, I use a lot of batteries.
abstract:
I use these batteries in a remote control, the annoying toilet flusher, a portable radio, my owl alerts, flashlights, and many other battery powered gadgets that normally discharge batteries. So far they work really well in these gadgets and the charger surprisingly charges them faster than I thought. Definitely worth the money because they last much longer than the non rechargeable disposable batteries and better for the environment. As for fit they seem to fit fine in everything so far without any problems which is really nice especially on expensive devices. I can tell you that they get a little warmer in the charger than I am comfortable with which concerns me. Because from personal experience fast charging getting batteries hot is not good for any rechargeable batteries it runis them plus its not safe I wish they had a slow or low charging setting. I can honestly say these easily out perform the Rayovac, Energizer, and Duracell rechargable batteries that discarge quickly saving you money and headaches. For just normal homeowners use for remote controls and around the household these should work perfectly fine. I have bought other batteries from EBL off Amazon and absolutely love them. I will have to keep taking notes on discharge, charging, and start measuring voltage on these to see how consistent they are and update this review. Stay tuned.

Truthfully the only reason why I bought these is they do not offer the red EBL 1.5v AA Li-Ion rechargeable 3000mWh batteries in any quantity greater than four with a charger on Amazon which is why for value for my money I only rate the "value for the money" partpurchase at 3 stars. EBL needs to make those available here just like these batteries why they do not is a mystery to me. If you need an honest to goodness AA 1.5v battery for something sensitive to voltage read my review on those batteries they sell.

title: Critical review. Great for original Wayfarer frames. Thank you
abstract: First time buying this brand. At first I was a little disappointed because when they first they arrived they would not slide on the ear pieces of my black frame "Blues Brothers" Ray-Ban Wayfarer frames of my eyeglasses. So I looked them over and couldn't find any defects in workmanship the stitching that I could see was actually very nicely done with the correct thread and correct upper/lower machine tension. So I gently slid the ends that go over the ear pieces over a hard plastic toothbrush handle almost the same size as the Wayfarer frame just a little smaller. When I slid each side over the plastic handle I noticed that what was stopping them from going on was glue inside of the openings which is not a big deal in fact it shows me the manufacturer is not afraid to use enough glue for the job. So now I clean my wayfarers with lemon pledge like I always have and wipe them clean. The retainer went onto the ear pieces perfectly not too tight not too loose just right the second try. So far they feel pretty good they keep my eyeglasses from falling off my face leaning down, they work great on a motorcycle, and I think they are going to do the job just fine for me. I would like to see if they have a design similar to another brand I have used in the past because I like the craftsmanship and quality of the retainer. Thank you very much.

title: Cut the cord now - working with HULU, DirectTV Now, HBO GO and more
abstract:
This is our second Fire Stick. Our first one is a first generation unit and we have it on the guest room tv now - it still works fine. We cut the cable cord completely six months ago and went totally to streaming. We added this new Fire Stick for the master bedroom and a Roku Express for the living room.

I love being able to link our Fire Sticks to Alexa. We have a Dot in the guest room and the original Echo in the master bedroom controlling both Fire Sticks. This one also works on verbal commands through the remote, but you have to think about what you ask for if you have several streaming services. We have Prime, Netflix, Hulu, HBO Go and DirectTV Now (still saving $165 a month over cable!) and Alexa can find a specific show, but perhaps not on the channel you wanted.

Comparing the Fire Stick and the Roku Express is pretty simple. The layout for the two is completely different and I actually think the Roku is easier to sort through and find stuff. It feels less cluttered actually. I do appreciate the full integration of the Fire Stick with my other devices through our Amazon account - I can pick up a show on Prime with my tablet, phone or tv exactly where I left off. Regardless of which streaming stick we use, we're still incredibly happy we dumped the cable.

title: Cute as a button!
abstract:
This little stuffed Doberman is so darn cute. My son has been begging for a Doberman puppy for some time but the family dog is not having it (he's spoiled and doesn't like to share-see photo). So for his birthday, I ordered this adorable stuffed pooch. He turned 24 and laughed (he's a good sport) when I handed it to him and proclaimed "I bought that puppy you've been wanting." And of course the sting was better since I placed some cold hard cash in the collar (the real gift).

This stuffed animal is:
-Well made.
-Closely resembles the real thing. Pointed ears and markings. Although a real Doberman's markings might be a little darker than the tan on this one. The one I use to own and he had more red tones in his fur, on his feet and muzzle. The button eyes and cute nose make it kissable.) FYI. It was so real looking that our dog continuously went up to it and tried to establish who was in charge of the house!
-Has a nice stance.
-The gold collar adds some bling.
-It is soft and cuddly, perfect for those youngsters who receive it.
-Nice sized. It stands about 12in tall.

I'd definitely recommend it. 5 stars

abstract:

title: DIY Ball Pit and Sensory Pool
abstract:
Why use a pool as Ball Pit?

In short: Ball Pits are a great therapy tool! The visual, auditory and tactile sensory stimuli and the proprioceptive feedback builds confidence and strengthens motor skills during occupational therapy. Using balls of multiple colors can help with visual sensory stimulus and they can be used to build early speech skills like color identification, counting and more. If properly padded and filled with crush-resistant balls, they can be great for deep pressure and vestibular activities (kids love to throw themselves into a sea of colors).

Using an inflatable pool means that you don't need this to be out all of time, it is soft and provides a decent cushion on the sides (we put a thick therapy pad under ours to protect kids who like to dive in). It is also easy to clean the pool and the balls all at once. Plus this can be used as a ball pit, put a duvet full of pillows and its a crash pad, fill it with water or sand, foam, goop, etc. There are loads of options to use this for.

Activities and games can also be created based on the child's age and goals. For example, one game we play a lot is a sort of tiny basketball. A therapist can ask the child to find a red ball and then a blue ball and shoot them into a hoop. Doing this works on color identification (as I mentioned before), receptive language, multi-step directions, and the fine motor skills of finding and grasping the ball, motor planning to throw the ball into the hoop, and so on.

To sum it up: They are fun, great for sensory and body awareness therapies, and I had this deep personal bias that it would just be so gosh darn fun to have one, even if just a temporary one to pull out as needed.

It cost us $37.99 and measures in at 90x 58 inches, which was a perfect size for the space beside one of our climbing towers/rope tree and the wall. If it ever gets a hole in it or gets damaged (which one has), I am not heartbroken, after all, it cost less than $40 and is easily replaced.

We blow ours up with the tiny electric air pump that we use on all of our inflatable therapy tools (peanuts and yoga and therapy balls). It is the same kind used for camping/air mattresses and works like a charm It is tough to blow up without this, so I definitely recommend picking one up if you don't have one!

There is a cap in the bottom that allows you to fill it up with water and then simply open the bottom valve piece to drain it later. We use this for balls, water, and sand play but you could fill it with foam or goop for another sensory-fun option.

I am still rating this as 5 stars though we have had to buy two. The first one we bought ripped along an inner seam (due to some of our rowdier kiddos) and was not fixable due to the location. Mind you, this was after month and months of constant daily abuse by multiple kids from age 3 to 12 all jumping off of, diving into, thrashing around, and generally having a good time with it.

title: DOES THE JOB—PLUS!
abstract:
I bought a 35 year old house and nothing had been done in all that time to stop the build up of deposits in the pipes. At first I was skeptical, but I noticed the other day that I'm getting more suds in the shower and in the laundry now, and I bought a new coffee maker and there're no deposits in there either.

Update June 22, 2019 I bought this August 2018 so it hasn't even been a year, and I thought it'd take much, much longer until I saw any real results—I was wrong! Besides getting more suds in the shower, and laundry my hair is smoother. Until lately I've had to use bar soap in order to get the right amount of lather—no more. I've been very happily surprised by the lather I get from my liquid soap.

Last year I had to get a new water heater and I was concerned about how long it'd last because of the hard water, but I've had the water tested and so far so good! Also, the shower is much easier to clean now because there are a minimum of deposits on the walls. I had to have a plumber install this and it was expensive, but well worth it!

Update, July 2019–it's been nearly a year and things keep getting better, so don't listen to the reviews who and said it does nothing because maybe they haven't waited long enough. I'm getting hot water sooner now which means the deposits are going away. The hot water tank is right across the hall from the bathroom, but I still used to have to wait and wait. I don't anymore. It's not immediate, but it's only a few minutes now and it used to take much longer. I just can't say enough good things about this—I'm so pleased with this and hope it lasts a long time.

title: Damaged! Stamps don't pick up the ink properly.
abstract: I've used Carter's for 4 decades in a work environment & home environment for arts & crafts, but I have never in my life received one looking like this. Looks like some kid stick their fingers in it. Lol. And the seal actually looked as tho it had been previously compromised when I went to open it. I wish I had thought to take a pic of that. I'm less than thrilled bc I needed this asap for a current project. The front of the pad is pretty beat up too. It has a very obvious dent in it which I would assume is when the interior pad got messed up making it hard to get stamps to pick up the ink evenly without applying a lot of pressure & then you get parts of the stamp that aren't part of the design. This seems like a scratch & dent sale ink pad to me which sucks bc I love Carter's & have used them for decades as I stated before. The pad appears to be inked well & is not dry. It even seems to close pretty well considering the huge dent in the lid, but it does not work for the purposes I purchased it for. I'm hoping I can return it or exchange it.

title: Decent dashcam for the price, a pain to configure, not the image quality I expected
abstract:
For the price this is hard to beat. It has lots of great features, including a Wifi app, but resolution/quality even on the highest settings are slightly disappointing. I have everything configured to provide the sharpest possible image (highest resolution and bit rate, etc.), and if a car is more than 30' away, zooming in on a screenshot of a license plate is iffy at best, even if the footage was taken in bright daylight (screencaps taken in VLC). Something seems off to me. Yes, I removed the protective films, and yes, my window is reasonably clean (normal conditions). I have attached two photos: one of the unit in a fantastic little case I found for it (see below), and a screencap showing the problem I described. The van in front of me is semi-readable, and was about 25 feet away. The car 15-20 feet further away on the left is unreadable, as is the plate close to me on the left. And yes, I have the CPL filter installed on the lens.

Configuring this was a bit of a hassle. The Wi-Fi app is not intuitive, and some quick googling led me to discover you have to temporarily disable your cellular data the first time you use it to get the camera to connect. Once configured, the camera itself acts as the network your phone connects to. This means your phone cannot be connected to any other Wi-Fi network while you are connected to the camera. I have no idea why they don't just allow you to use Bluetooth for this--it would be simpler to set up, that's for sure. Honestly, having integrated security video will be a factor in the next car I purchase. This is all way too much work.

Many PCs will not play the default file format this records in as they lack the correct video codec (H.265) or enough processing power. I think there must be a way to change the format it records in, but I was unable to find the configuration setting to change in either the app or the camera itself. To get this to play files on your PC, I suggest using VLC Player. It is free, and if you are running the latest version (check for updates in the application), it will run them just fine if your PC has the juice for HD at this level. If you experience dropped frames or choppy video when playing back on your computer, this is probably because your computer is not equipped with a GPU to support this high resolution of video (many aren't; if you don't have a dedicated video card in your PC, you may experience this). My office desktop does not have a dedicated video card and the video is a bit choppy if other things are running--expected.

If you are interested, the case is the "Mchoi Hard EVA Travel Case for Garmin inReach Mini GPS", (ASIN: B08F9QV1BQ), which is very sturdy and cost me $13.49 in Feb 2021. I looked for EVER for a case for this, and this was the best fit I found.

title: Decent quality, decent value....
abstract:
I'll admit it: I'm an adult who loves to color. I find it a great way to relax, and there are some amazing "coloring books for adults" gaining popularity these days (Johanna Basford, Angie Grace, etc.). And there are whole communities of "colorists" popping up on social media.

So naturally, I'm looking for different mediums to use when I color. I've used colored pencils and gel pens, so I figured it was time to branch out into the marker arena. Someone suggested starting with these as they're water-based rather than alcohol-based, and Amazon has them at a good price, so I got the 50-ct set.

Overall, I'm pleased. There is a good selection of colors, several shades of each, which helps to bring some variety into th mix.

What I DON'T like (and this seems to be a problem for ALL coloring mediums): the actual color of the pen/pencil/etc. almost NEVER matches the color of the cap/barrel/etc. I realize that colors will look different depending on the type a "color" of paper used as the background, but seriously, some of these are WAY off. I find myself having to make a "cheat sheet" on the paper I'm using just so I can get a clear picture of how the various colors REALLY look.

Like I said, this isn't just a problem with Crayola, but they make it a little more difficult because the pens have NO distinguishing markings on them whatsoever to designate a color number or code. I ended up putting little pieces of masking tape on each pen and numbering them myself just so I can keep the color charts coordinated.

All that aside, they work great once you figure out the colors. Colors are vibrant, and I had very little "bleed through" or feathering in an Angie Grace book. Bleed through and feathering depend a great deal on the paper used, so bear that in mind and ALWAYS test before coloring.

Overall​, I like these - don't "love" them, but they're good quality water-based markers at a very good price.

title: Decent, if having issues with back plate...
abstract:

I'm wondering if the one I bought was older stock that came with the difficult back plate and now they have a better updated one. Was able to put it together and now it works well.
Do note that the services provided for free are basic and do not include recording. First review below, I updated it above:

I'll change the rating if I somehow can get it to work but I don't see myself wanting to fight with this every time I need to put in new batteries. I essentially cannot use it.

title: Delighted with the Kindle Touch 3G
abstract:
Before buying the Kindle Touch 3G, I visited a Target store to see and handle the different Kindle e-readers. I immediately loved the simplicity, elegance, and convenience of the Kindle Touch 3G.

My sole desire is to read books easily without any distraction by the device that I am using. The Kindle Touch 3G is simple to use: "intuitive" is the word that ideally describes the operating features of this e-reader.

You can swipe the page to turn (as with any paper page) or tap.

Two toolbars disappear while you are reading, but both are accessed simultaneously with a simple tap at the top of the screen. A functional toolbar (allowing you to shop at Amazon, see battery status, etc.) appears at the top; a reading toolbar (allowing you to change font, etc.) appears at the bottom. Both are easy-to-use: just tap the choice you wish to make.

You have only two buttons to click on a regular basis: the on/off button at the bottom edge of the device and the Home button (looks like a tiny speaker) located just beneath the viewing screen.

You must hold the on/off button for approximately 7 seconds in order to power-off completely; otherwise, the screensaver will appear indefinitely.

Other features are available and are easy-to-master; however, you can begin reading out-of-the-box if you have a Kindle on your PC. The system automatically duplicates your archived items.

If you do not have a Kindle on your PC, you can begin reading once you register by entering the email and password that you use at Amazon.com. It is VERY, VERY easy to register: very user friendly. The screen and enclosed guide "walk you through" the simple process.

The Kindle Touch 3G is elegant. I also bought the case ($39.99). Together, the two items are almost as slim as a DVD and case rented from a Red Box. The design is sleek, slim, and pleasing to use.

Convenient? I found myself yesterday racing to an emergency room at my doctor's request. While waiting to be seen, I pulled-out my Kindle Touch 3G, began reaading a Sherlock Holmes short story, and had "no worries" about battery life or connectivity.

I heartily recommend the Kindle Touch 3G to anyone with an older relative who loves to read and may not have WiFi access OR who needs larger type in order to better enjoy the reading experience.

title: Deserves less than 1 star
abstract:
This drone is the worst we've ever tested. We've tested cheap ones and expensive ones and this one was the biggest disappointment and it absolutely is a safety concern! It randomly just stops responding to the remote and even with a full charge! Unlike what it claims- it doesn't just land when it loses signal- sometimes it'll continue to climb up into the air way over the house, sometimes it'll fly into things including almost hitting people at the park!

We got the first one and charged it fully and took it out back. Within a minute it went crazy and stopped responding and flew into the house, shattering 2 of the blades. We replaced those and tried again only to have it go unresponsive and run into our patch of sunflower stalks where it continued to run into my sunflowers cutting at them and after a few seconds of that it managed to burn up one of it's motors!

So we got a replacement and charged it and took it to the park. Within a couple minutes it went haywire and started flying at people when we weren't touching anything and it wouldn't let us land it or anything. Literally unresponsive!

We calibrated it multiple times and nothing helps. This thing is just a fancy looking dangerous paperweight. We've tested drones 1/3rd of the price that were way better made!

title: Disgusted - no USB cable was included in my purchase, and neither were there any instructions.
abstract: Perhaps I shouldn't write reviews when I'm so angry and frustrated. They say they include a USB cable (without a plug) and the seller DID NOT include a USB cable of any size. Standard USB doesn't fit, the Kindle trapezoid charger doesn't work as the seller suggested. I have no idea WHAT size each end of the USB cable is assuming had I actually received one with my purchase, which I didn't, - so I can't even try it out. I have a dozen or more different cables we've collected over the years and NONE of them work. No worries on the electrical connector assuming it really is USB - I guess I will never know what It is because it is NOT USB as it says on side of the player, and I have no idea what size the other end of that cable is because it's not included and there are no instructions included in the box. I finally need to charge it and looked again for the supposed cable or instructions and realize there is no cable or instructions, I suspect this may be one that has been used before and they just stuck it in a box without adding all the cables. As far as sound - it sounds like a cd being played in a tin can. I'm not one bit particular and I think it sucks - my son-in-law bought me a speaker block that does work and now it sounds like a high-end stereo. The writing on the device is back on black. I had to use my glasses, a magnifier and a small flashlight to read what it said just to turn it on. I guess it now goes in the trash because the original charge wore out and I have no idea what size each end of the non-existent charger should be. I only wanted this for when I am in the shower or doing my nails - to avoid needing to use my hands again so it doesn't get hours and hours of use. I just wanted a simple USB (identified size) and the correct size plug for the other end. I'm using this in the bathroom and there is no place to put my computer in there for additional usb ports. I'm perhaps a little old-fashioned but I don't care for laptops- screen size is way too small and I need two screens, a regular mouse and a standard size keyboard so I use a regular but top of the line, Alien computer. Laptops are difficult to work on while almost anybody can build (or repair) a PC

title: Do not trust your flock with this.
abstract:
*8-11 Dead chickens

This unit started to close early so every night I had to go put the chickens in by opening the door. Last night I put them up early only to awaken to the sounds of slaughter as three raccoons killed my chickens.
I should have trusted the bad reviews.

I like this unit it has been working very well so far.

 I really like how the crush sensor works, I have mine set on 2. When I installed the rails I made sure I was centered and even. I wrapped the sides of the door in several sheets of paper for a buffer and took it off after I set the rails. I did feel like the setting of 5 was too much. And once it's almost closed that crush sensor doesn't work, wouldn't be any different with the space below a light curtain or proximity sensor so I'm not knocking off for it, but it is worth noting.

There are a few reviews where people claim the door didn't open and even one review on a different site claiming the battery runs out quickly, where the author seems to be confused that this unit operates off a battery. Now I don't know what happened for those users but here is what I discovered testing this in my garage.
If the power has been off when it should trigger for time or light it didn't always do it until the next cycle. When the power comes back on you can hear an audible click in the linear actuator, I don't know if that's a relay that's just what I have observed. To avoid any such issues I bought a battery backup unit so even in a power outage not only will it either open or close, it will do it when it is supposed to.

I wish I had taken pics as I was installing it but I was rushing to get it on before vacation. I built it into a piece I attached to the front of the coop. you can see the box with the control unit and the red box next to it is the light sensor. I drilled a 5/8 inch hole through a 2x4 ran the cable through, sealed the cavity with silicon, and painted it red works great.
I put a cheap night vision camera up and it's been working exactly as it should. I don't have any complaints, it didn't come with the CR3032, not a big deal I had a pack. My only real complaint is it won't always do what it should have done later if the power is off and comes back on. The solution of course is to pair it with a battery backup.

title: Do your research before buying a feeder!
abstract:
No complaints from the birds. I like the ease of filling it, as well as it's easy to clean. I really like how many spots it has for the birds to drink from.
PLEASE do your research before buying a feeder and as well on how to "properly" feed the birds, clean the feeder and the nectar you make. Never add more sugar than needed. It's very bad for the birds. I use 1 part sugar to 4 parts water. So I cup of sugar and 4 cups of water. If ants become an issue, take care of it swiftly. Dead ants in the water will contaminate the water very quickly. Most hummingbird won't like to drink when this happens, but it also can make them very sick. My feeder is hanging from a long wood piece I hammered into my wood fence.
When ants make their way to my feeder, I remove the feeder, spray a ant/ bug spray along the fence and half way onto the stick I hang the feeder from. It works for about 6 weeks to deter them from finding their way to my feeder. Always remove the feeder first, and never spray the feeder or anywhere the birds perch. Hope this helps some of you. In the summer, I get an average of 20-30 birds at once all day long coming to my 4 feeders. I live in California, so we get a lot of hummies.

title: Does what it says
abstract:
This mouse trap works just as expected. After a lethal trap failed to do it's job twice, this trap worked after just 12 hours. I set this trap at night with peanut butter, and the next morning, the mouse was trapped. Unfortunately, the mouse had to sit in the trap until a few hours later. This meant the trap was a MESS when I finally was able to release the mouse. And I could smell the mouse droppings as soon as I walked within 10 feet of this trap, it was really bad.

Cleaning this trap is also not as simple as they make it look. And please DO NOT clean this in your kitchen sink as the image in the ad shows. I ended up putting enough Clorox water in an empty tidy cat pail and letting the trap soak over night. Then I took it outside to rinse off and clean with the provided scrub brush. (I do not recommend using this scrub brush more than once for fear of contaminating areas of the house with it).

It was difficult to remove the "cartridge" where the food goes the first time. But when I went to remove the mouse from the trap, using that same "door" the door came open easy enough without a struggle.

So far I am happy with this purchase and would recommend to anyone who is able to check the traps daily. I would hate to see a mouse get trapped in this trap and have to suffer and die. That would be a worse death than a lethal trap.

title: Doesn't focus on what you want
abstract:
I have a hard time with this camera. Maybe I'm just not camera savvy enough, but I seriously just wanted a simple point and shoot that would produce good quality photos. This camera comes with a ridiculous amount of fancy settings which I'm sure a lot of people enjoy.

A big reason we got it was to replace our DSLR which I never really learned how to use and I wanted something simpler. I try to take photos of birds in the back yard and this camera is completely hopeless with that. It will not focus on anything you want it to focus on, especially if there's any movement. It'll focus right next to the bird or behind the bird or under the bird or wherever. So you have to try to zoom in to the bird so the camera focuses on it, then zoom out again and hope that it stays focused on your bird (or whatever).

If you're looking to take photos of wildlife or anything of that sort, I'd find something else. We've switched back to the DSLR for wildlife photos so this camera will sit around to be used once a year with family or something. Hopefully it takes good landscape photos but I haven't seen a setting for that yet.

title: Don't Waste Your Money
abstract: [[VIDEOID:156bce087230e64ed84d164fbfe04140]] I'm highly UNimpressed with this product. The first coat did little to the glossy sheen on my old cabinet door. The directions encourage a second coat if needed, so I added another coat and let it sit overnight. By morning there were huge swaths of mold growth in a swirling pattern -this product is to be applied in a circular motion with a coarse cloth. I'm kinda mad! Sure these cabinets are old and in desperate need of attention - that's why I was trying to use this in the first place! Also, I guess you don't have to rinse it despite the residue remains because the directions say only "product will leave a slight residue that can be painted." Still, it scratched easily enough with a fingernail so I worried anything wouldn't adhere properly anyway, plus I now needed to treat the mold. I spent about 30min with steel wool scouring at the residue and still only got most of it. Besides that, the gloss is only barely off the portions where it was intact on this door so that it's now more like a satin finish (see short vid) instead of high gloss. It would've taken less time and effort to just take my hand sander to the door! And I now have to worry about the mold!! I'm disgusted!

title: Don't be fooled by the size/amount..!!
abstract:
These are absolutely perfect with the exception, and if you're advertising them with the larger size rock- it can be a bit misleading at best. tbh, it would be SO helpful if seller showed what 50 of these look like in a glass cup, then 100, and so on…
It's better to order the amount you need the first time and that usually isn't done by a number quantity but rather a volume capacity! Something I find would make all the difference and save the buyer a lot of frustration.

Take notice of the photo included… I had filled this just over 1/2 way full and was hoping by adding these it would bring the volume to 3/4 full. Ha..!! Not even close- it would've taken five orders for sure- again, something that could've been avoided by sharing a visual of the volume these small stones would fill.

Otherwise, aside from being small like the size of a peanut out of it shell- they are a pretty color and at least add variety to a fun mix. Anyone interested be aware.. volume you receive from a single order is approximately 1/4-1/2 cup. Hoping this helps others not make the same mistake I did.. stay safe!

title: Don't be put off by this smaller blade size!
abstract:
I live in Southern California and ceiling fans are a great way to circulate air and keep a room cooler. Also, any way we can save on electricity, I'm for it.

I bought a two-story home two years ago but there were no ceiling fans in the upstairs bedrooms or office space. I recently had an electrician come and install ceiling fan boxes in all three rooms and also install two of these fans.

I could not be happier with the results! I hear absolutely NO noise (which is my main priority) unless I turn the speed up to level three…and then that's just the sound of the air moving. I don't even go over level two, since this is a powerful enough fan. You might hear just a slight click when the fan is turned on or off.

I knew I wanted a smart fan…this one comes with a hard remote but also provides an app to load on various devices. I don't even use the hard remote, since my iPhone and tablet app provide plenty of selections. The remote has a magnetic cradle that can be mounted to the wall if you want. I also can connect this to my Google home base, but haven't quite gotten around to that.

This fan comes in black and silver/gray and, while the gray was a tempting choice, I went with the white so it would visually not stand out too much. I am drawn to pretty fans but then wanted something low profile in my bedroom and office. I would consider this a hugger style that fits closer to the ceiling.

I was not used to the fan blades being so "short" (38 inches) and was concerned it would not be strong enough to put out enough circulation. My electrician said it is actually more functional, and he is right. I never need to set the speed over two. (He was impressed with the quality of this model and wanted to know where I bought them.)

The style of the fan has a contemporary feel to it but would fit well in most decor settings. While I don't use the fan light often, I like that it is dimmable. I selected the warm light so it would not be too harsh. I think I will be using that overhead light a bit more in my office once the days start getting shorter.

I noticed immediately that I was not turning my A/C on nearly as much. The second floor is, of course, warmer but sometimes all we need is just to get the air moving.

The remote app allows for reversing the blade direction and even a "breeze" function where it might change speeds, directions, etc. I don't really use that but it's a nice feature if you prefer that setting.

I like these fans so much that I might buy one for the living room. I think that it will put out enough circulation to accommodate that size space. So happy with this purchase!

title: Don't bother.
abstract:
My wife purchased this for me which was nice, she found it in my shopping cart and thought I wanted it, I wanted something similar but not this exactly. I tried to return it but the seller wouldn't respond, that is a huge disappointment and will keep me from ever dealing with them again.

Having not used the product here is my review. As someone else pointed out the nutes don't come in individual packets they come in a ziplock sandwich bag with a generic paper label from cheap home printer stuck in it.

The tub is very thin and I'm sure would need to be modified to stop light from entering and causing algae growth, likewise the short section of air hose is clear and preferably would be black for the same reason.

The air stone I received was not a 4 inch disk, but was a more conventional air stone although nice and large.

In summary, it's a little overpriced but generally kits like this are, and the nutes aren't packaged as advertised. Seller didn't respond even to say they wouldn't accept a return. I think you'd be better off building your own, which is what I ended up doing after looking at this setup.

title: Don't expect great vision with this one...
abstract:
Our faithful old sensor night light in the bathroom finally gave up the ghost.
It was time to look for another night light. Our cats both eat in the bathroom as well (long story short -
tiny place, tiled floors make the best place to feed messy eaters), and want light before they will
go in and eat (even though they should have great night vision!).

I bought this one, for the main feature of energy usage and not getting hot. (Our old light got very hot
there at the end.) Since I didn't want one I had to babysit, I thought this would be great.

The value of the package here (at least when I bought it) was really good. You get TWO nightlights in the package.
Both of mine were blue. they worked right out of the package, so no problems with that.

HOWEVER - I need more light than this little thing puts out. It gives everything a blue hue, of course, which is
fine, except it isn't bright enough to tell if you are missing the toilet seat, getting ready to step on something
(like a cat), etc etc. I need something brighter. Apparently, the cats also want a brighter light, because I get
head-butted at weird hours to go flip on the light for them so they can eat! Wish I could train them to turn the lights
off and on themselves.

I could see these being just great in a hallway where you just need more of a guiding light.
But for actual vision, this isn't the one. Nice product, fair pricing, looks very nice and the color is good, but
the actual light output just isn't enough to work for us.

title: Double wall stainless mug
abstract: Bought two, one black one stainless for husband and I - road trip. Each morning we filled with ice and then topped with water... the cups kept the water and ice EASILY through 10 hours - some of which was in a hot, parked truck. I hand washed them.. although you may be able to put in the dishwasher, top rack. The lids have a tiny hole and the the slot for drinking. I have a different style lid on another cup that has a "slide" to help stop spills... to be honest that lid sucks. SUPER hard to clean and get the soap out of. These lids rocked! Easy to clean and stayed put. Of course, if you do tip them over, they will leak. I recommend keeping them upright no matter what lid you have.:) They are not super heavy... they do seem to be double walled as they kept the ice in the glass easily to the end of the day. Oh, and they are narrower at the bottom, as shown in the photo, so they fit into cup holders easily. I would totally buy these again and feel comfortable recommending them. Just fyi... I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful or that would change my review.

title: Durable Stainless Steel Black Pen
abstract:
I purchased this Add-On set of two pens based on the recommendations of others. I am a Pen Connoisseur. I love office supplies and am constantly buying new products, as well as re-purchasing those which really write smoothly for me. I kept forgetting to add this set to an order over $25.00. Received on August 1st of 2018. I'd waited so long & was very eager to try them out.

Unfortunately in my pen set the first pen was not as smooth writing as I expected. While it certainly was a Fine point I was disappointed - that is until I tried the second ZEBRA 301 pen. It wrote smoother, but I like a darker coloring in my black pens. I see these as more of an utilitarian pens.

I don't see myself purchasing this pen again, but I will keep it inside the spirals of my Reviews of my STENO notepad since it's so thin. It'll be convenient. Not having to press down hard to write is a decided advantage. I would recommend them to others. The ink doesn't bleed through or look visible on the back of the page.

If both pens wrote equally as smoothly I would have offer 5 stars instead of 4 stars. I'll keep one pen in the car. The stainless steel body gives it some weight and it is refillable, as well as a retractable ballpoint pen. I hope you get a chance to write with this pen and you find it to your liking.

title: Durable, Adorable, and Awesome!
abstract: Arrived early. I bought this because I wanted the Tab 4 with a thick silicon case, tablet stand, keyboard, and mouse to all fit in one envelope. I'm glad that it arrived in a box that matches the definitions of the envelope because I was hoping that it wasn't rolled up. The envelope is extremely well made and adorable (also water proof too)! The envelope is extremely light and the red satin material with help protect the screen. It has the internal demensions of the envelope printed on the envelope in red as well as showing that the envelope is super tough with foam protection, inner lining and tough outer skin.It even has a bar-code on it! On the fake white stickers located on the outer side of the flap, one has sender and zip code with some space to write on (yes you can write on this!). My favorite sticker is the one on the right side. It says "Delivery Instructions: Beware of the dog, small post box, neighbor is a thief, probably on holiday, leave in shed, and Beware of Grandma (all with check boxes beside them). The only thing I didn't care for was the length of the 3 red vertical vinyl strips on the back of the envelope. The back of the envelope is 16.5 in. while the strips are 11.75 in. So you can fold the flap over any distance on the strip but that causes the envelope to bend and I prefer it unbent. I also wish the sellers included more detailed pictures about the stickers and especially the back side of the envelope. Over all, I would definitely get this again!

title: Earth friendly biodegradable dog waste bags
abstract: I purchased these for my two nieces who both have BIG dogs. I like that the bags are biodegradable. While we all like convenience, we have to think about land fills! Comes with a dispenser too. These are Christmas gifts I know they will actually use.  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - nearly 6,000 reviews posted, viewed over 50,000 times, and over 24,000 likes. I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Echo Dot 2nd gen
abstract: So... I own both the tower and now several dots. Of course the dots are more reasonably priced, however, the speaker ability is really where it's vastly different. Obviously the tower is much better in the speaker department. However, I did find that there is a cordless speaker you can buy to go with your 2nd gen dot that is an improvement and still at lower price point than the tower when combined with the cost of the dot. (Mokcao cordless speaker - amazon sells it too) Because the dots are so reasonably priced we have them in all 3 major rooms and use the cordless speaker to drop one dot in and take it outside to our sunroom when we like. Over all, I am pleased with both my tower AND dots... but probably will stick to dot purchases in the future because of the price point. I would say if you've been on the fence, the dot is well worth a try. It's very easy to set up, you will need to download the app, also easy to follow step by step setups. Once you're hooked up you will be amazed at how often you use Alexa. At our house she helps me keep track of where I am supposed to be every day... timers... night time meditation... the occasional argument and even plays games with us as well as much needed comedic relief. It may not be "necessary" to have Alexa, but I am always surprised at how often we use her assistance. It's nice and worth it to us. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: Egg Cooker
abstract: I usually don't have single function items in my kitchen. But I have a 9-year-old who wants boiled eggs all the time. I'm not comfortable letting him use the gas stove on his own, so I thought maybe this little device would give him some egg freedom in his life. I tried it the first time to make sure it wasn't going to be too dangerous for him. But it was fine. I actually didn't read the directions, so I didn't know about poking a hole in the egg the first time I tried it. The eggs turned out fine. The second time, I stabbed holes in the eggs per the directions, but I still have no idea what it accomplished other than making weird webs inside the thing. Anyway, back to the purpose of this purchase. I explained the process to my 9-year-old and gave him warnings about how hot the eggs would be when he opened the device. He was able to cook his own eggs start to finish without help. He used a dish towel to remove the hot eggs from the tray and place them in a bowl of ice water. So now, he won't be bugging me to boil him a bazillion eggs every day. He'll just be bugging me to buy him a bazillion eggs. As an adult, I can get the exact same effect with a pan of water. But for a kid, this is easy and much safer than using the stove.

title: Excellent Feeder; Works Well and Well Made
abstract:
My wife has always been an avid bird watcher and there has almost always been a couple of bird feeders in the yard. Several years ago she bought a Squirrel Buster Plus and it has served well. This is the first time we have has a chance to use a Squirrel Buster Classic and it has proven to be an excellent feeder. Though we have only had it in the yard a couple of days it is already attracting a variety of birds to itself.

The idea behind this feeder is straightforward. The feeder has several feeding ports and is encased in a sliding cage that moves with gravity. So, when something heavy gets on the feeder, like a squirrel, the outer cage slides down and closes the feeding ports so there is no way to get the seed out. The cage is metal and is very resistant to gnawing and chewing so squirrels will have a difficult time damaging it. There are no batteries to replace and there is no harm that is done to the squirrel (other than frustrating it).

The mechanism is adjustable so that it can be made more or less sensitive as desired. If the larger birds like crows and grackles are monopolizing the feeder, make it more sensitive so that it responds to less weight. If it is too sensitive such that a small group of smaller birds triggers it to slide, make it less sensitive.

The perches at the feeding ports are removable, but to do so requires a screwdriver to gently bend the clamp side open. They will not come off by accident, but rather the ability to remove them requires deliberate effort. This allows for discouraging birds like house finches that sit and gorge all day. Without perches, you'll see more birds that are able to cling to the cage versus birds that perch.

It is a little more complex to fill than most other feeders we have used but this does not mean it is difficult by any means. Be careful to keep track of the smaller parts so that when you reassemble it after filling you can actually put it back together properly.

We put this feeder in the yard, filled with black oil sunflower seed. Within 24 hours, we were getting chickadees, titmice, goldfinches and a downy woodpecker.

This is a fine feeder and it works very much as designed. It can be adjusted to keep out nuisance birds and it definitely keeps even determined squirrels from getting to the seed inside. It is well made and will last for years with proper care. If you like feeding the birds in the yard but do not enjoy feeding the squirrels so much, this feeder is very much worth a look.

title: Excellent Hedge Trimmer, Electrical Cord Not Included
abstract:
This [[ASIN:B0012FRZFU Black & Decker HT020 Electric Dual Action Hedge Trimmer]], with its 20-inch blade, made quick work of trimming my privet hedge this morning. Even though I will use this tool only 4 or 5 times a year (because my condo's garden area is so small), I feel the trimmer is worth the investment.

Instead of this trimmer, I've been using a rechargeable battery powered Sears Craftsman Cordless Combo Clipper with a 6-inch blade. It's hardly worth taking out of the box. The Combo blade is so short, it feels like you're trimming the hedge with scissors or pruning shears. Hand-powered (manual) hedge clippers feel much the same, and they don't cut easily through the woody parts of my hedge.

This Black and Decker HT020 is lightweight enough for any woman to handle and control. It's simple to set up (attach the handle and guard to the body with the two included screws) and operate (pull back the lock and squeeze the trigger handle). This model has a one-position handle, but Black and Decker makes a similar [[ASIN:B0012FRZFK Model HT022]] with a plastic knob that adjusts the handle to four different positions.

My one surprise (probably because I don't often buy power tools) was that this HT020 hedge trimmer comes without an electrical cord. To operate it, you will need to purchase a separate outdoor extension cord (at least medium-duty). Fortunately, I already had a 25-foot, heavy-duty outdoor extension cord on hand. It works fine with this trimmer.

title: Excellent Pie Dishes Made From Borosilicate Glass
abstract:
Because I loved my [[ASIN:B0016LOCMO 10-Inch Marinex Pie Dishes]], I came back to Amazon and purchased two of these 9-INCH MARINEX GLASS FLUTED PIE DISHES. The Marinex brand is superior to the present-day Pyrex brand, because Marinex makes its glass cookware from borosilicate glass. Borosilicate glass is less susceptible to thermal shock than tempered soda lime glass, which Pyrex uses. (Years ago, Pyrex dishes were also made of borosilicate glass.) Borosilicate glass has a slight green tinge.

Pyrex pie plates have (or used to have) a flat, fluted flange that makes it easy to press the top and bottom crusts together, and to make a decorative crust edging. The Marinex pie plates have similar fluting, but it's more vertical, so I'm having to learn how to create really nice-looking crusts with the Marinex plates. However, I feel much safer using products made with borosilicate glass, because some of my newer Pyrex dishes have shattered when set down on a room-temperature, ceramic-tile countertop.

These Marinex pie plates are the right size for all recipes calling for 9-inch pie plates; and the 10-inch pie plates are great if you like to make thicker pies with more filling. I've found that the Pillsbury Readymade pie crusts from the grocery store's cold case will fit both the 9-inch and 10-inch Marinex plates.

Marinex warns that a pie dish taken from the freezer should not be placed immediately in an oven, if the oven has been preheated above 100 degrees Fahrenheit. (Thermal shock is still something to be careful about, no matter what kind of glass is in your baking dish.)

title: Excellent Set of Four Custard Cups Made of Borosilicate Glass
abstract:
The custard cups in this MARINEX SET OF FOUR 8-1/2 OUNCE GLASS CUSTARD CUPS are conveniently sized for single servings of baked custard, pudding, or ice cream. (They are slightly larger than the small Pyrex custard cups that many cooks are familiar with.) These are genuine Marinex custard cups, with the usual markings, including "Made in Brazil". They are not absolutely uniform in shape but they stack fine in my kitchen cabinet.

For some time now, I've been replacing my Pyrex glass cookware with the more expensive Marinex glass cookware, because the Marinex products are made from borosilicate glass.
