Borosilicate glass, which has a slight green tinge, is less susceptible to thermal shock than the tempered soda lime glass used by Pyrex. (Years ago, Pyrex dishes were also made of borosilicate glass.)

I feel safer using glass cookware made with borosilicate glass, because some of my newer Pyrex dishes have shattered when they were removed from the oven and placed on a room-temperature, ceramic-tile countertop. (Now, of course, I always place glass cookware on a hotpad or oven mitt to avoid thermal shock.) I've been very happy with all of the Marinex products I've previously purchased, which include pie plates and baking dishes.

title: Excellent audio quality and small footprint
abstract:
I placed this under my 55" HDTV. It is a narrower but is a good width for getting stereo sound. I used a stand for the TV, and the speaker sets on the foot with about 2" to spare. The subwoofer was hidden behind my computer desk. Connection is by Bluetooth, so there is no wire out the back. The speakers and subwoofer both provide plenty of volume. If anything the subwoofer is overwhelming, but you can adjust its volume independently. The visual feedback through some blue LEDs hidden behind the speaker mesh works well. There are multiple preset buttons for music, conversation/voice, etc. They shape the response of the system and tend to work okay but are not exceptional. Overall sound quality is very good across the entire audible spectrum.

My biggest complaint is that the speaker will go to standby way too often and revert to the ARC input while I use the AUX input. Ut results in a lot of pushes of buttons to get the speaker system awake and on the right channel again. Small things like this prevented me from giving it 5 stars, but the speaker system is very good and a good value.

title: Excellent disposable one-use teapot filters that simplifies cleanup for me when making one pot of tea
abstract:
I love tea and have a lot of tea infusers but have become lazy as I get older. These disposable bags allow me to make one pot of tea (up to 10 cups) and then just throw out the bag without having to dump an infuser and wash it. Although I have automatic teapots with their own infusers, sometimes I just want to use one of my regular ceramic teapots.

I just fill the filter with enough tea for the size pot I am using and then hang this inside the pot by using the teapot's lid to keep the top half of the filter in place and closed. I make sure a piece of the filter sticks out between the secured lid and the teapot. Since there is no way to close the filter, this method is necessary to keep the leaves in the bag. I learned this from watching my German friends who use these regularly.

These filters also are made in Germany. I purchased the 400 count which comes in four 100 count boxes as shown. Since there are four separate boxes, they can be gifted to other tea lovers as well if 400 is too much for one person. The price I paid on Amazon was $18.22 which I consider a good deal especially since the price went up $7.48 since last week.

title: Excellent for moving & storage & floods!
abstract: I purchased these for multiple reasons. The main reason was that I was moving. I was moving bc my apt kept flooding. Luckily having been through other floods I generally store all my stuff in plastic containers anyways. Sadly a couple of my vintage Singer's in wooden boxes had been left out during the last move & the last flood got them moldy & ruined them. I am a bibliophile & these bags held not only huge stacks of my hardcover books, but my 40 pound Singer sewing machines. I also carried hundreds of pounds of yarn (50 per bag) and thousands of pounds of quilting fabric during my move. It held up to paints, plants, garden pits, & pretty much anything I threw at it. I even put my pots & pans in these bags. While I still thought they were a bit pricey I did buy some on sale & I think I bought 18 total that I was able to pack & take to my new place & unload & go pack again. Tho I now intend to leave some of my yarn in them as it's waterproof. Tho I intend to place it on a top shelf just to be on the safe side. Lol. Not one bag ripped, tore, or had an issue so far that I am aware of tho I have not checked them over very well. And I had no issues with the zippers tho I am positive that I packed several bags well over the weight limit on accident bc I was trying to keep certain quilting fabrics together for a quilt project. I've bought some real duds on Amazon, but this was not one of them. This has by far been one of my better purchases & I've told my kids that are planning to move to buy the bags too bc it is just so much easier imo. I literally used a taxi to move half my stuff (disabled & don't drive) & was able to fold the bags back down to how they arrived after unpacking to take them back to be packed again. I also made little tags and used color coded handkerchiefs I hung on the handles so I knew which room the bags went in or knew what was in them without having to open them in the wrong room once I moved. It saved time. I live in an apt & these bags take up a lot less space than the massive sterling & Rubbermaid hard sided plastic totes I normally use for moving & craft storage. I still have them & use them, but storing them is a challenge. Also, the bags fit under my zinus/spa sensations type elevated platform bed. It's a frame amazon sells & you buy your own mattress. Normally I can fit 8 hard sided tubs under my bed (queen bed), but I'm limited by the height of the tubs. The bags fit or I'm able to squish to fit if I overfill them which is nice. Depending on how full you pack them you can get 4-8. They are different sizes than my plastic tubs tho. I only wish I had stumbled across these bags years ago given how many times I've moved. Lol.

title: Excellent for the Price
abstract:
I spent a good deal of time researching colored pencils before I bought this particular set of Prang pencils. I compared a number of brands and read reviews for Prismacolor, RoseArt and even Crayola among others, and I finally settled on Prang after reading the many positive reviews. So far I am very pleased with these colored pencils.

One of the main things that I was hoping to avoid with a colored pencil set is brittle, crumbly cores that require frequent sharpening. So far this set has not suffered from that issue and the cores seem to be solid. I have not had the misfortune of dropping a pencil yet so I am not sure how well they hold up when subjected to such a physical stress, but at least they're not disintegrating as I draw.

Colors are rich and bright. These pencils are neither too hard nor too soft so coverage is smooth and creamy. They blend nicely too which is good.

There are 50 colors in this particular set of pencils so finding the right color (or combination of colors) is easy. There are pencil sets with over 100 colors but those cost a lot more (50 was the largest set I could find offered by Prang). Right now as I write this, this set goes for under $13 full retail, bringing the cost of each pencil in this set to about $0.25 apiece.

So far I am very pleased with this set of colored pencils. The price is right and the pencils themselves seem to be of good quality. You can probably find a better set of pencils out there if you look hard enough but expect to pay more.

title: Excellent value - good sound & long battery life
abstract:
I've been using these for a few days now and I'm pretty impressed. I use them mainly for listening to audio books & podcasts and some music while working out in the barn or cleaning house, that sort of thing. My normal usage pattern requires comfort when wearing for a couple of hours at a time in some serious heat & humidity outdoors. These Kinivo bluetooth headphones have just enough padding to be comfortable, but not enough to make it hard to hear oustide noises. The distance is pretty decent too - I know for a fact they are recieving & playing a clear signal at least 100 feet from my cell phone out at the barn. Now, that is in a relatively unobstructed line in any direction - just one or two half walls & gates. At home, they work throughout the entire house and only start to break up or lose the signal when I go outside to the yard and leave the phone inside. To my thinking, that's pretty darn good overall reception!

I have been VERY impressed with the battery life. Yesterday I was doing a hard clean in the barn and listened to 4 hours of an audio book non stop while I worked. Then got home and used them for another 2 hours straight while cleaning house and the battery was STILL strong. When I do charge these, I use the USB to wall plug adapter thing that came with my Kindle and it works just fine - you can also charge them via the USB on your laptop. I have only used these headphones with my Samsung Galaxy Note cell phone so I can't speak about how well they work with a laptop or other brands of phones. I have taken a couple of calls with the headphones and the sound is clear on both ends, so the microphone works fine. Overall....an excellent purchase!

title: Extra gimmick/tool to keep thieves away
abstract:
We mounted one on each of our Lectric Xp bikes. With a few real thick zip ties (the ones included are useless) they fit perfectly and solidly in the bike rack. And once you load your cargo or in my case mount a thin board on top of the rack. There will be no access for anyone to reach or destroy the alarm if it goes off. It is the perfect fit and hiding spot for those with a similar bike or rack set up. Although, I know some hide it in the seat above the post. It has enough air gap to hear the horn/alarm and can't be messed with or even found/seen.

Now as for how well the alarm works. It arms and works great as a bell with the 3 tone options. No idea if it will deter thieves. But I know I would not be able to waste much time trying to cut any locks with this alarm blaring for the 30 seconds it takes to reset.

You can see in my photos that it fits perfectly flush on the rear rack. So it is easy to place cargo on the rack and not touch the alarm. I installed it facing down to the fender. There is only a 2 inch gap between the fender and rack so the alarm does not touch the fender and not enough room to reach alarm this way either. Once I mount the wood panel to the rack. It will be totally covered and unreachable to the average person. Sure it will add a extra step should I need to change the batteries. But minor detail. And should this post reveal a way to defeat the location. Still likely to get enough eyes on the thief to show anyone around that a bike is being stolen. Bike is only used in daytime and mostly for trail riding.

For the price. This is a worth it expense to try for a well rounded security in conjunction with one or two bike lock methods. We have three!

title: FIVE STAR WEDGE!
abstract: I hand split my wood and I purchased this wedge after wearing out another that I had for six years. I like this wedge as it is.5 pounds more than the competition and it seems to have a sharper tip. I use a 4 pound maul with it and I am able to split a 24" wide tree cut in 18" lengths in about three hours. The tip makes it so easy to tap into the wood. It looks as if it splits four ways,but I have never had that kind of luck. It splits faster and wider than a standard wedge. I have been using this type of wedge for about 10 years and I won't go back to the old split wedge. If you are splitting hickory or a harder wood caution is needed as sometime the wedge will pop out and rocket into the air. One other thing about these wedges, is that they are very easy to lose. If you have an can of fluorescent paint, it would be advisable to spray the wedge intermittently or you may be spending half of your time looking for it. I have to give this a five star because it is easily stored and so inexpensive and doesn't need to be put on a hard surface like a floor splitter. I am not into moving ricks here and there. just to accommodate an hydraulic splitter..just doing the job on the spot and throwing the split wood into my truck to haul off straight from the tree.

title: FIVE WELL DESERVED STARS...
abstract:
As a long time Kindle Fire user I was happy to see the new HD8. I waited until the price was unbelievable before purchasing because I didn't want to be disappointed. I loved the old Kindle Fire, the body, the features, all of it. I was extremely disappointed when Amazon did away with the indestructible design of the old Fire. My HD6 has been thrown, tossed, dropped more times than I can count (in a subway station, on concrete, on asphalt) and it just shuts itself off until you're ready to respect it. Turn it on and pick up right where you left off. I've had it for two years and I never planned on giving it up..until now.
I wanted the HD8 because I am a reader and being limited to how many books I can have at my fingertips is hurtful. I have over 3K books in the cloud and selfishly I wanted to keep about 1,000 on hand. New book, favorites, classics. Not having expandable memory affected that. With the HD8, I now have the capability to have my requisite 1000 books on hand at all times.
As a lover of all Amazon, I have a Fire TV. Last weekend my very sweet teenage children lost the remote and I was too in awe of their skill to search for it. I downloaded the app on my HD8 and it connected in under a minute. I know this app was always around, I've seen it but...on the tablet it's amazing. I have a blank screen and I just swipe using my finger to my hearts content.
Now to the technical stuff that I don't always get...the screen is crisp, very bright. The size is perfect and that was my initial concern. I didn't want a huge tablet but when I use the case I prop it on my tummy when I'm laying on the couch reading and it's perfect. Text to Speech is the best thing ever as of this minute. My books read to me...no need to pull up Audible as well!
I haven't seen any other major changes and I've been using a Fire HD for years, but I am in love with this one.
This will sound strange but my advice is get a case for it. Amazon sellers have a wide variety of cases and with the delicate feel of this tablet I am still a little wary of dropping it. Also, being able to prop it up makes it great for using it in the kitchen for your cookbooks, reading while laying down or watching movies in the bathroom (bubble bath-highly recommended).
As with my other Fire I take this one now with me EVERYWHERE I go. When I leave the house I grab cellphone, car keys and Kindle everytime. I highly recommend.

title: FUN!
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:acf9cdcacff8949d90bca373ad735d4e]] Very fast and easy to use.
I know others have asked questions about does it work in the snow. Yes, but you will 20 minutes of work to get the snow out when you get done so it can dry. I've had it out in the snow twice. And it's so much fun, but it's hard to control to make jumps or anything. I can't wait to try it out in the spring.

Update. 4/22/2020. This truck is a lot of fun. Snows melting and there's lots of fun mud puddles to jump through.

The only downside that I have noticed. Is the wheels. They are plastic rims and they crack fairly easy. I've only cracked one to the point that is not usable. I don't know exactly what I did to break it... Hit a rock when I hopped over a pot hole. Honestly Idk. I inspected the rest of the wheels 3 out 4 cracked or chipped although 2 of those still work fine.
I also don't like the wheel pins that connect the axle to the wheels. They are really easy to lose and hard to replace. (no hobby stores near by plus no one is allowed to got out for nonessential stuff anyway) You really need to make sure that you have the pin in the axle evenly and that it goes in groove on rim all the way. You can feel it when it's correct. Incorrect and you'll loose the pin as soon as you you drive off.

I'm pretty sure this truck is more than just water resistant because today I was almost fully submerged once unintentionally of course, and then once more because it was kinda cool... It seems to be fine. I cleaned it up and dried it out.
One of the tires filled up with water and made it hard to steer. Nothing major.
I'd probably buy this truck a second time.

title: Fantastic looking - descriptions are accurate.
abstract: Unit arrived on-time, the packaging was crushed on at least 2 sides. I was nervous, but there were firm corner supports and the unit was set back from the edges and undisturbed. Installation was accompanied with an exterior support; just as a precautionary measure. I chose to skip the side skirts and carved out an exact cut-out of the unit into 1/2" plywood; approx 12"x18". I covered the plywood with white paneling and trimmed with matching corner round for a finished look. The appearance is both stealth and rich. The remote did not work. (I suspect battery). The app worked great; so I use it exclusively for now. It is somewhat louder than expected, but my wife enjoys the distraction, and this is in our sunroom - so it's not that big a deal. The eco mode setting on restart is apparently Gov. required. I'm not really interested in what the temp setting is; I just lowered until I was comfortable and use that as my baseline. Overall, so far it's met our expectations. Would have been higher rating if it was slightly quieter with a working remote, but the apps work just fine on ipad, iphone and Android devices especially the ability to program on and off settings, or remotely control the unit while away.

title: Fantastic printer!
abstract:
So so so SOOOO pleased with this printer. I'd set aside an hour and a half to mess with it to get it set up an for a good mid-set-up frustration cry, it took less than 20 minutes to go from sealed box to spitting out shipping labels, even WITH a small cry out of relief in there.

The manual directs you to their website for the Android/oS app. The page just says to go to the app store and download an app which is very succinctly simply called "Shipping Printer" (icon is a black printer w blue paper). There's nothing else on their website of relevance to set up so save yourself some time and just download the app. As per a tip on here I just screenshot the label, rotate and trim it in my Gallery, and then once the app is open you just hit "file", pick your image, click the next arrow, then click print. Easy parcheesie. Idk if there's a way to bulk print or not, but at the bulk I'm shipping I'm not fussed to find out.

It spits out labels lighting fast, and while they could be a little darker they're still plenty dark and totally readable.

Another cool thing is it comes with a USB to USB-c (newer phone port) adapter so you can actually plug the printer straight into your phone if you don't have a computer, and connect that way if you don't have blue tooth or it's being buggy or whatev. AND it comes with a USB protector thing. And a good-size roll of thermal paper.

Absolutely no complaints. Feels well-made and sturdy and looks like one of those Glade aromatherapy smoke things.

title: First tech gadget to drag my husband from 1997 into 2014! GREAT tablet!
abstract:
Wow! I got the Fire 8.9" tablet for my husband as an early Christmas present while he's recovering from major surgery. (I used a gift card for another store, so thanks Mom!) This is his first ever tablet - dragging the man into this century is like pulling an ox out of quicksand with a rubber band. I needed a tablet that would be: easy to use, back itself up, was big enough for his giant hands, light weight to use while in recovery, have access to all our photos in the cloud while he was in and out of the hospital and bed rest, and easy access to movies and the books already on his ancient Kindle Keyboard. As expected, the first hour with his new Fire HDX was full of complaining and cursing and shoutiness. (This also happened with our new car, the Kuerig coffee maker, yogurt, blue underwear, and every new toothbrush in the past 18 years. )

Two days on....The man is carrying his new Fire everywhere he goes. He's doing email on it, SKYPEing with a buddy, Twitter, reading the news, watching movies, shooting video and pictures of the dogs and throwing them to the TV via the mirroring with the Fire TV stick. (That is a neat trick). In short, my beloved Neanderthal has finally arrived in 2014 and I am delighted! To be honest, I love my 7" Fire HDX, but after seeing and using his new 8.9" in person, I am jealous and sort of want the bigger version myself now.

title: Fit in dishwasher great, Made in the USA..
abstract:
Up-Date,
I have now had these Glasses for almost 8 months..I have to say one glass hit the side of my granite counter, and fell, and broke.
Other then that, Not one other glass has broke,or chipped..
I have bought 12 for one of my Grandkids. They love them, and they have not broke also.
I love these glasses, and they still look like brand new, and I use them everyday.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
I have not found a problem with these glasses, as some others have!
Although I have not had them for long.
I put them in the dishwasher, and they came out looking fine.
Before I start my dishwasher, I turn my hot water on, so the hot water goes right in, Nothing cracked or broken.
I also like that there not as wide as my other everyday glasses I have, so I can fit more of these in my dishwasher on the top rack.

 There modern looking straight from top to bottom, and heavier at the bottom. They do not tip over. There a clear glass.
$21.00 including shipping for 12 Anchor Hocking glasses made in the USA is a great deal. I see other sellers are charging more money..

Some people took off stars cause there was bar codes stickers on the bottom of each glass!! No big deal. It does not take away the quality from these glasses.
After you peel off the stickers, use a little Alcohol on a cotton ball, and it takes off any residue, there is no problem..Its only a one time thing,

It seemed that people that bought these glasses a few years ago, had a problem with the way they where package, and got broken glasses!
 Mine came packaged VERY Good. No broken glasses..
If these start to crack or break in my dishwasher, I will be back to give a update.

title: Fits in Lookout Tower
abstract:
I felt like I needed a Paw Patrol car lesson while shopping for cars to fit in the Lookout Tower. Let me tell you there are three main lines I found on Amazon, Spin Masters website, and in Target/Walmart:
- Basic Vehicles
- Transforming Vehicles
- Ultimate Rescue Vehicles

I wanted cars that would fit the Lookout Tower, and finally figured out that although some people may say that the Ultimate Rescue line fits in the tower, they are the biggest of the three lines and some reviews say those are too big.
The Basic Vehicles are the original vehicles (the Basic Chase car comes with the Lookout Tower) and those were originally intended to be the cars for the tower. The Basic Zuma car is simply called "Zumas Hovercraft". However, the Basic line is hardest to find, and they are currently either marked up by third party sellers on Amazon or I could only find one or two Basic cars at each Target I visited.

Enter this Transforming line. They are a bit smaller than the Ultimate Rescue, and I was able to find them for $12.99 each on Amazon. They all have a little button that pops out the pups gear. For Zuma, it's actuslly a little frustrating that my 2.5 year old can't reset the gear by himself because you have to push it in gently at the right angle while gently closing the hood, but all of the other pups seem fine for him to do himself.

Long story short, this will work in the Lookout Tower. Best of luck finding them all for your kid.

title: Flexible Blades Perform Like Old "Rubber" Blades
abstract:
Recently, I purchased a Rubbermaid spoon-shaped spatula to replace an old one (with a "rubber" blade) that had been in my kitchen drawer for more than 10 years. Unfortunately, the new Rubbermaid spatula had a stiff blade (probably silicone) that didn't perform nearly as well as the old "rubber" blade. The stiff new-model blade didn't conform easily to the sides of the bowl or pan that was being scraped, and it left behind a lot more ice cream, icing, sauce, and gravy than the old "rubber" blade.

The blades of this wonderful set of silicone spatulas have exactly the same flexibility as the blade on my old "rubber" spatula. All of them, but especially the spoon-shaped spatula, make it easy to scoop out thick mixtures quickly without leaving a lot of the mixture behind. I am really pleased to have found this product, especially because the 3-piece set cost less than the single replacement ([[ASIN:B0000VLZK8 Rubbermaid FG193300WHT 9-1/2-Inch Spoon-Shaped Spatula]]).

Other reviewers report that the spatulas are not durable, and that the blades come off, especially with dishwasher use. However, for me the spatulas rate 5 stars, because what I need most are the flexible blades. I use them for scraping bowls, not for mixing thick batters or for cooking on the stovetop.

title: For monkeying around
abstract:
This weird little tripod is a useful addition to the gear of any amateur or hobby photographer with a DSLR and the inspiration to take breath-taking and/or unusual photographs. (I'm using it with a Nikon D7000)

Pros:

1. Light and portable. If you don't have a side pocket on your camera bag, just wrap it around a strap or loop.
2. Flexible. As advertised, the legs can be bent into loops and angles for getting shots from weird angles. It can also be wrapped around posts, tree branches, bench rails etc.
3. Convenient. An easy way to get shots requiring a stable camera almost level with ledges or sideways attached to a tree. However, you can only shoot in landscape format unless you get the accessory BH1 ball head. Naturally, with its little legs, you'll be pretty close to the ground if there's nothing available for wrapping around, but you'll be sure to get great camera angles from a worm's eye view.

Cons:

1. Attaching your camera to the tripod is a bit of a pain, requiring a coin (any currency) or a strong fingernail. A better bet is to get the accessory Joby BH1 Ball Head with Bubble Level and attach the quick release clip to your camera beforehand.
2. You need to practice with it a bit to get the stability right, and if you have the legs in an unbalanced position, or on a smooth surface, you can get sagging and camera movement.
3. Trying to get the camera level without the ball head can be quite challenging, and you may well miss the shot. (Of course you can always do the straightening with software, but it's better to get it right the first time.)
4. Can't shoot in portrait format unless you get the ball head.
5. Hard to get the legs back straight with all the segments in line.

Note: It comes with a 1/4-to-3/8-inch adapter attached to the mounting screw, so you have to remove this to attach the camera or accessory ball head.

Recommended (with the [[ASIN:B002CVU4G0 Joby BH1 Ball Head with Bubble Level for Joby GP3 SLR-Zoom Gorillapods]]) for photo walks, theme parks or general walk-abouts where that prize-winning shot may be just a Gorillapod away.

Amanda Richards, January 10, 2012

title: Fred & Friends Dinner Winner kids trays
abstract:
These are a big hit with my 2 and 5 year old grandsons... I usually put a mini hersey's bar at the "end" surprise.. but they are just as happy with a couple of m & m's or marshmallows. I tried a sliced strawberry once, that didn't get quite as good a response, but they ate it.:) Honestly, it's hard to get the 5 year old to be interested in food, while the 2 year old needs to do everything the 5 year old does, thus I needed 2. I think the price is too high for what they are... but obviously I did it. It's nice to have something "different" at grandmas house. I never hesitate to update my reviews with important info should anything come up and I will do so here. So far, they are have washed up nicely. While they can be washed on the top rack of the dishwasher, I have been hand washing them.
UPDATE: 5/22/2016.... I could have been more "helpful" by including some usable info... Each plate is about 9" x 6".. the lip of each tray is around 1/2"... I am eyeballing this measurements... I continue to hand wash them with ease. They are fairly weighty for plastic. If there is any other info that would be helpful I always respond to questions/comments.

title: Fun, but really loud and cannot turn it off
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:3ff1a927a97195cb8ef0b1bdd1b16c0d]] My 6 month old likes it enough. The buttons are easy to push, so he has no issues engaging with it. The problem is that it's so much louder than other "noisy" toys and there's no volume control options. It's much louder than every other toy we have When they have the volume turned all the way up/at the highest level.

There is a switch on the bottom to turn it off/on. Unfortunately, this switch does absolutely nothing (as you can see in the posted video). This is very frustrating when I'm trying to clean up and it starts blasting music and sounds. It has woken him up on multiple occasions. We took the batteries out for a while, but then it loses its appeal and he never plays with it.

Maybe we just got a dud. There is an on/off switch, so we may have just received one that's defective. If it worked, I would probably rate it 3 stars. Baby enjoys it, but due to the high volume and no option to turn it down, I can't justify a higher rating. There are thousands of options for baby toys and I'd much rather have one that can't be heard through the entire house.

title: Functional little budget friendly planner
abstract:
This planner is pretty much as described in the listing. The front cover is a plastic pocket with a design card slid in. You can do as you want with this- keep it in, take it out- replace it with what you want, or use it to store a few extra pieces of paper. The next few pages before the calendar begins has a "quick reference" page that includes a spot to jot down personal information, emergency information, and family/friends information. Next couple of pages has a "yearly overview" and "holidays" listing. The next two pages are lined pages for contact information. Then it proceeds into the month calendar followed by weekly pages (2 pages- all within one view for that week). At the back of the book, just after the calendar finishes up there are 10 pages (front and back, + one side of a page) that are blank, lined pages for whatever. A one page thicker card stock completes the planner that includes a map of the United States, the capitol of each state, and the time zones. The wire spiral binding diameter is large enough to comfortably hold a mechanical pencil or pen. The planner comes with little sticky tabs with the months printed on them.

I typically use a mechanical pencil or an Ultra Fine tip Sharpie in my day to day use. I currently have a mechanical pencil attached to the spiral binding. However for the purpose of this review, I decided to try out a Sharpie so as to give you an indication of how the paper handles the ink saturation. While the paper is thicker than a typical legal pad, the ink of the Sharpie does bleed through. Not terribly, but enough to plan to just keep on using my mechanical pencil. This is not a negative for me, unless I was expecting it given the product description: "The planner is resistant to the most passionate artist giving reduced bleeding,"...
(I intend to include pictures)

In summation, I like this little planner. It is better than I anticipated, and I am using it daily to jot down what I need to do, or to keep track of what I did. I like that month sticky tabs came with it, for better organization and quick reference. I added in use of binder clips, a rubber band, a paper clip, and a stack of sticky notes to further assist me in making use of this planner. The larger full month view is set up like a typical calendar- Sunday through Saturday (I have seen some run Monday through Sunday, and that is the worst for a full month viewing). I really like that the weekly section is all within one view. On the weekly view it runs, Monday through Sunday, with Saturday and Sunday sharing a block. And that works very well. I have seen many that go into a second page, and that does not help a visual person like myself. If I can see it in an organized manner, then I can copy it to memory. This layout is solid, and happens to have enough space to jot down notes, and really use it in an active manner. Nice job!

title: Fuzzy images. Not a good choice for a first telescope.
abstract:
This isn't a good first telescope, if the intent is to introduce and encourage someone to pursue the hobby of astronomy further. The images were fuzzy and distorted and varied in focus across the field of view. Any reflector telescope, even this small one, requires the mirrors to be precisely aligned (collimated) to get sharp images. Out of the box, the two mirrors were not aligned well. I did take it apart. I unscrewed the primary mirror holder from the bottom and drilled out larger diameter holes so that I could adjust the positioning of primary mirror I reseated the secondary mirror (below the eyepiece) which was not level. The 3 existing screws in the secondary mirror can be adjusted to adjust the alignment of the secondary mirror. After some manual collimation, the image is now much better. Stars no longer look like fuzzy balls. But this process isn't easily done in this telescope, nor is it described in the included instructions. Reflector telescopes can be quite persnickety because of their need to be precisely adjusted. My advice is to either spend more money on an reflector which has better optics which can be collimated, or choose a refractor telescope which I think is easier to use for a beginner and doesn't require such adjustments such as this one for not much higher cost:
Celestron 21035 70mm Travel Scope https://www.amazon.com/dp/B001TI9Y2M/ref=cm_sw_r_other_taa_QTn5zbPV2FBNX

title: Glitchy under certain conditions.
abstract: It seems to work fine for everything but games, and it seems that the sound processor may be the source of the audio and video glitches. Certain sounds seem to cause more problems than others, including dropped audio, glitchy video, and sometimes a blank screen. This happens with both XBox Ones and a PS3. I mainly play Forza 6 and Gran Turismo 6, and certain engine sounds seem to be associated with these problems more than others. Streaming video doesn't seem to cause any problems with any of the input devices or either TV. The normal solution is to cycle the power off and back on. Different cables or settings don't seem to make a difference. I'm not using the audio splitter at all. Personal opinion (from decades of experience with processors of all kinds), is that whatever processor is used simply cannot process some sounds correctly, even to pass the signal through. I may be wrong. I've been wrong before. This may be a quality control issue, or it may be an engineering issue. Either way, I'm looking for a better product, and most of the ones in this price range seem to be identical except for the name on the box. In fact, many more expensive devices seem to be exactly the same layout, and likely use the same circuitry. There's no way to tell from the name on the box, or the Amazon description.

title: Going the distance
abstract:
This is my current go-to lens. I wish I could afford one of the more fancy-schmancy professional telephotos, but until then, this one is the one parked on my Nikon D7000.

Uses:

1. Birds, bugs and other critters from a safe distance or on the fly/run
2. Portraits of one or two people (gives excellent bokeh)
3. Landscapes and seascapes, especially in vertical/portrait mode.

Limitations:

1. Buildings from across-the-street distance
2. Large groups of people
3. Macro shots from thisclose

Depending on the type of photography you enjoy, this may or may not be the lens for you. It works fine for me for the uses above, especially when the subjects are a respectable distance away, but it doesn't have a wide enough angle for limitations 1 and 2, and if you're closer than a couple of feet it won't focus properly.

It's also pretty heavy, but makes up for this by making you look like a pro who knows what they're about, especially when you use the lens hood (included and highly recommended for use)

The auto-focus is not as smooth as it should be, and you can sometimes hear the mechanism moving around trying to do its job, but image stabilization and the tripod detection mode are huge pluses. (It also attaches/detaches from the camera in the opposite direction to my other (Sigma) lens)

For the type of photography I'm doing at the moment. even if it's not on the camera, this lens goes with me wherever I roam.

Amanda Richards, March 30, 2012

title: Good Product
abstract:
The irritating thing about Fire pits is that they disintegrate. I purchased this as a replacement for my 24" bowl. I would have preferred a bowl that was an exact fit, but unfortunately there doesn't seem to be much of a market for replacement fire pit bowls.

The 29.5" bowl fits in my fire pit stand well enough. There's a bit of a lip around the circumference, but it works just fine. I'm still able to set my grill in the bowl. I wish this bowl were a little deeper, but it's fine for cooking/grilling/making s'mores.

There is no hole drilled in the bottom of the bowl, so it doesn't drain after rain. Rain collecting in your fire pit bowl is inevitable because you often have to let the ashes cool overnight.

Essentially, I'm glad I'm able to purchase a replacement bowl rather than a whole new fire pit. However, I wish the perfect size and shape bowl was available for my fire pit. Also, I think the price is a little too high. I would have been pleased to pay $20, but $30 makes me wince just a little. Still, the product does what it says it will do. Hopefully I get a couple years out of this. It seems sturdier than the original bowl, but we'll see.

title: Good Quality Line
abstract:
I bought this trimmer line to re-spool my trimmer. I was encouraged by the other positive reviews here on this product and selected it over others I had researched on that basis. This was a good purchase and has worked out very well for me.

This is not traditional round line, but rather it is actually almost square. It is made of two different materials and the edge/corner material is the harder, more durable of the two. It's somewhat stiff though not brittle, and as a result the line holds up when trimming in close quarters. Where the line that came with my string trimmer is soft and wears very quickly, this line holds up better and wears slowly, even when trimming along concrete sidewalks, aluminum gutters and rust-covered pipes and poles.

I spooled my trimmer and went to work in the yard, and I had to feed line about half as often as I did with the original string. In the long run, this will save me a lot of money.

I'm very happy with this trimmer string and wish my trimmer came with it instead of the cheap stuff that was on it when I got it. This is a much higher quality string that is more durable, meaning less work for the user and less expense over time.

title: Good Quality, Appropriate for Jigsaw Puzzle Experts
abstract:
This GLISTELLO 1000-PIECE JIGSAW PUZZLE FOR ADULTS - DE HAAR CASTLE, NETHERLANDS (27.5 x 19.7 inches) is a good quality puzzle, highly appropriate for jigsaw puzzle experts. It has many similar cloud and tulip pieces that present a challenge to assembly, because the pieces need to be placed by shape as well as by color. Of course, jigsaw puzzle experts love these difficult jigsaws!

The puzzle pieces are small, which makes the 1000-piece puzzle fit easily on a worktable. The fully interlocking pieces are thick enough to be handled easily, and the interlocking tabs don't bend if the pieces are handled with ordinary care. The pieces don't click together like Ravensburger puzzle pieces, but they fit together unmistakably by feel when properly joined.

Unfortunately, the pieces don't fit tightly enough to allow joined sections to be picked up and moved without falling apart. Completed sections need to be picked up on a sheet of paper, or pushed along the tabletop, to reach their proper locations in the puzzle.

The puzzle picture looks exactly like the photograph on the product page. The picture is nicely printed on the puzzle itself, and on a big sheet packed inside the box for reference during assembly. The price (about $19 on Amazon) is very reasonable for a jigsaw puzzle of this size and quality.

I wouldn't recommend this puzzle for group assembly, because of the many pieces that are visually similar in color and shape. Puzzles like this one require a lot of sorting of pieces in advance by color and shape if the actual assembly is to proceed quickly.

title: Good for desktop laptop cooling
abstract: I had to replace my current laptop cooler. The fans were going bad (very noisy). I use this with a 17" HP dv9000t laptop with two high speed hard drives generating a good amount of heat. The laptop is a desktop replacement. If you use your laptop actually ON your lap, this cooler is not for you considering the open back on the fan. If you use the laptop on your desk, it is very effective, especially for the price. It is VERY quiet. In addition to the large fan moving a lot of air at low speed which reduces the noise of the cooler itself, it is so effective at cooling, the fan IN my laptop has not had to go to high speed since I started using it. This lowers the overall sound. Just by having my hands on the top of the laptop when I type, I can tell the laptop is running much cooler. The cooler is a third of the price of the last one I had, but more effective. It does raise the height of the keyboard up more than my last cooler, but not to the extent that it causes a problem. Happy with this purchase.

title: Good for light watering
abstract: It really does stretch pretty far, though perhaps not as far as claimed. What I really like is that it's very light weight and easy to move around in my yard and patio areas without having to stop every few feet to untangle it, then it just slides right into the hose pot and you don't have to untangle it when you get it out the next time you use it. I haven't had it long enough to address durability. The only downside is it doesn't carry enough pressure for tasks like cleaning the bird bath, garden tools, patios etc. that's kind of the trade off. It's at its best when you don't want a burst of water, like watering flowers, but just fair for heavier cleaning tasks. In fairness, I subsequently read where the hose wasn't designed for situations where you want a heavy flow of water, so you should consider your main needs. I do have another supposedly non kink hose cleaning, applying hose end fertilizers, etc, but while that hose delivers plenty of water it has to be the worst hose on the planet for kinking, so it really is a blessing to pick up this hose for most other purposes.

title: Good percolator for an excellent price
abstract:
For years I pondered buying a percolator because I remember when my grandmother use to use a percolator such as this to make coffee. To me coffee brewing in a percolator smells just heavenly. Even though I rarely drink straight coffee, preferring my beverage to be more of a coffee drink than just brewed coffee with milk and sugar, I finally decided to purchase this one since it was reasonably priced at $19.99 and because my boyfriend is a regular coffee drinker.

PROS:
- The basket insert has very small horizontal openings for the water to drain through. This means not many grinds fall into the brewed coffee. With a round disc coffee filter such as [[ASIN:B001M8K5TU Melitta U S A Inc 628354 White Disc Coffee Filter]], almost zero grinds fall in.

- The outside of the pot has a cup indicator so it's easy to measure the water. Four (5 oz.) cups of water is the minimum level; eight (5 oz.) cups is max.

- The lid fits snugly.

- The pot pours easily.

CONS:
- The basket sits on a spring and that part is very easy to lose down the drain or in the garbage. I'm afraid that one day I'm going to forget to remove it from the post before dumping the coffee grinds from the basket.

- I would have preferred a glass top instead of the pastic one supplied. Apparently a [[ASIN:B0007Y8MDG Clear glass percolator top, fits Farberware, etc.]] can be purchased for an additional $6. It would have been nice if this product came with a glass top for an extra $3 in cost.

- The major con for me is that there's about a tablespoon of water left in the pot after I hand wash it. Hand washing is recommended. The lip on the pot prevented me from dumping this small amount of water out so every time I wash this pot my drying towels get soaked.

Despite the cons, I'm very pleased with this purchase and coffee brewing in a percolator still smells heavenly.

title: Good plastic tool box
abstract:
Good plastic tool box. The one-touch latch is quick and convenient. It is sturdier than the majority of plastic tool boxes and is easy to carry around.

The dimensions listed for the this box are outside dimensions and the shape of the box reduces usable area.

To me this box is one star less than the Stanley 023001W 23-Inch Structural Foam Toolbox.

The Dewalt is taller than the Stanley, but the Stanley is wider.

The Stanley feels solid, with a tight water resistant seal, and the Dewalt is not as solid and the seal is not as tight. The Stanley has two latches and takes a little effort to latch or unlatch. By comparison, the Dewalt feels effortless.

My circular saw fits in the Stanley, but not in the Dewalt. Both boxes have trays that do not extend the length of the box. The Stanley tray holds more and feels more ridged.

If I were carrying tools in the back of an open pickup, I would use the Stanley. It's less likely to open and unlikely to leak.

If I was in and out of the box all day, carrying it to different places, I'd use the Dewalt.

I have both boxes. They are the same price in the box store. I keep some mechanics tools in the Dewalt in the garage. I have the cordless Circular saw in the Stanley.

title: Good quality 12" non-stick pan with lid that I can move from stovetop to oven
abstract:
I ordered this pan because I needed this size in a non-stick pan for a recipe in one of my cookbooks and it came highly recommended by the author. I also needed a pan that could go from the stovetop into the oven and this can.

It comes with a lid that is very light and has two-vent holes on the rim side. The pan's handles are great for transporting / carrying this pan from stovetop to oven or to sink. They do get hot, so I needed to use a pot holder. Also, since they are large handles, the pan with the handles extend over the sides of the stove. I had to move things around to get the "working room" I needed.

I always lightly oil a non-stick surface and never cook without at least a thin coating on the pan.

Note that the instructions are useless. They are in 24 different languages with only one page dedicated to each language. The first page has a few sentences on how to assemble the lid (mine came pre-assembled). The one English page just mentions that the pan should be washed before first use and how to clean it after use. It also mentions that the warranty does not cover glass lids or scratch marks and that although it is dishwasher safe, that washing method is not recommended.

There is no mention that this can go into the oven, what is the maximum temperature to use, what the lid holes are for, or that there is even a lifetime warranty (although I understand there is a lifetime warranty). I suppose this would have to be shipped back to Denmark to claim the warranty.

Note that I have a gas stovetop but this can be used on an induction top as well.

Overall, I am very satisfied with my purchase. Only time will tell if this will hold up. I will update my review if this fails in any way.

title: Good so far could be better, read my full review for details
abstract:
They do the trick. I use yellow day to day and I twirl my keys around just a little and I havent had any tearing or breaking of as of yet.
Now my wife uses the white day to day and hers has already frayed by the metal hook, I twirled hers one morning and she noticed it later that day. So I'm guessing it's my fault. Point being they can tear up if your going to be rough with them. They do hook and stay hooked. No issues as of yet with it breaking or loosing. I will update if any of this happens even if it's a year from now.

If you find this review helpful, please vote, so Amazonian browsers can better learn, research and understand how products work for them.!. Thank you and Happy Buying

title: Good value. Simple, elegant design. Effective.
abstract:
I admit I was skeptical. However, the ad copy hit the major reason I went looking for an outdoor shade: late afternoon sun, and the effects on room comfort.

The shade comes already assembled, in a long box. Got here quick too, about a week. I live in California. All you need do is take it out of the box (it's light, about 5 lb for a six foot shade), and screw it into a (preferably wood) surface. I made the 1/16" starter holes as the directions say, and the self-tapping wood screws went in like butter. If you must install in stucco, brick or other surface, consult a pro; you want the installation to be semi-permanent, since you will be pulling on the string a lot, and you don't want it to loosen with time! As it was, I had to install a cross beam to get the surface I needed to install, which I painted the same color as my patio. It took all of 1 hour to install, taking my time. It was not hard at all. Here is a picture of the shade in my patio: [...]

Once you have the shade up, you just unroll it, and screw in the bottom stays, that keep the shade from flapping in the wind.

It does what it says it does: it keeps the hot sun from shining into the room through the window, while allowing breezes to flow in. It does something else that is not advertised as much: it casts a colorful glow over your room - the room takes on the hue of the shade. The effect is really quite pleasant, kind of like a sunset effect in your room.

The shade seems to be of high quality, the aluminum mechanism that holds the shade at the top is painted the same color as the shade, and overall there is a quality with this product that inspires pride and confidence. I highly recommend it! 5 stars!

title: Great Educational Item
abstract: I believe this microscope may be for teens and older students, but I ordered two of these microscopes as gifts for families with young children, three are age seven, in Puerto Rico and Florida. Last year, I decided to spend my money on true educational "toys" instead of computer games or other ridiculously expensive gadgets for kids. The two scopes went to my siblings, grandparents who spend a lot of time with their grandkids and who would hopefully put them to good use. I also sent them a lab manual and several Golden Book nature books. The microscopes have proven to be such a hit with most of the family, namely three generations who have been collecting leaves and all manner of specimens to view with the children, photograph, and upload to the computers. One seven-year-old is using it to do his school's science presentation. I'm so delighted with their enthusiasm that I'm ordering a third scope for a family in Virginia that home schools there four children who range in age from two to ten. Spring will soon be here and it's the perfect time to enjoy and learn about their environment. By the way, if I had more time, I would love this science tool for myself.

title: Great Laptop for the Money!
abstract:
I ordered this laptop about a month ago and have been very impressed with both the performance and the look/feel of the notebook. This is my first ASUS after bailing off of the HP bandwagon for the last few years. The slim design and light weight package are very attractive. The keyboard gives a nice resistance when typing (almost as if it has some kind of magical 'type-assist'#....as well as plenty of space between the keys. The other comments regarding resolution are somewhat right, depending on what you're doing with it. The Video Magic software from ASUS allows for enhancement for videos, and I've been impressed with the output. The only disappointment would be if you do a lot of work in PS CS4...the resolution isn't the best for fine-tuning high-res photos. Not really a big deal.

The only other downside is that my webcam is upside down. Jeers to ASUS for not yet addressing this problem with this model on their website. I used a 3rd Party workaround and it seems to work now #in most cases#.

Otherwise, great speed....loaded CS4 in under 30 minutes and it boots Photoshop CS4 in under 10 seconds, twice as fast as my duo core HP.

Overall, for the price, this laptop is hands-down a GREAT value.

title: Great Mats.
abstract: I have painful plantar fasciitis and bone spurs on the bottom of my foot, so standing or walking barefoot for any length of time is always painful. Also, I have cats. I sweep right over them and mop over them, too and they look and feel clean without the inconvenience of having to wash a rug that gets soiled so easily due to high traffic and kitchen messes. These have really been a blessing. I'm also glad they are a modest price, in case I need to replace them. The do shift a little under your feet if kicked or scooted but they do not slide all over the floor like my cotton rugs did. The edges of the mats are tapered so they don't stick up and catch your feet and cause a tripping hazard- a safety essential in the kitchen where boiling water and hot dishes frequently pass back and forth. I love the design, as well. I looked for a design that would be suitable for all holidays and everyday use. Buy these rugs- they really will help take pressure off of your joints and your back and feet won't hurt so much if you spend a lot of time in the kitchen (most of us do).

title: Great Outdoor Bin...
abstract: This bin is easy to put together and easy to move around when empty. I was pleasantly surprised at how much stuff I can actually get into it. The lock will keep the honest people out, but I wouldn't count on it for anything of real value in it. I use ours on our patio and it's perfect for holding the charcoal for the grill. Everything is always nice and dry when I go to use it. I have multiple bins in there holding furnishings for the patio table as well. Table cleaner, grilling utensils, bug spray, bluetooth speakers, etc... It will hold just about anything you will ever need for the outdoor living experience. I even thought about putting some wood in it for the fire pit. It would easily hold a nights worth of dry wood in it. I'm gonna stick my neck out there on this one and say that pests would have a hard time getting in there as well (Bee's mostly). This unit is pretty tight. I also put my tv on top of it when I'm gonna be outside for awhile. My guests really enjoy sitting outside watching the Sports games. Make sure you measure the spot that this bin will be in and if that's gonna be okay for you, then buy it, you won't be disappointed. I love mine. So if you're actually reading this and have gotten this far, "What are you waiting for?".

title: Great Pan with Lid, Great Price.
abstract:

 I can't find anything wrong with this pan, or the 10inch Contemporary Omelet pan I have.

 My other Cookware is Calphalon Commercial (two simply)

 This Pan is deeper then most 12inch omelet pan's, which I find this makes this more useful then just for Omelets.
