 Great Pan, Great Price.

title: Great Quality!
abstract:
This seemed expensive, but now that I have it, I see it is very well made and well worth the money! It is very well designed and easy to use. It has little stickers on it at all the right places to tell you how it works. I got the large version and I am glad I did because it gives me more space to fit my Surface Pro keyboard and monitor and also a portable external monitor in the book holder using the slot at the top and there is till room for and 8 1/2 x 11 page of notes.

Some examples of the thoughtful design are that the book holder has a place for it to be stored on the underside of the lap desk. There was a sticker there forcing you to read the instructions about which direction to pull the book holder out from where it clips in to be stored. The book holder fits into the slot at the top and it also has fold out arms, so if you want to use it on any surface without putting it in the slot, you can do that also. The surface of the lap desk is a little bit textured. It is enough that I can lay my phone on it when I have the lap desk at an angle and it does not slide down. It is not always enough though to keep my mouse from sliding down (depends on how much tilt I put on the desk), however, there is a tiny lip just above the slot at the bottom (the one that holds the laptop stopper) that keeps the mouse from sliding off the lap desk. The fold out legs are simple to use and seem very sturdy. The "slide" design of the legs work very well to be able to slide the desk across the mattress (if you're working while sitting in bed) and the legs are spaced well so that the lap desk is pretty steady even though on a soft surface. The little drawer is perfect to store some pens, so they are easily accessible. The little slot at the bottom can also hold two pens end to end and is deep enough that you can rest your wrists over top of that slot while you're typing on a laptop and can't feel the pens. I don't have a light clipped to my lap desk yet, but it is designed so that one would be easy to clip on. The slot at the top works well to hold an iPhone.

This is a great addition to my COVID-19 mandated work from home situation and even though I have a good home office set up, I'm not sure I'm going to want to go back to sitting at the desk all day now that I have this option!

title: Great Receptacle, Not-So-Great Egg Separator
abstract:
Because I regularly make meringue pies and home-made ice cream, I separate a lot of eggs. What I love about this WILTON BETTER BAKING EGG SEPARATOR is the 10-egg-white receptacle that stands firmly on your kitchen countertop--and the snug fit of the egg separator atop the receptacle. What I don't love about it is the design of the egg separator itself.

The egg separator design is fairly standard. There is a central round section for the yolk, with cutouts on both sides that allow the white to slip through. But the central yolk section is not very deep, and is not large enough to allow the yolk to move around. This means that if the white doesn't immediately drop through completely--and you have to gently rotate the yolk to finish the egg-separation process--you are at risk of breaking the yolk and contaminating the whites already in the receptacle. This is especially true if you are working with older eggs that have been in your refrigerator for a while.

Because of the less-than-optimal design, I rate this Wilton Egg Separator at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). A couple of egg separators that I like better are the plain, bargain-priced [[ASIN:B0079G2EQ6 Mini Egg Yolk Separator]], and the excellent [[ASIN:B00A2KD8NY OXO Good Grips 3-in-1 Egg Separator]] that hooks onto bowls of all sizes.

title: Great SSD for SMALL workloads.
abstract:
I've had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a "heavy" user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It's basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you're paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn't include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn't make sense to me. C'mon Samsung start adding that stuff! I would've happily paid a couple dollars more for it and it wouldn't have cost Samsung that much so they could've made a little bit of extra profit by adding it.

I still recommend this drive though and would buy it or the 860 Evo again if I needed more storage.

title: Great alternative to expensive pots
abstract:
I have been looking for affordable planters for patio shrubs for a long time. Even the plastic planters are expensive when looking for the larger sizes. I decided to give planting bags a try. Wow, what a great affordable solution. I purchased 18-20" planter trays and set these bags in them to catch any overflow. These bags are really strong and stand up straight and smooth when full of soil. There is no sign of any damage from the sun, high temps or watering. The best surprise is how well my flowering shrubs are doing in these grow bags. I've planted 4 three gallon shrubs and they have all more than doubled in size in a month. The black planting bags sitting in plant trays look really nice on my patio. When I water, there is no seepage thru the sides of the bags. They hold the water, well. I am able to turn the shrubs by rotating the plant trays.(The bags are too heavy to try to turn with the plant bag handles)
I am so happy I decided to give these a try. I could not be happier with the price and quality. I ended up with 4 beautiful patio plants at less than the cost of 1 large shrub-sized planter.

title: Great bag!
abstract: I very seldom review products I purchase on Amazon but felt this one merited a few minutes of my time. I received this bag the day after I placed the order- faster than the shipping speed I paid for. It is a beautiful, beautiful bag. The look is just what I was going for- vintage, without actually being old. The material and craftsman ship is superb. It looks lux, without the lux price tag. It is sturdy and lightweight and the front buckles keep things secure. The strap is adjustable which is great, since I typically like to wear my bags/purses cross body. The inside is padded and also adjustable. It has three "compartments". I have a Cannon Rebel T3i and when unassembled, the camera body fits in one compartment and the lens fits in the second compartment. These compartments can be adjusted so I can combine two of them into one large compartment and store the camera assembled...which is great if you don't want to constantly be removing and adding the lens. Either way, that still leaves a third compartment to hold other things, as well as a back pocket for additional storage. Overall it's just a fantastic bag and a price that can't be beat. It doesn't look like a camera bag so really could be used for all sorts of things. I am excited to take this with me on my next trip!

title: Great case and good buy!
abstract:
I purchased my case for protection and convenience purposes. I was pleasantly surprised at the overall look and construction.
The stylus/pen was also a nice surprise because I did not recall reading about it before ordering.
After reading other reviews and following advise, the keyboard was a snap to pair up. However note! The instructions do not show the keys to press that tell the keyboard your devise is an android, ios, or windows item. It says to use them, but not where they are. I also noted a couple grammatical errors in the instructions. Things like that make me question manufacturing.

It also would be nice to have a light that dictates the charge level of the keyboard. Mine came just slightly bowed in the center as did others according to reviews, however did not seem to affect performance. The magnets hold it securely, making it easy to use and light work of emails etc. If there only were a full size USB... Oh well one can hope. A mouse would complete the package!

Regarding the case its self, my only mention is that if you do not angle the tablet enough it tends to fall back because there is not quite enough support regarding weight distribution vs size. But it's by no means a deal breaker. Everyone I have showed it too is impressed. It is a clean professional design and an excellent addition to my electronic accessories lineup.

title: Great case for my first serious build (i bought it...
abstract:
Great case for my first serious build (i bought it a while ago). It's still in use, and I would really recommend it for a first timer or a pro

Pros:
-active cooling is awesome. watching the fins come up when i open a game is pretty sweet.
-great looking in a room. It's kind of a monster, so this is subjective, but it definitely lets people know there is serious power inside.
-SO MUCH STORAGE. seriously I ran out of SATA ports before i ran out of drive space.
-excellent cooling. my roommate has a similar build as mine in a phanteks case that gets uncomfortably warm.
-lots of room for modding or decoration. for the DIY inclined i would strongly recommend it
-the GPU holder is a great addition

CONS:
-didn't fit my motherboard. did not have the correct standoff holes for an MSI 970-A KRAIT edition, which i believe is a standard ATX motherboard. The right side of the motherboard is to this day completely unsupported. this makes changing RAM a pretty scary endeavor.
-a PSU basement would be nice
-the front dust filter sucks. it is removable, but i would much rather see something more like the PSU filter than the flimsy grate thing that sits behind the door.
-the fins on the top don't line up too well. again, at this price point I don't expect the mercedes of cases, but I would gladly pay more to see satisfyingly perfect alignment in the plastic bits.
-it looks great from far away, but once you start building in it, you notice that a lot of the parts are a bit cheap

title: Great design read full review for details
abstract:
I love this flag pole. I recently bought a F*ck Joe Biden flag and I hate how it would wrap around and tangle up on my old pole. So I searched out flag poles and came across this one. It works perfectly. Flag doesn't tangle at all. "Until the flag is wet" and that's not a pole issue it's a flag issue.
The pole is very easily put together, very easy to adjust and just has a great looking shinny finish. No runs, no chips, actually made really well. The design of the non tangle rings ate genius, i was wondering how they did this and now i know. I'm very very happy with my purchase 💯 all the way. Its a nice solution for a bad problem.

I have NOT been paid for this review nor any other review so far. (I wish I would though).
This is, as always, just and only my opinion thought my own eyes and felt with my own hands. I take reviews serious, as I rely on them to make my decisions before any and all my purchases. So if you have found my review helpful please vote and let the other Amazonian Browsers get a better judgment of what to expect and how the product works. Thank you for your time and happy buying

title: Great for DVDs. Excellent manual
abstract:
I bought this TV to watch DVDs with my 3 yr old granddaughter. We were streaming on my tablet, but it was not comfortable. With this TV we can snuggle on the couch & enjoy Dora & Molly 😉
The picture quality & color is good for our purposes. The DVD plays smoothly. The sound is from the back of the TV, so I plugged a small speaker into the headphone jack, which solved the problem.
This TV comes with the best User Manual I have ever seen. It describes every button on the 50 button remote 👏👏👏. It also shows an image & description of every setup screen. Excellent Manual.
CON: The tv stand is horrible. It's super hard to screw in the 6 tiny phillips head screws. 1. Because the angle is so awkward no matter how you place the tv & stand piece. 2. The included tiny screws are so soft it's nearly impossible not to strip the head. We ended up with a tv on a stand that tilts forward a bit. imo, they need to completely redesign the stand. In hindsight, I should have used gel gorilla glue instead of the screws.

All in all, this is a great little 24" TV with lots of features, an excellent manual, good picture & built in DVD player for a great price. As long as you have a small speaker with a headphone jack, you will be all set.

title: Great for a small container water pond or fountain
abstract: I was trying to save money by using an old 325gph pump in my little container water garden, but it was splashing water all over the place bc it was too strong. I ordered this small filter/pump set and I'm very pleased. The water is gentle and perfect for this approximately 30 gallon pond plant container. I didn't use the extra attachments to make bell-shaped water - I just left them off as I like the natural bubbling water look. It makes a small, peaceful water trickle sound. What I love the most about this is that most of the smaller units I researched didn't come with filtration. This one has a filter inside that can easily be rinsed out, and it will also provide biological filtration through utilization of good-bacteria (over time) in the filter/sponge. To ensure you don't kill off the good bacteria in chlorinated city water, get a large bowl of water and pre-treat it with chlorine remover, drop the sponge into the bowl, then use your hands to squeeze the filter/sponge in the bowl. Done! Never use soap on the filter, as it is seeded with beneficial bacteria (this happens over time), which is good for your water feature if you have plants. Dump the "dirty" water on your yard plants. Please note - this is meant for a small container pond, bird bath or similar. You really shouldn't add fish to such small containers, and especially if you live in a hot climate. The fish will fry, and the container is too small to house living creatures. Opt for a larger pond and filtration system if you plan to house fish.

title: Great for light office or home use...
abstract:
I needed a stapler for home use, and of course came to Amazon to see what they had before hitting the office supply store. Found this one, liked the choice of colors, read the reviews, and decided to give it a shot.

VERY happy with this. The stapling mechanism has a different design than most staplers. You squeeze it, and toward the "end" of the squeeze, it sNaPs! the staple into the papers. I'm using it primarily to staple together pages of patterns and recipes as well as corralling some of my financial paperwork.

I got the green color -- it's a little darker than the photo -- more of a "kelly" green, but I'm OK with that. It takes standard staples and isn't difficult to fill once you figure out that you slide the BOTTOM section instead of the top to reveal the staple chamber. And it stores on the end (see the photo above), so it really doesn't take up much desk real estate.

I've stapled as many as 10 sheets of fairly heavy (26 lb) printer paper with no problems at all. I may purchase a second one to keep in my office, and have one in the kitchen to use with recipes and receipts.

title: Great for resticted water
abstract:
We live in the hills of southern Oregon, where water is notoriously a problem. Wells dry up, and I have a few neighbors who truck in water on a regular basis. I just added 10k gallons of water storage, as we resorted to pulling water from our pool last year due to low well flow, but we had already lost 5k of water because of a broken fitting. And now the city is restricting water usage to for non-commercial use only, as there's a lack of available chlorine due to the pandemic, and they can't sanitize enough water effectively. We'll see if this becomes more restrictive.

I've had one of these for a few years now, and it has always been my favorite shower head. We have another water saving shower head as well (Niagara N2615 Tri-Max), but I'm about to buy another Delta to replace that as the Niagara puts out a lot more water than I'd like, and the lowest setting feels like someone's spitting water at you, which isn't at all pleasant. I've found that this Delta shower head also helps if you have any issues with sores on your head. I have an autoimmune disease where this is common, and this shower head is the 'only' one I can use that won't make my head hurt even more.

If you have a need to conserve water (we all should to a certain extent), and want a good shower experience, this is it. I can easily take a pleasant half-hour shower and only fill the tub a quarter of the way, if I dial it down a bit. If you have the means to install this in a camper or RV, I highly recommend it, as your shower time would be extended, as long as your pressure is high enough. The only downside to the small water droplets is that the water will rapidly lose heat in comparison to larger droplets, but this is a negligible tradeoff IMHO. You'll definitely make a steamy bathroom, which may actually be desirable for some.

This shower head may look simple, but is worth every penny. You won't find a better shower experience while conserving water.

title: Great for storage, as a cat bed, or for turning an open clothes closet shelf into a drawer - 3.6 stars from me
abstract:
I originally thought this was foldable and that's why I ordered it. It is my mistake in not reading the description.

I like the design and neutral "gray" color. The quality of the workmanship on the basket I received is good. Note that this is not always the case with DII products, so beware. Their quality has been variable in the past.

This container tapers out at the top, so storing these side by side will leave space at the bottom. The holes for the handles are sturdy. Many items such as clothing, toys, bags of pasta, towels, books, etc. can be stored in this bin. However, if I were moving it around, I would only put light items in it and not books and magazines.

In addition to its standard uses, it can also be used as a cat bed. As you can see from the photos, one of my three cats claimed it as his. I plan to store my winter PJs in it but right now I'm "storing" my cat.

For the current price of $12.99, I think this is competitively priced on the high side. I do feel there are many other options available on the market for that price and some that are even sturdier than this. However, this type of cloth over cardboard bin looks good in a clothes closet because the cloth "matches" the clothing material in the closet as opposed to a plastic bin. Also, it can be used to store items on a large open shelf thereby turning the shelf into a "sort of" drawer.

UPDATE: Besides the matte finish of the larger [[ASIN:B01MTCGALR 13 x 13 x 13" Trapezoid Storage Container in Chevron Gray]] above, I also ordered the [[ASIN:B01N13TMG6 11 x 11 x 11" Trapezoid Storage Container in Chevron Copper]] which has a high shine metallic finish in the same design. That also arrived in good condition as you can see in the third and fourth pictures. At the current price of $10.99 for the medium, this is also competitively priced on the high side.

title: Great grill, portable or not
abstract:
This is a great portable grill. That being said, I have yet to carry it anywhere. It stays on my front porch ready to cook after briefly preheating. It burns very hot and a cylinder of gas lasts about five or six sessions. It is large enough to cook for the wife, teen daughter, and myself at on a single grate. It is made of thick cast iron and seems to be a very durable, well made product. The regulator is flimsy, but I try to be pretty careful with it and have had no problems as of yet. Despite the cheap regulator, this is the best all-around grill I have owned, portable or otherwise.
 Down to the nitty gritty. I have grilled probably twenty five times since I received it and cooked pork, beef, chicken, and vegetables on it. The grill performs excellently on anything that is an inch and a half or thinner, but much more than that and the center turns out a bit raw. My opinion is that it burns too hot at even the lowest settings to cook thicker meat. Keep it thinner, however, and it turns out perfect.
 This is touted as an infrared grill; the grate has a series of ridges which have a line of small holes in between. Does it work as promised? For the most part, well, yeah. I've noticed far fewer flare-ups than with a traditional grate. Steaks, burgers, chops, and chicken will cook up juicy and tender after getting used to grilling with it. Cleaning is a not a problem with the included tool.
 This grill isn't made for everybody. if you're planning on cooking thicker cuts of meat, then this grill may not fit your needs. My advice is to know it's limitations and I think most folks will be pleased with their purchase. I know I am.

**UPDATE**
Regulator went bad in Sept 2018. Replaced it with a third party regulator. It's been a great little grill and hopefully it'll last a few more years. Still the best grill I've ever owned.

title: Great ladder!
abstract:
After many years, my six-foot ladder and three-foot stool both became so unsightly (the stool was rusty, as well) that I finally decided it was time for a change. I bought this five-foot ladder to avoid replacing two products (the ladder and the stool) and had it delivered to my home by Amazon.com since my car is too small to transport either product home from the "hardware" store.

I am pleased! I bought the ladder because of its safety specifications. It is light-weight and stable, and the height is perfect for my needs.

I read in some of the reviews of ladders that the product sometimes arrives dusty. This ladder was reasonably clean but did have dust on some of the steps and grooves -- as if it had been sitting in a warehouse. It had a few tiny dings -- nothing major -- similar to the kind of dings I would expect to see at my local hardware store for this kind of product.

I weigh about 120 lbs and can't carry heavy objects easily. I am very, very careful when using ladders or stools. I follow all recommended safety practices; I like this ladder and feel safe carrying it and using it. Anyone who ignores safety guidelines is not safe on a ladder or stool, so you should know that my recommendation is only valid if you use the product as recommended. Safety first!

title: Great light
abstract:
I wanted a powerful light that recharged as well. I was skeptical of the lumen count but it is super bright. There are a few modes on this to where it could be used as a stress signal (it blinks, there would be no Morse code style relaying here). I thought I counted 4 modes but didn't need anything other than the primary high mode.

I did charge it the day I received it but have not had a need since then. Oddly enough this came the day before a big storm and the power was out for almost 24 hours so it was used quite a bit (and on for quite some time).

I do like the zoom feature on it because I like this similar feature that is/are on maglight flashlights. This worked well because I pointed it toward the ceiling to help light up a room for my kids when the power went out.

It did rain when I needed it but I wasn't expecting to get a shock from the light. In terms of how waterproof, I am not sure but it worked just fine with no glitches during the storm.

I am very pleased with the purchase and everything has held true from the features I was after.

title: Great little camera
abstract:
Ultra compact cameras like this one don't take pictures as nice as SLRs, but the best camera is the one that you use and not the one that sits at home. And with the size and weight of this Canon you'll use it everywhere. Another huge consideration is LCD size. Despite its small size the SD750 has a 3-inch LCD which is bright and crisp. The size difference over a 2.5-inch LCD is a lot more than it sounds like because it's measured diagonally. Definitely get a big LCD no matter what camera you buy.

As for photo quality, the SD750 is better than any other compact digital I've seen. In full automatic mode under the right conditions (good light, stationary subjects, etc.) the photos are outstanding. In less than perfect conditions if you want great shots you'll be well served to learn the controls and particularly the numerous scene modes. My indoor shots in moderate light were coming out overexposed in the foreground and dark in the background, but once I started using the Indoor mode those shots looked great. The Cloudy mode really helps bring out the colors in outdoor shots on cloudy days (as intended). Take a little time to learn scene modes and other settings like High ISO and the different types of autofocus and you'll get much more out of this camera than if you just use full auto all the time.

As for special features, there are more on this camera than I would ever use. Color swap modes, red eye reduction, slide shows and all kinds of stuff I'm sure I'll never touch. I just want to take good pictures. If I want to edit my pictures I'll do it on my computer and not in the camera. But if that's your thing you'll be kept busy for a long time playing around with all the stuff the SD750 has to offer.

Finally, a great thing about the SD750 is the SPEED. It's much faster starting up and taking shots than any other digital camera I've used. From pressing the ON button to being ready to shoot takes less than a second. Master the art of pre-focusing your shot by pressing the shutter button halfway and then framing your shot after it's focused and you'll virtually eliminate all shutter lag. And oh yeah, the battery lasts a long time, though it would be nice if there was a battery indicator to tell you how much charge is left.

title: Great little mic
abstract:
The microphone easily attached to my camera. I did like that there was a replacement camera mount included (the red piece) as I've heard of people breaking those for similar looking mics. This one DID come attached to the red mount so there were no issues and I have a spare. The red piece is fairly flexible which has both pros and cons as the mic can move a little and not stress this piece, but the con being the mic can move.

As far as the mic audio, there was a good improvement when about 3 feet away and a major improvement when up closer. The audio is cleaner than the on mic camera which makes this a nice minor cost improvement.

There are different cables which allow you to attach the camera to a standard audio port or a TRRS port like on some iPhones.

The mic does not need batteries so there are no issues with needing the check the batteries before each use. This does seem to have a downside somewhat in that the mic doesn't really have a power boost which would come from the batteries.

The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition.

The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter.

I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

title: Great little plant stand!!!
abstract: I am loving this new plant stand! I needed a plant stand to help keep my plants off of the floor and decided on this particular plant stand and I am so glad that I did. I have purchased other Zerla items and this is why I chose this one. So far Zerla has made very good quality items and I have been happy with them. This is a great plant stand and at a great price. It is so very easy to put together too. Unfortunately mine didn't come with directions, but it really wasn't that necessary. All that you do is put the two pieces together like the pictures I provided below. Once the pieces are together, turn the stand upside down. Put the screw in the center of the plant stand (there is a hole there) and tighten. Very easy to put together. This plant stand will work best for medium to a little bit larger pots to help give it better sturdiness. That is why I only gave four stars on the sturdiness. The further you expand the stand, the better sturdiness it has. It was a little wobbly on carpeting for my pot, but its perfect for hardwood floors. I love how it adjusts from smaller pots to larger ones. If you are looking for an affordable plant stand, I definitely recommend this one. It is lightweight and easy to move so you can vacuum underneath.

title: Great pan, cleans easy,,lid sucks!
abstract:
This is a sturdy pan that will not worp or bend.
 It's made very well, and such a good price, Amazing!

 I have made a cake in it, a Meat loaf, cassarole with cheese etc., and just running it under water, everything comes off easy. (of course I still wash it).
 I don't think anything can stick to this pan!

 I didn't have this size pan, and it is good for about 4 people depending what your making, but I don't think its that big.
I'm going to buy the next size up.

 I would have given the pan a 5 star, but not with this lid I couldn't.
 The lid does not fit that good. It did keep popping off when new. I kept putting it back on, and it seems to stay on now when I use it. I keep the lid on it in my pantry, so it forms to the pan.
 It is not air tight, but is better then having to deal with plastic wrap or tin foil!
The lid is raised up abit so it doesn't smash or stick on your cake, cassarole etc.

 I think Amazon sells this pan without the lid, for less of a price, if you do not want the lid.

 I would buy this again.

title: Great purchase!
abstract:
This is the greatest! We have purchased the mosquito magnet ever since it came out. Not a single one has lasted more than 1 season! I was so fed up! Then when this year became unbearable, we have had an unusual amount of rain & being zone 10 it's a mosquito paradise! I worry about our big animals & west Nike. We treat our horses, donkeys & goats but I still worry. We have many cats as people abandon them in the country & we give them a home so we have in excess of 30 cats living in our barn. Of course we feed them but it is cost prohibitive & impossible as many are feral and no one except us can get near them, to vaccinate them. We also have 13 dogs. Many also dumped. So Mosquitos present a real problem!
I did my search for a new mosquito magnet. Our previous one died at the end of one year! What else is new! But now the price was over the moon! I couldn't okay that for one year of use! I saw this mosquito killer that works on the same principle. It was affordable (cheaper than vaccinating all the cats and then tending to the claw wounds!). We bought it and no regrets! It is working like a trooper! The tray is full of Mosquitos! It is already more bearable to go out & feed the animals. Additionally the reviewers who have no skin in the game, the cats, approve! They now sleep around the mosquito defender! They love it! Now they certainly have no reason to hang out there except that they have no reason except relief from bites!
I am so happy! It works and it is much better built than the magnet. I am confident that it will last more than 1 season due to the sturdiness of the equipment. It is powder coated steel which will certainly help here as we are on the gulf w/ lots of salt and rust problems. This equipment comes with everything you need! It even has a cover for the propane tank. Now the magnet had one also, but it was stupid and useless! It was like a big bag that rapped moisture and caused the propane tank to rust! The defender has a cover that is open at the bottom so the condensation doesn't just remain on the tank causing rust!
Now it does appear that the lure may be (and I say may as I am not certainly n what magnet is charging now) more expensive than the magnet. Regardless the magnet having to be replaced every year and costing sooo much more than the defender, but the cost of the defender is so much more reasonable there is no comparison.
I will update this at the end of the year as to the durability. I can still tell you it is made far better. Also it catches Mosquitos like nobodies business! If you are plagued by the nasty little blood suckers, you can't do better than the defender. I speak from experience, having owned both. The magnet is a zero thus far rhe defender is a hero!
Delivery was perfect and prompt. The defender arrived in excellent condition and assembly was easy, no tools required. It can be assembled by one person in just maybe 15-20 minutes. You need to buy & fill a propane tank ($3 off coupon is included). It comes with a lure, set it up and enjoy the outside again! What else comes with thirty little kitty paws of approval!

title: Great shredder at an even better price.
abstract:
I will admit this is my first Amazon Basics purchase, and I was a little bit leery about buying it. I thought about buying a different brand that was more expensive because I wasn't sure how great Amazon would be at making a shredder, I mean I love their kindles, but a shredder isn't really something I associate Amazon with. When it arrived I was excited because I had a pile of stuff that needed shredded including credit cards. There is literally no set up to this thing, just set the top on top of the trash can thing and go, that's it.
I tried the credit card shredded area (its a spot in the middle) first, and I was pleasantly surprised at how well and quick it worked. I also tried out varying thicknesses of paper as well, I wouldn't recommend more than 3 pages thick, but it does its job and really quick. It is a tad on the noisy side (more so with plastic cards then with paper), but I was expecting that a shredder was going to make some noise. I am really glad I bought this shredder and in the future will be trying out more Amazon Basics products.

title: Great sound quality
abstract:
Great sound quality from this ingenious mini-speaker. The value is terrific. I also own a Bose mini speaker and I can say without hesitation the AYL mini Capsule Speaker delivers sound quality equal to the Bose mini, at a fraction of the price...... actually, not only cheaper than a Bose, it does not require any software and is truly portable - small enough to throw in your purse. I did not expect this sound quality for the price. I am going to buy a few as gifts.

PROS
collapses into a ball with a secure and easy to operate twist-lock design - throw it in your purses
includes ALL the cords required to connect, extend and charge:
- 1 is a a dual-split to connect and charge at the same time
- there is also a small 2" connection cord tucked into the bottom, so if you forget the loose cord, you are still able to connect (super design detail)
sound quality is excellent, enhanced by the 360 design
full range volume control that operates smoothly
on/off switch to preserve the charge
the directions show how to easily connect multiple mini Capsule Speakers together
arrived prior to the expected delivery date
Solid, quality material - this will not break if you accidentally drop it.

CONS
none so far

title: Great squirrel feeder!
abstract:
We love this squirrel feeder! It is well made out of steel and works remarkably well. I installed it on a 2 foot high post near a large tree. I've read some negative comments which I will address.

Access: it does take a short while for squirrels to figure out how to lift the lid but they certainly have gotten the hang of it; you hear the "clunk" of the lid closing each time they grab a peanut. Perhaps lower IQ's in some parts of the country?

Durability: I've had no problem with the hinges; they appear well made and well installed; Rust: the feeder is steel which will rust with time. The company has done a great job in painting the feeder to retard this process; I may need to spot repaint as the years go buy but unless they were to make it out of stainless steel, copper, plastic {no good} or titanium, rust occurs. Aluminum could be used but the lid would be too light and painting aluminum well is a more involved process.

All in all, a really well thought out design that is well built & substantial, that both the squirrels and we have most enjoyed!

title: Great storage for a super-large king-size comforter; but bag does smell like a new shower curtain.
abstract:
I have a custom made king-size heavy comforter in XXL that measures 118" x 120" and weighs about 10-15 pounds. It is very difficult for me to find storage bags for this and when I do find them they break almost immediately. After doing a lot of research, I figured this bag would work and I was right.

I can only fit this one comforter in this bag but considering the size of my blanket, that is a lot. The handles appear to be strong and the bag did not rip, which is amazing compared to the garbage sold elsewhere. I do hope it lasts and will update my review if it does not.

Obviously, I won't be carrying this around or using this as luggage but it seems strong enough for light mobility. I actually plan on buying another one in the blue color.

Do note that it does smell like a new shower curtain so anything stored in this bag will have that smell. Nevertheless, I believe a bit of airing out the comforter after storage will rid it of this odor and if it does not I'll just launder the blanket. Of course, if one has a garage, my recommendation is to air out the bag for about a week first before use to see if the smell dissipates. Unfortunately, I do not have the facilities to do that.

title: Great table, just not for me
abstract:
This table had everything I was looking for! Leg room, the sled legs made it easy to maneuver (this is a MUST!) and the ease of adjustment in setting up and collapsing for storing were smooth and frustration free!

However, I was so disappointed that the height adjustments weren't suitable for my comfort. I've had neck surgery so having a desk at the correct height is essential. Even at it's lowest adjustment height the desk was still too high. I did order another to try, sadly it was also perfect except for it was ALSO too high!

If there was more maneuverability to raise and lower this desk, it would meet all the qualities of a great laptop bed tray desk!

I also noticed the measurements on the description were off by at least a couple of inches. Perhaps I wasn't measuring in the same manner? Anyway, I had to return them but I am still waiting for a LOWER adjustable height setting so I can have the perfect desk laptop tray for my comfort!

No ordinary lapdesk will do, this is the one for me, I need a lower height adjustment so my arms are comfortable and not reaching out and up to type! Keeping the table level is also essential for supporting me while I type.

For instance, say the lowest height from the bed to the table (keeping the table level and not tilted) is 9 inches, if it were able to go lower, down to 6 inches at the lowest height, that's what I'm watching for!

If you work sitting non the floor, couch, or bed THIS table desk tray is sturdy, easy to open and close, it's quality materials are as described. If you're here looking, just order it!

title: Great while it lasted
abstract:
I've had this unit for nine months, almost to the day. I have been very pleased with the software and the hardware; it had even been accepting recycled ink cartridges (which are still expensive!) without a fuss. The only thing I haven't liked about it is that, if any one of the FIVE ink cartridges is empty, the unit stops printing altogether. No black and white, no nothing.

This morning I replaced the Yellow cartridge and when the ink tank carrier moved back into place it started grinding like a car's manual transmission gears being stripped. I managed to get it to print again, but the prints are now banded, off color, grainy and otherwise unusable. After several diagnostic procedures there is no change.

It was at this point that I found the Canon support website to be pretty useless, presenting me with nothing but a non-working link to press like a hopeful capuchin monkey after entering my unit's serial number and date of purchase. I'm not too happy about the idea of spending the money to ship a 30-lb. hunk of electronics somewhere with the unlikely prospect that it would work when I got it back after a 2- to 5-week wait. (I was once a Denon technical support CSR; I know how these things too often go.)

I've used the Pixma MP560 for my home office only, and only rarely for color printing. Sometimes a week or ten days go by before I even turn my printer on, so I haven't exactly overworked the thing.

If nine months of light use seems like a short lifespan to you, as it does to me, I'd try something else. As for me, my next printer is going to be strictly black and white, with as few expensive ink cartridges and moving parts as possible, even if I have to hand-feed the bloody thing. I'm really tired of throwing good money after bad on consumer electronics. Pretty disappointed with Canon.

title: Greatly regret buying this printer!
abstract:
The Epson ET-2650 was ordered Oct. 2, 2018, and delivered Oct. 4, 2018. It worked as promised in the description -- at first.

First issue: It drinks ink! I had no reason to think we used more ink than average until this printer. I quickly went through the first four Epson color ink bottles and was already halfway through the second box of Epson ink refill bottles when the unit failed, after only 4 months of moderate use. The description suggested the ink refills would last up to two years. I didn't expect the refills to last that long, but less than four months is quite a bit short of the predicted ink use. We don't print every day, and certainly not in huge quantities.

Second issue: From the time of purchase, I needed to clean print heads frequently due to the print quality being unreadable on parts of the page. I'd never experienced this with previous printers. Photo 2.

Third issue: This printer became unusable when it could no longer print documents from a website, like Amazon. Instead of the printer recognizing and printing letters and/or numbers, it substituted blobs of ink instead. End result, I had a printer that couldn't print receipts or other online information. This problem developed about two months after we purchased it. Photo 1.

Replacement policy: When I contacted Epson, the phone rep indicated that he thought it was possibly a hardware issue. To get a replacement printer, Epson would send a box for the printer. I was to mail the printer back to the company. Once they received the printer, they would send me a replacement. However I had to send them a check for nearly $200 before they would send the box.

I would have been happy to receive the return box and mail the printer to Epson, then waited for them to OK the return, and send me a replacement printer. That wasn't an option.

I opted to NOT send Epson either the printer or the money. Instead, I'm recycling the printer and have purchased an HP.

-- Former Epson customer

title: HIGH quality weighted blanket - definitely recommend!
abstract:
I understand that this blanket is an investment - I never would have imagined I would pay so much for a damn blanket - but this is a "must" for people with trouble sleeping/relaxing due to anxiety.

I have lived with anxiety and panic disorder for years. After a particularly bad flare-up where I was waking up in the middle of the night most nights with attacks, I did research and found this as a solution. This blanket definitely helps me sleep better through the night. I definitely feel more relaxed when I crawl underneath it and it is covering me from neck to toe.

I did a LOT of research before buying and went with this brand. First, the promo video with the young women made me want to buy it - very relatable. And the color section was the nicest/most feminine around of all weighted blankies. But from a practical perspective, out of all of the ratings I scoured regarding durability, this blanket's reviews objectively had the least complaints about long-term issues. If you are using this blanket as a throw, I can see how the inside ties can degrade and break - though they could be sewed to reinforce. I use this blanket on my bed to sleep at night, so it is always flat, and I don't have an issue with the ties. The weighted blanket doesn't really slide around that much inside the cover, and it is easy to fix. I only had to re-tie the shell to the blanket after a full 2 months of daily use. The weights are reinforced within the patches and I can't foresee anything going wrong with the actual weighted blanket. And the minkies on the shell are incredibly wonderful. When I get anxious I rub my hands over them. I know it sounds weird to anyone who doesn't live with anxiety/panic - it would sound weird to me pre-anxiety too - but the minky texture is SO calming omg. Really a huge plus.

This is my first weighted blanket experience. I am muscular at 160 lb and I went with 15 lb. 15 lb felt heavy for the first few uses but I now feel like I could have gone heavier. This is coming from a Highly Sensitive Person, for other HSPs out there.

The blanket is pretty heavy. I was sweating on 65 degree nights in August. I plan to buy a "summer" version of a weighted blanket next year.

title: Had to return it due to connectivity issues
abstract:
I got this internet radio and tried it for a few weeks. At first I was happy with it - the sound quality is quite good, it seemed pretty easy to set up, and I was able to find my favorite NPR station streams as well as connect to my Pandora stations. But after the first two weeks or so, I started having problems with connectivity.

- I'd come home from work and the thing would be on, not playing, with "error connecting to network" or some similar message flashing on the screen. The best way to solve this seemed to be to turn it off, then turn it back on, and then it would work (for a while).

- While listening, it frequently stops playing in the middle of a song. Then the display says either "Buffering" for a few minutes, or more frequently, will actually say "Connecting" for up to five minutes at a time! This happens, on average, every 4-6 minutes. The thing is, I have a wireless router upstairs on the same floor as the radio (Apple Time Capsule) and the wireless signal is quite strong. The other devices that connect to this router never have a problem with connectivity - devices that include a Roku box, a Chumby, my iPhone, my HP netbook, my Macbook, etc.

The problem with losing connectivity started infrequently but got worse and worse over the past two weeks or so, to the point where I can't really listen to music on it at all anymore. So I'm returning it. Too bad, because in terms of looks, sound, and basic functionality, it had everything I wanted.

title: Had us crying
abstract:
Absolutely love this game. Not only does it have high playability (i.e. you can play it again and again), but it is also simple to learn and hysterical. Played this for the first time at a small party and my friends and I were rolling with laughter (some of us even shed tears). I immediately purchased this game thereafter.

A couple things to note, though. Firstly, My friends and I are currently in our late 20s/early 30s. I tried playing this game with my parents and they didn't get the references to some of the cards (like "flossing", the dance move). There were plenty they did understand though so we just made sure to play with those. We still had a lot of fun!

Secondly, this game is meant to be played at gatherings. A minimum of 4 people is required to play this game.

Finally, this game is pretty obviously not for children... Not just because it requires a LOT of memorizing and memory recall, but a child wouldn't understand the vast majority of the cards. And, I mean, some of the cards have mature/adult content... Honestly, I would recommend this game for ages 13-16+. Don't be that selfish person who ruins everyone's night by trying to make your 8 year old play this game.

Overall, I would highly recommend this game to any adult. This is one of the few games I won't get sick of playing. I am very happy with my purchase.

title: Handy, easy to use, easy to clean!
abstract: I was skeptical when my husband insisted that we get this grill after the giant gas grill died. However, we've used it twice and I am very impressed with it. First off let me say I hate those gas grill things.... you might as well cook inside. I love the flavor of meat cooked over charcoal or wood chip smoke, but for just two people, making a big fire etc is so not worth it. This little Cobb cooker is a wonder - just 5 or 6 charcoal briquets in the center and you're done! The cooking surface is the perfect size for 3 normal steaks or 4 small ones - or 6 skewers of meat & veggies etc. The Cobb is very light and easy to move around, plus it doesn't get terribly hot meaning if you need to move it due to sudden rain, you can just do so - while cooking. Nice. We've done steaks, hamburger and some veggies on it and the meat cooks quickly, correctly and with minimum drama. (Always a plus!) I also like the clean up with this grill - super easy and I love that this grill is light enough to take it with you on a beach trip etc. Just pack it up in it's travel bag and go. This has just been a great purchase all the way around!

title: Hard-to-Identify, Hard-to-Set-Up Buildings Destroy Fun of Assembling Kit
abstract:
This 4D CITYSCAPE CHICAGO SKYLINE PUZZLE is great in concept, but falls way short in the execution. It's a three-part puzzle. First you assemble a standard jigsaw (an 1867 Chicago street map). Next you assemble a foam-based jigsaw with identical interlocking tabs (a modern Chicago street map) that goes atop the first jigsaw. Third you add three-dimensional plastic buildings to the foam jigsaw.

The first jigsaw is difficult, especially in the large blue Lake Michigan area, but the street names and the boats on the lake help enough to make this an expert-but-fairly-easy jigsaw. The second foam jigsaw comes partly assembled, with several large pieces, and is very easy, taking less than an hour. (Unless you separate all the smallest foam street-grid pieces, which will require a lot of close comparison with the color map, and a lot of extra unsatisfying puzzle time, to reassemble.)

The third part, adding the buildings, is where the whole puzzle concept breaks down. Unless you're familiar with Chicago already, the buildings are hard to identify by comparing the plastic pieces with the photographs on the color buildings poster. You have to identify each building by finding its numbered location on the color map, and then matching the appearance of the roof to the line drawing of the roof found in the punch-out foam puzzle piece at the location in the foam map. (With some similar buildings, this is quite difficult, and you have to check the size of the plastic bases as well. It also helps to know how to read architectural diagrams.)

Finally, inserting the buildings is a major problem. If you punch out the foam piece where the building goes in, you will NOT be able to tell how the building is oriented to the street and the buildings around it. If you don't punch out the foam piece, but merely jam the building down onto it, the building will fall over whenever you jostle the foam as you add more buildings. Another problem is that some historic buildings are gold and the rest are silver-gray.

The puzzle kit also includes a set of silver-gray "generic" buildings that you can add to make the Chicago downtown look more like a skyscraper city. However, you don't know when these buildings were built, so inserting them destroys the historical timeline that helps you see how Chicago grew.

I was really excited about this puzzle, because I wanted to see all the buildings added after I departed Chicago in the sixties. However, adding the buildings was fiddly and far too much of a hassle, so I bailed on the project after 25 buildings. (If I ever decide to go back and finish it, I will glue the buildings in place atop the foam.)

In sum, although the standard jigsaw is fun to assemble, it is overpriced at the cost of the entire kit (about $30 on Amazon). The rest of the kit was a big disappointment. Now I think I'll try to find a book of photographs that will show me how Chicago has grown since 1867, or since the sixties.

title: Heavy and durable fabric
abstract:
This is a very interesting product. I'm using it to make a sheltered place to keep my car, and it would work equally well over a patio area.

The fabric is a tight mesh which is somewhat porous to water, so there probably won't be puddles overhead when it rains. It provides good shade. Each of the four corners is fitted with a heavy metal triangle "ring" to fasten it to the mounts.

Included in the package are 4 mounts you can screw onto your house or garage, plus hardware (hooks and turnbuckles) to attach the sail to the mounts. Everything is of high quality. The parts included might not be exactly what you need to mount the sail for your particular site, so be prepared for a trip to the hardware store for more mounting stuff.

Although the sail is described as "square", it's not really a square. Each side is indeed the same length, but the sides are curved inward. This makes the sail look very attractive in use, but I had difficulty installing it and making it fit where I originally planned. The instructions are pretty helpful, but nevertheless, expect the installation to take some thought and time.

title: Heavy duty and large capacity for the price
abstract:
I purchased this as a drum kit hardware bag for a Tama Club Jam (small size) drum kit. It easily accommodates the center tom holder, the bass drum mounted cymbal holder, a Tama classic straight cymbal stand and a Tama HP30 bass drum pedal. I was also able to fit the floor tom legs. I could have managed the Tama classic hi-hat stand and classic snare drum stand, but that was pushing it and I was afraid that those last two components would have damaged the zipper. I am using a separate, small Tama hardware bag for those, plus a throne base and small stick bag.

The padding is superior to the Tama hardware bag, and the overall construction, including zipper is as good if not better. This bag actually holds more than the Tama one that was designed for drum hardware, and is about half the cost.

I also own a nice camera tripod that this case would easily protect and I will probably order another case for that. However, this case is a lot larger than the tripod, and I so rarely transport it, that the value proposition is nowhere as good as for my current use as a drum hardware bag. I am totally pleased with this bag!

title: Heckuva deal!!
abstract:
These little lights are the bomb!
Considering that they run off of one
" AA" battery they are extremely bright. Add in that they also have a COB ( Chip On Board) light panel built into the side that is also extremely bright and acts as a miniature floodlight… You do need to cycle the switch in the tail cap in order to access your desired function so the only two things that are detrimental are: cycling the tail switch and battery life. I think that there might be an inverter or voltage doubler to boost the 1.5v of the AA cell up to 3 volts or so to get the brightness that is produced, but at the cost of battery life. Feed em some good Alkaline batteries and scatter them around wherever you expect to need a flashlight or give them to family and friends. I'm ordering my 3rd package (15 lights) and I think I still have 2. These are cheap enough to scatter far and wide, and powerful enough to actually be extremely useful.
Nothing like the dim penlight flashlights us Graybeards grew up with!!
Great product and a
Great price for a decent quality product! ( And no- I wasn't paid or comped to write this! )

title: Hefty tool that will be great for pulling nails or prying apart paneling, molding, and perhaps some doors away from its frame
abstract:
I purchased four of these pry bars as an emergency tool should I ever get locked in an inside room. I have four inside rooms with no windows and last year (due to a construction worker's accidental carelessness) I got completely locked into one room without any tools to get me out and no one around to help. Lucky I live in a condo where my screaming was finally heard after 40 minutes. The police, who unsuccessfully busted my front door but could not open it, were able to get to me with the help of a neighbor who climbed the side of my building to enter from another location. They finally freed me after 1 hour and 35 minutes of confinement.

Since then I've been looking for a pry bar that I could keep in each of these inside rooms as a precaution to not only save me future embarrassment but to also possibly save my life.

I researched ordinary pry bars like the [[ASIN:B00002N5VN Vaughan B215 15-Inch Long Original SuperBar]] but settled on this one because of the angle. After receiving these, I made sure they could get a grip between the door jam and the door of each room. Although this tool is thick, there are spots along each door that would provide enough space to slide this tool and where there would be enough leverage to work. Since these are hollow-core doors, even if I'm unable to open the door, this tool would probably allow me to break it apart.

My initial impression is that these are hefty and the angle of the pry bar acts as a fulcrum to provide leverage for prying apart various materials such as paneling, molding, and even prying up nails. This may also come in handy to lift up or tilt furniture in a pinch for moving purposes.

title: High temp meat chopper
abstract: High temp meat chopper is super handy. It works so quickly - even faster than a spatula - had to see it to believe it myself. Wonder how I got along without it. I know it's just another kitchen tool, but - this one is a keeper in my book!  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - nearly 6,000 reviews posted, viewed over 50,000 times, and over 24,000 likes. I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Highly Effective at Handling Kitchen Odors, Smoke
abstract:
This GERMGUARDIAN GG1100W ELITE PLUGGABLE UV-C SANITIZER AND DEODORIZER is FAR more effective than I ever could have imagined. I purchased one--just to try it out--at a substantial discount on the July 2016 Amazon Prime Day. I didn't really believe the claims that it handles both cooking odors and smoke. But it does!

With the GermGuardian plugged in, there is far less ordinary kitchen smoke (from the toaster and the broiler) going upstairs and threatening to set off the smoke alarm. There is also far less grease odor going upstairs into my home office. Lesser cooking odors are basically gone.

The GermGuardian is very large, though you can plug it into the top plug of a two-plug wall outlet and still use the bottom plug for other things. The main drawback is that the fan is quite noisy, but for me the advantages compensate for the noise. I don't even hear the fan now. It's become part of the background noise, along with the refrigerator motor.

Mine is still working fine, after being plugged in and running constantly for almost seven months. It has survived a number of power outages. Fairly soon it will need a new UV light bulb (see [[ASIN:B001TLRSOA GermGuardian-LB1000-Replacement-GG1000-Sanitizers]]), but as far as I can tell, that is the only ongoing maintenance expense. If my basic unit lasts for more than 1 year, I will be totally satisfied.

title: Hmmm - minor flaw
abstract:
I would have given this frame a 5- star rating because the menu is simple and the frame displays the pictures very well - crisp, sharp images. There is one flaw that I found frustrating. I loaded 20 pictures to test the frame prior to loading/reloading the final 46 pictures. (I used a USB flash drive attached to the frame for this purpose.)

I notice that pictures I had previously deleted were showing on the screen. The menu did not show them as being imported into the actual frame memory... Couldn't figure out what the cause was. The good news is that the Micca website had a common question section that addressed this issue and informed me that the deleted pictures were in the recycle bin located on my jump drive.

Huh? Never heard of that one. Followed their directions to right click my desktop recycle bin and click on the USB option and delete the files/recycle option. I did this and it worked beautifully. Reloaded my pictures onto the USB flash drive and place the drive into the frame. WA-LA - no more old deleted pictures playing.

Gave it 3 stars because - if this is a common problem... they should fix their programming. Who ever heard of a recycle bin for a USB drive being loaded onto my desktop and creating a problem??? I shouldn't have to look this up to fix it. They should delete this program from their system.

Other than that, it's a beautiful frame that shows quality pictures and the menu is intuitive.

title: Holds many batteries but case tops will crack easily - must handle with care - 3.5 stars
abstract:
I purchased a battery keeper a long time ago but it was one witout a lid. I dropped the batteries all over the floor so many times that I decided to buy this case. I know of no other case that has a cover. Both the front and back have storage and even the handle. I did try the tester and it works well. My only complaint is that the case lids are made of a hard, thin plastic that cracks easily. I can see this breaking in no time if I accidentally drop it, or put something on top of the case, or just with regular use. Since I am pleased with the storage for now, I give this 3.5 stars. I also purchased two of these on Amazon for $14.99 each plus tax, so cheap is what I expected. Attached are photos of one of my cases in use.

I did not count the slots but the insert claims the following storage:

FRONT
22 AAs
70 AAAs (2 of which are in handle)
10 Cs
8 Ds
8 9-Volts
12 Button Cell (I assume this is in the center hole)

FRONT
54 AAs
2 AAAs in handle

UPDATE - My boyfriend finally put his case in service and he really likes it with the exception of the compartment for the button cell batteries. He said, "They end up randomly touching each other's polarity. I honestly don't know if that is a concern."

title: Holy MAC, FOUR Tuners, this is unreal!
abstract:
We are the TiVo family: as it is all in the timing, we were seeking to get a new TiVo and so glad we waited for the few weeks as the new model revealed the four tuners! Very easy to set up and we are Verizon Fios Customer and now you can grab a cable card from the Verizon shop or pay postal for it to be delivered to you.; now you can initiative the cable card on your own via the automated phone or website. It took all of 15 minutes to activate the cable card! Sooo easy. no more making an appointment with a technician.

So with four tuners it means we can record four channels simultaneously, record one Internet program whilst watching a pre-recorded show!! We were coming up with needing to record three programs and our two tuner TiVo couldn't cope! So much storage that we don't need to buy an external hard drive to store the HD program that we have for our TiVo Series 3.

We love that out TiVo series three and Elite can talk to each other. We notices if we started watching one program in one room, we can pick it up where we left off on the other TiVo! How cool is this. The transfer replay quality is great as if your were watching it from the original TiVo that recorded the show. Note that transfer is wireless and hence if you have N then it will be a lot quicker.

We love that the IPad has an app for TiVo and now I can search for programs to record without interrupting the program that we are watching. How cool is that! The new TiVo interface allows a smaller screen of the program that you are watching (top right of TV screen) whilst you are searching for shows to record or to search in 'my shows' that were previously recorded.

Didnt even think about it, we bought the lifetime license for it as most TiVo last about 7 to 8 years for us; so it really pays off for us.

Only wished they kept the clock on the front screen!

title: Hope this is an answer to a prayer.....
abstract: Just received this lock. Will give 5 stars later if it continues to work as good as now. Arrived when promised. The lock when you open it does not feel as smooth as when you open a regular padlock. I reset the code with no problem other then being a dummy and not looking in the upper right hand corner of the instructions for the original code to open it the first time, duh. I needed something I could use on my bedroom door. I have a roommate that is the ONLY person who could have possibly taken jewelry of mine. I have only left the house 1 time since the 1st of the year and he was home. I needed to put a hasp on the door as somehow he can got through the exterior lock on the bedroom door. A little wood dough and paint can always cover the holes later and that is cheaper then my 1 ct diamond hoop earrings, etc to replace and god only knows what else. I figured something like this would make it more difficult to enter and help me keep my sanity and I can change the code and there are no keys that can possibly be duplicated..

title: Huge, built like a tank and super comfy. Awesome in it's own way.
abstract:
I've had this Taft chair a few weeks now. It is very well made but huge. I mean if you're Shaq O'Neal this is your perfect chair. It is a handsome chair but I will say again, it is huge. That being said it is very comfortable, the seat is sooo perfect, firm but gently supportive. My butt never gets sore sittng on it for many hours. The seat is so deep (meaning length from front to rear) my legs dangle over the front but I put a firm pillow at the back of seat and that problem is solved. I want this same chair with a normal size seat and am trying to reach manufacturer to see if they make one I want everything just the way this chair is but with a smaller, normal width and depth seat. So, get a firm pillow and like me you will have a monster size chair that is super comfy. I also noticed it holds me at a perfect height and angle for typing at my desk. This chair is awesome in it's own way..
Ok several days later I have lowered seat and it fits my body type much better> I was just used to sitting higher with other chairs. This chair just keeps feeling better to me. The ergonomic mesh back really has the perfect shape to support your back. The hugest chair ever is sooo awesome.

title: Husband is Handy Again!
abstract: I purchased this for my husband last Christmas as he had hinted that he was in need of a new level as his was "beginning to show grey". LOL! I took the hint and bought this one after reading the reviews and also due to the trusted Black & Decker name. Hubby LOVES it!! He doesn't complain anymore when I ask him to hang a picture or shelf. He has commented on how well it is calibrated. He loves the Accu-Mark feature. Makes hanging things a breeze with the easy sliding targets and marking the wall guides are wonderful too. His favorite feature is the Gecko Grips on each end. I usually help and offer another set of hands during house projects, but with this level and its grips, he can be a one man show - easily marking and hanging with needing to apply only the slightest amount of pressure to engage the grips. Best of all, the grips help the level to not mark up my paint! I love this level as well because I can use it too. I have had surgery on both shoulders and am limited on how much I can lift and at what distance away from my body. This level is so light weight (in comparison to others on the market) that I have used it by myself.

title: I Like It
abstract:
I just started using this product and so far so good. I only used 2 trays so far and i'm going to do another tray today. I used some of the seeds that came with the sprouter in one tray and I used an organic 5 part salad mix I bought in another one. This is my 3rd day and I have sprouts but I have a ways to go, it's a lot of fun watching them grow. I also bought things I needed to grow microgreens but I wanted to try growing sprouts first.
UPDATE: Well I still like this sprouter but for tiny seeds it does not work very well for me, even after letting the seeds soak overnight. I used some very tiny seeds in one tray and some bigger seeds in 2 others and I poured 2 cup of water in the top and went to bed and woke up the next morning and the tray with the small seeds which was on the bottom was still filled with water, the seeds covered every single hole in the tray. The other trays worked perfectly as those have a mix of bigger and smaller seeds. I'm going to start another tray tonight which will be a different mix of small and bigger seeds and I may try the smaller seeds again.

title: I could not wait any more!
abstract:
I love the Kindle for all the reasons that everyone else has mentioned: light, no lcd screen, instant download, storage is pretty impressive, the ability to lend some books pending on rights and eventually (soon I hope) to borrow library books through overdrive software). I have tried to read through the kindle app on the ipad, but the weight and lcd sceen (even turning the light all the way down) still screwed my eyes and I couldnt read for more than 30 minutes at a time! Now, I cannot stop reading, it is a bmuch better e-reading experience. The only think I need to get is the light for night time reading. I definitely think this is a very close experience of reading a book.. I notice I am so engrossed in the reading that I forget that I am reading from an ebook. It does have some weight after holding it for a long time, but much lighter than a 250 page hardback!

I noticed that I prefer browsing and buying a book from the iPad/pc/mac as the browsing experience is better. I knew I wanted the kindle as a reading and storage device and so far it is living up to my expectations and more. Love it. Since the color Kindle is unlikley to be available for Gen4, I finally took the plunge on a well designed Gen3.

title: I don't get the reviews. Mine are garbage.
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:63276c19932aa4f3687042b8b9f8613c]] Update: tried again to return them. I have prime. Amazon wants $7.99 to pick them up. Why? Bc I return garbage products & I don't feel like I should be penalized when third party sellers & amazon send damaged/defective products & then expect me to be happy with them & keep them. Why should I bear the burden of a billion dollar plus corporation as a disabled veteran living on disability? These skip all over the place. The yellow won't write no matter how much I shake the ball bearing. It and the black give a second of ink & stop. I even tried warming the ink up. The black finally became more viscous, but the yellow won't lay down. If you have a fast hand & are used to taking fast notes these are useless. At least my set is. Garbage. Utter & complete garbage. Some work better if you write slow like a toddler, but I have never had to slow my hand with a zebra fountain pen nor any of the 200 others I own. And you don't have to shake the zebra pen!

I purchased these bc of the reviews. Maybe I receive a bad batch. Idk. Mine are awful. I have fountain pens I purchased online for a dollar and less that works better & that write every single time I pick them up. Half of these did not even work after I attached the ink. I had to squeeze the cartridge repeatedly & even then I'm lucky if I get anything to come out. For $18 I was expecting to at least get something that would write every time I picked it up. These are a scratchy mess. I have tried them on cheap paper & expensive Tomoe River paper with the same results. I have hundreds of fountain pens, but I was looking for something that I could visually see at a moment's glance what color was in the pen & I thought these would work. I will give them a few more days, but if the ink doesn't settle in & lubricate the innards so that the writing experience is improved then I will definitely be sending these back bc they are garbage as-is.

title: I eas surprised read full review for details
abstract:
When I first felt this the plastic I was disappointed. It feels cheap and seems to be easily broken or cracked but so far so good and I carry with me every single day to work and use just as much. I keep my receipts books time cards and few other things inside for easy access and great for someone like myself who strives to be organized.
