So if you have found my review helpful please vote and let the other Amazonian Browsers get a better judgment of what to expect and how the product works. Thank you for your time and happy buying.

title: I had it...!
abstract: I wasn't going to write a review(a bad one, especially!), just cause Amazon has been so good to me - but by sending me the inquiry about, why I've so many returns on this product: Now you've asked for it! I've ordered a total of 6 Kinivo BTH360S Bluetooth Stereo Headphones so far, one after other - the first one turned out to be the best, which I gave it to my sister as a gift. Then I wanted to order one for myself, so I did - I got the packaging, opened it up. Charged the headset fully, as required by the product specs - then started using it, just to find out: Either 1. The power switch is too hard, or 2. It loses the sync, or 3. Sound is gone, or 4. The range is not enough, or 5. It doesn't pair anymore, or 6. Have to reboot my laptop, in order to pair 7. Sound is distorted, or last but not least 8. My last order was an open box, used one - even though I bought a new one AGAIN. I've followed the Amazon policy for returns, and have got my money back every time - but come on, five in a row! You gotta be kidding me, if I could - I would give (-1) star, so there it is. I've ordered one more, and hoping - I won't be in the same situation, talk about being a LOYAL customer!

title: I hate this darn thing - meaning my kid LOVES it!
abstract:
For the record, I rue the day I purchased this ball popper for all of the reasons my little one loves it.

With the press of a the smiley faced lever thing, she is fascinated by extremely loud carnival sounding music and balls popping out of tube, into the tray (sometimes - or around the room other times) and another ball popping out - rinse and repeat. If you only have 3 of the balls going at once, most of the time, they will pop out of the toy into the tray. If you have more than that, then chances are they are going to be flying around the living room. The balls are a nice size, so no worries about little ones choking on them. The opening of the toy is big enough to fit legos and other things (they will not pop up - they are too heavy). It's also easy to extract the legos from the tube by turning the toy over and yes, my little one likes to put her big legos (and anything else that will fit) in this toy in hopes of seeing it pop up. Thank goodness, nothing else seems to work besides the light balls included.

My only real complain with this toy is it only has one volume - REALLY FREAKING LOUD (which is why it got 4 stars instead of 5). Many of the toys we've purchased have two volume options so you can put it on the lower volume when you are watching TV, trying to think, or just want some peace of mind. This one doesn't have that and it's so loud. Have I mentioned it's loud? We have a lot of noisy toys and only two of them bother me, this one and the Dora microphone.

With that said, my kid really enjoys this and it will keep her occupied for precious minutes at a time. If you can stand the noise - this is definitely a winner.

title: I legit thought I was going to have to repaint my interior!!
abstract: I had my house painted, inside, before I moved in; it is an older ranch (built 1985) so it has that whole 'tomb' thing going on - where the old way of building houses was to allow as little light as possible in, to keep floors and furnishings from fading (I think that's the explanation I've heard... otherwise it must be a vampires built the houses issue). Needless to say I've got a lot of lights with a lot of lightbulbs. And I've tried different types of bulbs over the years (warm white, soft white - standard, cfl - lower wattages/lumens, higher wattages/lumens) and it STILL made everything look yellow inside. I had legitimately started picking paint colors, thinking the *slightly* warm ivory/tan walls just had too much yellow undertone. Thankfully, I'm poor so I didn't run out and buy paint. And in the interim of saving, my Dad picked up a pack of lightbulbs at the home improvement store that were "daylight LED" and was so impressed he was group texting the kids about his lightbulbs. I compared prices and these here - well reviewed (and no, there wasn't a little slip of paper enclosed offering any incentive for a 5 star review) and substantially closer to my budget - seemed like the way to go. As soon as they were delivered (PRIME DRIVERS ROCK!!!) I tore open the package and, well, "let there be light..." that isn't harsh, orangey-yellow, or deceiving me into thinking I need to paint. I honestly just went through and pulled the newish 'old' bulbs out of my bathroom fixture, replaced them, and now my son's bathroom has two sets of spare cfl bulbs and my bathroom has the most natural light it's had since I moved in this house. I cannot believe that lightbulbs could make me this happy - lol

title: I love this flashlight!
abstract:
Well, my husband actually suggested that I get this one, because I am the one who cleans
the kitty ears, clips toenails, etc. I also go a lot of crafts, so I can see this coming in VERY handy!

It is a little heavy on the head to me. It'll take getting used to, but definitely worth the trouble.

The light clicks into umpteen positions - I love it. You can get the light exactly where you need it.
This beats my former method of trying to hold a flashlight in my mouth when I needed both hands!

To those who had trouble making it work - there aren't any markings for the positive/negative on the battery
pack that I could see, but just put the "nipple" end of the batteries UP if there's a flat spot, and flat end
UP if there's a coil in the lid.

I really love how adjustable both the headband and the light is - you can get about every angle you could need.
My husband, who does maintenance, decided that he'd like to have one as well, to help with those times under
a sink when you need both hands and a flashlight just can't quite get to the place where you are trying to look.
I ordered another one for him today.

Thank you Rayovac for a really great item.

title: I now have "remote" access to so many devices
abstract:
I love these KASA plugs. I even gave them to family as gifts last Christmas. I make sure I have extras available in case I need one. Sometimes you just realize it would make life easier.

I do have some smart light bulbs that can't seem to decide if they want to connect or not, depending on the day (or the way the planets are aligned). I never have trouble with any commands to my KASA devices, so I find them to be reliable.

Having hooked them up through google, I can give voice commands through my home hub or on-screen commands on my phone or tablet…when that feels right. (Sometimes I just don't feel like talking, you know?)

I use them with certain lamps and many fans and small heaters set up around the house. We even used them to turn Christmas decorations on and off. It's especially helpful if your appliance or lamp is hard to turn on and off or reach.

Sometimes I find that little button at the end of the plug to be helpful just to turn something on when I plug something back in.

Set up isn't bad but I do agree that they prefer 2.4 ghz WiFi.

I like that, if you unplug one for a while, it remembers its name and will still work when you plug it back in. If it's unplugged for a longer time, however, (weeks?) it may need to be set up again.

I am really not that technical but have managed to work with these just fine.

I recommend and would purchase again.

title: I will likely buy again
abstract:
Winter is here, partially shaded window, it's cold inside & out and the heat isn't on yet so my plants have been suffering big time. I've been using this unit for 3 days and I'm impressed. The pink elephant ear's leaves were severely limp and curled. Within 3 days, she's perking up nicely. The light source from this unit has not harmed any plants like another unit I tried from Amazon. The remote is super simple to use. The adapter gets faintly warm so I'm unbothered. The light seems to be supportive of both adult plants and pups so I'm very hopeful. If all plants revive, I will get another of these grow lights to help the plants in another room destroyed by that other unit.

TWO CONS

My biggest con is this is a heavy unit. (It's not heavy to lift.) It's clamped on a strong shelf but when I try to adjust the arms down, the unit stays on the shelf BUT it definitely moves out of position due to its wait and has chipped the paint slightly. Once I figure out the best position, I'll likely use very strong velcro to secure it.

The other issue is that the cord is VERY short. So, if you're like me and don't have an outlet near your plants, you'll have to use an extension cord along with your surge protector.

NOTE: The lamp's bulbs do not get hot at all. Nonetheless, it does seem like the chill is reduced a bit in this small nook.

title: I'm small and these made my chair too tall
abstract:
I'm petite, only 5 feet tall. Was looking to replace the factory wheels on my new desk chair because they were scratching up the vinyl flooring in my apartment. These wheels are great and I don't think they would scratch the floor because they are made of a soft rubber-like material (not rubber). They look great on too for those wanting to consider aesthetics and are pretty quiet and smooth. They glide VERY EASILY. Almost too easily, especially since I now cannot reach the floor even at the chairs lowest setting, it's a little hard to get the chair where I want it and stay there. Overall all I think this would be a great product/solution for those who are average height or taller.

Unfortunately for me though, I'll need to return them. Also, I may have received a used product. The wheels had minor signs of wear and came in a plain, white box with no paperwork or stickers of any sort. Not a big deal since the installation is pretty self-explanatory but I really think Amazon should disclose when it is a "used" or "refurbished" product. You order and pay for a new product so that is the expectation.

title: INDOOR ONLY item
abstract:
I spent $81.99 for this umbrella and owned it for 4 weeks before it was placed to rest in the local land fill. Looks really great but is made of the poorest material / quality I have seen in a long time. I guess I should have known by the price but was hopeful. The main support pole is so thin that a light breeze (yes light breeze not heavy wind) picked the pole up from the cast iron holder and bent it right over the glass table. I have 2 other quality umbrella's on my patio and they were not affected by this breeze at all so I know it's the poor material as the root cause. This particular brand of umbrella will only work if it is under cover and not subject to weather. It is for looks only and not durable.

When I broke it apart to put it in the trash can it was literally no effort at all. It is of very light construction and is not meant to stand the test of time. I snapped the entire contraption into pieces to put it into the trash in less than 1 minute. Should have taken longer if this was quality built. Very frustrated that I have to now buy another umbrella. $81.99 down the drain.

title: If you are in the Samsung camp this is great
abstract:
There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.

title: If you are small, cute, and perfect, clap your hands!
abstract: [[VIDEOID:2be902e52b42437d5405bf23a766a0c4]] I love my new tongs! I specifically ordered them so I would no longer get 'Trump Fingers' 😂 I love my puffed cheese balls, but hate the orange fingers that I get while eating them. I also make hats and toys for the needy, so need to keep my fingers clean. And because I'm in long term care, I have little space; so these are a perfect size. Another plus, it comes with 8 tongs in a variety of colors. So if you are having a party with your Bestie, and she says she wants one, you can tell her, 'Be right back', go grab a color you know she will like, and give her one. That way you're both happy, and she won't try to sneak one into her purse as she's leaving..hopefully 😂 At such a great price, you can afford to buy several sets to share with friends, if you're a party animal. And because they are small, you can keep one handy in your purse or pocket, then if you are at someone else's party, that is mind numbingly boring, you just pretend you're reaching for a mint or gum, then 'accidentally' pull one of these out by 'mistake', and well, Bob's your uncle! They will most likely ask what the heck that is, and one of two things will happen. Either they will recognize how cute and cool these tongs are, and for a few minutes, you can forget about the snoozer party. Or, your host will think you're REALLY WEIRD, and make an excuse about it being really late (even though it's only 8pm), and they need to get up early for work, and rush you out the door. So, if you REALLY want to get out of that party and burn the party bridge to the ground, pretend you use the tongs for a really personal reason..like scratching the kitty, walnuts or bottom cheeks...😂😂😂

title: Impossible to get working, can't even put it on my wrist
abstract: I"ve really had it with apple stuff that is too complicated to use. Since there is no instruction book it needs to be intuitive. Got the band on with the shorter piece - I have a VERY small wrist, but the watchband is so thick that it won't wrap around my wrist so that I can put it on. The watch face is bigger than the top part of my wrist. If the band were thinner or more pliable I might be able to put it on. Interestingly, the WATCH keeps telling me when it fails to pair that "the watch must not be on" If it"s giving me that message it"s obviously "ON". For what this cost they surely could include that part. FRUSTRATING FROM THE MOMENT YOU GET IT PLUS IT'S REALLY UGLY WITH THAT BIG HEAVY BAND. title: Inexpensive solution for two things
abstract:
I purchased this sight unseen, and solely to give my eyes a break from the much smaller laptop monitor I had been using. Since others have gone into the technical details (which are also amply described on this page), I'll stick to what I love about it and how I am now using it.

The main thing was price. At less than a hundred fifty bucks I took a chance. Hooking it up was super simple: a power cord, a VGA connection to my laptop (using the included cable), and screwing in the VESA adapter from my [[ASIN:B005C2914C Mount-It! MI-705, 3-Way Adjustable Tilting Desk Mount Bracket]] took literally ten minutes. This comes with a pedestal base that is more than adequate, but I wanted the mount I mentioned to free up desk real estate as well as to make this monitor a grab-and-go solution for a second use, which I'll get into below.

If there is one thing that I do not care for, it's the cramped area for connecting cables. The cable adapters for VGA, HDMI and power are inserted vertically, and the VGA and HDMI connections are closer together than necessary. Since I am connecting and disconnecting cables often this is a peeve, but if you plan to install it and leave it in one spot it's not even an issue.

The speakers are not the loudest when you are running sound via the HDMI port, but are more than adequate when you directly connect to the audio in port. This monitor comes with a 3.5mm cable for that purpose.

For my laptop (an aging ThinkPad) it is literally plug and play. I have finally migrated from XP to Windows 7 and this monitor's model was immediately recognized.

My second use is to press this into service as a large sheet music display. I am mirroring the screen using an [[ASIN:B00ZWOU5R2 EZcast 5GHz Wireless HDMI Streaming Media Player]] to display [[ASIN:B00WLIDHA4 MobileSheetsPro Music Reader]] mirrored from a tablet screen. Since this monitor weighs less than ten pounds it is fairly easy to set up at a gig. As a side note, if you do intend to use this on a gig or as a karaoke display this is an excellent mount: [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]].

Do note that the HDMI port will not power devices. For the EZcast dongle I have to use either a battery backup or a small wall wart (the same kind I charge my phone and tablet with), but that is not an issue either. I figured that for the price some corners had to be cut.

Although this is designed to be a desktop monitor I do wish there was a remote option for it. When I am using it to extend my laptop display it's perfect. For the screen mirroring use I mentioned a remote would be helpful.

The bottom line is I am thoroughly pleased with this monitor and may, in fact, purchase a second one so I am not swapping my laptop monitor out to take on gigs.

title: It Works, It's Affordable
abstract:
I would have originally rated this three stars. The timer works fine but you had to find EXACTLY the right position and tightness against the hose spigot otherwise it set up a horribly howling wail that echoed throughout the house. Too tight and it was horribly noisy, too loose and it poured water everywhere. Worst of all just dragging out and setting up the hose to fill the pool would change the position of the timer requiring you to spend five minutes loosening and tightening things just to keep the leaks or noise at bay. I was about to return the thing and spend more money on a better model but this is the brand our pool care company uses so I took the risk and bought a $5 bag of hose gaskets. Adding one to the timer where it meets the house and like magic I was able to tighten the timer down all the way, no leaks, now howling throughout the house. So you may need to add a gasket (ask a neighbor I bet one has an extra they can 'lend' you, we just don't know anyone we live near to ask) to your timer or you may not. But it wass all I needed to get things working perfectly.

January 2017 - leaks a bit while in use. Not horrible and it wasn't worth the hassle of returning. Normally takes about two hours to top off the pool, we might lose a gallon of water onto the patio due to leakage (have tried several gaskets to no avail) but that's really not a lot to worry about. Still happy with the timer.

title: It wasn't as good as I had hoped
abstract:
When I bought this, I had read many of the reviews and the entire description and it seemed like a good solution for my needs. One of the selling points for me was that you could use any paper with it and didn't have to buy anything special to go with it. Immediately though upon opening it and reading the pamphlets that come with it, you find out this isn't true. They recommend that you use the special paper their company makes or the device may not work as well as it would otherwise.

That was only problem number one. The app you have to use with it is the only way to make changes and it is a pain to get the documents to go where you want them to go. Sometimes the app wouldn't connect at all and the blue tooth refused to even try to connect. The battery life is not nearly as good as advertised and I was only able to find a mobile app to use, not a pc app, which makes it hard to edit the document, since everything is so small.

The text conversion is a nightmare. You would pretty much have to write all in block letters for it to understand what you wrote, being extremely careful of the pressure you are putting on the pen in order for it to recognise what you have written. Truly, it was worth a laugh, but not much else. I bought this in order to save time, but it ended up just wasting time instead. It was a good idea in theory, but not so much in practise. I was glad Amazon allowed me to return it.

title: It will break and Logitech doesn't honor warranties
abstract: In the beginning, you will love this remote. But it will break. Guaranteed. We had one stop working, and Logitech replaced it. We dropped the replacement once (just from coffee table to floor, but it's fragile!) and the screen cracked. We were upset that it broke so easily but knew it was damage not covered by warranty, so we didn't submit a claim. We figured we'd just had a freak accident/bad luck, and bought a third one. One day I picked that one up and the screen was whited out. Over the next few days, black started to seep across the screen from one edge. By the time I had to send a picture of the remote to Logitech for our warranty claim, you could see cracks at the edge. That remote was never dropped. My best guess it that I set it down on the side table as though it were a remote, not a Faberge egg. Logitech refuses to honor their warranty. It's like beating your head against a wall. Lots of "I understand you must be frustrated," and no actual help. Not acceptable for a product that costs so much. Mine is not the only review that says this -- please believe it! Unless you have the money to buy a new one every 6 months (the longest that one of our three Harmony Ones has ever lasted), just don't do it.

title: It works
abstract:
Pros: This works pretty good. It picks up most of the small pieces at the bottom of the pool, as long and you are patient and go nice and slow. I is also very easy to use, and shipped pretty fast.
Cons: The threading was off on one of the pole pieces, so I can't use all of them, making it a little shorter then I would like. Also It can't seem to collect the silt at the bottom of the pool. I live in a really windy area with a bunch of new construction in the neighborhood, so there is very small particles of dirt constantly blowing into the pool. This vacuum will pick up the dirt and direct it up into the mesh bag, but then there's just a cloud of dirt coming out of the tiny little holes of the mesh bag back into the pool. It does help circulate the dirt back up into the water tho, so my filter has a better chance to get some of it.
All in all, it does a good job and I would recommend it to anyone with an above ground pool needing a solution to help keep it clean.

title: It works and it's NOT in spray form unless you want it to be
abstract: I just love this seller. I bought some air plants from him and they came with a half of a bag of fertilizer and my plants kept growing bigger and bigger and looked healthy. So I found this auction which is a bit confusing but they mention it's a 1 yr volume/12 gallons. That means you'll dissolve 1/4 teaspoon in your water once per month when you are soaking your plants - I can't find anything else like it - they're all liquids and I don"t want to spray my plants due to the damage it might cause to the service I've got a plant on - but while I soak my plants in tap water (his recommendations unlike you do with the carnivour type of cactus that must have rain water or distilled water. I just got it the other day (I still have some left over from last time and got two healthy sized plastic bags that were tightly sealed. I am keeping one and sending the other one to my step-mother that I sent some air plants to. She was initially a little upset about getting plants to "take care of' but I explained how easy and clean it is to take care of air plants I think? she was pleased. I know I am. Thank you This seller and his family provide things like schools and playgrounds to their country based on some of the profit they make. Great seller.

title: It works, but...
abstract:
This mouse is fine, but nothing special. The small USB transceiver is nice. It's out of the way and won't catch on anything. The mouse itself tracks on just about anything and is very reliable. The battery compartment is easy to access, no hassle replacing the single battery. I comes with a brand name battery uninstalled which is very nice. No software to install these days, the old Vista machine recognizes it without issue.

However, it's too lightweight for my tastes. The "click" feels cheap to me and the scroll wheel is stiff. I have an older Logitech wireless mouse that has the larger USB transceiver and the batteries are a hassle to change, but it feels solid and works great. To be fair, this is a "Mobile Mouse", so maybe lightweight should have been expected. I just didn't realize how much I would dislike the weight difference.

I won't send this Microsoft mouse back, but I wouldn't buy it again. I haven't had any problems with this mouse, it's just personal preference. I'll just use the Microsoft as a travel mouse. I suppose it's also possible that operation becomes smoother with use, but I'm in no hurry to use this mouse.

title: It's Okay
abstract:
This heater is okay, but I would not recommend this Sylvania Electric Stove. We purchased this heater for our guest bedroom when we thought we were expecting guests for the New Year's holiday. Our house is older and two of our upstairs rooms do not have heating vents so they are extremely cold during the winter months. This little stove was perfect due to its description and cute appearance that would fit into our country decorating theme. We had seen this exact model on the floor at our local K-Mart and decided to buy it from Amazon mainly because it was cheaper and the return policy here is superb and second to none.

This stove arrived fast with the two day prime shipping. The packaging seemed fine, no visible damage to the unit upon removing it from its box. We attached the legs (easy job, less than five minutes for all four legs) and plugged it in to get it warming up. Well, it wouldn't warm up after being plugged in for two hours! Also, when we turned the TV off, it was then quiet enough in our living room to hear a very faint, but annoying, squeaking. We didn't disassemble the stove to verify, but we figured it was the fake log lighting rotor (the thing that spins to change the colors of the 'burning' logs). This sound was just faint enough and just loud enough (think lightly, but constantly dripping faucet in the middle of the night) to be annoying enough to be returned two days after it arrived. Amazon was second to none once again in accepting and processing our return.

We have not yet purchased another stove since, mainly as we are not in the need of one (no one is using the guest room at the moment, or near future). However, when we do buy another stove it will be the [[ASIN:B0047O2M5Q Dimplex #CS12056A Compact Electric Stove, Black]]. We purchased one of these during Black Friday Lightning Deals Week and could not be more pleased. We should've simply purchased another of the Dimplex instead of trying this Sylvania. Lesson learned.. stick with what you know and like!

title: It's a READER, not really a tablet
abstract:
Listen, for the price, it's good. It's a reader, not really a tablet, but Amazon sort of marketed it to compete as a tablet. As a reader, it's exceptional. As a tablet it needs some work. Be prepared... there are glitches, app failures, files that cannot be loaded or used, no external volume control, once you put in in a "cover/holder" it is difficult to use the controls, you cannot delete files you have looked at without removing all and even though I SHOULD be able to access my paid Dishnet online account to play movies, I cannot on the fire because it will not accept a tiny video enhancement file. Further, I get a lot of "connection error" tabs when accessing the web or app store and more recently, it just freezes up. The only remedy at that point is to push and hold the power button.
I just heard they have a new version next Spring and they are supposedly working on software upgrades for the current release. It would be nice to have a camera so that you could Skype. On the "up side"? I watched a free video (provided via "Prime" subscription. The video was flawless. Some "apps" are great and work well... about 1/2 do not.... I'm a glass 1/2 full kinda gal, so I consider this on the "up side." Some have complained saying it is too easy to turn off the kindle fire... I don't find this to be an issue.
I've updated my review to say that as a reader, the Fire rocks. As a tablet, you probably want something more reliable and solid.

title: It's just string....
abstract:
Well, I guess it is my own fault I was disappointed.
I thought the ball I'd be receiving would be a lot larger for the price.
People, read the square footage when shopping.

My husband is in chef school and requested some butcher twine for cooking meats.
(We had the bi-colored thinner twine, but he said that is hard to tie when dealing
with meat and his big hands!)
I should have just got the bolt - this was too small.

It also took quite a while to ship, but I think that was Amazon, not the seller.
I guess they held up this item while waiting for the rest of my order to be in stock?
Not sure.

Anyway, if you have any hardware chains or wally world chains in your area, just shop
for the "butcher twine" there. This was just thick string, and I feel the price was too high
for what was received.

SPECIAL NOTE: The comment about reading the "square footage" was an attempt at humor.
I forgot that many people do not possess said humor, and prefer to be anal.
Just read the dimensions of the twine and/or carefully. I did not read the total
LENGTH I would receive - the photo is a bit deceiving.
Hope that helps clarify the Sq Ft comment.

title: Its all about convenience...
abstract:
I had an edger that was electric powered and that did the job of edging my driveway. I only considered this cordless as a replacement because fooling around with an extension cord is a bit of a pain.
I've become a fan of the 40 volt Green works tools and decided it would be worth the price to get this attachment even if its just to avoid extension cords. Now that I have it, I can honestly say that I was right! Being able to pull this thing out and just go right to work is what it's all about. Convenience is the key! My yard and driveway are looking better than ever... not because I couldn't get it done before, but rather because its so convenient to just grab the tool and go to work! It's all about convenience! The handier the tool, the more likely you'll be to use it. At least that's been my experience.
As for functionality, it's straightforward in the way it attaches... adjustment is easy, etc. Its a pretty basic tool and it does a nice job.

I should also point out (if you don't already know), this is just an attachment... so you'll also need another tool to attach to. In my case. I bought a 14 inch line trimmer (also a nice unit).

title: Junk AT&T has given up
abstract: ATT always had great telephones. I still have a 530 that works fine. Perhaps outsourcing (to the Philippines), or all the money spent on athletic advertising has taken away from any monies better spent on continuing the tradition of making great telephones. I got a 210 because I needed a basic telephone that was inexpensive and would be dependable (an ATT). Instead I got garbage. One by one features would not work. I needed a longer cord so it went to a hardware store (where the owner use to work for Verizon) and he said the telephone was defective. The cord would not work. Radio Shack said the same thing. I called the service number and got the outsource who asked me to describe a couple of the issues. I was then told it was defective and to send it back. I also said I needed an extension cord and could I get one from them? They said anyone would work. I said I did not feel I should have to spend several dollars to send a $13 telephone back (received through Amazon free shipping and I should risk receiving another defective unit?). They said they could do nothing else. I asked for a supervisor and was given a complaint email address [...] to write to about it and instead of a written reply I get a telephone call and who do you think calls me? The same outsource office. They want me to contact them so they can work something out. I email them that they can certainly send me a prepaid label with a new and working telephone and I would return the defective one in the box the new one comes in. I had not heard from them in months so I called them before the warranty ran out to ask why did you have to speak with me and not respond to my emails. I was told we prefer to speak with our customers personally about their options. OK. What are they? I was told there were two: I could pack up the telephone and all its original contents to send back to them, or I could fill out a form received the next day authorizing a new telephone would be sent to me WITHOUT mailing in the defective one, IF I paid a pre charged $14.99 (the telephone was $12.99) fee. This allows (are they kidding?) me to continue using (I told them it was sitting in its box) the telephone until the replacement arrived. I asked she email me these `options' for my record and she did. Garbage telephone and sad to say, garbage customer support (games and ignoring the consumer does not make for good customer support, or goodwill). Keep spending money on advertising for product that isn't worth the marketing.

title: Just what I needed....
abstract:
The Aube TI071 totally rocks. Here's my situation:
When I purchased my house 18 months ago, it came with a piece-of-garbage timer switch to turn on the lights flanking my garage door. That hunk of junk was nearly impossible to set, and seemed to reset itself if I looked at it the wrong way, or breathed on it too hard. It finally gave out, which gave me a good reason to upgrade.

I'm very happy with the Aube TI071 -- it was a breeze to install, and super easy to program. I'm using the nearly-automatic solar time table mode: you set the current date and time, along with your longitude and latitude, and the switch automatically turns "on" at sunset and "off" at dawn. So far, this is working just great. And I can "override" the program to turn my lights on and off independently. There are a number of other modes that allow you to set specific on/off times, too. But so far, the automatic mode is working just great. The back-lit panel is nice, too.

I purchased this model specifically because it works with compact florescent lights. I'm using 13W (60-watt equivalent) CFLs for my exterior garage lights, with no problems. Some timer switches limit you to a minimum of 40W total load, so if you want to run CFLs, be sure to check the specs.

title: Just what it says: Easy Flyer
abstract: I bought this for my 2 1/2 year old and 1 1/2 year old to play with at the park. With a light wind, I can launch it with my hand - no need to play out lots of line, run, or anything -- just hold it over my head and let go. I have flown it up to the limit of the provided string -- I think it's about 300', but it's most fun to fly it lower where the kids can see it better. At really low altitudes it can drop quickly when the wind changes, but you can pull on the string or run to keep it up. If I fly it up to about 80' or more where it's more stable, my 2 1/2 year old can hold it. If I pull it in to about 10', I can run around the park with it flying just overhead, buzzing the toddlers with the tail. It doesn't handle violent wind and gusts well, but it's not intended for that. It's so easy it might get boring for someone capable of handling multi-string stunt kites, but for any Charlie Brown, this is the right kite. There are other kites that fly easily, but these Easy Flyers are also supposed to have lighter line pull, making it less likely to pull or jerk the string out of a child's hand. Still, for under 5 year olds I do most of the flying. Therefore I'm going to try some helium balloons on the kite string instead. I'm also keen to try a KongMing lantern. Our area is popular for hot air ballooning and maybe when the kids are older we could build an RC balloon. A kite like this can get a lot of things started. Enjoy.

title: Keeps up to 15" laptops elevated (and provides extra space) when using a wireless keyboard and mouse
abstract:
I have limited space on my breakfast nook and for the few times I work from home, I needed an option that would provide me with extra space so that I could add on a wireless keyboard and mouse and extra monitor without making it impossible to move. This loft did the trick because it sturdily elevated my 15" work laptop, allowing me space underneath to store the wireless keyboard/mouse combo when not in use.

FEATURES:
- This is designed for most 11 – 15 inch laptops. I do wish, however, it held larger laptops.
- It has a rubberized strip on both the bottom and top of the loft so that there's no slippage on the table or with the laptop.
- It is also easy to assemble by inserting the center clip and sliding each piece of the platform into the channel on the clip.
- It is also easy to disassemble. In fact, I consider it a bit too easy to disassemble. Since the top part of the loft comes off the moment it is handled, I do not recommend moving the loft with the laptop resting on top.

I tried this with the following three laptops:
- 15" Dell Latitude E6430 (my work laptop)
- 17" Dell Inspiron 1720 (not recommended, it was a bit too heavy for this laptop)
- 15.6" HP Omen Laptop

According to the box, there's a 2-year limited warranty on this stand.

In general, I love this loft. It works perfectly for my 15" work laptop which is what I got it for. Although I wish it did not come apart so easily, it remains sturdy when the laptop is resting on top and the easy dis-assembly is the price you pay for the ability to swiftly break this down for storage.

I attached a picture of this stand in use with my work laptop with the wireless keyboard and mouse attached.

title: Knockoff brand works for *SOME* Sirius and XM 5 volt radios
abstract:
Buyer beware. The item that I rec'd is not a Sirius brand adapter as described in product name. The product # that I rec'd is model #SMPS5V2A-XM. There is no red light indicator as described.

This power adapter does NOT fit *ALL* Sirius and XM 5 volt satellite radios. This adapter does not fit an old Sirius radio "SV1" model which is a 5 volt model, the tip is too small for this model.

This adapter does fit an old XM radio "XM2go" model which is a 5 volt model, and works well.

But it is much cheaper than buying the Sirius brand adapter, and it works if the tip size is correct for the radio model. For that I give it 3 stars.

Side note on satellite radios: Sirius and XM satellite radios are not one and the same, and neither are the subscription channels...depends on what your radio receives. The Sirius & XM radios are made differently and the stations that they receive are different. On that note, be sure to check with SiriusXM.com for specific subscription costs before you buy a radio to help you choose whether you want a Sirius or XM radio.

I learned this the hard way. I hope this saves you some time and hassle.

title: Kohler Flappers work in Kohler Toilets
abstract: We have 3 Kohler toilets in the house, they get a lot of use, over the years we've figured out that basically Kohler (and Lavelle (Korky)) flappers, made specifically for the valves, are the only ones that work reliably, just about everything else leaks. We generally get about 5+ years usage. The local Home Depot's and Lowes seem to be uneven in terms of stocking this item, the plumbing stores similarly (they'll order it for you, of course), but I find the best approach is to just have a spare available, and I mostly get those from Amazon. There are a couple of tricks to ordering and installing them. First is that Kohler has had a lot of different flapper valves over the year, generally best to find the number from the installation instructions or their web-site (the toilet lid will have the model number stamped into it). Second is that when installing them, you try first with just the flapper, work that into the seat, if that doesn't stop leaking fairly quickly, a bit of petroleum jelly will help it to seat in. If you have high mineral content water, you'll need to clean the flapper from time to time, ours turn white, but so long as you keep them clean, they should still work fine for quite a number of years. This is made from high quality rubber, the flapper is quite substantial, definitely not a flimsy part, perhaps that's part of why they work better. Not cheap, but as with many things plumbing, you get what you pay for.

title: Large stand with room to store necessary office and other items; however, the stand I received is not level.
abstract:
I purchased two [[ASIN:B0036RA5EA Allsop Metal Art Junior Monitor Stands]] for my work monitors. Since I have my own monitor for my other computer, I also wanted a monitor stand for that which is why I ordered this.

This one is very nice but it is larger than I expected. It is 20 inches wide (side-to-side) and 11-1/2" in depth (front to back) where as my Allsop stands are each 14-3/4" x 11" respectively. Had I purchased two of these for my work monitors, I could not fit them on my desk.

Nevertheless, this mesh stand is beautifully made and has a drawer that easily slides in and out. The front drawer is protected in back from sliding out the other side. The right side pockets offer additional storage. If one has the room, this stand is perfect.

This would have received five stars from me except that it is not level. As you can see in the first picture, one leg is a half inch too short so it tilts back and forth like an uneven chair. However, once the monitor is on the stand, it is not too noticeable. Due to the large size, I am using this to elevate a speaker I have and since it is sitting on carpet, the uneven leg is not an issue for me.

title: Let there be LIIIIIIIIGHT!! (A LOT of light...BLINDING light!)
abstract: For what it's worth... my kitchen is *the world's smallest kitchen* that isn't in a camper. The width (including appliances and cabinets) is maybe 10' and the length is maybe 12'. It's like a hall between cabinets and appliances. There is one normal (for 1985) window over the sink. And the day I took the photos, Hurricane Sally was already bearing down on Georgia. It was dark, for the middle of the day, and rainy. This light kinda blew me away. I had initially looked at the 3500 lumen one that was maybe $5 less, but opted for this 5000 lumen. Which works for me, as there is a pantry at the end of my 'hall' of a kitchen and there is no light in the pantry. It's like an above ground cellar, tbh, but I can now flip the light switch on (I don't have a dimmer switch yet) and see in my pantry. I couldn't with my other light fixture (a 'boob' light). VERY VERY HAPPY with the output of this light for my space. Was also surprised at how easy it was to install. With "this old house" I've run into issues with every light I've swapped out - any install or swap out that should take 15 minutes to 45 minutes for a dunce, can take me up to an hour and a half because of ridiculous wiring issues. (I'm guessing there was a lot of palm-greasing the county inspector back in the mid-80s where this house is located. I've ended in tears of frustration several times.) Obviously I cannot comment on the longevity of this fixture, but I 'splurged' on the extended warranty that was offered.

title: Lid very loose- needs a gasket imo. Small base.
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:c87e962bc893a948856b0f1b285ce6cc]] I wanted to love this bc I previously bought a matching turquoise teapot, but the loose lid (defective or design flaw? Idk) on the cups is driving me batty. I'm disabled so my gait is not great to begin with & the lid just bangs non-stop while I walk from my kitchen to wherever I'm going with my tea. It's incredibly annoying. I had hoped it was just a one-off so I purchased it in another color & sadly it has the same exact problem. They could fix the problem by adding a rubber gasket or flange to the lid imo & I even thought of doing so myself until I accidentally knocked the cup over due to a design flaw that has a small base on the cup. I like the lid bc I run a fan continuously & I live with 2 service dogs so I like to keep my drinks covered beyond just the brew times so I really hope they update this cup bc it does keep the tea warm & the size is perfect for a 2 cup brew.

I wish they would fix the obvious design flaw of the base that is too small for a cup that tall & wide bc it is also very easy to accidentally knock over as I mentioned above. I did it several times before I yet boxed them both back up.

Overall I like the product as it seems as it was made with quality in mind, but missed the mark in the design phase. The colors are pretty & the cups I purchased keep the tea warm, but the lids are either defective or a design flaw. I really hope the company fixes these issue bc the colors match teapots I already own. Lol. I intend to see if the company has another design that works better for me in the meantime.

title: Light & simple, ***UPDATED***
abstract:
Overall I think these are decent walkies. If you want basic push button to talk and small lightweight with adequate range. This is a decent choice. Choosing this model for the Secret Service earpiece can be hit and miss. Guess some earpieces can be just as bad as the black over the ear units the other companies use. In all but a library, the earpiece audio is too low to hear in outdoor conditions. ***see update***

The RT22 cost the same as other models with displays and buttons (thicker and heavier walkies) to control functions this model has to do with button combos, but it does talk to you as you change settings and channels. Sadly as with many other models I tried. VOX is near useless. VOX works as bad as any sub $100 walkie I've tried. It lags and maybe sends half the message at best. You won't know how good/bad VOX is for you till you try it yourself.

Get these for size, lightweight, basic, rechargeable walkie needs. Try to catch it on sale...if possible. I paid a fair amount.

Btw, my wife and I use these for trail rides on our e-bikes. The true two-way communication devices did not fit our non-helmet style and will cost substantially more.

***UPDATED***
Company did reach out to offer a refund because they thought I was unhappy. And only the earpiece was a bit of let down for me. They told me about another similar earpiece that seems to be working a bit better and now I can actually hear outdoors with the earpiece. It is still a Secret Service style, but somehow it is a bit louder. Maybe my original earpieces were faulty.

Let me be clear. I still paid the retail price, kept the walkies and did not take any money/refund for my review. The walkie has so far been a great trail ride walkie. I might have received a bad earpiece. The company seems to care about their ratings and customers use of their products. And we all need to keep what we buy if it works to avoid landfill waste. I just came back to add a star and let others know. Good walkie. And maybe consider one of Retevis's many other earpieces or handset mics. Some of their other walkies include better headsets.

title: Light n' Easy
abstract:
The one important thing to note when buying electronic equipment is that once you pop, you can't stop. Every time you think that you have the perfect system, something else comes along that you absolutely HAVE to have, which leads to something else, and so on ad infinitum.

Having bought new surround sound speakers, we needed a new DVD player, and then, naturally, a new receiver. The weight of this system is a big plus, being less than half the weight of our old one, but the new one's not as aesthetically pleasing with those shiny silver buttons.

Leaning over the shoulder of my resident techie, I can now advise as follows:

1. You cannot connect a turntable to this receiver; there are no phono inputs. Not good for those of us who still have LPs.

2. It's DVD-Audio ready for the audiophiles among us.

3. Setup is relatively easy, controlled by two buttons only: a multi control button and the input selector button. This can be irritating if you need to adjust the tone after you have finished setting up, since there are no separate bass and treble buttons, and you have to go through the setup menu again. You can however adjust the level of the surround speakers and subwoofer from the remote.

4. No onscreen display available

5. No switched AC outlets to allow you to plug in other components.

6. In addition to the receiver, the universal remote can be used to control a TV, tape, DVD player/recorder, VCR, CD player and the radio. This reduces the number of remotes you need around you. It has a weird shape that takes some getting used to, and I still use my separate remotes - guess old habits die hard.

7. Input jacks on the front make connecting camcorders, video games, etc. quite easy.

8. When listening to music or looking at a movie, there are SFC (Sound field control) modes which you can choose to enhance the sound environment. For music there are six modes (live, pop/rock, jazz, etc.), and for movies another six (action, drama, sports, etc.) However, to the untrained ear, like mine, I cannot detect a significant difference if any of these modes are selected.

Overall, the sound from this receiver is quite good, very clean, though it doesn't seem as powerful as my old receiver (a Technics SADX930). This could be due to differences in the calibration of the volume control, but since I rarely play it at very high volumes this is a non-issue. The centre channel seems a bit weak compared to the other channels, but with so many sound options to choose from and customize, it is very possible that I may have missed something and need to tweak it some more.

A very nice receiver for the price and features.

Amanda Richards, December 14, 2004

title: Light weight ruff wooden spoon, spoon size good but not a long handle, cheesy wood.
abstract:
I ordered this small wooden spoon thinking it had a long handle, couldn't find the length of it here too much going on in this page, and the spoon size was what I was looking for.

What a shocker when I recieved it. Not only was the handle short for a child, but the wood was ruff, and lightweight
Like balsa wood that I can remember as a child.

I was going to return this spoon to Amazon I was so disapointed, but the 5 yo saw it and thought it was for him. got bored with it And I just took it back, sanded it smooth, and have been oiling it with Howards, the spoon doesn't seem as porous but
I would Never buy OXO again.
Although I use to buy there brand, it's obviously has gone down in workmanship.
I have also noticed that when I was in Bed bath & beyond two weeks ago.

I would never put wooden utensils in my dishwasher, or knifes, and my cookware...
I have slim hands, and long fingers, so It fit, but the quality is not there.
That said, I have bought other inexpensive wooden spoons that are far better and have lasted me for years, and other OXO, but no more.

title: Lights The Way!
abstract:
Fits great. The batteries and light on my forehead aren't uncomfortable. Not having the batteries in a separate box on the back of the strapping means I can lay on my back and read or just watch the stars in comfort. The top of the head strap keeps the unit in place and from sagging down your face.

The white lights have three levels, two, ten and eighteen LEDs on. Two are good for rummaging in your pack, looking for your boots in the tent or reading. Ten are good for everything else; walking at night, working around the campsite, working on the car, etc. Having all eighteen lights on at once is overkill. I found the ten lights to be all I'd ever need. Eighteen just run the batteries down faster. The two red LEDs are useless for anything but an emergency signal. When they're on they blink and there's nothing you can do about it.

My only real complaint is you have to cycle through all the lighting modes to turn it off. So if you want a dim light so you don't wake or annoy other people, great, click and the two LEDs are lit but when you want to turn it off it's bright, brighter, flashing red and finally off. It's only a slight annoyance to have to cover the lights but it is something worth noting. Separate switches to set the intensity level and power on/off would make this a five-star light. Still, as it is it's very nice.

title: Lightweight, Decorative Fence Keeps Swinging Gate From Damaging Flowers
abstract:
This ORIGIN POINT GARD'N BORDER FOLDING FENCE (32" high x 10' long) is a decorative, lightweight metal fence that's easy to set up in your yard or garden. You can use it to surround a flower bed, alongside a pathway (to keep visitors on the straight and narrow), or in many other places. Just don't make my mistake: 32" is the height of the fence, not the length of each folding section.

My fence--just a single section of it--is set up next to the sidewalk that leads to my front door. It prevents an entrance gate from swinging back too far and crushing the flowers in the bed beside the gate. For this purpose, the 32" height is okay, but if I had understood the product description, I would have purchased the 24" high fence instead (see "Origin Point 052410 Gard'n Border Round Folding Fence, White, 24-Inch x 10-Feet").

These folding fences can easily be shortened, using only a flat screwdriver (to pry with) and pliers. They're intended to hook together into a circle, but you can buy two or more units and hook them together in straight lines, squares, or circles. The metal is about as thick and strong as a wire coat hanger, so all you need is a hack saw for removing unwanted connector extensions. The prongs that hold the fence upright go easily into the ground. Just bear in mind that this fence is mostly decorative, and it can easily be bent or knocked over by children or large pets.

title: Liked but, I did x4 of same color.. all black!
abstract:
Ordered these for my son in high school… He's into the necklace wearing theme! In the photo you can definitely see that there are four distinct colors. Brown, green, blue, burgundy.. unfortunately, the color I received were solid black x4 of them??!! Now, I would not mind a black color but because, I wanted the variety… This did not for fill the need we had.
The necklace itself hangs on a nice softer piece of leather cord, The knot to hold the pendant in place is a bit bulkier then, I expected. But, it is not a dealbreaker… Especially when being used by a teenage boy!
If, the quality control was there to make certain the variety pack held x4 different colors…this would have been much better. I removed a star for this issue- and a star for the bulky knotting. I'm not unhappy.. I just wish we could have gotten walk through photograph had shown.
The price point is very reasonable to receive four necklaces- and if the issues I had won't cause you any concerns (ie. maybe these are gifts for different people and therefore, color is not as important?) then, you may be happily satisfied with the purchase. It is quite nice you can slip off and on without having to undo any type of clasp-

title: Linen Santa bags
abstract: I was so hopeful for these - however, I would highly recommend you do not purchase. The arrived individually wrapped in a cello type wrap. I opened and the stink just hits you. Smelled like musty old socks and an odd combination of stale petroleum products. It was really strong. So I didn't want to put my grandsons toys in them. I made the choice to wash them (turned inside out) on the handwash cycle and tumble dry on fluff cycle ( meaning no heat). No harm right? I mean they are a thin type of linen. I couldn't have been more wrong. They literally fell apart completely. The hems didn't open, they frayed - bottom, top, sides. The draw strings were the thinnest most ridiculous thing you can imagine. They were thinner than most shoe laces. I had hoped the boys would be able to use these bags again, but good heavens, what a joke. You couldn't use them without washing them and they couldn't even take a gentle soaking wash. I returned them both. I am so disappointed because these would have been so nice - so much nicer than the bright red fuzzy or plastic bags. Considering the price you would have thought they'd have lasted a few years. I will update if the return process is hindered in some way.

title: Looks fantastic and is comfortable to lounge around, easy to assemble but has a few minor-ish issues
abstract:
All in all this is a nice sectional for your outdoor area. I put it on my deck and to date have received a lot of compliments. I do really like it but it is not perfect.

It was not difficult to assemble but I wish it came with slightly better tools but they worked. The instructions worked well and it really was fairly simple to assemble, it just took a bit because there are quite a few pieces to put together. Mine had a few pieces missing, like screws but I was able to make do. The seller and I worked things out about it which is great.

My least favorite part about the set is the table. I wish it was a little smaller and a tad higher so you can put it more in the center and it would actually stand above the seating area. The cushions are a bit thin so they do wear through a bit, so since it is mostly me I just rotate them. The back rest pillows do not stay in place on their own but when you lean against them they work just fine.

I would not recommend leaving them out in the rain because if they get really soaked they take some time to dry out again. So if a storm is coming I take them indoors so I can use them again right away.

I have seen a few rust spots already, not even a few months into using it but that doesn't really bother me since I doubt it will fall apart now and it is in spots that are not that visible. It is holding up pretty nicely but I do see that if someone around 200lbs sits in one spot for a little longer the sectional is hanging through a bit but it evens out if you leave it be for a while. The worst part of it is trying to put those little plastic pieces on them that connects them so they don't drift apart. I was not able to do that really so mine tend to just drift apart when I use it, again not a big deal but I wish they had a better system that is easier to apply.

All in all it looks fantastic, was pretty easy to assemble just takes a bit and so far overall is holding up nicely. It is a decent value for what I paid and fits beautifully in the space that I put it in. In the winter I will either bring it indoors to protect it or cover it with a sturdy cover since winters here will get bad and I don't want it to get ruined. I think I should get at least a few solid years out of it without any issues at all. I love the lounging feature on it and se it a lot. I am out on my deck pretty much every decent day now and enjoy this a lot. I am very happy about it and glad I got this. Now I can actually entertain friends on my deck for a nice glass of wine or beverage of choice.

title: Looks okay
abstract: It's exactly as the one on the picture but I am worried about durability, the handles look very cheap and make picking it up very heavy and difficult in my opinion, the handles could be better. That being said I mostly bought this because I wanted it for small spaces and easy storage, this bag fills all those standards for that purpose. It's really very convenient and easy to move around anyway because of the small legs at the bottom, specially if you have a hard floor (which I don't but just saying), it doesn't use a lot of space and can easily be stored in your closet and it's not very heavy so it's easy to move around. The only downside I see is that it does already come with limited space for the clothes and then to top that off it has this mesh bag at the top that seems to be glued on and unable to take off, this mesh part at the top makes it almost impossible to even fill the bag completely and only lets you carry a certain amount of clothes at a time, which is, mind you, not a lot, given the already reduced space. I think the mesh bag at the top is unnecessary because it's not even a complete mesh bag it's just like the top part that is this way and doesn't really serve any purpose if you ask me, it's supposed to help to close it but really not necessary. Comparing it to a much cheaper version of another laundry bag I bought alongside with this I'd say it's only worth it if what you want is easier storage like myself.

title: Love Tegu Blocks
abstract:
I love playing with Tegu blocks with my kids. These and Magna Tiles are the toys I get most excited about, and the kids love them too. We got the 42 piece set back in the spring, and we have a Tegu monster and a whale, and this makes a great addition. Each block has a very nice feel, is smooth, and nicely painted in bright colors. The magnets are totally enclosed - no choking hazards here - and are very strong! It does take a while to get used to building with the magnets since the polar forces create a right side and a wrong side when you are trying to connect them. For that reason, although even my 1 year enjoys playing with them, kids will probably be best with these when they are 4 or older.
This expansion, with all of the columns, cubes and planks, is great for having the necessary pieces to stabilize most creations. (This set does NOT come with any angled pieces or wheels that come in the 42 piece set)
They are definitely pricey, but they really are top notch quality, and really all magnetic toys are on the expensive side. I feel the price is justified for such a well built, reinvented classic toy that will last for years.

title: Love double wall!
abstract: I ordered three different sizes of these glasses and I have to say I love them. I am huge fan of double wall as it doesn't sweat. You can use these glasses with hot or cold drinks and they will stay hotter or colder longer. I have to admit I have not had this brand before so I was hesitant... I think there can be a big difference in quality... however, these arrived (all three size sets) well packed, completely intact and washed up perfectly in my dishwasher. I have dropped one... on to a wood laminate floor... did not break. (probably a lucky drop but I was so glad) Having owned this type of glass for years and years...This particular "style" with the dip in the middle sort of acts like a grip and makes them easier to hold onto... much nicer than my other brand which is a bit more awkward to hold and is narrow at the bottom which makes them less stable.... I do recommend careful use... put a bit of liquid in before adding ice cubes, just to be safe... and do be sure they are banging together in the dishwasher... Having said all of that... I have never (in 15 years) ever had one break with ice cubes, in the dishwasher or on even an occasional drop... but with a different brand. Hopefully these will stand up just as well. Having said that, I always update my reviews with any issues or useful info.

title: Love the headphones - great range
abstract: These are fantastic headphones and I love that i can have my cell phone plugged in at a central location in my house and walk around the house and still listen to music or my book. the range for me is about 30' and the headphones will disconnect if i go outside and then reconnect when i get close to my phone again. If my phone is in my pocket it will stay connected where ever i go. I love listening to things without being attached or tethered to my phone. It also makes it harder for my kids to pull the earphones out of my ears when there is no long cord attached to my phone. I love the 1 click pause feature so i can quickly pause what i am listening to talk to someone (i don't have to go find my phone and swipe and pause). They are comfortable and stay on really well for my ears. I have taken them running and they stayed on as well. I had an issue about 1 year after I bought the headphones and the customer service was wonderful and understanding. really great product and I will continue to purchase and recommend these to my friends.

title: Love the point it makes for Polychromos
abstract:
I've bought different brands of manual sharpeners and this is my favorite so far. It's the only sharpener that gets my Polychromos to that super fine point that I like. I like that you can adjust to different kinds of points. I prefer the 3 setting for my colored pencils. My complaints are that the close setting doesn't close anymore and that they don't last a super long time. I've already thrown one away as it didn't sharpen to that pin point anymore and that was after several drawings. If I find a sharpener that sharpens as well as this and lasts for years then I would switch but for now this is the one that works best for my needs. It is a bit pricey to me (about $6 at the time of this review) considering how often it will need to be replaced. I have been buying the 2-packs for that reason.
UPDATE:
Well I said if I found a better sharpener that I would switch and I did. For about a year now I've been using the Derwent Superpoint Manual sharpener and I love it. I still use the T'gaal sharpener when my pencils are too short to use on the Derwent.

title: Love this book. I hope it never goes out of style.
abstract:
Unlike the RING or SPIRAL telephone address books, this book design allows your palm to glide over the middle crease. When there is a ring or a spiral attachment for the pages, you have an obstruction when writing. If you are particular, and want to get a few words into that corner, without obstruction in the middle, this is THE best book.

The tabs are reasonably strong, and will last several years of use. The cover skin is durable. Since my needs for the address book were well served 10 years ago, when I purchased my first of this exact design, I was glad to purchase a second, and continue with the same design. Maybe I will need to buy a third, in 10 years?

It was a good buy.

The trade-offs were as follows (1) pages are thin, so flair pens will bleed thru. (2) tabs are not plastic coated, so there can be some wear and tear. (3) cannot add, delete, or replace pages. Anyway, this is just a telephone address book. I can remedy all of these trade-offs. Either with label stickers masking over deleted addresses, or other issues. So, I was glad to buy this.

Please let me know if my review was helpful in making your decision. I tried to be objective.

title: Love this purchase!!! Must buy another now-
abstract:
Wow! I'm in love with ease, convenience and clean lines this bed provides! We needed a bed to fit small apartment space for our daughter and this was perfect! What you do not know… I had to go back and post this review, even after owning the bed x1 yr!! Why....??
My daughter lives out of state and visiting her last week, I got the pleasure of staying at her apartment. Much to my surprise, I inquired about the bed and when she got flash replaced the original… The shock and all came when she informed me, the bed was still the same bed..!!?!!

Honest, it wasn't the look as much That impressed me...it was the Structure, sturdiness, strength and durability of a small full size metal bed frame. I hoped purchasing this- it would suffice but, my standards were college apartment level. To see it almost 1.5yr later...
The structure is 100% still tight and intact. No loose connections or stripped grooves causing bad to rock/sway… Or, worse.. squeak and creaks! I also forgot about amount of storage available under the bed! Being low profile… 14" still allows plenty of items stored out of sight and in a small area this means everything!!
I inquired and was told Assembly took one with brain/bronze and one with holding pieces skills. Power drill/screwdriver were used… And within two hours it was complete. Difficult level I'm told was having extra hands to help hold/align and that made things go smooth.
I'm in market again for another small bed For guest/office room and looking for something similar to purchase… Great quality so, I had to share for those who may be in the market!

FYI- we set this up without box spring and purchased rolled mattress in a box from amazon. Sleeping at home on a standard style bed with invested quality/money into… knowing difference in $$ between the two beds- I hate to say.. but, I did not feel major quality/comfort Discrepancy on lesser bed/mattress. I do have padded mattress cover on to protect her purchase, keeping her safe and clean. I did purchase 3" mattress topper and $350 tuft/needle mattress- It may sound like a lot-
But, all items included… barely total over $500 for everything. A lot cheaper than expected, without major quality difference- and lasting this long/nice!

title: Love this silicone splatter guard..No BPA, easy to use.
abstract:
I love this Silicon splatter guard, and I have other Silicone splatter guards also, just a little different, and in different sizes.
These are BPA free, and they Do Not melt.
This farberware silicon lays flatter on my pan then the other ones I have, and its a bit cheesy, but I like it.

This farberware silicone guard is lighter weight then my other ones, and maybe the silicone is a bit thinner,
 but the price is lower, and I still get good results.
I don't use high heat.

If the little handles are getting Too hot, your flame is too high, and you might be using a burner that is too big for your pan, or this
Guard is too big for the pan.
Also there are silicone guards that have handles that come up higher, do not get hot, but the price is almost double..

I use these instead of a pan/ pot lid, for pasta water, i also can use this as a cover for left overs in the pan..the guard is lower then a lid and Fits in the fridge better.
I now have so many Calphalon etc. pot lids in a big box in my garage I don't use.

This can be used to drain pasta water, or draining fat from your pan.

The guard has a medal rim in it, and cannot be used in the microwave. Use a paper towel, or paper plate over your food.
I do not put this in my dishwasher, as the dishwasher detergent is not good for it.

Easy to hand wash with a short handle kitchen brush with a little dish soap. The brush gets in the little holes to clean it.
I Let it air dry, on a dish towel, or dry with a dish towel.

title: Love this wrench. Better than socket set!
abstract:
The main points:
I use this instead of a socket set for most jobs. I also use it for wing nuts, cup hooks, eye hooks, and knobs.
It is more comfortable and durable than the tools it replaces.

The details:
At work we call it the "happy wrench" because it makes jobs we used to dread go very quickly. One thing it does well is work on wing nuts. (We encounter a ton of those in our work). The right angle is great for hard to reach nuts. The notched shape of the jaw makes it grip very well.
The handle has a comfy grip and the ratchet direction is very easy to adjust, but hard to swap accidentally. The width of the jaw is also easy and solidly adjusted. Overall the unit is solid and strong, despite abuse. (Seriously - it has gotten used as a hammer many times and survived!)
Now I realize many folks don't think they need a right angle ratcheting adjustable wrench. But you'd be surprised how often it comes in handy, and I have often used it even when a standard adjustable wrench would have worked, simply because it is more comfortable. I obviously also use it instead of a socket wrench a lot, because it is much easier to adjust than a socket. No more fishing for the right size!

The only con comes with using it for really long bolts. Obviously it can't reach then. But the jaw is long enough to catch a bit more than the standard socket can. So it still beats a socket set. (And did I mention no swapping sockets to change size? Think about how much time that saves!)

I love this wrench. I gave one to all my colleagues as christmas presents. I use mine all the time and it is still strong as ever.

title: Love this!!!
abstract: After reading many reviews on many different shower heads, I bought this one. I have only replaced one simple shower head before so I was a little nervous to install it. There are a lot of complaints about it being plastic, and yes most of it is plastic. It looks great though and feels very substantial/sturdy. The fact that it is plastic does not bother me. The first thing I did was watch a YouTube video on how to remove the water flow restrictor. I then removed it with needle nose pliers, and It came out easily. I installed the shower head in about 10 minutes. I had a small leak where the shower head meets the shower arm, so I took it off, wrapped the shower arm with some thread seal tape, and replaced the shower head. Voila!!! No more leak!!! I really wish people would troubleshoot before leaving negative reviews. The water pressure is amazing after taking out the flow restrictor. I don't know what it's like otherwise. When I ordered this product, I also ordered an 8" shower arm due to reading the complaints about the shower head hitting the wall. I did not have to use it. It worked fine on my shorter shower arm that was already there. The magnet on the handheld part is very strong. I am writing this review after using this for several months, and the magnet hasn't failed me yet. I am very happy with this product. It works great, and I haven't had any problems with it over the several months I have used it!

title: Lovely, but front bent corner & toner (?) splotches throughout.
abstract: It's a nice heavy journal with thick pages. The rose gold color is very pretty. Of course the first thing I noticed when I pulled it from the package was that the upper right hand corner had already been bent. For some reason the quick reference page has been glued in weirdly imo so that there is no margin to the left & it makes it hard to write ur information there. I haven't written mine in there yet bc my entire book seems to have toner or printer ink or something on every single page like someone decided to just sprinkle some fairy dust on every page. As I intend to use this partly as an art journal I would prefer one without the added splotches all over. I believe there are 43 sheets of lined paper after the journal section & I am quite happy about that added bonus. The envelope in the back is quite roomy & will hold a lot of receipts. It's a pretty journal & I suspect I will buy more from the manufacturer in the future albeit hopefully without these issues bc this one needs to be replaced & hopefully Amazon will do so.

title: Made a world of difference in my cabinets
abstract:
I was thrilled with the lighting this product provides in my cabinets. I attached the magnetic strip to the inside top of my cabinets with command strips (just so I can removed them later if I want). When I need to recharge the lights, which really isn't all that often…I just slide off the light and charge with the USB cable provided. After an hour or so, they are all charged up and ready to go. Easy enough to tell with the green light coming on. They attach easily again.

I like that the light just starts getting dimmer when it needs to be recharged instead of just going off completely. That way I have enough time to recharge when convenient.

I first installed them in my linen cupboard by my bathroom. All I need to do is open the door and the lights come on. I close the door…and the lights quickly go off.

I made sure to attach them close to the front so my motion would more than easily be detected. There is still plenty of light for me to see everything in that deep cabinet.

I also put them in my kitchen pantry and one of those corner lower cabinets that often turns into a dark hole.

You may want to avoid putting in a cabinet where you store items close to the top. It is sometimes too easy to knock the light off. No big deal if you do…you just pop it back on.

Just walk around your house and I think you might think of a functional use for these to make viewing cabinet interiors more easily.

I love that there are no batteries to replace and highly recommend this product.

title: Made in China!
abstract:
My mom is a war bride from England and insists on having Christmas crackers made in England. I did a lot of research, and no where on the product information did it say they were made in China. Instead, the title is quite misleading: Handmade English Festive Decorations. One would gather from that headline that these were indeed made in England. So, I ordered them. I was crestfallen when they came (very timely) and behold! Made in China.

Maybe these will be the best Christmas crackers we've ever had. In my heart of hearts, I hope so. They weren't the most expensive, but they also weren't the least expensive. I just wish all sellers would be upfront about the country of origin of their products. I'm not averse to buying Made in China products, but I do try to source American-made... and Mom had her heart set on genuine English crackers. I'll do better next year.

If anyone has a source for English-made Christmas crackers, I'm all ears. My cousin just arrived this week from England to spend the holidays with us. I really should have had him bring me some. But who knows? Maybe theirs are Made in China as well!

title: Made of Borosilicate Glass, Less Susceptible to Thermal Shock
abstract:
