Marinex glass baking dishes are expensive, but they're made of borosilicate glass, which is less susceptible to thermal shock than tempered soda lime glass, which Pyrex uses. (Years ago, Pyrex dishes were also made of borosilicate glass.) After two of my newer Pyrex dishes shattered from being set down on a room-temperature, ceramic-tile countertop, I began converting all of my glass cooking dishes from Pyrex to Marinex. So far, I've been very happy with the Marinex brand.

This 10-inch MARINEX GLASS FLUTED PIE DISH is exactly what I wanted for making homemade apple pies. The dish is not too large for commercial crusts (e.g., Pillsbury Readymade Pie Crust from my grocery's cold case), it produces a larger pie, and it's deep enough to hold extra filling. Apple pies aren't difficult to make, but they're time-consuming because you have to core, pare, and slice a lot of apples. It doesn't take much extra time to prepare a few more apples to fill a large-size pie, and after the pie is baked you can get a few more servings out of it. The extra filling means that a slightly narrower pie wedge is still a generous dessert serving.

Marinex warns that a pie dish taken from the freezer should not be placed immediately in an oven, if the oven has been preheated above 100 degrees Fahrenheit. (Thermal shock is still something to be careful about, no matter what kind of glass is in your baking dish.) This 10-inch pie dish is larger in capacity than either my Anchor Hocking "deep dish" pie dish or my Pyrex 9-1/2" large pie dish.

title: Marvelous Printer - SUPER easy setup -printer has email address - immediate Wifi recognition-
abstract:
Easy printer to set up. Once I took it out of the box, unwrapped it and plugged it in, this printer was printing within 10 minutes. The screen leads you through each step..no need to look at installation instructions. I went on my Macbook Air, pulled up a document and it printed. I did NOT have to install the software on my Mac or the printer. ( I am in the transition from a Windows 7 to a Macbook Air. Review is for either a windows or a Mac.)

This is, by far, the easiest printer that I have ever installed. I bought a Cannon wf printer 2 weeks ago, and it would not recognize the wifi, so I returned it. I am so very pleased with the simple no-hassle setup. A small child, who can read, could set this printer up. The only thing I was unsure of when installing was how to install the ink cartridges- the "case" that houses the cartridges looks different than the old printers.. But, don't worry, there is an automated video on the screen that shows you exactly how to install the cartridges. You do not force the cartridge in past when it wants to stop and there is no "clicking" sound when the cartridge is installed correctly. If the cartridge is in wrong, the printer will reject the cartridge- just push it in.

There is an Email assigned to the printer- a nice feature! Your printer has it's own email account- who needs a fax anymore? Send an email to your printer, or, better yet, give your printer's email address to others, and when they email the printer, the document will print AND you
get an email notification that a your printer received a document. That saves you steps! You don't have to open your email to send it to the printer!

Can scan to flash drive, an email address, your computer.

Found out I did have to download the HP drivers in order to scan. It was flawless..HP knew what my operating system was and took about 5 minutes to download. Now, I can clean printheads, see ink levels, scans, etc from my MacBook.

 I had an Epson and a Cannon within the last month that constantly dropped the Wifi connection, after one print job. I had to reestablish the wifi connection multiple times, and that was frustrating! For some reason, I thought I would venture out and try something other than an HP. I had always had HP's. That was a mistake! HP really has the user in mind- from setup to operation of all functions. Kudos to HP for their design and easy installation.

title: Maybe A Little QC Check Is Necessary...
abstract: Just received another set of these from Amazon. They have been very solid in the past. I have ordered 3 or 4 sets of these previously and they all worked just fine. But this set has a few issues. First off the slot in the screw in the pieces that hold the speaker wire in place is too small to even get a very small flat head screw driver head into. I had to use a box cutter blade (which got a little dicey!) to screw them in because I couldn't get even the very small flat head screw driver into the slot. It was just to small. Made getting the screws tightened in more difficult than it should have been. Also a few of the banana plugs appeared to be bent out of shape, enough so that it was difficult to get the sheath part screwed off. One of the plugs actually broke as I actually needed to use two pairs of pliers to try and get the sheath screwed off. Out of the 3 or so sets of these that I have used this is the first time I had any issues. So a little Quality Control check may be in order at the plant in China where these suckers are made. QC is obviously slipping. I would rate the previous sets I received four stars, but since I am reviewing this most recent set they only deserve 3 stars. They work but were more difficult to install because of the apparent QC issues. Get on the case Sewell and make sure this continues to be a good product.

title: Medical Practice Applications
abstract:
This is an update of this Acer Iconia Tab W500-BZ467 tablet, which seemed promising at first, but after nearly three months of use, we're singing a different tune and lowering the rating from "I like it" to "Don't like it". I chose it for a friend who needed it for her medical practice. Now that patient records need to be digitized, she hoped to use this less expensive tablet alternately with the Asus Eee Slate EP 121-1A010 to keep track of all her business's management needs, which include patient vitals, records, and billing. In the doctor's own words:

"I log into Athena, which is our electronic medical record and practice management, and then all the info regarding a patient gets put in. So, the girls will use the tablet to populate BP, pulse, etc, past medical history, chief complaint, etc. Some of it is clicking onto specific fields and it will auto-populate with a touch. I think the ASUS Eee Slate is the perfect size screen by the way. I really like that one. The Acer is good but, screen is small so it's difficult to maneuver over fields."

The doctor purchased the recommended digital pen for the Acer, but it didn't provide the accuracy or manueverability that the ASUS has. It was also impossible to get the Acer to interface with her printer.

The Asus has the added advantage of a wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a digital pen, which I believe can be an asset for anything that requires a signature, e.g. a prescription or an MS Office Word business letter. It can also interface with the recommended HP wireless printer. The Asus also comes with a mediocre MS Office program that can be upgraded for a better version.

My initial favorites were the Apple iPad2 or a Toshiba tablet. However, neither of them comes with a Windows operating system (OS), which the folks at Athena.com, the doctor's business out sourcers, had recommended. Toshiba uses Google's Android and Apple uses its own system. While you can change Toshiba's OS to a Windows OS, I wouldn't recommend it if you're not technically savvy.

title: Medical Practice Applications
abstract:
This is an Asus Eee Slate EP 121-1A010 update; we've changed the rating from "Like it" to "Love it" and we're adding a couple more to the office. I chose it for a gastroenterologist friend who needed it for her medical practice. Now that patient records need to be digitized, she uses this tablet to keep track of all her business's management needs, which include patient vitals, records, and billing. In the doctor's own words:

"I log into Athena, which is our electronic medical record and practice management, and then all the info regarding a patient gets put in. So, the girls will use the tablet to populate BP, pulse, etc, past medical history, chief complaint, etc. Some of it is clicking onto specific fields and it will auto-populate with a touch. I think the ASUS Eee Slate is the perfect size screen by the way. I really like that one. The Acer (an alternate tablet which we tested) is good but, screen is small so it's difficult to maneuver over fields."

The doctor had been advised to get a Windows tablet and the ASUS fits the bill. She tried it and an Acer tablet so that she and her staff could get the feel of two different products. The Acer is considerably less expensive, has less memory, and lacks a few features that the Asus has. We had hoped to get tablets with the anticipated Windows 8 that MS announced around March 2011, but by August 8th, the anticipated release date was 2012. Failure to comply with new federal laws for digitized medical records means incurring penalties, so she wanted to have everything by September, hence these two touch tablets seemed to be the best choice as of August 2011. After nearly three months of use, it became clear that the Acer couldn't meet her needs, but the ASUS has been wonderful. The doctor and her staff can download medical templates and macros directly from her provider, Athena Health, onto a main computer or the tablet.

While her medical staff handles the initial patient consultations, the info can be transfered to or from a tablet into the office's mainframe computer, athenahealth.com, and to the doctor's own tablet via e-file or e-mail. They no longer need to transcribe handwritten information into the office's computer; it can now be done on the spot, saving time. The tablets can also be used to read Kindle books.

The ASUS has the added advantage of a wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a digital pen, which I believe can be an asset for anything that requires a signature, e.g. a prescription or an MS Office Word business letter. It also interfaces well with a wireless printer, but it does have USB ports. The ASUS also comes with a mediocre MS Office program that can be upgraded for a better version.

My initial favorites were the Apple iPad2 or a Toshiba tablet. However, neither of them comes with a Windows operating system (OS). Toshiba uses Google's Android (aka Droid) and Apple uses its own system. While you can change Toshiba's OS to a Windows OS, I wouldn't recommend it if you're not technically savvy.

title: Mezzaluna knife with protective cover
abstract: This is a very sharp and effective mezzaluna knife. You definitely need to keep track of the protective shield. So as you're washing, don't lose the protective shield. I always hand wash my knives and this is one is a handwasher, in my opinion - in order to keep the edge sharp longer. I like to use this type of knife when chopping herbs, veggies and when I need to shave firmer cheese or cooked meats. Overall, I love it.  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including well over 25,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Much Better than TomTom's EasyPort Mount
abstract:
I have a TomTom Start and I have disliked the EasyPort mount from the day I got it. I had been telling my wife for months that I was going to get a "proper" mount for my TomTom and that day finally came when I accidentally broke the EasyPort mount. After a little research I decided on this particular mount, and so far I have been very pleased with it.

I wanted a more "normal" windshield mount - a suction cup with a lever instead of a twist ring, and that led me to this particular mount. The design is simple - press the suction cup against the windshield and flip the lever to make the cup stick to the window. In operation this is an easy-to-use mount and it seems to hold the navigator in place without too much trouble. As expected it does not hold well when it the windshield is cold, which is an issue with every suction-based mount I have ever used - including the EasyPort.

The ring in which the TomTom attaches to the mount holds the TomTom in place well enough but I have observed that it does not hold the navigator tightly. That is, the TomTom has a tendency to turn a little in the ring. So far this has not been an issue and the TomTom has not fallen out of the ring so this really does not bother me.

The mount is adjustable and provides for a couple of places where the position can be tweaked for maximum visibility. There should be no issue with getting the position of the GPS just right so it can be seen but not in the way.

So far I am pleased with this mount and am happy to recommend it. It's a lot easier to use than the EasyPort mount that comes with the TomTom and it's adjustable enough to make visibility a non-issue, even while in motion. If you have a TomTom and you don't like the EasyPort mount, this mounting system is a big improvement.

title: Mult purpose, light, flexible fence for outside or creative use inside
abstract:
Super light and flexible. I bought two for use in making a cozy garden area where I have a table and chairs as well as some hanging baskets. I wanted a backdrop, and it didn't need to be anything too complicated or expensive.

I chose this product because of a combination of price (was $15 at time of purchase), shipped item (vs me having to drive around to stores to find something), its ability to be shorter, taller, wider, narrower depending on my needs. Multi purpose, too. If I didn't like it for what I had in mind, I knew I could use it elsewhere. Outside or maybe even inside.

The more it is stretched, the shorter it gets. The narrower it is, the taller it is.

I bought some bamboo stakes to go along with it to help stabilize it, which works perfectly. I stuck them in the ground and used twine to tie it all together.

I didn't think it would hold together as it seems so dainty in construction. BUT, it totally stayed together when I got it snagged in some branches. I thought for sure it would break, but it came out unscathed. I don't know how as the construction of these don't seem like they can take much rough handling. Did well though!

Right now it's working out for my needs. I don't know what the life span of these are, but hopefully I get some time out of them. If I learn anything new, I will be back to edit.

title: Must have for anyone smoking - best bang for the buck!!
abstract:
Awesome little product! I have an expensive smoker but I still use one or two of these smoker tubes. I have the 12" for quick cooks - 2 hours or less and the 18" for 6 hours or less. I use both when I want real extreme smoking! The trick is to fill the smoker tube with pellets and use a little torch with map gas to light the pellets, wait at least 5 minutes and blow out the flame and set in the smoker or barbeque. Remember to set the tube on some aluminum foil because the ashes will fall through the grates and make a mess. Note: if you light both ends of the tube, you get double the smoke but half of the time before it goes out. I have bought several of these for gifts for friends with smokers and they all say great things about this product.

Update: I have a RecTec smoker and I use their wood pellets because the burn so clean as compared to my old Traeger with Traiger pellets. I tried using the RecTec pellets in my smoke tube this past weekend and I didn't get as large of volume of smoke but they burned a lot longer than the Traeger pellets. I switched back to the cheaper Traeger pellets for my smoke tube because I like the larger volume of smoke and because I set the smoke tube on some aluminum foil, I don't get all of the ash in my smoker.

title: My favorite highlighter for work and personal use
abstract:
I've worked for years and have used many different highlighters and markers. Fat ones, thin ones, different colors, etc.

My main use is to "highlight" print…not write with them.

My work consists of different jobs that I receive over email. I print off the emails and highlight contact information, part numbers, pricing, etc. I then create my quotes on my computer, referencing what I have highlighted. It's important for me to focus on just what I need and not get distracted with other information on the pages. That faster I work, the better my production…and the happier my manage is!

I think many of us started out with the yellow highlighters, but I realize I actually SEE pink better than any other color. My eye is just drawn to it.

These particular highlighters are my all-time favorite. I don't want thick markers, but something with the shape of a pen for comfort. No rough edges. The chiseled point helps for better control.

I find the color does not bleed through to the other side of the paper, so would be good for two-sided printing or book pages. These last for quite a while, depending on how long you keep the cap off. I do not leave mine uncapped for long, just to keep them fresh longer.

I find this pack of 12 to be a good value and will certainly keep buying. I highly recommend them!

title: My favorite hurricane weather radio
abstract:
Living in Houston, I have owned several weather radios in this price range over the years. This radio is my favorite.

I like the fact that you can re-charge it easily with AAA batteries (not included). I have found that re-charging with a hand-crank is too slow. Solar re-charging works well on most devices if you keep the device stored on a windowsill for the year so that it is fully charged during a weather event. Having the option to use three AAA batteries is great because the radio can be ready to use immediately. Another feature that I like is that no screwdriver is needed in order to open the compartment in order to change-out the batteries. This is important when evacuating and also when the power goes out.

During Hurricane Ike, I evacuated to a friend's home. The storm made landfall around midnight or so. In the dark, it is hard to find anything, so it's good to be ready before the lights go out. I can remember lying in bed alone listening to my friend's radio (not this radio) in the dark as the NOAA forecaster reported the progress of the surge up through Galveston Bay and into the bayous, lakes, and streams inland. It was so helpful to know exactly what was happening to the area in which I lived.

My friend's radio was a very expensive radio, and the main difference between her radio and this radio seems to be the reception.

Hers ran all night with no interruption with reception. With this radio, I do have to turn the radio off and then back on if I lose reception to the channel. A really expensive weather radio would probably have better reception if you want to listen non-stop.

For my needs, however, this radio is excellent and is the best that I have owned in its price range.

title: My new best friend.
abstract:
I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE my Kindle Fire. I had resisted Kindles for many years mainly because I wanted to borrow free books from the library and I read in the dark with a back-lit unit. Once that hurdle was overcome, I started to seriously look at the Kindle Fire. Not one to jump on the band wagon, I waited a few months and started comparing - online and in stores. My final test was between the Fire and the Samsung Galaxy Tab 7.0. The Fire was faster! The start up time is faster on the Fire than the new iPad...that is not from reboot.

Ever security conscious, the first thing I did was to download Dr. Web anti-virus and created a password. I bought the Fintie cover [[ASIN:B006GLEZ8U FINTIE ® Dark Purple PU Leather Folio Case Cover Value Package with Free Screen Protector/Stylus/USB cable for Amazon Kindle Fire 7" Tablet]] with the car charger and USB connector which came in handy as I needed to connect with my computer. These are such a good price that I can colour co-ordinate with the season.

I have had my Kindle Fire for two months now and am still in love. I am particularly enjoying the whole Amazon experience: the free app a day, the free books every day, the lending library with Prime and the free TV and movies with Prime, as well. I can not say enough good things about this system.

My husband was so taken with my enjoyment of the Fire that he just bought one himself. He is in love, too! Now I can loan him books. I was going to purchase the new iPad this summer, but now I think I will wait another year.:-)

title: N95 respirator masks with metal nose clips
abstract: These have metal nose clips and reported to be latex free. They work well as far as I can tell. I usually wear a reusable, washable mask - but occasionally you need a bit more so I keep these at hand. The bands stretch over your head, not your ears.  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including over 24,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: NO drinking spout.unless im missing something.. not very powerful either for the $$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$
abstract:
UPDATED: just as i suspected 1 ice cube and it did NOT crush anything!!!! its ok i guess when it dies ill find a better one but seriously for this price it should be AMAZING and its not!

SECOND UPDATE: one day and the next day the charge is gone......that's wonderful!!!

not as good as i expected for the $$$$ it doesnt even have a spout to drink from whats portable? i dont need it to be portable i drink it in the house but now i have to pour it into a glass.. there's no drinking spout you have to unscrew the top completely.....not impressed i should return it actually ill see how it goes in the next few days i only put protein powder and water in it for now im afraid to try ice chips and/or fruits, veggies, etc. i dont think it has the power to chop them cuz even the powder was still stuck on the sides of the container and although it comes with the USB charger cable it doesnt come with the "brick" attachment to plug it in the wall!! im wondering how long it will be before the battery inside this thing dies like a cell phone!! and the USB connector (the little one that is on the blender) is VERY tiny and hard to put into the blender itself!!! just a matter of time before it breaks too soooooo not worth what it was price wise

title: NOT THERMAL INSULATED
abstract: I ordered the olive and in my opinion, the color shown on my computer and what I received were pretty dang close.. they work perfectly, in color, for the room. In all honestly these are NOT, I repeat, NOT "thermal insulated" curtains.... The packaging confirms this, and of course, once you get them out of the package, you can see they are just polyester curtains...The "up" side of this is that polyester washes up nicely. Now...if you're looking for strictly a "room darkening" curtain, these really do make the room darker. I purchased them for our Arizona home so I was hoping for the thermal insulation, as noted in the ad. The seller really needs to remove that part to be honest and fair. I purchased 4 panels and one of the panels is a good 3/4" longer than the others. Awkward. And belies a quality control standard that is probably less than stellar... I do not see any holes noted in other reviews... I will probably be looking again to replace these with real thermal insulated curtains. Hopefully I can find some that are as good a color match as these. In the meantime, we'll see how these do. I always update my reviews with relevant info if any issues pop up.

title: Needed to wait a day before writing a review
abstract:
I've been using the Kindle since it first went on sale, buying every generation as it became available. My 3G KT arrived yesterday, and let me tell you, I was not impressed. Nothing worked in a way that seemed at all intuitively. It seemed awfully clunky. But I know me and knew I just get used to this version. It's a really good reader. Once you figure out how it works, it does become fairly intuitive and works well. I'm used to buttons, where they are, how hard to push, etc., so this was new for me, at least on a reader. It took very little time for it to become an extension of my hand.

If you already have the KK, you don't need this. You may like it a great deal, and think it's cool and all, but you don't need it. If you're coming from a K2, yeah, you kinda do.

Regarding not being able to use 3G to surf the web on this device. I don't care. The web on the Kindle has always been pretty awful, so less accessibility is meaningless to me. However, if it does to you and you have the KK, don't switch.

The one thing I really don't like is the fact you can no longer rotate your books to landscape or flip it upside down. When I'm in the middle of a book and running out of juice I flip it upside down with the plug on top and that's not doable with this. I'm sure that's something that will be addressed in one of their updates.

All in all, it's a really decent device, and super great looking, but lacks the spectacular awesomeness I'd decided it had without ever having actually seen it.

title: Nest Traveller Tripod Legs... 100% satisfaction all around
abstract: I started out using a Manfrotto 324RC2 light duty grip ball head (the side grip joystick) with a Fuji S5pro and Sigma 50-100mm Art lens. Not sure of the total weight, but did not notice any flexing or leg slippage once set. Once I changed over to my Nikon D750 w/ 200-500mm...I felt a little less secure that this was the right setup. Anything smaller (video camera, Lumix fz200, spotting scope,etc) I am 100% confident in these legs. Not really fond of that particular tripod head but was all I had when the legs arrived. Big problem was that it would not fold back neatly because of the design of the head.... So, having recently purchased a Sirui K40x for my super heavy Bogen legs, I was so wowed by that head that I bought a smaller Sirui head k30x. I could not be more pleased with the function of either. I'd never heard of this brand or seen one, but took a chance based on the first few reviews. Really like the hook at bottom.. Never been a fan of the twist locks, but I can change. Only other CF I have is a small Monopod for traveling in a suitcase. I have no regrets... I got a quality product.. Light and strong. Don't think I'll ever pull the leg off for a monopod, but it's nice to know it's there if I need to splint a leg or need a walking stick. Have yet to try it on a sandy beach... that will be the ultimate test for me. Have always used heavy aluminum pods that are easy to disassemble and clean from sand and salt water. Will update if find issues later

title: New! Ads. Ads, and more ADS!
abstract: I have Echo's all throughout my house. But, as a writer, I quickly learned that recently, distraction has now become the norm with Echo Show. Pop-Up Ads show up every 5-10 seconds, disrupting my photo collection and my train of thought. And then to integrate Avatar items into responses is annoying as can be! No, I don't want to play all those games you are showing continuously. I've contacted Amazon and was told that they are paid ads and I cannot remove them or refuse them. So, I am no longer a fan because you see, I also have Google Nest in my home, and truth be told, they show my photo collection much sharper, the sound is better when playing music and I have found, much smarter when in need of information, and the best part... NO ADS! NO INTERRUPTIONS! NO TRYING TO SELL YOU ANYTHING. So you make your own choices, but Google also has a sense of humor and I am done with Echo Show... Do you want to pay money to be inundated with Ads! Some every minute (see Jeopardy photos). Amazon has lost all my respect as to how it respects its purchasers of their products!

title: Nice clock, eay to operate and use. Bright green light that shows the time/date. Def a worthwhile purchase.
abstract:
I read so many things about this clock I did not know what to expect. Some said cheaply made, some said worse and I will tell you what I go. I got a nice looking clock with everything I was looking forward to. Bright snooze light, easy to use buttons that do what they say they will, easy to read and operate, nice beeping alarm etc.
It was easy to set up with the date and time and alarm time viewable. Big numbers that see and a handy feature I never have seen before.. there is cool green light that illuminates the time even when you are not hitting the snooze/light button that is on all the time and you can turn it off too if you choose. This makes it nice at night if you wake up you can tell the time... it is dim but bright enough to see.

If I had to say one thing slightly negative is that one of the pads on the clock bottom has slightly come off when I was setting up the time, but there seemed to be enough glue left on it and I stuck it back on with no worries. If that is the worse thing I have seen I will take it, truth be told little padding or not you did not need them anyway.

I like this clock a lot and would buy another in a heartbeat.

title: Nice leash, but I hate the snap!
abstract: I bought this specifically so yhst when my adorable grandkids walk my dogs and theirs they don't drag our other very expensive 6 foot long leashes o. He ground and running mnhhem by fraying them. I live on a budget so making things last and jerking then pretty and I'm working order is a big deal to me. The fraying breaks my other leashes down and loosens the weave that makes them strong. I love these leashes. They are the perfect length for waking gigs and making them heel right next to you. The bungee part allows them to step off the sidewalk and go their business in the grass. I like them so much I now have 2 with 1 red and 1blue. The only hbu g I'm not grilled about is the bolt on the end. They have a spring that renders them useless sometimes on other products I've purchased. I would normally and probably should return this product now yhst I can see what type of snap/bolt they use, but I am disabled and returns that I have to drive to ups are a pain in the butt, but since this snap is functional I will use it until it eventually quits working and then I will take the bungee leash apart and replace the snap and continue up use it because the rest of it is very well made. I purchaed it to Ide with my daughter Samantha's husky/German Shepherd mixed dog who is still a puppy and does not know his own strength. He tends to pull on the leash in training and I was hoping to avoid that in the future due to my disabilities that include pins and rods holding my back together. The bungee part of the leash gives me enough notice to brace for impact when Bjkrn decides to try to bolt after bunnies and my grandkids. He's just a big old baby that wants to have fun and I'm a broken grandma trying to hang on! Lol. This leash allows me to do that without risk of further injuries!

title: Nice looking but flimsy
abstract: We bought this umbrella and it looked nice on our deck. The tilt feature was difficult to figure out since the umbrella did not come with instructions. We found from research that the way to tilt the umbrella was to keep on cranking the handle more, after the umbrella is fully extended, and it will begin to tilt. Last week in a 10 minute heavy rain storm, the umbrella came out of the "hole" in our wrought iron table and flew up on our roof and then fell back on the deck broken into pieces. Luckily, it did not fly into our new bow window and break the window! That would have been a very expensive repair. Once the umbrella landed back on the deck, all the "arms" were broken and the umbrella was unusable. We were surprised that the "arms" were so easily broken. To break it down to cart to the dump, we bent the remaining frame with the slightest amount of pressure, and it was very easily broken down into small pieces to take away. We only had this umbrella for a few weeks and the wind accompanying the rainstorm was a normal amount of wind you would expect in a heavy rain. Needless to say, the next umbrella we buy will not be from this manufacturer- we will be looking for one with "heavy duty" attached to the description and pay more than this umbrella to get a more sturdy umbrella. It will be worth the extra money to save on roof repairs or potential new window replacement! If you have the umbrella anywhere near a window, beware!

title: Nice product except for paint.
abstract: For any little girl into art and Disney/Frozen, this easel will be perfect. My little one loves this and will probably use for several years. It seems fairly sturdy, except for the baskets/shelf at the bottom. It looks about the same as the photo and was fairly easy to assemble, with step-by-step picture directions included. You will need a multi-screwdriver (ideally electric) to assemble. The white-side is a dry-erase board that is magnetic. This easel includes a magnetic Olaf puzzle (9 or 12 pieces) and magnetic alphabet. The Black side is a non-magnetic blackboard, which will probably not be used much, and no chalk is included. I rate this 4 stars because of the paint issues (see my attached photos). First, the paint has a strong nasty smell that will fill your apartment and last for days, maybe longer. Second, paint is missing/chipped on some edges (photo), roughly textured in some spots (photo), and other colors are smudged in some places (photo) to give this a classic made-in-China look. Only the paint on the Elsa/Anna art at the top is nice. Whoever painted this is worse at painting than my 5 year old is. Overall, it's still a nice gift and a good price, but expect some paint flaws and a strong smell if you buy this.

title: Nice product for the price
abstract: I don't really print all that much, so I haven't really "put it through its paces", but can say it was very easy to set up. I still haven't really got the fax part set up. The instructions indicate there could be confilcts between the fax function and voice mail, which turned out to be true in my case, and I still haven't wanted to get back to it. Every all in one I've ever had (HP, Canon Pixma)was a hassle to get phones, faxes and voice mail all on the same page. My only disappointment was with the cordless telephone that comes with the machine. I had hoped that having it's own phone might eliminate that problem, but it didn't. I then ordered two more handsets, thinking the mix of the Brother machine and older Panasonic phones might be the problem. I never got around to fine-tuning the fax vs. voice mail with the new handsets because they are pretty cheesy and I just didn't like them. For example, the display is tiny, does not let you know when you've missed a call, and most annoying, you have to do phonebook entries separately on each handset. That got real old real fast, so I returned the Brother handsets and went back to my old phones. The other features of the machine, such as the touchscreen menu screen, ease of wireless network set up, Bluetooth, and ease of use, accessibility of the print cartridges et. outweigh that one issue, and I would buy it again.

title: Nice, both pans functioned perfectly the 1st time.
abstract:
I baked a cheesecake yesterday in my IP, way too yummy!!!...but back to the Springform pan... always wrap foil underneath the pan and up the sides in any springform pan, no matter what brand. Cheesecake in the conventional oven is best cooked in a water bath, so you should always make it water tight with heavy duty foil. For the IP, same thing, rap the outsides and bottom outside of the springform pan good and tight or you will not like the moisture than seeps into the bottom of your precious Cheesecake. It you want the top less wet, I'd suggest you seal the top well with foil, too but a little loosely just in case the cheesecake rises. I didn't wrap the top yesterday and my cheesecake was a bit creamier than I'd prefer, but still definitely a great cheesecake recipe from the Rootitoot cookbook Volume 1.

I have three springform pans now, and this one is every bit as nice as the Pampered Chef one that doesn't fit in my IP. This one being an Instant Pot pan doesn't negate your warranty, either. Stick with IP accessories unless you want to void your warranty.

This pan doesn't leak. Don't test it with water, as you won't be baking water in the pan, and it's not meant to hold water, it's meant to hold CAKE. Please test it with a cheesecake, wrapping the outside the pan as I strongly suggested with foil. If it leaks the first time, the foil will catch the product. Then you call Amazon and tell them it leaks. OR you'll be amazed that it function as a Springform pan is supposed to... with a tasty cheesecake.

Update: I also bought the 7 inch fluted pan. Used it today for the first time. My cake exited like a dream, see pic. Excellent buy with Instant Pot pans. Please as punch.

title: Nixplay 10.1 touch screen digital picture frame
abstract: I purchased this digital frame on a treasure truck deal - it works. You will have to load the app and follow directions to bluetooth transfer pics you choose from your gallery to the frame. I purchased an additional memory chip - but it turns out there is no place to install the chip so don't waste your time there. You can set a regular time to 'run' the frame or manually turn it off and/or on. You can 'shuffle' OR play all your uploaded pics. You do not get to choose the 'fade' that happens between pics, but you do get to choose how long each pic stays on the frame before moving to the next pic. Picture quality is pretty good - about as good as the pics you download on to it. It's close to an 8x10 frame. Not sure why they call it a 'touch screen' cause I can't figure out what you can do by touching the screen - but ok. It comes with charging cord, regular plug in - there appears to be a mini USB port, but I haven't tried it. Having said all this I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: No More Soggy Weetabix!
abstract:
This CEREALMATE NONSOGGY CEREAL BOWL is perfect for eating [[ASIN:B003XFOXQ6 Weetabix]], which is currently my favorite breakfast cereal. Weetabix soaks up milk in the blink of an eye, so I avoid soggy biscuits by dropping them into the milk and dragging them right back up onto the platform, one by one. If a biscuit doesn't get enough milk, I just dunk it again. The fact that the bowl doesn't have a barrier lip or ridge makes it easy to move the biscuits in and out of the milk.

The bowl is 8-1/2" across, divided into a 5"-wide platform for cereal and a 3-1/2"-wide reservoir for milk. The platform is large enough for an adult-size serving of any biscuit-type dry cereal (e.g., Weetabix, shredded wheat). The reservoir holds about 7 oz. of milk (just over 3/4 cup).

You can use this bowl for dry cereal other than biscuit-type cereal (e.g., Cheerios, mini-wheats, cornflakes), but the cereal will tend to slide into the reservoir. For those kinds of cereal, a bowl with a low barrier that holds the dry cereal in place will probably work better (e.g., [[ASIN:B00EDQCOX8 NEW Anti-Soggy Cereal Bowl]], [[ASIN:B00A2L1Q78 Obol Never-Soggy Cereal Bowl]]).

The bowl is made of Melamine, which means it is durable and dishwasher-safe. However, I did break one in half by dropping it onto my kitchen's tile floor, which breaks everything I drop except for metal, nylon, and plastic objects.

title: Norpro Honey Syrup Dispenser
abstract:
UPDATE BELOW....A very elegant honey server and it does seem less "sticky" than the stick dauber style. The resting cup and the honey reservoir are glass... the disappointing thing to me is that the rest is plastic! I was hoping for stainless steel. *sigh*.... So it will not last for long I'm afraid... but we shall see. I never hesitate to update my reviews with useful info. A tag inside suggested keeping about 1/3 of a cup of water in the resting cup to keep the honey from crystalizing at the tip of the reservoir. An interesting suggestion... I will update with news of this.... In the meantime, remember, that just because honey has crystalized, it is NOT spoiled. In fact, honey is the only food on earth that doesn't spoil. And even has some antibacterial properties. If you were in the wilderness and had a cut, you could put some raw honey on it. Heating the honey up in the micro for a few seconds breaks down the crystals if you don't like them. Personally I like a little crunchy honey with some peanut butter on toast. This dispenser is useful and I HOPE it will last for a while. If it does, I may buy another for syrup. Further... I am NOT compensated for my review in ANY way.
6/27/2016.... UPDATE..... In use for several weeks... works GREAT. Doesn't leak out the bottom, drops honey at a lovely rate... honey is not crystallized, which would clog the dispense (just fyi) While I am still concerned about the the plastic pieces of the top, it seems to be working well. I will continue to update as time goes on.

title: Not Perfect but Functional If...
abstract: Where to start? I use only brown paper for all my gift wrapping and shipping needs. I'm always looking to simplify and use space wisely, so putting a dispenser on the wall was a no brainer. Well, they're not easy to come by and can be really expensive. This one is less expensive than average and is sort of "mid weight" as sturdiness goes. Oddly, there is no way to install it with the paper dispensing "downward" as one expects. Literally, the paper roll and dowel just fall out. My husband is a mechanic and COULD NOT make it work in a "right side up" position on the wall. When flipped such that paper is dispensed "upward," it works fine. That said, the cutting edge is a bit on the thick side, for safety I guess, and cuts are inconsistent. How we made it work: Have good quality paper! Light weight paper tears everywhere BUT on the cutting edge. Mid-heavy weight paper works much better. Dispense at least 3 feet at a time: less and it's likely to tear mid pull. Upside down, good paper, 3 feet or more and you've got yourself a perfect cutter! (I just didn't feel like sending it back 🙄)

title: Not Worth the Cost of Returning
abstract:
This is advertized as a 'hard case.' It is NOT a hard case it is simply formed vinyl with minimal rigidity. You can easily compress the sides with one finger.

The description also claims this has a 'padded inner pocket.' The elasticized strip that divides the case in two is no thicker than a heavy-weight T-Shirt. It offers your GPS no real protection at all.

The walls, sides, faces of the case have no padding whatsoever. I was forced to improvise padding with a divider taken from one of my camera gear bags.

The case does not seal. The zippers come ¾'s of the way up the side and then there's an extra piece of vinyl stitched to both sides of the case. Forming something like a collar. The flap that velcro's over the top does not hold the collar section tightly closed. You can easily slip a finger into the case with it 'closed'. This means dirt and moisture, etc. have an easy path to your GPS. Additionally, I've had this for less than four hours and the velcro patch the flap attaches to is already pulling free of the case!

My [[ASIN:B005HSDL8S 5" Garmin nüvi 50LM]] barely fits in the Zeikos IR-CA101 Large Hard Case side to side but there is a lot, too much really, front to back room. Along with the improvised padding I was forced to add to the inner side of the case where to protect my GPS I've also wrapped my 12v car power cable in a piece of towel to keep it from thumping around. I would NOT recommend putting a window or other mounting device in this case with a GPS unit.

If it wouldn't cost me half of what I paid for it to ship it back I'd return it in a heartbeat. As far as I'm concerned this product is NOT as described. It's not a hard case. It's not padded. It offers almost no protection AND it's already falling apart just hours after arriving.

Do yourself a huge favor and don't buy this, it's overpriced junk.

title: Not a whole lotta shaking going on
abstract:
This remote works perfectly with a Nikon D7000, and reportedly will also work with Nikon models D40, D40X, D50, D60, D70, D70S, D80, D90, D3000, D5000 AND D9000 Digital SLR cameras.

It comes with frustration free packaging (albeit too much packing material) and once you remove the plastic tab to make the battery connection, you're good to go. The remote itself is a one-button deal, so there's no need for complicated manuals, at least for the remote.

Getting the camera set up for remote shooting is the major challenge, as the Nikon manuals are not easy to follow. It's much easier to do a search on YouTube and follow the videos there.

If you are using the remote to include yourself in family photos, take sneak pics of unsuspecting wildlife or minimize camera shake while taking lights at night or portraits by day, this can be done simply by rotating the camera's release mode dial (on model D7000) which is below the mode dial (the one that says P, A, S, M, scene, U1, U2 etc.) to the second to last setting, putting your camera (and tripod if necessary) where you want it, setting up the shot, and beetling off within a 16 foot radius, pressing the single button when you are ready. That's it.

For long exposures, rotate the release mode dial one more place to the last setting, which is called Mup, or Mirror Up. One press raises the reflex mirror and the second press releases the shutter and resets the mirror. Of course shooting fancy stuff like lightning, star trails and the craters of the moon requires a full knowledge of the manual setting on your camera, a sturdy tripod and a lot of patience, but this remote will do its part of the job with just one button.

If only the manual camera settings were as easy to use as this remote, I'd be a pro in no time flat.

Amanda Richards, November 13, 2011

title: Not as Pictured
abstract:
This cord meets the standards of an appliance cord, namely 125 volts, 14 gauge (which is a nice thick wire that can withstand the flow of a heavy current), and can handle 1875 watts. In addition, the jack's socket is nice and wide, making it easy to insert and remove the prongs of a second cord. The plug and socket ends are large and comfortable to handle, and I'm certain that this extension cord will perform well. What's my gripe then?

The item is pictured with the ground prong (a male part of the plug) on the outer edge. I ordered a second cord (Petra, which is UL rated) with the ground prong on the inside, so I would have one on the outside and one on the inside. The ground prong's location is important because some socket strips have the receiver (female part of the socket) on the inside while others have it on the outer edge of the socket. If I install this plug into a socket that has the ground on the inside part of a dual or multiple socket strip, the plug and cord will cover part or all of the adjoining socket. It could also cause the cord to bend in order to accommodate the awkward positioning. Such bending can reduce the life of the cord. I've experienced these problems with other appliance cords and it's the main reason why I paid an extra $2.00 for this particular cord, which appears to be no different than any other. Another let down is the fact that it isn't UL rated (United Labs, which sets the standards for electrical equipment); it's ETV (and I don't know what ETV means).

title: Not as Soft as Other Microfiber Sheets
abstract: First let me start by saying that I am a fan of microfiber sheets. Of course I love expensive high thread count cotton sheets, but in recent years I just haven't been able to justify spending that amount of money on them, so for the last 3 or 4 years I have been using microfiber sets. In general, microfiber sheets are soft (not quite as soft as the high thread count cotton) and long lasting (definitely don't become threadbare like the cotton ones). Now let me focus on these sheets. On the softness, they are soft, but I expected softer. I've had some microfiber sets that are super soft and these are not. They fit well on my Sleep Number mattress/bed. They easily go over all of the corners without coming up. The biggest issue that I have with these sheets is that the stripes go horizontally on the top sheet. The picture has the stripes going vertically, but because of the finished edge on the top sheet, the only way it goes is horizontally which is strange, but also frustrating. This may just be a manufacturing error and not representative of all of their striped sheet sets. I will use these because they are okay, but I would probably not repurchase these particular sheets.

title: Not as awesome once we had one at home
abstract:
We first found came across the other Melissa and Doug Hide and Seek board at a play date at around 18 or 19 months. He was amazed, so of course I had to get one for him. And silly me, I saved it for Xmas when he was 23 months old. I wish I would have gotten the other version and not the farm one. The farm theme is everywhere (in his books, in his tv shows, and in other toys and puzzles) so I feel like the other board exposed him to different subjects he doesn't see as often.

Also, the magnets are not very durable. At 23 months, we had a bit of a regression and he started putting everything in his mouth again. While I tried to stop it as soon as I saw him doing it, probably less than 30 seconds in his mouth, he was able to chew the drawings right off two the magnets.

While still totally awesome and a great idea, I feel like the excitement of this puzzle was short lived. We've played with traditional wooden puzzles far more often. Maybe I gave it to him too late and possibly would have gotten more use out of it had I bought it when he was around 14-16 months old.

title: Not as spacious as my usual bag but I like that it cinches tight
abstract:
This review is for the unbleached bags. I usually purchase these [[ASIN:B0773DJ8Q3 300 PCS Disposable Tea Filter Bags]] but decided to try these unbleached ones. The first picture shows how small and thin these are compared to my white ones.

My major like is that the string cinches the bag very tight and it stays closed unlike my white filter bag. However, since this is small, it is harder to insert one teaspoon of tea into the opening. It is amazing that the filter does not disintegrate in hot water. Also, I am shocked by how thin these are. A 300 pack of these filters take up one third the space of my white filters. I almost thought they did not send me what I ordered. However, the thinness is a plus for me for storage.

Overall, I like these. I do not know yet whether I will order these again over the white ones as there are pros and cons to both. For instance, the white filters I order never stay shut. I will decide when I need to place another order.

UPDATE October 23, 2019 - I have decided to lower my rating of these bags from 4 to 3 stars after using them for several months. These are smaller than the [[ASIN:B0773DJ8Q3 300 PCS Disposable Tea Filter Bags]] I am use to and they are easier to rip unless handled gently. I will only order these in a pinch and prefer the other bags instead.

title: Not bad!
abstract:
Very good light that works better than anticipated. I use this for a makeshift home office, which I use for work, study, and hobbies. The light does a great job with illumination, but sometimes maneuvering it takes a bit more work to find the sweet spot. But it's almost always discoverable, so the frustration doesn't last long.

Initially, I received this lamp without the clamp at the bottom, but the seller issued a replacement swiftly. The lamp is easily foldable, which is perfect for me since the table I use it on is our kitchen table, so I need to be able to set this up and take it down quickly and easily. The lamp doesn't come with a power adapter; that's fine for me since I plug the USB end into a USB power adapter I have, but it's good to keep in mind so you know what to expect. The lamp has three segments that make it easy to find a good angle. It has a soft, almost matte-like finish that's pleasing to the touch.

The only change I'd make is having controls at the head of the lamp. The only way to control this lamp is by the remote connected to the wire.

title: Not good "gaming" laptop
abstract: I bought this as a replacement for my 1200 dollar helios 300 that was 4 years old. I thought the technology would've improved that a 800 dollar new laptop would perform better then a 4 year old 1200 dollar computer. I was wrong. I averaged 60 fps with major lag spikes in teamfights in League of legends a 10+ year old game. I expected 120+ with the screen at 144hz. But it wasn't the screen holding me back it was the gpu, I guess. Also had poor performance in Dota 2. I wouldn't recommend this laptop. Also the volume on the speakers never rose over 50% it seemed. I couldn't hear the other players voices in dota 2 with everything on max. It was the computer, my note 20 is faster, clearer, battery stronger, and a smoother experience in League of Legend wild rift. So if you don't mind dying everytime there are more the 1 thing going on like single player games, go ahead and get this. But if you want to be frustrated every time you play, go ahead and get this "gaming" laptop. I didn't even try any of the AAA games, so maybe it's just the games I play. SMITE, DOTA 2 LOL PALADINS

title: Not great in an indoor hallway, blurry faces unless standing still, problems with app
abstract:
*UPDATE: Now that I have used this for a while, it has become clear the app was not tested thoroughly on Android phones (cannot speak for iOS users). I have a recent Android phone and using the Eufy app destabilizes the OS. I know that if I use the app to watch recorded videos of activity, the phone will hang or crash at some point later that day, usually within an hour or two. This is new behavior since installing the app. Nothing else in my phone configuration or app usage has changed - only the addition of the Eufy app. Disappointed.

I would like to add that Eufy support has been in contact with me about these issues and has been very responsive.

---

Medium-light performance (not night, just not the brightest indoor hallway ever) is mediocre, and resolution is lacking when a person is in motion. The person must be standing still to be recognizable - walking results in a blurred face.

I had issues setting up the doorbell in the app. The app refused to recognize the QR code the second time around. You must scan the QR code at two separate times in the setup process: 1) when setting up the chime/base, and 2) when setting up the doorbell. The problems were with the second scan (the first worked perfectly immediately). I eventually gave up scanning the QR code on the insert in the box after probably 60 scans. It finally worked - but only with the tiny QR code on the back of the doorbell, and even then it took at least 5 minutes and probably a hundred scan attempts.

Additionally, there seems to be a bug in the setup process. The user is unable to assign a name to the chime in the setup process, even though it looks like you cannot continue without doing so. "Failed to add name" repeatedly, endlessly. I had to exit and return to the app and it then allowed me to edit the default name which had apparently been assigned. REALLY frustrating - a terrible setup experience. I almost gave up, packed it up, and sent it back.

There are better solutions out there, I suspect. This was on sale, so a good deal. When I replace this (which I may sometime soon) I will specifically look for something better at capturing light in an indoor hallway, and at a higher frame rate to avoid the blurred faces.

title: Not my favorite by far
abstract:
Well, this is the first time I have purchased a Buffalo product, and it will also be my last.
I've had other brands of hard drives. What I was hoping for was one that I could just plug in, maybe click a couple buttons, and it would back up my hard drive. Nope!

First off, this has a lot of miscellaneous software that it wants you to install. You don't have to, but it
all says "Buffalo", so I installed several of them. So far, I don't see even one that was useful. It also offers to install other stuff like Picasa, but again, it's optional.

The cord: ARGH! Someone was on drugs when they chose this one.
It is VERY short, as in, it has to be sitting on my CPU in order to use it. You can't just buy a longer cord, because Buffalo has used a very unique plug-in shape so nothing you might already have will work. Sure, the USB part is the same, but the other end is unique.

On backing up my hard drive - basically, you have to copy and paste, like this was 1990.
There is no auto-backup, nothing that I've found that will work the way I choose for it to work. The minimal manual comes in something like 19 languages, and the English version is lacking in detail. It tells you how to install the software, how to find the drive, how to plug it in, but not how to get an automatic backup to work!

Did I mention that it was also pretty? That's all I can really give it points for. It looks good.
All in all, VERY disappointed, and won't purchase again. It's a pain in the rump.
Right now, after the third time to use it, the backup "time left" is sitting on 1 min 50 sec, like
it has been for the last 20 minutes. If I cancel it, I am sure I'll lose some files. It won't tell me which ones
didn't copy, or which folder there might be a problem with. BAH!!!
I'd return it, but I waited too long to do it (not sold by Amazon, but an off-site seller who doesn't want to accept returns after 20 days).

Look elsewhere, and buy a different brand. Save yourself the grief of something that should be a simple
plug-n-play.

title: Not what I expected, Hard to wash, Wasps/Bees attracted to Yellow!
abstract:
Up-Date.
Just read this, how to keep wasps. bees away from feeder:
When you're looking for a bee resistant hummingbird feeder, there are a few things that you need to keep in mind.
First, bees are drawn to the Color YELLOW, so if your feeder has a lot of yellow on it,"YES".
the bees and wasps will be more likely to target it.
So keep yellow to a minimum and red and other colors to a maximum.
Also try and keep your feeder in shade, as bees/wasps would rather be in the Sun.
Now I'm not sure this even deserves a 2 star!!!
 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The larger top does not come off, as I thought it did, which means, this is hard to get inside to wash.
To fill this,The smaller part at the bottom comes off in two pieces, then snaps together, then screws back on.
I have small slim hands, That said, I cannot get my hand inside the bottom part
to wash this. I have to use a special brush with soap to clean this little humming bird feeder, which
is a pain in the butt.

To make the hummers food.
Its 4 cups water, to one cup white sugar (NOT powdered sugar)
I first use one cup cold water to one cup white sugar.
Boil and stir while the sugar is melting, then for a another few mins. to simmer...
Then I add the other 3 cups of cold water.
Doing it this way, the water is allot cooler and you can then pour it into the
the bottom part of this feeder.
If its hot you will ruin the plastic holder, and you can throw it out.

I'm having a awful problem with Bees/Wasps that come to my feeder
and the Hummers cannot compete.
Any suggestions?

title: Not worth the money, not worth anything
abstract: Wow. I should really listened to the other reviews written here about all the "glow" products. This was just terrible. The directions are nearly unreadable. Once we got it working we were all just baffled. You can't see the markers on the board-- like really can barely see them so the kids have no idea what they are drawing. So we tried to take it into a totally dark room and then it sort of worked? but it still barely showed up. none of us could figure out the point. there is this one thing you draw on the "glow board" I guess? but you only get one - so you have to keep erasing your drawing (that you really can't see) and then there are some gel like things that you can stick on it - but the kids weren't interested in it at all. So, we tried this for something like 15 minutes and that's it. The kids are done with it because there is just nothing to it. What a bummer. There was so much hype in the commercials and the kids were so excited to have it for Christmas. What a let down. I'm really disappointed in Crayola. I expect so much more for them. But I'm also disappointed in Amazon for paying as much as I did. Right after I purchased these I happened to go to ToysRus for something and found them there for 1/2 the price. I'll think twice before making a purchase like this again on Amazon.

title: OK on a Toshiba Satellite P755d with a few fixes
abstract:
This is a decently made caddy, aluminum not all plastic like one I had purchased for an older Dell (never worked but too cheap to send back).

Two issues for my particular hardware, the Satellite and a OCZ Agility. First there is a small bracket in my laptop that secures the optical housing to the machine with one screw underneath the memory bay. There are two screws from the laptop of adequate length to reach the original equipment optical housing though this bracket. These screws cannot reach down to the thread portion located deeper inside this caddy. Although I have probably hundreds of screws, none were both long enough and thin enough to get through the holes in the Satellite's hold down bracket to the caddy. I ended up using electrical tape to secure the bracket to the caddy. I think it will be fine.

Second, the Agility did not appear in the bios or in windows when laptop was booted. After much messing around with other drives in the caddy I finally realized that the Agility was not shoving up tight enough to the connectors. I had to push it from behind with a thick screwdriver. Success. A Vertex was not a problem nor was the mechanical drive. Just the Agility. I believe it is just a problem with this drive, probably connector board a little off but not noticeable when regular SATA and power cables are applied to it.

Last is I guess a non-issue from function but not from form. The bezel or lack thereof. Yes, it will look a little funny without a bezel. I had quite the time removing the Satellite's bezel from the optical drive but did manage it in the end. And I can still pop the optical in when needed (like when I was troubleshooting) and run it without its bezel in a pinch. YMMV

Overall OK certainly for the price. They might want to look into how deep those threads are where a hold down bracket is applied. My mfr screws certainly were not long enough. Would be nice if they could supply two in addition to the HD screws they already do. And the lack of even some sort of generic-ish bezel were the only reasons for the one star off.

title: Obviously dropped while packing!
abstract: Aside from the fact that this was obviously dropped while being packed bc it has dirt on it & is so damaged I cannot believe it was even shipped I still cannot believe how lacking in quality these are. I ordered two & while the second is in a little better shape I already know this will be a return for me. As a disabled person I tend to take falls & maybe the bad packaging person that dropped the book did me a favor by pointing out its obvious flaws. The main reason I purchased these books to begin with was because the company donates a book for every book you buy and I always try to support companies that give back in this manner & to this degree, but for my personal needs these just won't work. They just are not sturdy enough. If they had arrived I damaged & I could have used them for a while & found that out for myself I probably would have given them a higher rating, but I think 3 stars is fair as they are usable for most oriole & priced okay currently. They are actually cheaper today than when I purchased them days ago. Amazon always seems to lower prices after I purchase stuff. Lol. So much for Irish luck. Lol. These will do for grocery lists or general to do lists, but you won't want to trust your poetry or fine writing to these imo. The paper is very thin & see through & some of my pages are glued together weirdly. Idk why & it's driving me crazy. Definitely a return.

title: Ofiyaa P2 and the P2 Pro are worth every penny!
abstract:
Update! 4/10/22: My P2 Pro was found with a slight scratch in the screen deep enough to affect the picture quality. It shows as a tiny dark spot that draws the eye to it every time you look at the screen. I contacted Aleceway first, then Amazon Customer Service who were both prompt to replace it. What I received was even better! New cables and they provided me a case to protect the screen. Aleceway and Amazon are just amazing! So incredibly happy with these purchases!

Original review: The Ofiyaa P2 Pro is worth the money. At 13.3" it matches my Lenovo ThinkPad T490 14" screen perfectly. When showing both the P2 and P2 Pro to coworkers, they couldn't really tell a difference from the 12" Ofiyaa P2 and the 13.3" P2 Pro. Everyone who has seen these at my office have mentioned how awesome they are. Once again, I'm the cool kid with the cool toys.

I also own the Ofiyaa P2 12" screen and both of these tri-screens work perfectly when I need to travel, rest in bed and work, or just need the extra screen real estate while sitting in a conference room or the couch. Super versatility with having it attached to my laptop or even using it as an external, separate screen. I seriously recommend these products!

I have also been able to try this on other laptops like the Lenovo Thinkbook, the Lenovo X1 Carbon and these items perform perfectly every time! For my Microsoft Surface, which is more of a tablet style laptop, I use it as a separate screen.

Overall, I do like the P2 Pro for the connection features, as well as the changes in how it sets on the monitor. The 12" P2 is a little bit lighter in weight, but both are portable connected to the laptop or carried separately. This is an amazing solution to needing an external monitor where it is just not feasible to carry one or set one up.

In addition, I also recommend purchasing from the company Aleceway as they are awesome in communication and customer service. Both items were purchased from them and each time they were very quick to provide communication and shipping expectations.

title: Okay individual colors - sometimes weird when combined and requires effort to get a 3 color line.
abstract:
Soooo, I had high hopes for these markers. I thought my little one would be highly amused by writing in three colors at once (she was mildly amused for a short period of time). I think the issue is that in order to get the even three color lines when writing or stamping or coloring, you have to hold the marker perfectly upright and ensure all three tips are somewhat evenly on the paper. This is not easy for little hands (my little one is almost 3). I myself had to concentrate to create the images I posted. It's much easier to end up with 2 of the colors in a line or even one depending on how you hold the marker.

The colors individually are nice, but sometimes when they cross over, they create kind of ugly mixes and combinations. Again, this depends on how steadily you hold the marker and what colors you have on top or bottom (as shown by the squiggles under my first picture).

All in all, I would call this an interesting novelty - for slightly older kids. I'm guessing my little one might make some stamps and then these will go in with the rest of the markers. If she was doing more freeform drawing - it might be more amusing.

title: Olive Oil sprayer
abstract: Ok, if you're like me and you've tried every possible oil 'sprayer' - try one last one - this one. Now, it's not technically an aerosal like mist. HOWEVER, it's as close as you're going to get. It's easy to pull the spray trigger. Two 'fan' sprays are 1/4 tsp - at it appears close. You can chose a fan like spray or a stream. I use the fan. I have 2 sprayers, one for avocado oil (higher smoke point) and the other for olive oil. It's so nice not to finally have a sprayer that works. Granted, I have only just used them for a couple of weeks, so time will tell. I hand washed them to be sure I got all the nooks and cranys, easy. I really love the fan spray of both the avocado and olive oils. I say it's worth a try, just one more...  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including well over 25,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Olivia Dress Up Kit is not What I Expected
abstract:
Olivia Dream It, Be It Role Play Set is a simple yet fairly fun dress- up collection aimed at fans of the television program Olivia. This set includes several items and accessories, like a tutu, slippers, crown, telescope, and other items that encourage kids to change into a different role and let their imagination run free.

The Olivia Dream It, Be It Role Play Set has two sets of accessories: One for princess dress- up and one for an adventurer. My girls like both of the options, but they tend toward the princess set of accessories. The tutu, slippers, and crown are their favorites, but they like the other items as well. Having two sets in a single package is good for those with two kids because it means that both can have fun without fighting over who gets to enjoy the dress up set. There are items for two, so both are satisfied.

This dress- up role play set can be fun and most girls will like it, but I do have a few issues with this dress up set and the main one is that there are simply not many items included. The trunk is small, and it surprised me when I saw it for the first time. Upon opening the trunk, I noticed that the small size made sense, given the small size of the included items. There are no actual clothing sets with this role play kit. The tutu is the closest item to an actual piece of clothing, but it is still very limited. The lack of complete outfits will frustrate some children and parents alike who purchase this expecting something more.

My girls enjoy the Olivia television program and they like to play dress up, but they are only lukewarm about the Olivia Dream It, Be It Role Play Set. The items are quite small and there are only a few of them, so don't buy this expecting something incredible. Add a few more clothing items and the set would be much better, but considering its low price, it isn't too bad and it has just enough good qualities to award it with a small recommendation.

title: One of the Most Effective Egg Separators Around
abstract:
This bargain-priced MINI EGG YOLK WHITE SEPARATOR is one of the best egg separators around. With any egg separator, the size and arrangement of the holes in the area that catches the yolk is critical. With some separators, the white doesn't want to slip through the holes; with others, the yolk wants to slip through along with the white. This little gem catches the yolk in the center bowl, and nearly all of the white goes through the holes in the bowl and sides.

This egg separator is made of "food-grade resin", and carries a warning not to store it near heat "as resin may cause melting, burning, or deformation". Clearly it's not dishwasher safe, but it's easy to hand wash. It's also a bit fragile--one of the center-bowl struts became detached from the handle part of mine, although the strut snapped back into place so that the separator remains perfectly useable. (I don't know whether the break happened during shipping or during use.)

This item ships from Hong Kong, but my order arrived in less than 4 weeks. Priced at less than $3, this well-designed egg separator is a good deal, even if it turns out not to be durable. If you're wanting a top-of-the-line egg separator, you might consider [[ASIN:B00A2KD8NY OXO Good Grips 3-in-1 Egg Separator]], although it doesn't do quite as good a job of separating the yolk and white.

title: Order and Supply issues
abstract:
Total disappointment... the mattress that was supposed to be INCLUDED did NOT arrive and I had gotten rid of the sleeper sofa with guests arriving the next day!! I would stay away from this set unless you thrive on headaches and frustration. I saw that another reviewer had the very same issue. I had hoped it was a one time occurrence... Sadly, not.
As far as the frame goes, I am 55 years old, female and put it together by myself in about an hour and a half. It would have been easier with two people on several stages.. but I managed. It clearly states that it is "faux" leather... and there is a significant chemical odor (for those who are sensitive) I think it will dissipate some as it is open. It is pure black too. The feet are hollow plastic, the wooden slats are glued plywood that are "stitched" together with velcro strips. The "tool" kit are a few screws (you actually only use 2 of the larger ones - the rest are apparently "spares." and an allen wrench (I used my own screw driver with appropriate bit, much more efficient). A couple of hints... don't tighten all the screws after placing the side pieces until you have all them placed, even though the directions show you doing this, as it will be next to impossible to fit the last piece if you've tightened the screws prior. Also, I would wear gloves when placing the wooden slats as they are smooth on the wide edge, but extremely rough and splintery on the edges. The instruction booklet page is fairly easy to read with graphics, as you can see in the photos I provided.
I never hesitate to update my reviews, however, I don't expect my review to improve. There may be issues that would be helpful to report and I will do so.

title: Ordering Ink online: never a good idea I guess.
abstract: It's a beautiful color, but even though it had been packed extremely well imo it still arrived & showed considerable loss of ink due to shipping/handling disturbances. It also left a stain on my bathroom vanity that I am still working on & thankfully it's just a small one as I placed paper towels down before I opened the mess. Next time I receive a bottle like this I'm just going to rinse it off, pat it dry, & slip a non-latex glove over it to keep everything in the vicinity safe including my hands bc the ink stained the label & wont come off except if my hands happen to be wet/moist. The ink works well on both Tomoe River paper & cheap notebook paper & dries quickly. As for the ink itself: I love it! I don't understand why it stained my vanity tho bc to my knowledge it's not supposed to be waterproof. Luckily after much scrubbing there is only a tiny mark left & I know it's there, but I am really hoping my LL does not notice it. Gonna try a little bleach on it next. Also, I was able to mix a bit of it with a J Herbin red ink (scented red rose I believe) that I had on hand to get another shade of purple & I am quite pleased with it. It is currently in a Dryden pen rn & it's working beautifully with zero issues. This ink R&K is in a Lamy "Candy" purple pen & is also working beautifully. I wish they offered the inks in glass bottles instead of the cheap plastic. Tho I recently received a bottle of Pilot Iroshiziku ink with a cracked lid & zero ink as it had obviously been upside down at some point during transit so glass is no guarantee that ink doesn't get damaged. I'm disabled so I generally order everything online as it's easier for me, but it appears I am going to have to venture out of my cave at some point. Lol. The ink is lovely if you can get one that has not been damaged or lost too much of it's contents en route as I have. I did notice that the cap on mine was dented & I believe that's probably what allowed the ink to escape as they always tell us not to buy dented cans at grocery stores! Things are only as good as their weakest links.

title: Packing is awful will update pen review later
abstract: Literally one of the worst packing jobs I've seen. It's the lightest pen I have ever used & as I am post surgery on my dominant hand & am used to less than 5 minutes of writing even remotely comfortably I absolutely love that part. I think it's pricey for what it is though. The Pilot Petit are $3 on Jet pens. 8 x cheaper & imho write just as well. Where this has the advantage for me is tho I am a woman I am tall & have man hands so said two hubbies. Bloody mean things to say if you ask me. Lol. I am in love with it even though I hate the price point & truly believe it to be massively overpriced for plastic, but being s fountain pen junkie with well over a hundred including Montblanc I fully intend to buy bc thst is what we fountain pen ppl do. We collect them in all shapes & sizes. I have 5 kids & I tend to collect them in both my & my children's & my grandchildren's favorite colors. Some I gift while I am alive & others they will only inherit bc I use them daily for writing & art. It is a little beauty & I love that the cap screws on. This mint color is beautiful & just happens to match a cutting mat I picked up at Wally World recently. Lol. Yay me!

title: Paw patrol folding table and chairs
abstract:
Wow. I wasn't expecting much from this set... It's pretty heavy. And sturdy.
