The top is a cushioned plastic with the paw patrol gang on it... the folding chairs have the paw patrol emblem on the backs... plain blue seats. Honestly, these are quite a bit more study that I had expected. I bought because I could easily fold and store when my grandsons, 2 1/2 and 5 are not visiting. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful, nor do I shy away from answering comments/questions. I do NOT receive compensation of ANY kind for my reviews. My purchases are VERIFIED, FULL price and 100% independent. As are my reviews! They are fully my opinion, which could differ from yours - and that's ok. Happy shopping!
UPDATE: 11/15/2016.... I have been regularly using this set... up, down, up down.... I still believe it is a super sturdy set. Honestly, I really didn't expect it to be so sturdy. It's been heavily used and loved. It wipes up easily with the vinyl type material... I can still highly recommend this purchase if you are considering it. * will continue to update if any new info would be useful.
UPDATE: 2/17/2017... Still regularly using and very happy with the quality and sturdiness of this set. I would buy it again, but as sturdy as it is I probably won't need to. My grandsons will outgrow it before it gives out.

title: Perfect Replacement For Previous PaperWhite Version
abstract: We have two PaperWhites with the lower resolution screen. Viewing just text there honestly isn't a LOT of difference until you look closely at the edges. I replaced my PaperWhite with a Voyage (an almost regretful purchase) back in October and while there is a huge difference the added sharpness of an extra 88 PPI and the two extra LEDs make a difference. Since I tend to read in dim light the sharpness mattered more than the number of lights. when my mother's refurbished PaperWhite started acting up (reboots, updates, nothing helped) jumping forward or backward two, five, a dozen pages at a single click and often when turned on would be on the wrong page we decided to upgrade her to the latest PaperWhite. She's used to using the touch screen for changing pages and the lighting in the PaperWhite was more than adequate. In fact if I was asked to choose, right now, which Kindle to buy as a replacement I'd stare lovingly at the Oasis, look closely at its price, and honestly buy the PaperWhite. Two extra LED and the page turn 'buttons' just aren't worth the extra cost of the Voyage. They lured me in last year but after having had them since October I realize I could easily make due with the PaperWhite and the price difference would buy quite a few books. Now that this has the same 300 PPI screen, the adaptive lighting I turned off the first day and never turned back on. The PaperWhite has all the features you truly need and often goes on sale for a great price. In fact we were discussing replacing my mother's somewhat malfunctioning refurbished model she said to buy one when it went on sale and I swear the very next day Amazon had the Kindles all on sale (except the Oasis, grr). He unit had done three years of hard labor, that lady can READ so I didn't feel bad about replacing it. She's quite happy with it since it looks and functions exactly like her old one though slightly sharper. It even fit her customized case. Quite happy with the purchase.

title: Perfect fire in so many ways!
abstract: This is great. I love the fire. Lots of functionality & great for reading. I got the 8" because of reading. There are many terrific features for reading: auto turn, auto page save. It's so easy to use. I've got it chock full of books for my late night reads & it's perfect. I can read easily in the dark & even w/ my poor vision I can see! It's easy to add audio voice too, like having a bedtime story. Seriously it's soothing & helps w/ my insomnia. Also as a prime member I get unlimited kindle reads. Great books at $0! I spent forever reviewing products & researching what was best for me. The kindle fire hits on all the buttons! A great tech necessity, it's not a toy as it's how I can read & enjoy it. It's very easy to search for new titles & download them all in one w/ the fire. I highly recommend the kindle fire. I think it's a smart choice for so many reasons. I've added a bunch of magazine subscriptions too. The pictures are great & you get pics from your books. I'd give it 10 stars if I could. Love this. I highly recommend the fire kindle!

title: Perfect folding side table for a patio; and folds easily if picked up by the top
abstract:
I was looking for a small table to put in between my two chairs on my patio. This is the perfect size. I do feel I paid about $8 too much by buying this on Amazon because this should be priced for about $14-$15. However, I was unable to find something like this in the stores near me, so Amazon was very convenient and the shipping was free (or included in the price, depending on how you view it).

What I really love about this table is:

- It's small - like a TV dinner table (although it folds differently)
- Since it's made of a resin it is not going to rust and is easy to clean
- Setup is simple
- Breakdown is simple; just pick up the table to fold away (this is also a big drawback as I describe below)
- It's light and easy to carry around

The biggest drawback to this table (besides the slightly higher price on Amazon), is that the table cannot be picked up and moved without collapsing (folding up). The table immediately folds if you grasp it by the top. It is sturdy upon setup but I have to be careful not to lift it in any manner while items are on top or everything will topple over. However, I knew this would happen before purchase based on another reviewer's comments so I was somewhat prepared. This table would have been 5 stars if it were manufactured to open and close like a TV table instead of the way it opens now.

Despite the above negative, I still love this table but I must remember to keep it in one spot and only move it when nothing is on it. If I had room, I would even consider purchasing few others in different colors.

title: Perfect for dorm room- creates space where needed!!
abstract:

The top tier is a tight shelf that can hold items such as a jewelry or, decor... even though, made of canvas- it's pulled quite taut and stays quite straight. The drawers are nice- they can hold socks, belts, etc.. Or, they can be removed 100% as well. Yes... I would recommend and definitely would order again. (I'm fact, I want a few of these in my home closets...) For any who need extra space or have a bit of OCD tendencies (me!!) this is a great addition and reasonably priced- It does trick for a really good price and if it Can last through packing
And moving dorms the next 1-2 yrs.. I'll have gotten money's worth plus!! Ha, I'd be so ahead of the game. I'm grateful for making this purchase 100%.

Etc. and without closet options and a very small confined space. This was our go too item for the solutions (with lots of options offered..) it was the fix we needed!! So, this is a great dorm add-on if you're in same boat with a kiddo needing to create usable space in limited space.. Ha! Say that fast x5 times...!!!

title: Perfect for everything - minus stud earrings.:-)
abstract: I was really excited about this jewelry rack, and I couldn't have been more thrilled to see it hung on the wall. (Yep, hubs took care of that part.:-)) I researched quite a few storage solutions for jewelry and found several valet/racks that might fir the bill, but this one seemed to have the most versatility in terms of storage of different kinds of jewelry (bracelets, dangle earrings, long and short necklaces, hair ties, etc.) I love that the lower round racks actually spin in a circle - great for storing long necklaces & for easy access! I use one of the upper horizontal bars to store my hair bands to keep the cats from getting them. The mesh screen is perfect for dangle earrings. I ALMOST gave this 4 stars instead of 5 because there is no solution for stud earrings. The designers thought of everything else but a tray that could hold miscellaneous baubles & earrings with posts. My solution to this was that I hung a small jewelry pouch from the valet and stored those earrings inside the pouch. It means I have to go rooting through the bag a lot, but really this jewelry valet is just perfect for storing everything else and it looks so cute on the wall. Since I really love it I decided to give it 5 stars, since it does exactly what it's advertised to do. My friends always compliment it and it's helped to keep me MUCH more organized. I posted a picture for you with all my stuff on it so you can see how I've organized everything. Good luck and I hope you like it as much as I do!

title: Perfect for musical instruments
abstract:
I use this both indoors and outdoors as a protected outlet for two keyboards (my other gear is protected by two rackmounted [[ASIN:B003TUO6U8 Merit Series Power Conditioner]]s.)

One rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. The two keyboards I plug into this does not come close to overtaxing this device or power outlets into which I plug it.

Some features I love include the 25 foot cord, which is heavy duty and os sufficiently long for any conceivable placement situation I will encounter. And because the cord is heavy gauge, and the housing is metal, this protected outlet is designed for rigorous use.

Tripp Lite's reputation for quality, reliability and safety is another reason I purchased this unit. I am a firm believer in safety and will not cut corners.

I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. Thus far I have had zero problems, and judging from other reviewers I expect that to continue. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for.

title: Perfect for my application; battery life is less than advertised
abstract:
I use this to illuminate objects that I am photographing (mainly small items that I sell on various sites), but also to provide extra light for smaller rooms when I am making videos of my band at rehearsal and/or on gigs.

The battery life is touted to be 90-110 minutes under maximum illumination power, but I have gotten around 75 minutes. For me, this is still pretty good I especially like the fact that the battery is integrated, so there is no need to purchase extra batteries and chargers like the other lights that I investigated before purchasing this one. Moreover, this will work with the same external batteries that I use for my tablets and phones, as well as the wall chargers and cables for those devices.

Illumination is soft and can go from warm to cold, depending on your shooting environment. Since I am by no means a professional (or even an advanced) photographer, I found this light to be all that I need for easy to shoot videos and stills.

One thing that I am on the fence about is the mount. It is a little shaky in that it tends to not firmly hold the light steady when installed in my camera's hot shoe. I can live with it since I keep my rig stationary, but if you are on the move that mount is going to be the weak spot.

Despite my dislikes I intend to purchase one more of these as both a spare and as a second light source for some shots that will benefit from the added illumination.

title: Perfect for primary and temp storage
abstract:
I have tested this card in both a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and a [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch]] and it was immediately recognized by both devices. As I write this review the card has been running in my Tab 3 and constantly used for over a week.

Other reviews have dissected the specs of this card, so I'll share how I use it and why I prefer these over the 64GB cards (which I also own and use). The price point on these 32GB cards have dramatically fallen and as of the date of this review they are priced as commodities. I use a few pairs of these to rotate backups on my laptop, so I always have a daily snapshot of my documents. For that purpose alone these cards are well worth it.

For my tablet I have divided my extensive music library into genres and have them backed up to these cards. A 32GB card will hold about 150 CDs, so the space savings along over the physical media is significant. In fact one of these cards cost about the same as a rack for 150 CDs.

These are also excellent for saving practice sessions that I sometimes record using my phone or tablet. I pop my primary SD card out of the device and swap one of these in to video record. Since this card will hold about six hours of video it's perfect for that use.

Overall, these are reliable cards that have worked in a number of devices I own. I can assure anyone wanting to use them in a newer Samsung Note 2 or 3 phone or Tab 3 tablet that this card will work, and it is also excellent for HD video recording. At the price point it's an absolute bargain.

title: Pleasantly Surprised by this Router
abstract:
After my Netgear router decided to degrade to the point of uselessness I set out to replace it and researched several different routers. After looking at a number of reviews online and looking for any information I could find on mid-range wireless N routers I decided to try the MediaLink router. The number of good reviews on this router led to this decision, and so far all of these positive reviews have been justified from my perspective.

Without reading the directions and without running the setup software I had this router online and working with my network in only a few minutes. I did things a little out of order though - I allowed each of my devices to connect to the router first, then I connected the router to the cable modem after which everything worked without any issues.

Tapping into the router's configuration settings is simple, especially since instructions to do so are included. Once in the user is presented with a very simple and self-explanatory menu system that is easy to navigate. In no time at all I had my DHCP reservations set for each device (useful when connecting printers to the wireless network), I had my security key set and had my SSID set for the network.

So far, the router has been stable and fast. In addition to having good network speeds, booting up the router takes very little time - 10-15 seconds, maybe? This is far and away faster than my previous routers.

I have found only a couple of minor drawbacks with this router, neither of which are really problematic but are just things I have noticed. First, I have observed that the signal strength is a little weaker than my previous routers. The router is on the top floor of the house and the main computers I use are in the basement, with one floor in between. While the systems can see the router and connect to it with no issue, the reported signal is not as strong as other routers I have used in the past. Second, and this is a nitpick, I have a dual-boot box that has Windows 7 and Linux on it. When connecting with Windows, the router recognizes the box by its name, but when I connect with Linux it has no name at all - even when I reboot from Windows into Linux immediately.

The MediaLink wireless N router is a decent router that seems to live up to the numerous good reviews it is getting. It seems to be fast and stable and so far I have had no troubles with it at all. The price is very reasonable. If you need a decent and affordable wireless router and you're willing to try a less-familiar name, consider giving this router a try.

title: Poor camera, poor cloud
abstract:
Update: arrived 4/16, installed after charging on 4/17. Died today on 5/3. Roughly 2.5 weeks of battery life.

I really enjoy the camera overall. It was easy to install the app using the QR code in the manual. Then following the manual to register the camera and have it read the QR code to register the camera to the account.

I wanted a camera brand that had both Indoor and Outdoor cameras but needed the outdoor camera to have a battery and found that in LongPlus.

There is a slight lag in the camera but the quality is solid.
The motion detection can be adjusted which is nice as it is fairly sensitive.

The big downside is regarding the future of the online world which is their cloud service. There is only a 7 day free trial, not 30 days (and nowhere to add a code to get the 30 days that is promised in the description). Outside of that, rather than having one cloud service payment per month, you pay for each camera. The cost saved appears to be made up with their cloud services costing money if you want a full network of cameras. Very disappointed by something so simple. There is no easy customer service portal for questions in the app, only app feedback (which I submitted but there should be an easy line of communication).

There are also many misspelled words within the app itself adding to the confusion and overall trust. I rarely have one star for my reviews but this is just really a simple fix on the LongPlus side.

title: Powered from your Kindle 3, super super light
abstract:
I love reading my kindle as is, dont like the extra weight of a cover. So I ended up purchasing a LED attached light, super, but the batteries ran out real quick and I could feel the weight of the light on the kindle, not terrible, but I did not love. Finally, I splashed out on this light and it is pretty much all love: super super light that I really don't feel its extra weight, powered from the kindle, great light coverage for the kindle 3, easy to attach, and does not feel obtrusive even though it makes the left buttons defunct: i didnt notice as I can equally use the right buttons.
Although it has an on-off switch, the light will only come on if the kindle is not in sleep mode, hence if you fall asleep and the kindle goes into sleep mode, it automatically switches itself off!

I noticed that the light actually adds to the hold of the kindle: gives it more grip.

 If you like me, love to read the kindle without a cover, without the added weight, and conscious of the green impact of replacement batteries, this is the kindle light for you!

8/25 edit: just bought the RooCase super bubble case for kindle3: love it, it has enough wiggle room to fit both the kindle and attached SimpleLight together. Super price a d great color choices too.

title: Pretty Dish Towels, More Absorbent Than "Flour Sack" or Terry Towels
abstract:
These amazing cotton dish towels are actually more absorbent than classic cotton "flour sack" towels or cotton terrycloth towels! I ordered them because of the Ritz brand--Ritz makes excellent thick potholders--and Ritz came through like a champ!

The towels are what I would call "tea towel" size (17"W x 26"L after first washing), rather than "oversized", but they're actually a perfect size for drying dishes. When I washed the towels (cobalt and ming red), they proved colorfast. The colors did not bleed or run, and the color did not tint the white things I washed with them.

"Flour sack" towels have always been my favorites, but you can't dry many dishes with lightweight plain cotton towels before they get soaked through. These towels absorb much more water than plain towels before needing to be swapped out. These towels also dry thoroughly without leaving lint on the dishes. It's hard to believe that such pretty kitchen towels (almost pretty enough for guest towels) can be so effective!

Be sure to check the prices for the individual colors when you order: the sets vary in price by two or three dollars. My first order was for the least expensive, "cobalt" set in bright blue (1 solid, 1 checked plaid, 1 two-color checked, 1 blue-on-white windowpane plaid, 1 striped). Because I liked the "cobalt" set so much, I ordered a second, more expensive, "ming red" set in dark red (1 woven-textured solid, 2 fruit, 1 red-on-white windowpane plaid, 1 white-on-red windowpane plaid).

This is an example of the Ritz potholder that I love: [[ASIN:B0000CFSM0 Ritz Taupe Potholder]]. Ritz also makes classic "flour sack" dish towels: [[ASIN:B0006ACJJE Flour Sack Towel Oversized Bleached, 12/BG]], and [[ASIN:B000UE0PUQ Ritz Flour Sack Kitchen Towel, Set of 3]].

title: Pretty good for price.
abstract:
4 stars because of the price for 6 large 80" x 72" moving blankets. Being 100% polyester they have a rougher side and slick side, not like my old thick cotton ones. Will be mainly using to help secure mountain bikes when transporting in my truck bed- always use multiple layers when strapping.
I bought these knowing they are thinner but I wanted larger and orange moving blankets. Much different than basic blue. Will be great for sliding objects in a truck bed and not catch like cotton does. Packaging for me was great. All six fit well (took one out of box in photo).

Pros: large size and can be folded. Stitching will hold for medium use. Rougher side will "stick" to furniture and stay in place. Slick side can help slide in and out on truck bed or suv carpet. Got 6 blankets for a good price. Recycled material inside!

Cons: rougher feel and thinner. Not for heavy use or securing delicate items without using multiple layers. Stitching is loose in some areas but this is common for moving blankets, not a big deal. Slick on well polished/plastic/well coated surfaces. So be mindful when strapping down. Will catch fire. People say they smell (I can't smell anything) but all moving blankets have a smell.

Durability is just as described.
Thickness is fair- thinner than others but it is stated in description. They are also much larger and can be folded.
Value for Money is good!

title: Protects Tablet
abstract:
I bought this for my Nexus 7 with LTE. The tablet usually goes out with me, and sometimes replaces the need for me to bring my notebook. Therefore, with a nearly $400 device, it will make sense to try to keep it safe. This case does the job well enough. The front cover uses magnets which activates the screen when opens, and turns the screen off when closed. This does not work for the first couple of minutes as you turn on the tablet, but this is because the OS is booting.

There is one gripe, and that the tablet doesn't do well with Qi charging pads. This is a minor annoyance as of now, but I am a proponent of Qi charging as I feel more devices should have this feature. Therefore, case manufacturers should make a better effort in making sure that their case will work well with such charging pads.

[Update - 2014-06-28]
The magnets for the case is falling out. I would have thought they would have screwed or glued the magnets in. Now, every time I open the case's cover, the magnets come along with it. Since I bought this on 2014-02-08, this is less than 5 months since it is malfunctioning. Now, I can only hope that the company will honor the warranty. In the meantime, I have no choice but to reduce my rating of this from 4 to 3.

title: Purchased new- arrived already burned..?!!
abstract:
How does one order a new candle.. and when it arrives.. it's already been used?? Ok- No, it's not been used a lot but, it appears about 1" below the actual line.. and the wick is burnt!! I'm not certain how or, where this issue fell through the cracks- but, somewhere it missed Quality Control.. Guessing it was a return from another buyer.. restocked without being inspected appropriately and resold..?! See photos I included..

I've ordered this exact candle (brand, style and flavor) in the past and knowing how much I've enjoyed.. it seemed like a great choice when I found myself looking! So, being familiar with both Amazon and the candle company it seems out of character to receive this. A candle arriving in this condition is not conducive with either- Yankee candle company or, Amazon standards!! So, a disappointment or, let down for sure to receive this the way I did.

I mention this for those ordering for gift giving purposes.. sure! This may be a fluke!? Or, something that's not The end of the world for the buyer... then again- if buying a new product it should arrive new!?

Love the product, love the smell, love the quality, love the aesthetic's.. do not love it's been used before!!

abstract:

So since I was in need of a replacement, I decided it was better to have a new teapot than to holdout just because the color shown in the photo wasn't available.
Even though my current teapot was the same color as the one I received, I was still a little disappointed when I opened the box.
But I couldn't be happier with my new teapot.
Not only do I have a new teapot, & since the shape is so different, I don't have to worry about hot tea coming out of the lid as I gently rock the teapot.
This is a very good size as it allows enough room for the tea to expand and there's less leakage when rocking the teapot, & it's lightweight & very easy to handle.
I like this teapot shape so much that I plan on buying another in the near future & I hope this time the color shown is available.
I highly recommend this teapot.

title: Quieter, More Compact Than Cuisinart; But Cuisinart Has More Advantages
abstract:
I wondered whether this TRIPLE SCOOP 1.5 QUART ICE CREAM MAKER (TS-562-Red; about $59 on Amazon) would be an improvement over my much-used [[ASIN:B003KYSLMW Cuisinart 1.5 Quart Ice Cream Maker]] (about $48 on Amazon). The answer is "Yes and No", but mostly "No".

+++Yes, the Triple Scoop is quieter (a lot quieter); it takes up less storage space (freezer tub and motorized lid only; no separate motor base and big plastic cover); and it freezes the ice cream slightly harder (at least when you use the Triple Scoop ice cream mix (one vanilla, one strawberry, one chocolate packet included).

+++No, the Triple Scoop has a too-small, too-narrow spout for adding ice cream mix (the mix spills unless you're very careful or you use a funnel); the finished ice cream is difficult to remove from the paddle (most of the ice cream comes out with the paddle, too); the Triple Scoop motor element is difficult to remove from the clear plastic lid for cleaning (the motor element plus lid is also hard to grip when you're attaching it to the freezer tub); the Triple Scoop has no recipes for making ice cream from scratch with your own ingredients (the instructions say to buy the Triple Scoop ice cream mix packages).

The two machines make about the same quantity of "soft-serve" ice cream (put it in the freezer if you want more solidly frozen ice cream). Both machines use freezer tubs that must be placed in a freezer for 24 hours for best results. (Note that if your ice cream isn't freezing, you can't just run the machine longer than the recommended 20 minutes or so, because the tubs warm up during use.) The freezer tubs are hand-washable only (because they contain something liquid that freezes hard in the freezer). None of the Triple Scoop parts are dishwasher safe; some of the Cuisinart parts are dishwasher safe.

The notion that you need to purchase Triple Scoop ice cream mix to make homemade ice cream is kind of ridiculous. All you need for ice cream is 2 cups of milk, half-and-half, or heavy cream, plus some sugar and flavorings. You can use recipes from anywhere, as long as you don't overload the motor by adding two many extra ingredients like chopped fruit or nuts. I tried the included Triple Scoop Strawberry ice cream mix, and didn't care for it. It tasted like strawberries, but also faintly like artificial flavoring and preservatives (so it's not for anyone who wants to avoid the chemical additives in commercial ice cream).

Overall, I much prefer my very noisy, storage-space-hogging, Cuisinart ice cream maker (shown with a purple tub from an all-purple model).

title: Quirky and fun, but not a classic
abstract:
This isn't a hugely complex game. Each player is given a board showing the base zoon and a few coins they can spend for some special actions. The turn starts with a number of empty "trucks" sitting on the table, equal to the number of players. Each player can then.

1) spend coins to expand their zoo or move animals within their zoo
2) draw a tile from the bag. This tile then must be placed on one of the trucks. each "truck" can contain up to three tiles
3) take a truck and put the tiles that were on the truck into their zoo, [after doing this the player is out until all players have claimed trucks]

Strategy comes in because you cannot min animals in an enclosure and the basic zoo only has 3 enclusures, although putting a male and female animal of the same species in an enclosure with extra space will result in a baby animal being bred.

the game continues until there are less than 15 tiles left, at which time points are scored based on how full the zoo's enclosures are. Penalty points are taken away for having animals in the warehouse.

And that's the basic game. Not complex, but easy to describe and teach.

With good players the game goes fast, as the only real strategy is guessing when someone else might claim a "truck" you are trying to build up with the right animals for your zoo. You learn to pay attention to who is collecting which animals.

Sadly, I can't call this a classic game. It's plays a bit too much like a solitare game as the direct interactions are limited. It's not a bad party game as the simple rules will allow teenagers to play, but it can be slow, so I cannot recommend it for the 6-9 year old crowd.

This is definitely more of a gateway game. Good to get people interested in strategy and euro-games, but not necessarily the best game for long term playing. Unless you have a very patient group of friends this game will eventually seem a bit less exciting.

title: Really cheaply made!
abstract:
I use mylar bags a lot to break down large packages of dried goods into meal sizes for my family. I thought I would give these bags a try.

I divided my bagging into two separate days, not by design, but just due to time. I did rice and dried beans the first afternoon, and sugar the next afternoon. I heat-seal the end of my mylar bags for extra freshness.

On the second afternoon, I noticed some of the bags had the zip strips peeling off the mylar when I tried to ope them. Annoying for sure. I had to discard 3 bags because the zip came off. When I got out the previous day's bags, I found dried beans in the bottom of the box, from beans coming out of the bags where the zip closure had failed!! Sure glad I had not yet put them in long-term storage! But I had to repackage those beans, and the popped bags wasted an oxygen absorber as well.

I ended up having to toss a few bags, put new oxy absorbers and reseal a few. First time I have ever had that happen!

All the rest were heat sealed on the ends in addition to the zip seal. Note that my vacuum sealer (using just the seal function) did NOT want to seal these bags either. Not sure why. So I ended up getting out my iron to heat seal these bags. I can only hope those will hold up.

Overall, severely lacking quality control, and had way too many bags with the seal break. I CANNOT recommend these at all, and will certainly not be buying them again. Please choose a different brand.

title: Recessed lighting LED, set of 20
abstract: Recessed LED lights, set of 20. We have a very small kitchen and 4 recessed lights. Our old LED recessed lights, approximately 10 years old, began to fail and we purchased these as replacements. We replace all LED lights in a series (like in the kitchen) at once - even if only one is failing - as in this case. I am VERY disappointed in these. First, they are a fraction of the weight of the old ones - quality? I know things 'improve' with time- sometimes getting lighter in weight, but in this case - NO. We installed them and in the process discovered they have 4 light brightness/color settings. The lower wattage you go, the more 'yellow' the lights become. Now for the real kicker - and kiss of death - they strobe or flicker or phase in and out - whatever phrase you want to call it. When on the brightest setting, every 4 seconds - on the dimmest setting every 15 seconds. I get migraines over such flickering - so they are junk to us. I have read other reviews complaining about these since purchasing and a lot are suggesting you MUST install a 'dimmer' switch to control the flicker! That is not an option in our kitchen as we have dual light switches. But even if it was, I would return them. The old ones didn't flicker. Our house is completely LED and NONE of them flicker. So, they are being returned flat out. BEWARE. If you purchase these they are probably going to flicker - if that doesn't bother you, fine. If it does, as with most folks, do not purchase these. I cannot recommend these to anyone for any reason. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
