title: Reduce Water to Make Perfect Cream of Wheat
abstract:
This HAMILTON BEACH OATMEAL MAKER (25502, White) makes perfect Cream of Wheat (using ⅓ cup plus 1½ cups water) without burning it. The secret, I think, is that the appliance turns OFF when it's done. My [[ASIN:B0752VWV65 Hamilton Beach Rice & Cereal Cooker]], which I love, does a decent job with Cream of Wheat, but it requires stirring part way through, and always toasts the bottom layer just a little, especially when it holds the cereal on Warm.

Cream of Wheat is particularly hard to cook, because it boils over easily in the microwave or in a saucepan on the stovetop. What I wanted was a hot cereal cooker that wouldn't require stirring or supervision for Cream of Wheat. This Oatmeal Maker effortlessly cooks the cereal to the right consistency, and even allows the cooked cereal to stand for a while after cooking is done.

IMPORTANT NOTE: I found it necessary to reduce the water by half a cup or more from the "recipes" that come with the Oatmeal Maker. For perfect Cream of Wheat, I use ⅓ cup cereal and 1½ cup water.

IMPORTANT NOTE: Be sure that the handle holds both sides of the lid down when you swivel the handle to start the cooking. It's possible to close the cooker without securing the lid on both sides, and then it won't cook properly. (See the first of my three photos; the third shows the correct closing.)

The only thing that I don't like about this cooker, is that the cooking pot insert gets really hot and has a thin rolled lip that is hard to grip when you're removing the cooked cereal. However, it's only slightly harder to remove than the cook pots in my other rice cookers (Hamilton Beach and Panasonic). Be sure to use a hot pad or wear something to protect your fingers when removing the insert.

The nonstick cooking pot insert is dishwasher safe and easy to clean with handwashing. The lid is easy to take apart for cleaning and requires only occasional cleaning.

title: Reliable and expensive.
abstract: This product has honestly surprised me in durability compared to what is out there in the market. Usually, when buying from a retail store like Walmart or Target the bed tables end up lasting for about a month and they snap at the legs. I enjoy the size of the table itself, as it has enough room for a laptop and a notebook. It also has slots for a book holder and various other things. Where things started to slightly fall downhill for me was that the legs at times will collapse in on themselves if you're moving the table from time to time and that can lead to dropping all your items on the ground or whatever surface you're placing your table on. There's really no way for the slots to hold your phone up on the slots even with the case off without it falling down. The latches that level the table can sometimes get in the way of the optional pencil case which is not a big deal. The biggest fault of this product would really just be the inability to hold phones well enough and the price range. Overall it's been a pleasant experience and if it wasn't for the hefty price I would definitely consider purchasing again or recommend someone else to try it themselves.

title: Repositions and then stays stuck!
abstract: This sticky paper is a lot thinner than I expected, but I wanted it for lining cardboard boxes and storage separators so it worked out well for me. The color I chose, silver, is truly silver but not overwhelmingly shiny, in part due to texture, I'm sure. The textured surface is great, giving the illusion of heavier weight or linen paper, and it's a much better feel than the typical sticky paper I normally use that's intended to be "shelf liner." I don't think it's heavy-duty enough to truly be used for wallpaper as I can't imagine it would hold up well enough to paper a whole wall without tearing. But, I think it could work for a small sections like a backsplash. Surprisingly, overlapping or lining up edges practically disappears altogether so if you wanted to do a larger project in small increments, or try to paper a wall, it could be done without leading the eye to obvious paper edges. The sticky side is great too - it allows repositioning and still holds strong once done! That part actually impressed me because usually a sticky paper that allows repositioning just refuses to stay stuck even if you get it right on the first try. I will definitely be buying this again! Recommended.

title: Resolved: Issues with wireless performance only with keyboard
abstract:
Updated 6/5/2021
After having problems with the keyboard's wireless signal registering with the PC, I took another reviewer's suggestion and purchased a 6 foot USB extension cord, attached the wireless receiver to it, and mounted it to the top of my large screen display. This resolved the line-of-sight issues and now both the keyboard and the mouse function well.

I would have given 5 stars but...
I have purchased quite a few Logitech wireless keyboards/mouses/combos over the years and have been satisfied. With this purchase, I constantly have problems with the keyboard signals being received by the PC (never a problem with the mouse though!). The PC either does not receive the signal at all, or it takes a quite a few persistent attempts (usually by adjusting line-of-sight) for it to function. Doesn't make sense. If the mouse is completely unaffected, why would the keyboard if they are right next to each other?
Never had this problem with the other Logitech keyboard/mouse combo and it is the same model #.
Granted, I have a large 55" display between my desk and the PC, but still...
Going to try what another reviewer suggested and get a USB extension cable and attach the the receiver to it and tape it the top of the screen.
I definitely like the size and overall performance of this model, that's why I have ordered it twice.

title: Returned immediately - should have read the reviews first
abstract:
I have gotten in the habit of checking the low-star reviews of items and because Amazon makes this product for use with their own Kindle DX device, I (lazily) did not bother. I foolishly assumed it would work just fine. So...while I was waiting for my order to be delivered, curiosity got the best of me, and I checked out the 1 & 2-star reviews. *Whoops.* Turns out that this cover, which hooks directly into the Kindle DX on the left side with little metal hooks, puts a lot of strain on the front plastic shell of the Kindle DX, especially if you mistakenly open it up from the wrong side, which I am sure everyone does from time to time. Lots of users have reported the stress caused by the way this cover connects to the Kindle DX actually causing the Kindle DX shell to crack. No thank you. Not even willing to risk it. Returned, unopened. Bought another case.

(*Note/alternative suggestion: if you are lucky you might still be able to get one of the few remaining Otterbox Commuter cases for it here on Amazon. Otterbox no longer makes them, but if you hunt, you can find them around in small quantities. I got one for $12 + $5 shipping.)

title: Returned it - no sound & box was hot to the touch
abstract:
Ok... I KNOW better than to purchase any electronic gizmo with less than a four star overall rating. I took a chance this time - I was looking for a cheap way to stream video on my television via the computer without having to buy a Roku etc. This converter thing SHOULD have worked fine. I guess, technically it works, but not the way I needed it to and honestly, it's just a HUGE hassle to use on a regular basis.

Pros..... it's small. It does send the video to the television (you do have to tell your computer to send the data to another monitor). It was inexpensive.

Cons.... Our 3 year old tv has all the connections for stuff - USB, S-cable, that 3 prong thing, 3 HDMI outlets and it connects easily & streams Netflix via the Wii game box. It works with the DVD player and I've played DVDs through the laptop in the past with the USB connection, so I KNOW they all work. The ONLY way it would work with this converter box was to use the S-cable and the yellow prong cable AND the USB all at the same time. The picture qualtiy was fine. I tried for 20 minutes to get the sound to transfer through to the television - never happened. Which meant I had to leave the laptop speakers on in order to listen to dialog. Not conducive to sitting several feet away from the screen. Meanwhile there was a huge tangle of all these cables on the tv stand, the laptop, low sound and no ability to pause etc without getting up and going to the computer to do it manually. By the end of a single episode of Frasier (23 minutes) the little converter box was very hot to the touch and the wood underneath it was hot as well. I imagine if you watched a full length movie you might end up scortching the finish on the tv stand or table!

End result.... I'm returning this converter first thing in the morning. I'll just cough up the money and buy the ROKU I guess.

title: Ridiculously easy and fun to play!
abstract: This little game was a surprisingly huge hit in our family! The box itself is constructed extremely well. It sits flat on the table with no tipping or rocking at all. The logos, and numbers are all printed or applied well and look sharp and legible on the end product. The lid fits perfectly! The only issue we have discovered in our month of nightly use, is that all US coins (pennies, dimes and quarters) fit into and stand upright in the slots.. all except for nickles. They are simple too thick to fit. We learned this after our 3 yr old granddaughter tried to force a nickle into the #4 slot, gouging the surrounding wood in the process. This is not a big deal as my husband was able to re-router the slots to be ever so slightly wider so now all coins will fit into all slots with ease. Overall, this is a great game. Easy for all ages to play. Heck, it's a great game to have the littles play with you as they'll learn their numbers so they can place their coins. My husband and I keep this on our main table and play it at least once per evening. It's such a simply game that you can play it while having a conversation. It really takes no thought at all. We took it camping and played it when we were forced inside during a storm. Thinking of getting one to keep in the camper so we never forget it! Even grandma asked me to order one for her house so she can play with her friends! Highly recommended!

title: Rock solid with some advanced features
abstract:
I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.
Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios.
Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points.

This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees.

Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.

title: Roomba i4+
abstract: Roomba i4+ purchased off the Treasure truck listing. So far, a little disappointing. First off, to get it so sync up with the app - ALMOST impossible. Was just about to pack it up to return it and all of a sudden it linked. Not a great start. It did link up with Alexa quickly. A couple other notes, you can only "map" ONLY ONE room. Holy cow. Really? That's disappointing. You can name all kinds of rooms, but you only save ONE room. Also, when it returned to the home base it dumped a bunch of crap that it had gathered up at the bottom of the ramp it sits on. It seems to do a fairly good job picking stuff up. It also did really well getting under things without getting stuck, over minor cords and thinner carpets. You do need to pick up shoes, etc. You do need to clear the side brush of human hair. The self emptying part seems to work fairly well, unless that is the reason it dumped stuff at the base.. (?) Then there is the part that you have to look up a use manual. Nothing comes with it. Not even how to empty the base! We use Youtube. Overall, the price was good. But you'll need a lot of patience and ability (understanding) about how to get the manual or instruction on how to use. I am on the fence. Not sure I can recommend it just yet. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different.  I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers.

title: Round is small for men but otherwise a nice seat
abstract:
When I first sat on this I thought, Oh No. It's not made for a man's business as the hole is too small on a round toilet. Easily could have come in 1/4 - 1/2 inch in diameter. and opened it up substantially. I had 1.5 inches from the inside ring to the toilet edge.

So I have adjusted (literally every time I sit down) and gotten used to it. However, I have a toilet that now leaks and am replacing it with a tall elongated toilet. Ordered this again, hoping it would fit better. "I'll check the package before installing it and send it back if it's too small an opening again.

I do like the slow close feature. The other bathroom doesn't have one and I tip it and the lids crash down.

The thing I like most, and probably why I'm giving Kohler another chance, is the easy slide out for cleaning. Pop the back caps up and pull, that's it. Slides in just as easily. You have to see it to understand why it will last, well-built system.

One last note: Don't forget to install the rubber bumpers to keep the seat from sliding. After 12 months or so they will wear down and you will need to replace them. You can find them on Amazon but they come in a 4 pack, 2 white and 2 black for about $5+. I suppose all the toilets with rubber guards are the same that way.

title: Rub on mail box numbers
abstract: We just purchased a brand new mail box and I liked how these numbers looked, so I thought I'd try them. I've used rub on numbers before and knew it was going to be a bit of a challenge. I followed their step-by-step 6 step instructions - including wiping the area with rubbing alcohol first - even though the surface was 100% smooth, they just didn't want to some off - so I did have to encourage them a bit using the card I used to "burnish" - eventually they gave. However, the 5 tore - you get 4 of each number so you can redo if you don't reuse too many in your actual address. I would be sure NOT to be in a hurry to apply these numbers. We just set the box outside tonight and while we are not quite at freezing temps - we are at about 37 - 40 degrees - so fingers crossed they will stick. Instructions say not to put outside at freezing or below for more than 48 hours after application. Our new box is a granite gray - a bit darker than I was expecting, however, I think the black numbers show up nicely - please see pic. And just fyi... they are not reflective. Time will tell if they are going to stick - and I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. I hope this review and pics was helpful to you!

title: Rubbermaid Antimicrobial Sink Dish Drainer
abstract: I purchased this to replace a set that was nearly identical set... my old set wore out. It is the perfect size for my tiny kitchen sink area. It comes with a utensil holder, a suction cupped sponge holder and a brush. It is black as shown in the photos. While this set "looked" like my old set, it didn't function the same way. In order to properly drain the water from the bottom tray, you need the bottom tray to be lifted a bit (the old one did too), so I have a non-skid block my husband made to provide a slight lift for drainage. It's only about 1 1/2 inches. So why 3 stars? The problem with the new set is that with the drain lift, the rack slides off the bottom tray!! Why? Well.. the new tray has an almost teflon feel to it! Obviously it's not actually coated but it looks and feels like it. It is hard, molded plastic, like the old one and the "feet" of the basket are exactly the same as the old set... Is the sliding problem part of the "antimicrobial" benefit? I'd rather just properly clean!! Anyway - I had to come up with a solution that would allow me to still clean it. I included a picture so you see my "fix" and also the surface of the bottom tray for yourself. I used a couple of small floor chair glide tabs to provide a "stop" for the basket without effecting the drainage. Disappointing that the "feet" are more grippy or the tray wasn't so slippery. Disappointing, but not worth returning. It arrived quickly, well packed and in good condition (I have prime). I always update my reviews if new info would be helpful.

title: Rugged and Easy to Install
abstract:
We selected two of these lights to replace outdoor fixtures next to our garage. We needed something durable and able to withstand a little abuse, as these are replacing fixtures that have been destroyed by repeated impact damage in a play area (translation: basketball). After quite a bit of searching we chose these lights and they have proven to be exactly what we needed.

Installation was quick and easy and took me less than an hour to install two of them. Most of the delays were in removing the old lamps and getting the mounting bracket and wiring box cleaned of debris. Though there is some documentation in the box, no instructions are really needed to get these installed. I got these right the first time without issue.

I installed 40W bulbs in each and they worked exactly as expected. Even though these are rated to handle 150W bulbs, a pair of these lamps running 40W each throws out an enormous amount of light, sufficient to not only see the area at night but to work well as security lighting.

Within the first hour of these being installed they were subjected to impact strikes. They held up beautifully and seem to have been completely unharmed. This is exactly what we needed in this area.

We're very happy with these lights and are glad we have them installed. They look nice (if a little industrial) and they can handle some abuse.

title: SFW123GDC Seems sturdy
abstract:
I am sure the safe is a good one...but right now I am just trying to get a hold of Sentry Safe's customer service which is proving to be more of a task then moving the 97 lb safe for a 70+ yr old woman. The box wasn't opened until Mother's Day. When it was it seems someone else must have purchased it previously as the safe arrived LOCKED and no instruction booklet so I finally found the phone number by downloading the instructions from the Amazon website. I tried to contact Amazon but with the covid 19 problems they were unavailable for chat or for me to call them. I have called Sentry Safe only to have the call cut off, have a brief message leading someone to believe someone would be on the line after the message, but again cut off or like today, Memorial Day where there was an actual message stating they were closed for Memorial Day. I will try again tomorrow and maybe I will have my impression of Sentry Safe's customer service changed. If so, I will change my review.
 UPDATE: I finally have the problem resolved. I finally got a hold of customer service after 7 days of trying, I was on hold for 34 minutes but was able to talk with someone who was able to walk me through opening the safe. It was't a returned item (at least I don't think so from the explanation CS gave me) I guess they ship them locked and you have to call them to get the access code. After answering a great number of questions about myself to verify who I was I was emailed the code. I was able to access the safe within seconds after that. I just feel that somehow they should tell the buyer that that is what we need to do. I had the 97 lb safe all repackaged and was going to ship it back. I'm no spring chicken but I do have thieving neighbors and am at my wits end. To even have to unpack the safe was added stress when it was bought to try and relieve some of the stress. I would have given this 5 stars had I known I would need to contact THEM for the code. It would have saved me a lot of anxiety.

title: SO Easy To Install-Looks FANTASTIC!
abstract:
The towel bar in our master bathroom, that looks as though it is from the 1970's (it was here when we moved in 10+ years ago!) FINALLY broke! (I celebrated...this bar was U -G-L-Y!!!) I immediately logged into Amazon to find a new towel bar. As soon as I saw this Moen Yorkshire 24", my search was over. It not only was the nicest towel bar I'd looked at, it was the most inexpensive as well. (not including self-adhesive bars ) Best of all, it was a MOEN! We had Moen products in our other home and recently replaced the toilet paper holder (in current home) with a Moen. I immediately placed my order. It arrived as promised, 2 days later. It took my husband a whopping 10 MINUTES to install it. Included was the entire towel bar (and the round parts at either end...apologies, not sure what to call them), the template and hardware. While we did get out the tape measure to use, we didn't need it thanks to the template included on the instruction booklet. (my husband was especially impressed and appreciative of this) The instructions were simple to follow and within 10 minutes, the new towel bar was installed. And its in the wall nice and secure! It does not wobble or shake even a little bit. I VERY much love the chrome finish. It looks awesome with the grey metallic towel bar! Its really pretty neat and impressive how something as simple as a new towel bar breathes some new life into our bathroom decor! Next up...a MOEN robe hook (already purchased!) to match the MOEN toilet paper holder/towel bar!

I simply cannot recommend this MOEN towel bar enough. Its wonderful...absolutely everything about it is WONDERFUL!! The appearance, the price, the easy installation. AND...it comes with a limited LIFETIME warranty!
 (apologies for my not so great photos..my cell camera doesn't work so great!)

title: Salt lamp bowl
abstract:
I purchased two of these for my tiny AZ home... one for the master bedroom and one for the living/dining area. I have never purchased a salt lamp before and I cannot speak to the list of possible benefits, but I am hopeful for positive results. However, having said that, the lamp is lovely. The dimmer switch is very nice. You can control the brightest easily using the dimmer switch which clearly changes the mood. The salt chunks are large and each chunk is unique in color and size and shape as you can imagine. The bowl holder is a clear acrylic type material... about 8" in diameter - just eye balling it... and about 6" tall. It came very carefully and beautifully packaged. Once you put the salt in the bowl I can image that you don't want to move them around a lot as it could scratch the bowl. I did carefully move a few pieces to places I felt were better. I have had the lamps plugged in for about 8 hours... no odors. Just a really beautiful glow. The dimmer switch is hard. You just tap it to turn it on or off and gently press to dim or brighten. There is a very nice booklet with instructions on how to change the bulb (a spare is provided) Cleaning instructions say: regularly dust salt crystals with a dry, clean cloth. Do not wash or clean with water or detergents, If not in use for a long period of time, store the lamp in a cool, dry environment, covering the crystals with a plastic bag. The lamp may naturally moisten in humid environments - saying further that if you use in a humid environment leave the lamp on for several hours to naturally dry out (I'm thinking like in a bathroom?) They also note not to place to close to electronics as the salt may draw moisture. It says if the salt crystals become moist - gently pat down with a clean dry cloth - also noting not to clean the bowl with any organic or other solvents or it may become damaged.
I would say if you're looking to purchase one of these as a gift, they are beautifully packaged and look very high end. The price is definitely higher than some of the options but not the highest. I personally chose the bowl style of salt crystal because salt may draw moisture and I wanted it contained instead of dripping off a free standing rock without containment. I do really love the soft glow. That alone is worth the purchase to me. I do really hope the claimed health benefits will be a bonus.
I never hesitate to update my reviews if new info should seem useful. I also try to answer all questions to best of my ability. Hope this helps you in your decision.
UPDATE: 2/10/2017.... I have been using both lamps 24/7 for some weeks now. Both are still working perfectly. I still believe these salt lamps are a really good buy. I've looked at so many in person that were so much more money and so much less lamp. I think one of the best parts is the dimming light. You can really adjust to comfort, for instance, in the bedroom. Still feel these lamps are really 5 star items.

title: Same protection in a different form factor
abstract:
In 2011 I purchased a [[ASIN:B000WJB1AW Tripp Lite TLM825SA Safety Surge Protector 120V 8 Outlet Metal 25ft Cord OSHA]], which is still going strong. A few months age I purchased another and recently purchased a pair of these. That alone should tell you how satisfied I am with the brand.

This is a heavy duty protector, both physically and electrically. I live in Central Florida, which is notorious for power problems, so not using well designed protection is inviting disaster, which can be very costly considering my investment in the gear this is protecting. The main reason why I own so many is I am a musician who owns amps, a PA and keyboard and the power in many venues is marginal at best. This is inexpensive protection and I have witnessed other musicians' gear getting fried in the same venues in which I play, so I know these surge suppressors work.

My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly. I do want to note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. If the devices that you want to plug this into exceed the rated specs on this product page this is not the outlet for you.

title: Should've checked the size before I bought this.
abstract: It is just as pictured but it's really big I was hoping to find a smaller sized one and I didn't notice or cared to check I just assumed it was small to medium-ish sized, that is a mistake on my part but I honestly think it is very big and not very practical for my kitchen I was not expecting to get this size so now I don't have a place to store it also I don't like how heavy it is, makes it very difficult to move around and in my opinion difficult since it does heat up I'm not sure I'd like to get burnt with this... hopefully it will never fall on my feet. No I would not buy this again, check the sizing before buying, I still have to use it though so I will update after I use it and see how it works I don't think it's completely fair to say this before I use it as well but now I am even scared to use it too, cause at the same time I'd say it's a potential hazard with the handle and all and that size imagine it just slipping out of your hands while you pour it.

title: Simple is good.
abstract:
I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.

title: Simple, Excellent Corn Stripper (Better Than OXO, RSVP Corn Strippers)
abstract:
This ZYLISS CORN STRIPPER strips the kernels from an entire ear of corn with just 4 or 5 quick downward strokes. It takes up very little space in your kitchen gadget drawer, and it doesn't require any complicated setup for stripping an ear of corn or for emptying out the stripped kernels. You just hold your cooked ear of corn upright on a cutting surface (board, plate, or bowl), and run the slicer down the sides of the ear of corn. The kernels fall onto the food prep surface and are easily collected for immediate use, for reheating, or for adding to a recipe later.

The serrated stainless steel blade is very sharp, so it takes little pressure to strip the kernels. (You may want to save the plastic blade guard that comes with the slicer, to use for storing it away safely in your kitchen drawer.) The handle is comfortable to grip, and gives you good control so that you don't miss any kernels (not even at the narrow end of the ear of corn). This is a well-made, reasonably sturdy slicer, and it's dishwasher safe.

A less efficient, much larger, corn stripper is the [[ASIN:B007KRE9JO RSVP Shuck Deluxe Corn Stripper]], which strips a whole ear of corn with one pass and collects all of the kernels in an easy-to-empty plastic tube. Another less efficient corn stripper is the [[ASIN:B000V78JGO OXO Good Grips Corn Stripper]], which has to be emptied several times for each ear of corn, and is a bit awkward to take apart and reassemble each time.

title: Size wise this is perfect and fits great in the 12x8x8" critter carrier even...
abstract:
I only just bought the item but I did put it to use in a variety of situations. I'll be using this for a baby crested gecko once I get him/her in September from a friend/breeder. Size wise this is perfect and fits great in the 12x8x8" critter carrier even with a good amount of wood and fake leaves in there. I love the magnet portions because I've actually got this on the inside of the terrarium and I'm using a strong earth magnet on the outside which works great to save on space and placing it on the wall.
I tested this next to the house thermostat and it read as 71.6 while the house was set at 72 degrees so it's basically spot on... I had it in my room on one side and the temperature was reading around 68.6 and fluctuating around 69.3 degrees since it's next to a window and closer to the AC vent. So for the sake of the Gecko, I move this to the other side of my room and put a towel under the terrarium and eventually the Thermopro read at a steady 72 degrees which some slight fluctuation and 56% humidity - which is perfect for my little buddy who will arrive in a couple months. It runs off of a single AAA battery (I can't speak for battery life) but the size of this product is awesome to keep inside a critter terrarium and the magnetic backing provides good placement options.

title: Small fountain; looks better in pictures; water sound is too low on highest setting
abstract:
I wanted a fountain that was small and pretty. This looks better online than in person. It actually looks plasticky and not as nice as in pictures. It is small but only mildly attractive.

It is packaged very well. However, I thought it was broken at first because I could hear stuff banging around inside the fountain but those were pieces of plaster on the inside that fell off inside which apparently has no impact on the operation of the fountain. Nevertheless, the fountain is working fine.

What I don't like is that I can barely hear the water The pump is just too small. I adjusted the dial on the pump and the sound and flow was exactly the same whether it was on the + or - flow level.

There is a back panel that slips into place to cover the open hole in back. It has a cutout for the cord. This is a nice touch but the piece does slide out very easily. For example, if the cord moves, the piece moves.

It takes about three gallons of water and is small enough where it can even be carried with water in it.

In summary, I like this fountain but I am not in love with it. I am still glad I purchased it because I wanted something small and without a light.

NOTE - I have pictures and video of this fountain but Amazon is no longer allowing any photos to be posted to any review as of this writing. Also note that this fountain is discontinued and is not being sold anymore.

title: Smells like cinnamon & seems to work - no snakes & the feed room *** Update 2015 ***
abstract:
After finding a small snake lurking at the doorway of the feed room in my barn the other morning, I figured that was the ideal location for testing this Snake-B-Gone repellent. The directions are pretty clear - shake the granules out along a perimeter where you want no snakes and they won't cross. There is a strong smell of cinnamon and that's it, so that's nice. No chemical or poison odor and nothing sticky or wet to deal with. I used this in the hay storage area as well - snakes do tend to like to sleep there in the summer evenings. A week later and I haven't seen any more snakes in my barn areas, so I am going to say it works.

Update - April 2015

I have been buying a using this a couple of times a year at the barn and our house and we have no snakes in our populated areas as a result. The cinnamon smell diminishes pretty quickly, but the snakes stay away. I saw one recently about twenty foot away from our fence line where this Snake B Gone line is and it was moving in the opposite direction. Good enough for me!

title: Smells like gasoline! Going back!
abstract: First & most offensive: they reek of gasoline so if you are sensitive/allergic to petroleum products like I am you will want to pass on these. Second: the phone adapter is useless as-is. Mine was not drilled far enough to be able to tighten it into place for my iPhone 12 max. It just slipped & slid all over. Stupid me putting the adapter together first without picking up the binoculars to smell them bc I wasted 15 minutes trying to figure out how to put the adapter together bc it does not come with instructions! I had to come back here to the website which was a total pain. Third: the tripod is also useless. I would not trust the iOS to hold my $1600 phone nor even a Mattel Barbie for that matter. It's just inefficient for the job imo. Third: in order to try to give an honest review I did don gloves & eyewear to check the binoculars out. They seemed average except for mine seemed to be missing about 10% of the film costing in the lower edge of one of the lenses which would have ruined every video & photograph unplanned to take so for me these are a very huge hard pass. I expect the accessories that come with the main product to be as good or better than the product I'm buying. Otherwise I would just buy the product as a stand alone. Sadly, I found a decent pair of binoculars last year with a much better quality phone adapter & tripod, but they had a defect too. Guess I'm going to have to pay more. Ugh.

title: Smooth writing, but lots of issues - Read updates re price & quality.
abstract:
I borrowed one of these from a Staples employee when I went there yesterday and immediately noticed how smoothly this pen writes. Totally even flow, effortless glide on the paper. Feels like a top of the line fountain pen. I bought a combo pack at Staples and also two 2-packs of the green colored ones here on Amazon. I totally love this pen!

Note: July 21, 2012. Since the first part of my review in April of this year (i.e.: a mere 3.5 months ago) the price on these pens has increased by over 60%!!!! I bought mine for $4.18 per pack of two pens back then. Typical human reaction: product gets a few good reviews and the greed kicks in. Well, I came back to buy more, but will not be doing so until the price comes down again. Way down from $6.70.

Note: July 25, 2012. WHOA!!! Seems like somebody fell asleep at the wheel while updating this item's price... 4 days since my last update and the price has skyrocketed to a ridiculous 258%+ of what I paid for these pens in April. And I thought the $ 6.70 was an excessive price hike. I will adjust my rating when the price comes down to a reasonable level. Right now, so not worth it. These pens are not gold plated, nor do they spew magic ink. Absolutely ridiculous pricing at $14.99

My original rating was 5 stars at $4.18 for the set. Not anymore...

Update Oct. 22, 2012: I see the price is coming down some now. But it's still way higher than the $4.18 I originally paid for these. I will check back again to see if reason has caught up with these merchants.

Update: 4/25/2013: I originally gave these pens a very enthusiastic 5 stars. But now, sadly, I have had to amend my review, and not only because of the inflated pricing either. I bought a bunch of these in all the different colors last year and the writing action really is the smoothest ever. However, the body of the pen is unmitigated crap. I have been using these for about a year now and the thread is not holding up against the pressure of the pen when it is in writing mode. The bodies are now falling apart on me, one after another. When I try to screw them back together, they just fall apart again. I find myself saving the insert to use later in whichever of the casings happens to withstand the test of time. However, this means I will have to also be sure to somehow let myself know what color the ink is in the altered pens. I can slide the color-coded silicone sleeve off of the faulty pen and install it on the other, but that will not look so cool, since the top of the pens are also color-coded and so won't end up matching unless I am "lucky" enough to get a working casing that matches the color of the insert. Huge disappointment that this product's body is of such inferior workmanship. I do so love how the pen writes...

title: So Far, So Good!
abstract:
I've had this for a few weeks and have used it numerous times to navigate around Brevard County Florida. So far the maps (which I updated right after getting the GPS) have been spot on except for one time when I was in a wildlife conservation area (that neither Google or Bing maps has either) which wasn't mapped but it's dirt dikes in a swamp and not part of city, county or state roads. Amusingly the Garmin map did show the lakes I was driving around just not the dirt roads.

I've downloaded and tried several of the voices offered for the Garmin nüvi 50LM though the only ones I've used have been the TTS voices (those that actually speak the street names). After several trials I've found, oddly enough, that the voice 'British English - Serena' is the clearest and easiest to understand.

The 5" screen is great. The display is crisp and clear and can easily be read from a distance. The touch screen is quite responsive. I don't feel like I have to pound on the screen to make selections. I have mine mounted in an [[ASIN:B0015A6YN6 Arkon GN047 Removable Air Vent Mount]] in the passenger side center console air vent to keep it off the windshield and out of the Florida sun. {See uploaded photo.}

While this is a basic GPS unit the nüvi 50LM does what a GPS unit is designed to, get you from Point-A to Point-B (options for this are Faster Time, Shorter Distance or Off Road (straight line navigation)) without any extra, distracting, bells and whistles it still has some nice options:

* Lifetime free map updates.
* Maps can be displayed in 2D or 3D.
* You can change the level of map display information shown.
* You can turn on or off Map Data Layout information which adds driving direction, time of day, elevation and speed to the main map display.
* The icon for your vehicle can be changed. Garmin themselves offer numerous icons to download and there are also places on the internet to download custom vehicle icons.
* Automatic switching between day and night display settings.
* Lane Assist & Junction View helps you (in some areas) get in the correct lane ahead of time.
* Millions of Points of Interest plus the ability to add your own favorite destinations.

So far I really like my Garmin nüvi 50LM and enjoy using it. It's made getting out and about a lot easier than paper maps ever did.

I'll update this review, if necessary, if any durability issues arise over time. For now, this is one of my favorite pieces of technology.

title: So far so great
abstract:
We picked up this camera because we were getting a new puppy and needed to keep an eye on him during the day.

The clarity is pretty solid overall given the cost and can be seen in the photo above (which includes our little pup).

The camera can take snapshots which I am not able to save to my phone (or haven't quite figured out how to save to my iPhone but they do save in the app).

I don't really need this for motion detection but have tested that feature out as a just in case measure if we used in the future. The sensitivity can be adjusted but overall a very nice feature.

The camera does have a micro sd slot that would allow storage of footage (like movements) but we use the live footage as our means of checking the feed.

The connection to the device was fairly smooth but we did have to refresh our router when completing the process. It could've been a bandwidth issue given we have more Smart items than ever.

The app is fairly user friendly and my wife and I can both view the live feed at the same time. The feed itself is about.5 -1 second slow which we haven't found as a problem.

The audio in/out is also quite clear which was fantastic. We try not to talk to our pup too much but it definitely was a nice feature for the first 2-3 days of him being in the crate (and being able to hear him as well as talk to him if he got frustrated).

Highly recommend this one!

title: So far, I love the Wowgo cordless vacuum.
abstract:
I have a very good canister vacuum for "cleaning day" and just wanted something easier/lighter to take around the apartment for quicker/easier vacuuming without dragging the canister and wire around. I checked out reviews of quite a few stick vacuums before this purchase. I couldn't believe how expensive some of them are. I mentioned to my sister that I was looking for a stick vacuum and she told me she just got one on Amazon, had only used it a couple of times and couldn't say much about it other than it was quiet, good suction, light weight and only $99. She got it because several ladies in her apt. building had one and were happy with it.

I decided to take a chance and ordered one for myself. It came in a day, in good shape. It was easy enough to put together. It's lightweight, pretty quiet and easy to empty. The head swivels and gets into corners. I don't think it would last long with an aggressive house cleaner. The swivel head might not be strong enough to be slammed into walls or corners. I haven't yet used the other tools it came with, yet. The suction is very good and I used it mostly on the low setting, but I don't have pets or children and my floors are laminate or have low pile carpeting so I can't say how it would be on thick carpets, etc. The high power just shortens the battery life. I was happy that the suction was strong enough to pick up crumbs, etc. and didn't just fling bits out the other side. The battery lasted about 30-40 minutes, enough to do my whole apartment with good suction. It takes about 4 hrs to charge the battery, so I wanted to purchase an extra battery to have charged and on hand. It's $33...a third of the vacuum cost...Wow!

I haven't used it enough to comment on the quality (how long it lasts, parts break, or suction weakens) but so far, I'm very happy with the vacuum. It serves its purpose well. If need be, down the line, I'll add to or change this review.

title: So much better than those single-button openers
abstract:
My entire garage door opener was recently replaced but the installer only put a single-button to press on the wall by my back door.

I wanted something with more features, however, so purchased this one off Amazon.

It was quick and easy to install, and I was super happy it was compatible.

It also has a nice large backlit "button" to push that is easy to identify by touch without looking at it. I typically just reach over as I'm walking in or out the door. The raised area helps hit the button in that center spot, which probably helps get a good press.

There's another smaller button (also easy to identify by touch) to turn off the opener ceiling light when coming back in the house. (I like to save on electricity, even though it usually turns itself off in about ten minutes.)

There is also a slider switch that will lock the opener for some extra security.

This console has every feature I was looking for and looks sturdy enough to last several years.

I just wish the large button was not backlit red. Feels a bit "alarming," I guess. A cooler blue or green would have made me happier. I, of course, knew it was going to be red and I'm getting used to it. No big deal.

I'm very happy with my new wall console and would definitely purchase again. Highly recommend and I feel it is certainly a good value.

title: Soft pencils, blend easily, reasonable price
abstract:
I have been happily using Crayola pencils for 'adult' coloring books. I really do enjoy adult coloring as a hobby and wanted to learn a bit more technique. Decided to give this set a try since it was a very good price on Amazon with good reviews. So happy I did! Watched a couple of Youtube videos to learn how to blend with colored pencils, which I was able to easily apply using this set because they are 'softer' than Crayola pencils and blend easily. I found I can use a very light swirling touch using a sharp point to apply color in layers. The colors are really rich and you can make them as vibrant as you want with layering or pressure, which ever you prefer. I also like the range of shades across colors in this set.

For me, the two things I did notice as compared to the Crayola set, are:
1. It's not as easy to sharpen these with my manual pencil sharpener as the Crayola set - I might purchase an electric sharpener.
2. The colors painted on the ends of the pencils are muted and dont really represent the actual color - I select by 'tip' color

If you are looking for a softer colored pencil, that blends easily at a reasonable price, I would recommend giving this set a try.

title: Solid Performer For 35 mm Slides
abstract:
Okay, up front disclaimer. You are NOT going to get the same quality as a professional scanning service. YOu also fo not get the automatic slide feed everyone wants.

Out of the package, the unit worked well. I selected the correct holder for my slides, inserted my SD card (not included with unit!), set the film type (35 mm slide) and resolution, and started. While there is no autofeed, it is pretty easy to push the slides through manually. Positioning is helped by the LCD monitor, but I found it is not perfect. Expect some cut-off and some rounded corners with mounted slides.

I tried adjusting the brightness because many of my old slides were a bit overexposed. I found little benefit, so I went with the defaults and made adjustments in Photoshop instead. For reasonably well exposed slides, the defaults work well.

Picture quality was up and down. When I looked at some of the slides that appeared fuzzy or granular when I went to 100%m the originals appeared okay at 5X. On the other hand, I had several that were very sharp and well focused. I am still trying to decide if it is the Scanza or the slides.

Color saturation was a bit variable. Older, overexposed slides seemed to be lacking color and contrast even in good areas. Well-exposed slides were saturated with no obvious problems.

If you are interested in converting your slides to snapshots for on-screen slideshows and sharing, the Scanza is a good option. You can go through a few hundred slides in a day and get good results pretty easily. If you have many more, you should be considering a professional scanner. If you only have a few, I would try your scanner, if it has a suitable capability.

While branded Kodak, it is a Chinese product. It is meant for worldwide sales, so you can find instructions in virtually every major language.

title: Solid car, durable, mostly as advertised
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:aa2775d9378faee66bb1b179a1e96566]] This car was for my son's birthday so the pressure was on as the reviews were mostly positive.

He loved it when he opened it, "that's cool!" was the exact response.
-There was no assembly necessary.
-One battery pack was in the car and needed to be connected and the spare battery was in a separate box.
-The controller did require batteries (not included).
-There was a usb charging cable for the car battery packs, but there is no wall plug (so a wall plug or usb connectable device is needed).

The battery was fully charged in the car so we got to test it right away. Good thing is that we crashed several times but no cosmetic damages (fish tank stand, kitchen table, wall (twice), coffee table, my legs (yes, both).

The car was pretty fast but not as fast as I anticipated. That is probably a good thing for my 8 year old as the crashes like meant speed was about right for his first time using this car. His birthday was a few days ago and he's played with it for several minutes each day since then with no need to charge that battery (or use the secondary battery thus far).

The battery does say it will need 3 hours to charge though so BE READY to get that second battery on the charger right when you get this car.

Overall, very satisfied. It is a 4/5 for us and would get a 5/5 if the controller came with batteries and USB charger had a wall plug.

title: Sort of worth it
abstract:
*Update* after trying to use these for a few days, I'm disappointed. They are great except that they won't stay in my ears. There's nothing to hold them in place. They are okay for emergency use, but only if I'm using just the right one and I'm laying on my left side so it stays in.

I've got several versions of Samsung wireless earbuds. I get a new set about every other year. The case on these is about the size of two samsung charging cases put together. It's just massive. But it charged quickly and the wireless charging works just fine. I called my mother to test the call quality since she is the most discerning about my earbud call quality and she was impressed at the quality for the cost. My galaxy buds were a refurbished buy from Best Buy and she could never understand me when I used them (no one else really had a problem hearing me with them). The galaxy buds live has good sound and call quality, but very poor battery life and comfort in use. They always popped out of my ears if I smiled or laughed and they pushed against that little flap and caused pain.
So far, these little things are doing pretty good. I have weird shaped ear canals so the left one didn't hold in very well (but it almost never does with any of these) but, the right one is holding in good. I'm not thrilled with the shape because it's hard to know where to line it up, but for the money, I'm sold.

title: Sound will bypass your headphones and go to speaker. But awesome video footage! Lol
abstract:
This item exceeded our expectations. We were needing to be able to view our new puppy while we were away to see how he adjusts to us not being around. The problem is, we are at home with him ALOT, therefore we were concerned he would develope anxiety while we were away or hurt himself. This item allowed for us to keep an eye on him and monitor how long it takes for our little guy to stop crying while also helping put us at ease... Eventually we plan to get more to monitor the whole house and let our monster roam freely.

This camera has great coverage but excellent when mounted on a wall. Additionally, the night mode is impressive. Everything was still crystal clear and being able to adjust the sensitivity of the motion tracker /recorder was super helpful... otherwise we would have a lot of alerts for glare from other cars driving by.

My only complaint would be the sound... when i monitor my pup at work I have to turn off the sound because the app will bypass my headphones or blue tooth and go straight to speaker on my phone. First time this happened everyone in the office got to hear my puppies amplified screeches.. i was asked if someone was skinning him alive... i've emailed tech about the problem and went through the settings but no solution or response yet. We still love this item regardless of the one issue.

title: Sprout paper towel holders
abstract: Bought these to dispense paper towels with ease at our annual seafood boil... we've tried several different methods.. one thing we know is that you need to be able to dispense the paper towels with one hand. These work well with one hand... we use the warehouse brand paper towels that "double cut" so you can chose a short piece or a long piece - these holders held up well to one-handed tugs and pulls. These also happen to look a little like "art" on the counter when they are not working too. So that is cool. I went with the turquoise... it is a brighter, clearer turquoise - meaning it's not dirty blue. Really pretty in my opinion. They show one picture holding what looks like TP and think you could totally put one of these on the back of your toilet or counter or next the the toilet and use it as a TP holder too. The base is weighted - just the right amount. You will need to put them together and it takes a bit of strength to push the stem into the base - just FYI... My daughter helped me do it. Long story short I love them. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: Stains everywhere. Beware!
abstract:
I purchased 3 of these cartridges last July. I use my printer but not all that much because these toner cartridges are truly crappy and just scatter and bleed ink everywhere on the paper. So, I only finally went through the first cartridge last week. Since I have two printers, I do have some choices, fortunately. I was really hoping to use this one more, but I can really only use this printer for printing out personal stuff. Like ebooks that I don't want to read off my screen, but prefer to print out to read in the living room or dining room or elsewhere. As far as that kind of printing goes, it's mostly legible. Just waaay not clean enough to use formally or professionally.

I waited until I was on my second cartridge before writing this review. I figured, maybe the first cartridge was just a lemon - that can happen... I did not try to exchange it at the time because I bought these before my original cartridge ran out, just to have backup ready. By the time that happened and I realized that the new cartridge was crap, it was really too late to raise the issue. I bought it from Blake Printing Supply at the time but, since I never tried to return them or even complain, I can't speak to their service or responsiveness in this situation.

The second cartridge I started on last week seems about 70% better than the first one. Still not clean enough for formal applications, but less frustrating for my personal printing needs.

So, if you're OK with having a cheap cartridge that makes your paper dirty, but still can print out your personal stuff relatively legibly, then go for it. If you want it for an office environment, or for printing out your new manuscript, stay far away from it.

title: Stand Holds iPad Securely at Many Comfortable Viewing Angles
abstract:
This BEANPAD FOR iPAD is an absolutely great iPad 2 stand (and I've tested several). First, it's nearly impossible to knock over or drop. Second, it can be set to almost any comfortable viewing angle. And third, it securely supports your iPad pretty much anywhere you can set it down.

To use this stand, you insert your iPad (2 or 3) into the black, hard plastic holder. The holder grips firmly but gently, and easily releases the iPad whenever you like. With the iPad in the holder, the beanbag conforms to any surface (a knee, a table, a desktop, a chair arm), and makes a secure base so that the stand cannot suddenly collapse. The black beanbag is about the size of a large cantaloupe, and is just heavy enough that it cannot be easily knocked over or knocked off a table.

The stand's viewing angle can be adjusted to an almost limitless number of positions. The holder itself can be rotated so that the iPad is held in a vertical or horizontal position. Then the actual viewing angle can be adjusted by squishing the beanbag to find the most comfortable viewing position.

I purchased my first BEANPAD FOR iPAD from Woot! for the bargain price of $25 (including shipping). But when my husband needed an iPad, too, I purchased a second BEANPAD FOR iPAD (this one) for him at full price, because it allows the iPad to be used comfortably just about anywhere in the house.

title: Started acting up when I changed the batteries, disappointed in longevity
abstract:
Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

UPDATE—7/1118
We've had our new leapstart book (this time I bought at big box store with a warranty) for 5 months now since the last broke, so far so good but I'm still not sure on longevity still, however i have changed batteries a few times since we use ours alot and have had no issues. I am adding a star as my kids fight over this all the time. I've got 6yo boy who LOVES it who is also my reader and 4yo girl who always wants what her brother has but genuinely love this thing. I struggle with getting my kids to play with their $100 toy they got for Christmas but love this thing and it's a plus for me since it's educational. So i still can't give this item as high of a star as I would like because of durability I would recommend it if you don't care if you have to replace it. I'm glad I did but recommend getting some warranty because after investing in the books and how much my kids like It, you may want to get another.

title: Stiff Blade Performs Less Well Than "Rubber" Blade
abstract:
Does anyone remember when Rubbermaid products were actually made of rubber? I purchased this spoon-shaped spatula to replace one that's been in my kitchen drawer for more than 10 years. Unfortunately, the new, improved blade (probably silicon) doesn't perform as well as the "rubber" blade on my older model.

The new-model blade is stiff, and doesn't conform easily to the sides of the bowl or pan that is being scraped. It leaves behind a lot more ice cream, icing, sauce, and gravy than the old "rubber" blade did. Of course, the new blade is probably more sanitary, because the harder surface is more resistant to colonies of mold or germs.

For most uses, a spoon-shaped spatula (even with a stiff blade) is still superior to a flat spatula, because the spoon shape makes it easy to scoop out thick mixtures quickly. I do recommend this well-made spoon-shaped spatula, although I wish that I could buy another of the older ones with the more flexible blade.

ETA 10/22/11: Since writing this review, I have discovered a great set of silicone spatulas (including a spoon-shaped spatula) that have blades with the same amount of flexibility as my old "rubber" spatulas: [[ASIN:B000M8YMEU Wilton 570-1121 Easy Flex 3-Piece Silicone Spatula Set, Blue]].

title: Strange concept hides a great game
abstract:
The idea that each player is in charge of a stone age tribe trying to impress the others by civilizing the fastest is definitely not one might expect. There is no direct conflict in this game. You won't see people throwing dice because two warriors from the tribes faced off in a fight.

But strategy and tactics are vital in this game.

The key is how this game becomes a resource acquisition and dispersal game. You start out with a limited number of people. They can be sent to various spots on the board. Some spots allow you to roll dice and acquire resources. Others spend resources on buildings or civilization improvements (victory points.). You can even send workers to permanently increase food production, make tools or make another worker.

However, there are limitations. The "love shack", food production and tool production spots can only host one tribe each turn. The resource spots allow 7 total tribesmen. If your opponents swarm into the forest first you might end up having to send your people to collect brick, which usually means less resources that turn as wood is easier to gather.

Strategy plays out as you decide where to send your people. You have to make the best use of your opportunities, but also make sure to disrupt your opponents when possible.

It's easy to learn, but will not become boring too quickly as your opponents try tew strategies to defeat you.

title: Strong & Sturdy!
abstract:
When these first arrived, I gave them to my husband and instructed him to try it out. There were no instructions included with the package, so he looped them around a couple of trees & hung his hammock up. Then when he tested it, the straps stretched quite a bit to the point that the hammock touched the ground. He then proceeded to tell me that they didn't work. So I went to read the other reviews. There were several that mentioned a similar experience, but there were many that said it worked as it should. Then I checked out the actual product description. In the last picture of the product, there were instructions. There I learned that you need to wrap it multiple times and layer the straps a bit. We tried that & I am happy to say that it worked beautifully! I am a plus-sized woman and the hammock & straps held me in securely without slipping. We did not use the clips that were provided because I had left them in the house, plus our hammock has nice metal clips already. These will work nicely when you have larger trees and your hammock straps/rope won't fit around the tree. In the end, we are very happy with them. It would be very nice if written instructions were included though.

*I received these for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

title: Sturdy rolling "no-frills" book cart but not flawless; I was able to get between 75-80 cookbooks on each cart
abstract:
I purchased two of these in the "Tropic Sand" color because I wanted the ability to roll them out of the way when I needed to get to the stationary bookcases I positioned behind them. These are sturdy and roll pretty easily on carpet. When full with books, it takes a bit of effort to move but not too much. The casters are big and were the only part that had to be installed.

The quality is okay. After reading all the other reviews, I was a bit nervous that I was going to get a defective cart. One cart had a chip in it and the Sandusky label was pasted haphazardly on the side of the unit. Other than this, they appear to be fine. I was able to get 75 to 80 cookbooks of various sizes on each cart (about 25-27 books on each shelf), which works perfectly for me. See attached pictures.

If I were in the market for more of these, I probably would purchase the SmithSystem Booktruck or one of the other SmithSystem carts. I saw them in the library today and they appear to be better made and flawless in its finish. In fact, had I known about that brand I probably would have purchased them instead. Nevertheless, these carts are a "no-frills option, are sturdy, and hold a lot of books on three shelves.

PS I put the URL to the SmithSystem brand in the comments section of this review.

title: Sturdy, functional, nice size... but don't expect a long life...
abstract:
UPDATE: Feb 14. 2016
Mine bit the dust this week. The weld that holds the desktop to the middle support bar failed. It actually started splitting about 4 months ago, and I tried several options (various glues) to stabilize it, but nothing worked, and this past week it finally reached a point where it was just too "wobbly" to be usable.

This was used daily to hold my MacBook Air 13" (so not a lot of weight) plus a coffee cup or bottle of iced tea. Occasionally I used it for crafts projects (mostly coloring stamped images to use on handmade greeting cards, so we're talking a clipboard and some colored pencils). I was careful to move it by holding the middle support, not the desktop.

So... bottom line, it performed nicely for about 2.5 years, but daily use (not anything heavy) caused a critical weld to split. I would have expected a little more -- 5 years, perhaps. (I've replaced it with a slightly less attractive but probably more practical stand... )

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I purchased this to use in the living room for my laptop and crafts projects.

I'm no spring chicken, and I'm sometimes a bit "hardware challenged," but I was able to assemble this by myself in less than 15 minutes. The instructions are fairly clear, and as long as you're careful to get things turned the right way, it will go together smoothly. All tools are included in the parts packet, so you don't even need a screwdriver.

The size of the "table" is impressive for a stand/cart of this price. It's more than large enough to hold my MacBook Pro 15" plus my Akai LPK25 keyboard that I use for composing music. This gets me out of my office (where I have an 88-key Alesis keyboard for composition), and into the living room which has a lovely view of the garden.

I also use it for some of my crafts work -- assembling handcrafted greeting cards, preparing and coloring stamped images, making bows and trims, etc. Again, the size gives me a lot of real estate to play with. I can spread out a lot of "stuff."

It feels sturdy, too -- no wobble, nothing "flimsy" about it at all. I wish it had a "tilt" function for the table, but I can get a tilt just by turning the top 180 degrees (hard to explain, but it works).

Also, the platform with the wheels is a bit too high to fit under my sofa, so I've had to raise my sofa about 2" so that it will clear. Small price to pay for the convenience.

Anyway, the bottom line for me is: does it work for my uses? and does it look like I won't have to replace it soon? And the answer to both of those questions is a resounding "YES!"

title: Sturdy, multi-purpose table for people taller than 5'2"
abstract:
I'm the person who digs through hundreds of reviews on Amazon before I decide on a product to buy. After of several hours of research, I settled on this product. It comes full assembled (just have to put the optional laptop stopper in, hidden in the drawer of the table) and is very sturdy. The flip side of it being sturdy is that it's heavy, especially with a 15" laptop on it. It's also very large, so it probably wouldn't fit on a single recliner. In the pictures, I'm using the table on a reclining sofa and you can see there's plenty of room for your legs to stretch out underneath. I have it on the lowest height setting, which comes up to my chest and I am about 5'2" for reference. The surface (faux leather texture) is pretty grippy at an angle, so that's also nice.

Update: I used it for two days before deciding to return it because the lowest height (even with the desk angled) was too high and put strain on my arms. The heaviness of the desk also wasn't suited for my style of moving around a lot while I work. The desk is well-built, it's just too heavy and tall for my needs.

title: Surprisingly easy to set up, very quiet, moron proof so far
abstract:
Coming from a printer with 2 ink cartridges I was worried 5 of them would be a hassle, but considering my previous Dell printer lived a long and well used life and then died suddenly, I had to upgrade just as suddenly. No time for a drawn out, head banging on the desk learning curve.

Afer a full day of nothing but printer research both online and in the local stores, I decided on this Canon MP560 for a couple of reasons. The other positive reviews, the fact that it IS compatible with Windows 7 (with a download from Canon's website) for my new laptop, and it can go wireless or be used via a USB connection to the desktop computer. (Meaning my husband can print things without a chorus of cursing and hollering that ends up with me doing it for him)

The printer arrived today and I had it set up and printing in about 45 minutes. It probably could have been up and going faster than that, but I dropped the USB cord from the old printer behind a dresser and that ate up 10 minutes in retrieval. Note - the Canon does NOT come with it's own USB cable, you must provide your own! Anyway, the color and black & white documents are crisp and clean and the print time is fast enough for home office type requirements. It's very quiet as well which is a definate added plus.
****************************One Year Update March 2011******************************************

It's been a year since we bought this printer and it's still working great. The WIFI option is easy and makes printing from the laptop on the opposite side of the house a breeze. Took literally less than 3 minutes to activate the WIFI by the way. One thing I do love about this printer compared to our previous brands is that I am using less ink. Not sure why this is - we're not printing less than before, at least not that I have noticed. Just ordering less ink overall.
