title: TLDR, my favorite. Thoughtful game play, adaptable, HQ.
abstract: As a strategy game connoisseur, this game has become my absolute favorite that I have ever played. And I would say that even if it didn't have a Harry Potter theme. I'm not even a *huge* HP fan. The game play is super fun and I love that there are 7 levels ("school years") of difficulty. We played from 1 to 7 to start. As avid game players, we like to play year 5 if we want to sit down and play just one game that we're pretty certain we will win. Years 6 and 7 were a challenge to defeat; much is up to luck. I love that the game is so adjustable depending on who you're playing with or even what mood you're in for the night. And truly, the game play elements are really so thoughtful. Also, this game cards and pieces are HIGH QUALITY. This game is more expensive than some but without a doubt worth the money for what you physically receive as well as the different experiences you can have with it. If you're looking for a quick, easy game to play with young kids, this isn't it; particularly the higher levels take a good deal of brain power and strategy.

title: Tactical resource gathering game.
abstract:
This is a very complex and detailed game. It's not for children and it requires that the people playing are ready to spend several hours dealing with the complexities of the system.

At the same time, its a fun game. There are no dice which would be used to randomize events. The game is affected by your play and that of your opponents.

Overall, this is a resource allocation game. You start with two "meeples", who are effectively workers on you farm. Each turn you can send them out to collect resources or to perform special actions that build additional space or activate a special card. After certain turns you have to "feed" your meeples giving up some resources you had previously collected. In the end points are scored based on how big of a home and farm you have grown over the course of the game. The game winner is the one who manages to plan ahead and use his meeples wisely.

Of course, the challenge is to collect the resources at the right times. Most stocks grow if no one collects them that turn, so there is a bit of tactically plotting. Do you send someone to collect the small amount of wood this turn, or do you let it go and hope no one claims it. All of the resources play out this way, you have to decide which is going to be the most value at that time.

If you can find people willing to put the time in, this Is an excellent game.

title: Takes two weeks to kill, but kill it does - works on poison oak not on English Ivy *** Update July***
abstract:
This does work to kill a fair number of random weeds and vines, including poison oak. You have to use it with the understanding that it will take at least two treatments and and about two weeks to actually see permanent results. And...in some case, you'll need to spray the area three times in that two week span and cast some really dirty looks at the vines just for good measure. The leaves turn a spotty yellow, shrivel and curl and then the stem begins to droop - this takes four to six days with mature, strong poison oak and that's when you hit it again.

My one star deduction is twofold... First it did nothing to hamper the English Ivy. I sprayed it three times and there has been no change whatsoever - the dandelions and assorted trash weeds adjacent died, but the English Ivy bedevils me unfettered. Secondly, the spray trigger requires a fair amount of jiggling and gets clogged often during use. It works and is easy enough to fix but slows you down.

****** UPDATE July 2015 ******

It's been almost 90 days since the first application of this Ortho Max Poison Ivy killer and we have had absolutely no regrowth of any of the poison oak or poison ivy!! NONE of it has come back. There were a few really heavy, thick patches that took three treatments and I ended up using two bottles - our fenced back yard is a full acre. Additionally, the underbrush and trash weeds alongside the poison stuff has stayed gone, giving me a chance to address the fire ants we didn't realize had set up camp under the poison ivy.

title: Tebery 3 pk stainless steel rectangle divided plates
abstract: 3 pk of stainless steel rectangle divided plates. I purchased these because I love to make bento boxes, but, washing the delicate bento trays is a little bit of a pain. These are stainless steel trays are awesome! They wash in the dishwasher - top or bottom rack! Easy peezy clean up. They look a little - less refined, and create a more let's say - industrial bento trays - but I like it. Especially when I know I don't have to do anything but rinse and toss in the dishwasher. They are great! The metal material is heavy in my opinion. The edges are rolled so there are no sharp edges. And have 5 sections for your bento choices. Or, you can keep all your food separate. I like these - but they do look 'industrial' and not 'fine art' by any means in my opinion! Bon Apetite!  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including well over 25,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Tech support was poor
abstract: I bought this system in 2017. I found it difficult to install, but then again, i dont know much about wiring. I lost 3 of the screws used for positioning the camera and couldnt find replacements for them. I contacted tech support by email to order the screws but was unsuccessfull. Despite emailing 3 times confirming they were sending me screws, they never did. Communication was difficult (language barrier). I McGyvere'd the camera's somehow and got them installed. The remote viewing app at that time was not working. After they updated it a couple of times, I was finally able to use it. The cables that come with system are 4 x 50 ft. If you will be using these outdoors, be advised l, the cables are not good quality and will quickly deteriorate. I am able to view remotely, but it was difficult to do so. The cameras and dvr are still working fine, 2.5 years later. Ive also added 3 more cameras, different brands, successfully. The images are decent quality in the daytime. Nightime images are not too bad, but distinguishing a face would be difficult if the person is more than a few feet away from the camera. Would i buy this system again? Honestly, I would buy a different system.

title: Terrific for what it is designed for.
abstract:
Wow, we were primates that used to use a hand held roller to paint our walls! The back ooh the back. This item, for the price, is a terrific product for the sheer fact that it is easy to assembly, easy to use and clean up was pretty easy too because there were not many little parts. Sure, on the first paint pull, you find it all goes to the roller, but little on the wall for some reason. But one the second fill, you are off, and my Hubbie was dashing to the finish line in no time. Of course, you still need the roller/brush to do the tricky areas near the ceiling or floor. Only on star deduction was for the fact we had a tricky time using it in our 4 foot wide hall way as the plunger is long once you have pulled in a full tube of fresh paint. Other than that, I really love the item. We did consider buying the 'autonamtic' one that would have added an extra pound. I would recommend it as we found the manual process very easy to use, and the item is heavy once you have a full tube of paint in it.

Took this down to a 2 star from 4 stars: next day look and decided the roller is awful for us: left a textured and blotchy look. I know if the roller is not saturated enough, but we did a huge space, it all blotchy. I can't use other rollers with this product so I am suck with their brand. We are going to have to repaint with more professional rollers that will leave a smooth finish on the wall. Ooh yuck. Great concept, but couldn't they put in better quality roller, really.

title: The Cadillac Case
abstract:
I was really excited to receive my new clipboard to replace my previous one which had started falling apart! My first thought on opening the box was "wow, this is huge". It's longer than my previous clipboard, so I wasn't sure how I would like toting it around at work (I'm an RN). However, the difference has been like trading up from a rickshaw to a Caddy. Not that there is anything wrong with a rickshaw!

My new clipboard fits everything but the kitchen sink (see attached pic). I wear my stethoscope, but can store it in the clipboard when I leave work, so I don't forget it at home and then have to wear one of those plastic yellow isolation-cart throwaway ones that don't work for poop. My pockets are usually BUSTING at the seams with all the stuff I like to carry around. No longer! I can cram it all inside this beast! I don't know how well it will hold up to my dropping it repeatedly, so I will post an update in a while with the durability factor.

P.S. I am one of those endlessly-researching people who look up reviews online for 7,456 items before deciding on one. You're welcome. I've done all the legwork for you.:-)

**Update, December 2016: This case is still perfect! No cracks, the top clip is still tightly secured, still feels really sturdy.:)

**Update, after dropping the case a few times over the years, a piece of the plastic broke. I'm buying a new one now. It lasted a really long time given the price!

title: The VERY best shovel invented
abstract: This shovel is one of my husband's favorite tools. It makes short shrift of any planting job. Roots, it tears they up! Hard dirt, goes through it like butter! My husband has had 2 hip replacements and this shovel has improved his ability to plant any tree, no matter how large! He just put out 20 trees, 14 berries & several smaller bushes as yucca, star fruit I couldn't believe it & all in one afternoon. In his younger years he couldn't plant half of that. I think you'd have to pry it from his cold dead hands. He says it make planting faster,easier & less painful on his arthritic body. To quote him he has no idea how he survived w/o it. We have had it over a year & put it through its paces it shows no signs of slowing down (can't say the same for my husband)! I would buy it again & again. My husband's quote "how did I live without it!" It's a bargain at twice the price. We have a small ranch & have put in about 75 trees thus far. It would have been impossible w/o this dream of a shovel. It's so great it would make a much loved housewarming or other gift. I can't recommend it highly enough.

title: The absolute only ink pen I am able to use
abstract:
My local store can't keep this pen in stock. It's my favorite and I would be lost without it! I don't quite know what's wrong with my hand but if held in certain positions, it will get a cramp and draw up into a claw ( certain fingers), so my handwriting has become a mess and difficult at best for me.
I don't have as much trouble with my handwriting looking as messy when I use this brand. It has just the right amount of ink flow for my problem.
The only cons I have to say about this is that I go through a LOT OF THEM. I'm constantly writing so maybe I just use more than a normal person uses but in all the years I went through school I just don't recall running out of ink in pens like this.
I'll keep buying this brand as long as I can afford to buy and find them. I just got my order of 75 count I hope they last me for awhile although I'll be giving some to my daughter and I have other family members that will also use them.
If you haven't tried this brand, give them a try and see what you think, especially if you have difficulty with your hands and need help.

title: The best water bottle on the market!
abstract:
Now, obviously I haven't tested/used all the water bottles on the market, so my title is clearly hyperbole, but you get the idea. I love everything about this water bottle. The design is beautiful. The plastic parts (the straw and the cap) are well made and durable. There is no condensation, so you can take/place your water bottle anywhere, even in bed with you. The issues other people have had with the straw are a mystery to me. Maybe the manufacturer changed the design, but all I had to do was wash the bottle and cap and straw, fill with water and ice, and screw on the top with the straw attached. Voila--I was good to go. The best thing is that the water stays cold--really cold--for many hours. It begins to lose its coldness after about 18 hours, but even then it is not bad. I am a person who likes cold things cold and hot things hot, so this is important to me. I have not tested the bottle with coffee or tea, but I am willing to bet that hot liquids will stay hot as well. I recommend this product without reservation--it is well worth the price. I probably will get another one.
Update: I tested the water bottle with coffee yesterday. After putting some coffee in the bottle, I was surprised by an unexpected guest and forgot the coffee for several hours. When I remembered it later, I checked and the coffee was still hot. This bottle is marvelous!

title: The item you didn't know you needed until you tried it!
abstract:
I'll be honest, when I first saw this, I didn't think much if it. I read, a lot, and have never thought about something like this as something I'd need, or even want. But, decided I should try it, especially after seeing others give it a good review. I got it around Christmas, and immediately gave it a try.

I must say, I was wrong, this little gadget is pretty amazing. It's not so necessary when you first start a book, but about 1/4 - 1/2 way in, it is really helpful. I initially used it with a soft back book, and it worked great, but it was even greater with larger, hardback books.

The wood is sanded nicely, and the finger/thumb hole is a decent size. The holder itself is designed so that it doesn't damage the book, or leave any markings on the pages. It appears to be stained, but doesn't have any smell to it. The middle groove fits right into the center of the book, making it much easier to keep the pages open and keeps your hands from getting tired with larger books. And, it doesn't damage the books binding.

My only regret is that I didn't try this before, this is a great item to have and will make a great gift for any avid book reader.

title: The knives cut like butter; these are the best I've ever had
abstract:
It's taken me many years to finally break down and buy myself a quality knife set instead of purchasing oodles of individual knives. I'm finally glad I did. These are the best knives I have ever owned. The edges are sharp and cut like butter. In many cases I do not have to exert any effort to slice and chop food.

There are 12 pieces in this set as follows:
- one 3-1/2-inch paring knife
- one 6-inch utility knife
- one 8-inch carving knife
- one 8-inch bread knife
- one 8-inch cook's knife (a.k.a. chef's knife)
- four 4-1/2-inch steak knives
- one 9-inch honing steel
- one pair of kitchen shears (they come in two pieces for cleaning; originally I thought they were broken)
- one 13 slot storage block (this leaves two extra slots to store other knives of your choice)

They are forged in Germany from a single piece of high-carbon stainless steel. Hand washing is recommended and it comes with a limited lifetime warranty.

I've been using these regularly with three wooden cutting boards I purchased specifically for these knives. I use to use a glass cutting board which damages knives so in order not to damage these knives, I made sure to purchase wooden boards. Although end grain cutting boards are better, I purchased edge grain instead.

These knives are a dream to work with and I highly recommend them. At the beginning I was a bit annoyed that the storage block had two extra slots, but I learned to love that feature because I am able to store my Victorinox and other knife there and have gotten over the fact that they don't match.

UPDATE August 27, 2019 - Today the scissors that came with this set broke. I used them once or twice per week. I am so disappointed. I did contact the company to see if they would replace them. Other than this, I use mostly the steak knives in this set. I have had to sharpen them as is typical and they are still going strong. I also use the other knives but only about once per month because I work with the steak knives mostly. I have also sharpened the other knives about two times since I have purchased this set. I am very satisfied with everything but the cutlery scissors. Also, note that I only used those scissors for cutting herbs and not chicken bone or anything hard, which makes this an even bigger disappointment.

UPDATE August 29, 2019 - Today I received a replacement pair of scissors from Wusthof. I am incredibly impressed with the prompt service.

title: The ski feet have a rough texture that snags some fabrics.
abstract:
I appreciate the size and the leg room. It is pretty easy to adjust most of the time. I agree with others that I wonder how long it will take the plastic pieces to break. We have already used it a lot and it is holding up, but for how long?
As I mentioned in the headline, there are these little spots on the curved part of the ski feet that has this raised textured plastic, but it may be just a flaw in our desk. It is just a little rough and catches on my daughter's bedspread, but not as much on mine. I like the desk enough that we are keeping it and will try to sand it down to make it smoother.
Also, I wish there were two stoppers to catch the items on the desk and not just one. We usually have it tilted with either a computer and a notebook or a book and notebook on the desk and one stopper isn't quite enough. We are going to rig something up.
After looking at other desks, this lower height I believe would be best for most women and probably many men as well. Some of the other desks were taller, which can be harder on the wrists in a sitting position.

My daughter and I are already fighting over who gets the desk, so I suppose I should have purchased two when the price was lower. So far so good. I hope the plastic lasts!

title: The stickers look great! The font is beautifully done!
abstract: I placed two orders for two different shapes and messages. I thought I was ordering the rainbow stickers for the rectangle ones, but didn't pick the background color. So that was my fault entirely. For the oval ones, the white looks great on the cards I put them on, but the writing I was trying to cover shows through. My recommendation to the company is that they make the labels a little thicker, for those of us that may be trying to use these stickers as a cover up. The script looks beautiful, and when I realized the 'B' word I had planned to use on my 'Grumpy' bears was not the best choice, I emailed the company in a rush and asked them to change it, if it was not too late. They were able to change it in time, and my CNA's love my 'Grumpy Bears', which I hand out to my aides in my Extended Care facility, after being in severe pain and have yelled at them for not getting my pain meds fast enough or other issues...SMH. I definitely will order from this company in the future, and will recommend them to anyone needing custom stickers.

title: These cover a fair amount of space but not as much as I had hoped for. Good lights though.
abstract:
These light s have a heavy duty clamp on the end of them - thankfully I have an island in my kitchen and can just barely open it wide enough to stick on. I haven't tried the timer thing yet - they always aggravate me and I'm home mostly all day in my Senior Living apartment but I just barely able to get the clamp open enough for my 1 3/4-inch-tall island, but it did, and it doesn't seem to move around or come off. I was a little disappointed in how little area they covered but they light most of my plants nicely. Hopefully the bulb strips last a long time. The price was also very reasonable for the amount of coverage you can get. So right now, I love it. As I accumulate more plants, I'll likely need another one and this thing isn't the most attractive thing in the world, but it does work well.

I bought these lights in Oct 2022. The entire system just died all at once on Feb 18, 2023. I'll guess I'll try it again because I need the clamp style setup. Plus the five 5 light bars covered a large area. Like others have stated I think it's related to the plug too. The had been off all night and when I tried to turn them on again nothing happened, I have a kitchen item plugged into the same light socket - and it still works fine, Anybody have any experience on how to test the plug on this? I guess I'l try it one more time - I can't use the taller tri-pod ones - they take too much space and are too tall. This one covers my entire 2 1/2' x 5' long island

title: Third time buying this!
abstract:
This is the third time I've bought this mousepad from Innovera. When I first saw it online, I thought its biggest selling point would be its price. At $12, or thereabouts, it really is a steal.
Then I actually got it and was blown away by all the other qualities. First of all, it doesn't need to be adjusted to. I got it and my wrist just automatically found the best ergonomic position. The most important factor is the gel wrist pad. Its amazingly comfortable and soft without being too plush and provides great stability. Despite the material, it doesn't stick to your hand. And it's contoured in such a way as to provide a very natural resting position for your wrist and hand. I use it all day for work and gaming and have never ever had any complaints.
Second is the lightly textured surface of the actual mouse pad. I like the physical responsiveness I feel through this texture. It provides a great gliding surface for my mouse without sending it flying away.
Finally the sticky back (the underside) of the pad keeps anchored firmly in whatever position you decide for it.
All of this makes this my favorite mouse pad. I'll keep buying them whenever their lifespan reaches their natural course.

title: This Product Does Not Represent the Key to a Perfect Lock
abstract:
It is widely known that a small percentage of all electronic deadbolts fail too soon, whether it's the motor or electronics. This is why many are sold with the ability to also use a physical key, and why many people buy these because they have the backup keys.

This lock comes with 2 such keys. But, the keys are in no way traditional keys, which means copies cannot be easily made at a hardware or locksmith store. If you have more than 2 people who you want to give these emergency keys they can carry on their keyring, your only choice to get copies are to mail one of your 2 keys to the company. You must pay them a whopping $27 for a copy. This is $20 for the copy and $7 for them to mail your key and the copy back.

This $27 for just one fairly small key is outrageous, in my opinion. Especially considering I already paid over $200 for the deadbolt.

This company could have easily designed the deadbolt to take traditional keys. There are other electronic deadbolts that do. But even if they couldn't, they could have at least not made a copy cost so much.

If you do not ever need more than 2 physical keys, or if you never fear losing one of them, this electronic deadbolt has some nice features. It's easy to install and easy to program.

title: This camera has given me a semblance of freedom!!
abstract: Mother/legal guardian/sole caregiver of an epileptic, mentally handicapped, Autistic adult son. After a hospitalization for a brain bleed, in which the hospital policy would not allow me to spend the night in his room and the night nurses were IMHO 25% the quality of the day shift nurses, he has become SUPER CLINGY. He naps every day and I've been afraid he'd wake up, alone, while I was in the yard and become more traumatized (I suspect he was waking at night and finding himself alone, as I was with him every minute from 6am to Midnight unless his Dad was with him or a nurse in the daytime.). I was super excited when I found this camera...last time I'd checked they were $150 each or more. The setup was super easy, the picture quality is INCREDIBLE. High-def 1080p. The sound is great. The app works phenomenally, just take a bit to learn the controls (mute, moving the camera, zooming, etc). I have been able to get out and get a brisk walk around my little acre, do some yard work, or just sit and enjoy the sounds of a lovely summer night. I am so thankful for this camera!!

title: This dash cam proved a valet stole from my car.
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:3663a2b63cb37ea4d978a919015e9f28]] I've owned past viofo dash cams. Once I saw the A139 come out I decided to change it to this one because it had better camera quality and the inside camera.
The install was fairly easy, same as all dash cams to hide the wire and use the cigarette adapter or hardwire it.
The camera quality is much better than the A129 pro. I can definitely see license plates more clearly. Especially on the local roads. (Bonus it comes with a polarizing lens- it is suppose to block out glare during the daytime)
I live in NY and the weather has been very hot the past few weeks. Never had any issues with the cam falling off the window or the dash cam overheating.

A few days ago I left my car in a garage valet lot. Everything seemed fine until I needed money for some food. I usually don't keep money in my wallet. So I keep a few 20s in a visor organizer. When I looked inside, there was on a few dollar bills. Something felt off and I decided to check my dash cam. And I can clearly see the valet guy taking my money.
I must say I'm so glad I installed this 2 weeks ago.

title: This thing is sweet!
abstract:
I haven't had this too long, but I am thrilled with it. It does everything I hoped for and more. With just a little practice, it is easy to zero in on a target. The ability to "adjust" the sensitivity through the power up, is a nice feature. The varying vibration is pretty nice too and it gives nice positive feedback.

I have done some experimenting with it and I amazed at just how small and object it will detect. It has other practical uses too. You can pinpoint a screw or nail head in a wall, Trace the way wire is routed in a wall, find a dropped screw in the grass and it will also pick up metal like hidden nails in a piece of wood. If you do any woodwork and plane down reclaimed wood, this is something essential. It works as well or better that units designed specifically for that.

The size is pretty handy and it seems very durably built. The holster that comes with it is fairly nice too. Someone suggested that it falls out to easily, but if you turn it as you holster it, it grabs pretty snugly. I suppose a retainer strap would be OK, but I don't see it as necessary.

The LED light is nice. Not bright enough to use as a flashlight, but perfect for down in a hole. Any brighter might be too bright. This thing is very well designed. You can find some similar for less money, but I don't think you will find any better. It does what it was designed to do and very well.

title: This works! Updated review
abstract:
UPDATE-Spoke to a pest removal professional in casual conversation and he told me the steps I took was exactly what someone should do and any place you call is going to try to tell you different because they obviously run a business and want money. He said there is no need to spend thousands.
UPDATE-1 year later no bugs
Update: Been approx six months and NO BED BUGS after using this. I live in New England and we had a stink bug epidemic recently. This stuff killed all of those buggers that snuck in too! Those are harmless but driving me nuts.

I am a visiting nurse and have been lucky for 8 years not to get bedbugs. Well I have them now. I called several exterminators for the heat treatment. $2,600 for 1300 sq/ft!!!! Cheapest quote. Can't pull it out of my butt no matter how good your sales pitch is. We bought everything Home Depot has. You name it we got it. We got Diatomaceous Earth (Safer brand) which I think definitely helps but not cutting it fast enough. I put it everywhere. With all the sprays. No bugs in sight or bites for a day or two then would spot one and get a bite. Well I used this and it's been 5 days and not one bite or sign of bugs, eggs or poop. I got the bulbous duster. It is a must. You want that fine dust to cover lightly. I think I went overboard but I drilled holes in the walls and puffed some down the holes. Dusted the floors, baseboards, under my sheets, furniture, ceiling, walls, car, attic you name it its dusted. Once it settles it is not bad to breathe. Take breaks. Wear eye protection and a mask of some sort. Gloves! This stuff drys out your skin like you wouldn't believe. Put some vaseline or heavy emollient on after.
I still use the spray to kill any eggs every other day.
I will give an update on a couple weeks. If these babies aren't gone I guess I will be working double shifts for the next month for the heat treatment and my kids will live off Ramen noodles for awhile.

title: Tommy Bahama sealife quilt
abstract:
I purchased this quilt because the blues and grays were perfect for my masterbed room. It is cotton and washed and dried nicely. It is piped on the edges with a complimentary stripped print - one side is the sea life print - the other side is the stripped print that matches the piped edge. The sea life print is muted by the quilting - you almost can't tell what some of the print is until you really look at it. One of the reasons I like quilts is because I can wash them at home - as opposed to comforters that are nearly impossible to wash at home in a non-commercial machine. The material is soft after washing. The quilting is machined, of course - but is nice and creates a slightly poofy texture. The background is not a bright white - it would describe as a grayish/dirty white that is complimentary to the print. Over all, I like it. Having said that, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE:... 5/8/2021... There have been quite a few strings on too- the quilting.. I will continue to track.. but its disappointing. Thus 1 less star at this point.

title: Transfer punch center
abstract: Transfer center punch. Husband reports it dulls quickly on A36 steel plate. It is a normal, unhardened steel. So, he has sharpened it numerous times. Other than that, it works. Per husband. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including well over 25,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: Travel Laptop
abstract:
Husband travels a LOT and had his very expensive ($530) backpack stolen in what the police called a "bust and go" (drove up next to the rental truck - took a hammer, busted out the window, grabbed his backpack and drove off - all within about 20 seconds - on security camera). Long story short, he was very dismayed to have to find a replacement. After several weeks and research, winding down options to about 1/2 a dozen backpacks - he chose this one. He reports a few things...
PROS: 1. it's well made - well above the price. And a long shot from the cost of the over expensive backpack that was stolen. 2. It's roomy. 3. Everything he needs fits. 4. There are a LOT of compartments - they sort of fan out when all open.
CONS: None.... unless you consider his opinion as a "con".... It is entirely possible you could overload it and make it very, very heavy....
A couple of further notes.... he has not evaluated the charging aspects of the bag.. there are spots you can pull a USB cord through to attach to your devices... He also has not had any issues with the TSA - however he is authorized TSA "pre check." So you are, at the time of this review" not required to remove certain things from your bag.
I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and as he uses it.
UPDATE: 9/16/2017.... Husband continues to love this bag. It's just really useful to have the outer power connections and all the handles are reinforced and strong - he's "tested" them a few times - he is NOT "easy" on his bags....I think this backpack is well worth the price...

title: Try it at least once!
abstract:
I have a [[ASIN:B002ZIPKQO Samsung ML-2525W Wireless Mono Laser Printer]] that uses a [[ASIN:B002SU2A80 Samsung MLT-D105L Toner Cartridge]]. This toner cartridge currently costs around $66.00.

I've never had any luck refilling inkjet cartridges, so I didn't have much hope for refilling a toner cartridge either - especially when the refill is so inexpensive (I figured that it couldn't possibly work).

There was no "refill hole" on the toner cartridge that have, so I used a drill to make one (in the center of the top of the cartridge, right over the handle). I'd recommend putting down newspaper, and working very slowly and carefully - the toner can get EXTREMELY messy. It only took me about 10 minutes to drill the hole, fill with replacement toner, cover the hole and put in the new chip.

The printer recognized the chip as a new toner cart; the printed pages look great. I couldn't be happier! I don't know how long the refill will last, but since these refill kits are so inexpensive, I really don't care...

11/01/2013 - UPDATE: I have used several of these refill kits since I originally wrote my review. I still think that they work great. The refilled cartridge seems to last as long as a new one would.

title: Ultimate Computer Screen Cleaning Product!
abstract:
This is, by far, the BEST product I have used to clean my laptop screen! Extremely easy to use, small enough to fit into one of my laptop case pockets.. it is the only product I have used that doesn't leave ANY streaks behind! A clean screen, just as good as the day I purchased it, is worth it to me. I will never use anything else on my laptop screen again!

I like that the cloth can be removed and rotated to a clean section then reinserted.. and when the cloth is completely soiled, you can simply toss it in your washing machine (just don't put it in the dryer!).

For the customer who had the bottle dribbling problem.. mine did at first, but like any other pump product, you have to pump it a few times to get all the air worked out of the pump line. I pumped the bottle over my kitchen sink until the gel sprayed out evenly on the side of my sink (about 6-7 full pumps).

For the customer who had issues with the design for removing the cover.. I found that this was not an issue at all. I did not have to pinch the cover to remove it.. it is more like a 'press with your thumb and slide outward' motion. No pinching at all. It does snap into place really well which is a good thing.. not exactly something you want to just pop off all the time.

title: Unstable and Drawers Won't Slide
abstract: I was really looking forward to this cart to organize odds and ends that have been accumulating on the bathroom countertops. I purchased a 15 drawer version (2 tiers) at the same time for my nail art supplies at the same time, although the larger one was delivered a day earlier. I assembled it just the day before and as it turned out, that was a good thing, since no assembly instructions came with the 8 drawer cart. Everything seemed to be going together fine—until I started trying to insert the drawers. They were just slightly too large to slide into the slots! I loosened the bottom and top crossbars that connect the two sides and was able to get the drawers in with a bit of effort, but they could not be opened without bracing the cart and really pulling hard. Once I retightened the crossbars, it was nearly impossible. Fully assembled and appropriately tightened, the cart is wobbly and unstable and leans to one side or the other. The bigger issue is the inability to easily slide open the drawers, since that's the entire purpose of a storage cart! I considered trying to figure out ways to get the thing to be functional; I had just spent all that time putting it together. In the end though, I decided that I would very likely only be wasting more of my time with no guarantee that it would work any better. So I took everything apart, repackaged it, and will be sending it back. I'll get another 15 drawer model if I get another, but I'm pretty much over assembling (and UNassembling) storage carts for the near future! What good is a storage cart if the drawers won't open? What a huge waste of time! And now I have to haul it to a UPS drop off site too!

title: Up dateing my 3rd review, also how I got this Off..Whew..
abstract:
Up dateing my 3rd review!
#3 review..Btw, I was able to get mine off my wood cabinet! Not going to take any stars off, cause it does stick like glue.
I just want to say how I got it off...I took a old thin long kitchen knife with a round tip, (or buy one at a thrift shop)and kept sticking it down behind the sticky stuff, from the top, Sides, and underneath hoping I would not scratch the wood it was stuck to. Then I poured very careful nail polish thinner behind there. It melted the Gluey sticky stuff, I pulled and it came off..some sticky stuff was still on, I rubbed it off with my fingers..it did Not damage my wood that I can see.
Btw, keep a old dishtowel under it so you do Not get it on your floor..Whew..

#2 review. After using this for a few weeks, and since I attached this holder right below my kitchen sink, its a Pain
In the butt having to bend over all the time, and grab more of the bottom of the
Dishtowel to wipe my hands..Now my husband admitts the something!
I'm not tall, 5'2..but the towel it self,hangs low..
I'm afraid to take this off my wood, cause it could ruin my wood now.
If I had to do it over, I would choose a long cabinet Pull handle that is probably about 8 inchs wide, flat,in stainless or oil-bronze.
Then my towel would be at the right hight, cause its folded in half while hung, and not have to bend down all the time to dry my hands.
Btw I do exercise, but this for me was not a good idea!
Actually, I'm going to try and take this off using coconut oil..Just hope I'm not making another mistake lol.

————————————
#1 review.I love this dish towel holder. Its not big, does not stick out (less then a inch) like a sore thumb and goes with my stanless appliances.
It's actual next to my stainless dishwasher and Not in the way, matches good.
I put mine on the wood just below my large kitchen sink, but above my cabinet doors under the sink.
Before I stuck this on the wood, I took the back side of a NOT course emery board, and sand the wood for two second, wiped it off.
So far this does not look like its coming off. Its been up for a few days, and I have two thick dishtowels on it that I use all the time for wet hands.
Also is convenient for the little kids.

My stove is across from the kichen sink, and I get so much water marks on my floor going back and forth
to that side of my kitchen to go to my stove with wet hands..I'm always throwing down a towel so no one slips
On the laminate wood floor.
Using this talkraft bell adhesive dishtowel holder Now, I only get a few drops..No big deal.

title: Update: (Replacement is Great!) There's not much to review when it's broken out of the box.
abstract:
Updated Review (Original Below):
The new printer works great with my Mac and the auto duplexer is a nice touch. I struggled a bit at first, but a functional one is pretty damn easy to setup and use. The HP software is clean and well designed. Despite there being a bit of a snag on the first go around, overall I'm very pleased.

This printer was simply broken upon arrival. The paper try would not adjust to fit 8.5x11 paper. I was able to finagle it to print the alignment page, but after that, it simply would not go.

Pros:
1. Unboxing and printer set-up documentation is clear and easy to understand.
2. Guided set-up is easy.

Cons:
1. Well, it's broken out of the box.
2. Support was basically not helpful in the situation because it was a physical problem that was difficult to explain over the phone. Eventually they gave up and said they would just mail me a new one.

While I appreciate the offer, I have no interest in swapping a printer that was broken to begin with. I'll simply use the touchless return from Amazon and order from a different manufacturer.

I had previously sworn off HP printing products for lack of quality and support. I had decided to gamble on this one and take on chance hoping things have improved. There are a number of high quality reviews for this printer, so your milage may vary.

title: Upgrade my initial review from 1 to 5 stars. Time will determine if it keeps all the stars.
abstract:
After a very failed first gun and missing accessories. The seller contacted me after seeing my review to help. So with little review time, here is my revised review...much happier this time.

For now with an initial test of the replacement guns on a gas 3200 psi pressure washer with bypass:

Quality: 8/10 Looks/feels very similar to guns I have paid $40+ Just a shorter wand that I needed more than the long lance most are equipped with.

Operational: 7.5/10 Quick connects are much looser (slips in and seats perfectly). Easier to fit than first defective gun. Tip quick connect does not release quite as easy. Sadly, it is not an "eject" quick connect. When pulling release, you have to pull tip out. Trigger is smooth, solid, easy pull and comfortable to use.

Value 10/10: Most guns cost more and don't include wand, tips or quick connects.

Overall, this will be better than your OEM gun if you want a shorter wand and have a quick connect setup already. But be warned, if you get a bad gun on delivery. Contact the seller directly for help. They/he seems to be eager to help get you a quality working gun.

I gave 5 stars because I am tired of low quality junk and no one caring after the sale. This seller responded to my first failed gun and is trying to make a happy customer. That puts full stars in the review.

Stay tuned for my follow up review in August. By then I will have had time to use heck out of the gun.

Update as of 8-31-16.

While I still like the features of the gun. Sadly it didn't hold up under the pressure(pun intended).

After a full month and 2 guns being used for several cars a day. Both guns have died or stuck in the full spray despite the trigger not being pulled. While I will take them apart soon and see if I can fix them. I don't think the 3200 psi and commercial rubber hose I use in my detail setup is meant for this gun. It is likely better suited for electric pressure washers or light duty gas pressure washers.

To sum it up. Seller has been very helpful. The gun is Ok for the price, but may be better suited for light duty (lower psi) equipment. It does not claim to be commercial rated and that is what I wanted to try it out for. Once I take it apart, maybe I can beef up the interior. Or at least use it for my winter cleaning needs.
Did deduct a star for the guns failing in a month of heavy use...even though they may not be meant for the type of use I used them for.

title: Upgraded from the DT 770 Pro and am very happy I did!
abstract:
I had the DT 770 Pros 80 ohm for several years. I had been eyeing an upgrade to the 770's and I was looking for another closed back set. The main contenders were the DT 1770 Pro and the Massdrop 177x GO. I was able to try both and decided to stick with the 1770s over the 177x (I paid approx the same price for both, so price was not an issue). I'll discuss a few of the things I really like about the headphones below.

Firstly, the 1770 Pros are SUPER solid and very high quality. As soon as you pick them up, you know they are pure class. The 1770 was noticeably more solid than the 177x, so this was an easy point. The 1770 also comes with a nice carrying case for the headphones, which was a great selling point for me. The case holds the headphones, an additional pair of ear-pads (it comes with leather and velour), and the cables (both coiled and straight), which are detachable. The non detachable cables were a big pain point on the 770 Pros.

Sound quality- amazing. I know some people don't love the sound, but I enjoy a bass-y sound, and comparing these with the 177x's, these came out ahead in my mind (or ears).

Lastly, comfort- these SHINE here. Beyerdynamic is known for their comfort and the 1770 Pros are no exception. I wear these for 6+ hours per day (thanks WFH) with no issues at all. I think comfort is underrated when looking for headphones, and fortunately, these don't skimp in that department.

Long story short, these are great headphones. I came from the 770 Pro's and these are a worth successor. Very well built, great sound, very comfortable. Would buy again.

title: Usually cheap enough for off-line storage
abstract: The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.

title: VERY Cheap plastic - don't waste your money
abstract: I have a funny shaped driveway entrance, which I placed a wooded border around the garden part to keep the mulch in place. People (delivery trucks, pizza delivery etc) don't seem able to make it into my driveway without running over the wood border! so after replacing the pieces AGAIN, my husband found the reflective flowers for $12 each, he ordered two to hopefully help drivers to see the edge of the driveway. Now the problem is they are made from thin cheap plastic, the pole is two part that just slides together, the flower is held on but - yep a cheap plastic cap. The first medium wind came through and off the flowers came, as well as the pole came apart. The plastic piece that kept the flower in place is gone so now I have to figure out a way to keep the flower in place. The wind damaged the one flower but its still usable, the pole didn't break but came apart so we had to chase it down the street as well. Its not worth $12 - I would have thought a metal pole for $12, but the cheap plastic will snap if we get a hard gusty wind. These belong in a $ Store!

title: VERY Well Made, Strong, Durable and Flexible
abstract:
I sell nail polish online. I need good quality, strong bubble mailers to protect the polish bottles during shipping. I thought I had another box of my usual mailers and when I realized I did not and was nearly out, I went to order more. But the delivery would have taken longer so I ordered Fuxury Fu Global mailers 6" x 10" size instead. I'm very pleased with them. I will say they looked a tad thin to me but the material is incredibly strong and durable. I wrap the daylights out of polish bottles with bubble wrap then place them in sandwich bags and into the bubble mailer for shipping. I love that Fuxury Fu's mailers have some flexibility so I can easily place the bottles inside the mailer and not have to use a bit of force to get them in if they're a bit of a tight fit. The shipping label as well as the 'fragile', 'thank you' and 'have a nice day' stickers I palce on the mailers all hold extremely well and do not lift up/peel off at all. Once they're on the mailer, they're on and not going anywhere. The mailer has a super strong adhesive that keeps it closed and secure. Its so strong, I don't need to place any packaging tape over it to be sure it stays sealed up.

I'm so glad I tried Fuxury Fu's mailers. I'm so very pleased with them. I will continue to purchase/use these mailers as well as my regular brand of mailers. The price is reasonable, they're strong and durable as well as waterproof and I like using the purple mailers...nice to add a bit of color to my shipments!

title: Value and Quality
abstract: I ordered these pencils specifically for their colors and the little sharpeners in each pencil. These pencils are refillable which is a huge plus. WIth these pencils, I can sharpen them without them constantly breaking as my wood pencils do. I love that I can get fine lines as the projects I work on are very small, 4 x 6 and 2 x 3 and various other small sizes. The colors blend well with my other color pencils and watercolor pencils. The leads are soft but *not* easily breakable allowing them to be blended easily. I was surprised at the value and quality of these pencils. If you know how to mix colors, there are sufficient colors provided in the set. There are plenty of secondary and tertiary colors to allow for quality coloring book results. These would be great for certain children's ages because they don't have to sharpen them like wood pencils and endure chronic breakage. This constant breakage happens with my Chinese brand pencils especially and my Prismacolor pencils when sharpening but not so far with my Faber-Castell pencils and no breakage at all with these 36 mechanical pencils. I highly recommend that one try these pencils first instead of paying large amounts of money for some of the other "top of the line" pencils or buy these as an adjunct to the wood pencils. I believe one can never have too many pencils. This set allows for versatility and excellent value coupled with quality. Obviously, I highly recommend this set.

title: Vast improvement over the iPad 2, but...
abstract:
Since there are nearly two thousand reviews at the time I am writing this one I'll stick with a few observations.

First - and this is important - do not make the same mistake I did and opt for the 16GB model. Go for the 64 or 128GB version because, frankly, the 16GB capacity is insufficient for the newer operating system. Coming from a 16GB iPad 2 that was not at capacity I thought saving a few bucks and getting the same capacity here would be prudent. It's not and I have already run out of space before completely transferring my existing apps and data.

Second, this looks to be the same size as the earlier iPad I own, but the screen is so vastly superior that there is no comparison. Plus the speed difference is amazing.

Other features, especially the camera and battery life, are giant improvements as well. If you are hanging onto an older iPad like the 2 model I had, this one is well worth the upgrade. Just be aware that the 16GB model is not going to cut it, even if you are nowhere near capacity on an older 16GB iPad. For more specifics on features and benefits read through the spotlighted reviews here.

title: Versatile Dolly for Moving Groceries, Shipping Boxes, Storage Tubs
abstract:
This SAFCO PRODUCTS STOW AWAY DOLLY is one of the best purchases I've ever made on Amazon. I have a bad back, so I use it for transporting moderately heavy grocery and hardware store purchases (e.g., cases of bottled water, bags of mulch or potting soil) from my car to my house. I also use it to move indoors the large boxes that FedEx, UPS, and USPS deliver to my front door. And I use it to shift loaded 14-gal. and 18-gal. [[ASIN:B0014CVDA4 Rubbermaid Roughneck]] tubs around my house and garage.

A feature I find particularly useful is the bright yellow, heavy-duty, nylon pull rope. It makes it possible to move boxes (carefully) without strapping them down. It's a bit tricky to control the loaded dolly with just the rope, but you learn quickly enough. A word of caution: the pull rope can be a trip hazard, if you don't pay attention to where you drop it--I learned the hard way!

The dolly is lightweight, and very easy to carry with the built-in handle. It stores standing upright on one end, and takes up little garage space. The 220-lb. capacity is more than adequate for me, because I try to keep shipping boxes and local store purchases under 50 lbs. total weight.

title: Versatile and very strong
abstract:
This cord is overkill for most of my needs, but I purchased it as a package deal along with another Master Lock cord and a [[ASIN:B00E024E3I Vergo Industrial S300S Folding Hand Truck Dolly]]. It's perfect for securing larger objects. I have used it in my SUV to hold down a Roland electric piano in an ATA-style case. The entire package weights in at over 150 pounds and two of these hold it firmly in place.

I have also used it to move some heavy furniture in a borrowed pickup and, again, two of these securely held a heavy china cabinet in place during a short transport.

The overall length of the cord (exclusive of the hooks) is 36 inches at rest and 72 inches (give or take) when fully stretched. You can add another six inches to those measurements if you want to take the hooks into account.

One feature I love is the camlock feature. All you need to do is pull up the slack in the cord for an initial adjustment, then place tension on the cord and it holds very securely.

Although I have used this to secure some heavy items I was unable to find any rating for tensile strength. I know that it will support lifting one hundred pounds, and it will secure a much heavier object to a fixed position if there is no slack. Frankly, this is probably unsafe for any jobs that require rated tensile strength anyway. For what I use it this cord has performed flawlessly. In fact I am considering purchasing a few more because they are handy to have around.

title: Very Classic pattern,Heavy never bends.
abstract:
This is my 4th set of Reed & Barton flatware, service for 12..Although 1st time buying Crescendo.

it never bends, and never looks old.
There heavy, which I like.
Reed & Barton does not look like cheesy flatware.
I put mine in the dishwasher, and it
always come out looking like new after.
That said,I have been using my Reed & Barton flatware for years, and it still looks like new.

Crescendo is very classic, and has more of a Tailored look. Love it.
 Although it is not sliverplate or sterling,it can be used
for more formal dinners, and for everyday.

This set does not come with the serrated knifes. Just 12 regular knifes,
and not 24 teaspoons.(I don't use all those knifes and teaspoons anyway).Also not as many serving pieces as other Reed & Barton sets do!

Before starting your dishwasher. Turn on you hot water first, so you have hot water going right into your dishwasher from the beginning of the wash..

This set is made in China, as I think all there stainless flatware is!

title: Very attractive and reasonably accurate for the price
abstract:
I bought this weather station to hang inside my home after my outdoor weather station, which was much more expensive, fell apart during the last big storm. I was particularly interested in tracking pressure since we have so many big storms in the Houston area.

What I am finding is that (1) it is very difficult to set the needle on the barometer and (b) the needle tends to be just a bit off from the local reading at Wunderground. While I was setting the needle, I found that it would jump around even if I was very delicate while moving it to the desired setting. Once the needle was set in place, I decided never to set it again if possible. I am finding that the pressure reading tends to be slightly off from that listed for my location at Wunderground.com, my online weather source. The difference is minor, and one might expect a difference between outdoor and indoor readings. At this point, however, I would have to say that I'm not convinced that the barometer is reliable at all times concerning predicted rises and falls in pressure.

So for the price, I think it is very beautiful and reasonably accurate. I would recommend it to a homeowner such as myself who has an interest in monitoring the weather but would not recommend to the person who wants a really precise, accurate reading. The temperature reading seems fine, and I don't pay much attention to the hygrometer.

title: Very cute!!!
abstract:
I hesitated on ordering this since it wasn't from Matel, but the reviews varied. More good than anything.

Got it today & I am loving it!! I got three dresses - the one pictured with the red top is cute!! Very stylish. I also got a white dress that is lacey - can pass for a short wedding dress. title: Very disappointed
abstract:
Update: I've now had 2 of these flashlights. I LOVE the bright light, which I need at night. However, my second flashlight did exactly what the first one did, only this one lasted 6 months instead of 4. I bought the second flashlight thinking that whatever happened to the first was just a fluke, based on all the reviews. But after it happened again, I contacted Anker. They are replacing both flashlights which I greatly appreciate. So giving them 3 stars for now. If the new flashlights last the way they're supposed to, will be happy to add another star.

I bought this flashlight January 2 2021. I loved it. Super bright. I only use it for about 5 minutes a night when I take my dog out, on low mode usually, unless I hear something strange. I live out in the country and need a bright light because there are no street lights here. I charged it every 2 to 3 weeks. It has suddenly stopped working. The battery is completely charged. It comes on, then immediately goes out. This is a lot to pay for a flashlight that only lasts 4 months. I'm very disappointed in this flashlight.

title: Very good product...works as advertised.
abstract: This little dock adapter does exactly what it's supposed to do...allow you to dock your shuffle on a regular iPod dock. I tried it with my iHome alarm clock radio and my Phillips alarm clock radio. The dock adapter fits nicely. It will, however, come unseated if you just grab your shuffle and lift it out. You need to use your other hand to keep the dock seated. Small inconvenience. I would have given this item 5 stars if it charged the shuffle when it is docked but it doesn't. I use it at work so I just take the charging dock with me and plug it into a free USB port on my computer and charge it when necessary. It also does not work as an alarm, but that's a job for my 80 gig classic iPod. Good little product. October 7, 2008 - This is an update to my previous review. If I could change my rating to 5 Stars, I would. You can disregard the comment about not being able to charge the shuffle while in the dock adapter. I just realized there is a switch that you have to slide over to be able to charge. You can't listen at the same time, but that is a small inconvenience.

title: Very happy with the Canon ELPH 100 HS (Grey)!
abstract:
The Canon ELPH 100 HS is beautiful, and the Smart Auto feature takes great, no-stress photos for the user who has little or no experience with camera equipment.

Before buying the Canon ELPH 100, I read reviews and did a lot of research online to find a point-and-shoot camera that I would enjoy within the under-$200 price range. There are a lot of good products from which to choose.

I next went to Best Buy, Office Depot, and Sears to hold different point-and-shoot cameras made by the major producers: Canon, Nikon, Sony, Olympus, etc. For me, these visits to different retailers is an important part of the process of buying a point-and-shoot digital camera for the first time.

Another important step is to learn whether or not the camera's software is compatible with your desktop computer. Because my computer is old (2006), I had to research compatibility with the different cameras that I liked. You can find the information at the product websites.

Canon has a very user-friendly website that influenced my purchase considerably.

I had XP Service Pack 2 on an older Dell Dimension E310. For the Canon, I had to download XP Service Pack 3.

I ordered the camera from Amazon.com. From the moment I opened the box of the Canon ELPH 100 HS, I liked everything that I saw. The instructions are clear and organized well.

Finally, I love the pictures that I am taking. No, they are not the same quality as those taken by friends and family members who own thousands of dollars worth of camera equipment. However, these photos are beautiful and fun to take.

I am practicing now so that I will be ready to take photos at baby showers and graduations in the next couple of weeks.

Is it easy to learn how to use the Canon ELPH 100 HS? It is VERY easy to learn how to use Smart AUTO. The sliding Smart AUTO button is on the top of the camera: you slide the latch to Smart AUTO, and you are finished. The camera "decides" whether or not to activate flash and also determines other settings.

To learn to use all of the optional features (P mode) is fun but not essential to photographing great photos right away.

Another reason that I bought the Canon ELPH 100 is that it is considered to be among the best in its price range -- and possibly THE BEST -- in low-light conditions. The only time the colors seemed to be distorted somewhat was when I took photos of pets sitting in a semi-darkened room while they were directly under the strong light of a table lamp. I found that the bright light from the lamp washed over all objects close to the lamp; the objects outside of the lamplight were fainter in color. Since then, I've taken the precaution of composing photos more carefully so that I am not creating a spotlight effect.

I read that the ELPH 300 could be a better choice if you plan to use the video features a lot. For me, the video features on the ELPH 100 are fine.

While in Playback (viewing photos that I have taken), I am learning how to use the displayed menus to select options such as Slideshow and Erase -- so far, so good. While not as easy as Smart Auto, the menus are fairly intuitive.

I have been very pleased. The sheen of the dog's coat, the warm expression in her eyes, and the mysterious, bold gaze of the cat -- all captured beautifully.

title: Very heavy duty
abstract:
I purchased this to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] to a speaker stand (a very light weight [[ASIN:B006H0DY3C Adam Hall SPS023S Speaker Stand]].

Frankly this mount is far sturdier than the stand on which I mounted it, and is so well constructed and heavy that it's overkill for the monitor. My monitor weighs less than eleven pounds and I am pretty sure this mount could easily support a monitor twice that weight.

Note that you can rotate your monitor 360 degrees, going from landscape to portrait, and every angle in between. However, you cannot tilt the viewing angle. I am not sure why not since the gimbal upon which the VESA mounting plate looks as though it should allow it, but it doesn't,

The clamp that mounts to the pole has a thick, anti-marring insert that will protect poles. It's also one of the reasons why this mount is so heavy - the construction is very heavy duty. All of the tools you need are provided to mount this to a pole and adjust it. The four bolts that come with it are a bit on the short side, although they worked with my monitor (and you need to provide a screwdriver for those.)

I am thoroughly pleased with this mount, especially since I almost purchased an [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]], but took a chance on this at the last minute. That decision saved me a lot of money and accomplished exactly what I wanted.

title: Very nice gazebo. Here are some installation tips.
abstract:
This gazebo was easy to put together. It didn't require ANY tools, just a ladder. No bent pieces in our box, everything labeled and protected.

As others have said, when putting the roof on.
1. DON'T put the small peak on until the main canopy is installed.
2. Lay canopy out flat to determine which side is up. Fold in half, then in half again, (1/4 it) then put it on the frame to install.

**IMPORTANT NOTE I'VE NOT SEEN ANYWHERE ELSE**
3. One of the corners of the canopy has a handle/loop on the top corner, the other three don't. Put the other three corners on 1st, then use the handle/loop to pull the gazebo on. It is VERY easy to miss seeing this. Also once we spread the gazebo out on top, and got the 3 corners in, we left it in the sun to warm up and it was easier to get the final corner on.

4. We went to Walmart and got the cheap metal shower rings to put the screen on with. We also got 2 nice fabric shower curtains with a nice print on them. We hung these on the one side of the gazebo that gets full evening sun, this helps shade the gazebo so you can used it more. We added additional rings to the track and hung it outside the mesh screen.
5. We bought ABCCANOPY Premium Instant Shelter Weight Bags to anchor each corner. 2 bags of play sand is enough. I put the sand in quart size ziplock type bags, then put those in the Weight bags. Less mess to deal with.
6. Put the top piece on after everything is done on the main canopy. If you have one person stand on a small ladder (in my case a wooden end table) and had the crown/canopy to the other person reaching through the rooftop center, on a ladder. Then just snaps right in place.

I set this up at our campsite where we have an annual lease. We really enjoyed sitting out there and relaxing. We will enjoy this gazebo, and when the canopy needs to be replaced, it can be done for about $100.

title: Very pleased
abstract: Please note for the pictures I purposely selected dark cards to showcase the sleeves. Brighter cards are going to be much easier to see. This is my first time buying sleeves for my board game cards. Not sure what to expect but I really like them. They feel like quality sleeves that won't break easily. They are a bit slippery, not sure how normal that is. The slipperiness makes shuffling the cards along the sides really easy which also keeps me from having to bend the cards. A traditional shuffle is quite harder. These sleeves add considerable bulk to a deck, which is as expected with any sleeves. Don't expect to be able to keep any insert trays that come with a game. Keeping large stacks from toppling is an issue but we just break the stack into smaller stacks. A few times a little clumsy finger tap from trying to grab the top card has sent 2-3 cards flying off the top. I probably would not use these for a true card game. After having tried Gamegenic's sleeves made specific for a certain game and seeing how snug and perfect those are, I can attest to there being a little extra unnecessary room, if using standard card sizes, especially at the top, but it's not as bad as the extra space I've seen for fantasy flight sleeves. The extra space at the top of fantasy flight (from reviews) turned me off personally but I think these are tolerable. The only thing is that if all the cards are stacked facing the same way, the unused space causes a deck to stack with a tilt. With the matte sleeves, I haven't experienced any eye strain or heard any complaints. The matte does knock down the visibility a little but I don't think it takes away from the experience much and I think it's as expected for any matte sleeve. Lastly, I think the sleeving process was pretty easy, but again, I have little experience. The game-tailored sleeves were a bit tougher to put on in comparison but they were also bigger cards so they'd already be inherently harder to sleeve.

title: Very sturdy and worth it
abstract:
purchased for my grandsons to use when visiting..... it is large.... large enough for an an adult to get into. The material is a cotton canvas... not terribly thick, but not too thin in my opinion. It was relatively easy to put together... I like that this is a bottom floor attached. It is quite popular to stay grandma's and camp out.... I added some "nap pads" which are perfect for the 5 and 2 year old. I also added a stuffed bear and alligator and a camp lantern that is a lantern or a star map night light. Honestly, I keep it up in the corner of my living room so it is ready for any visit. It does come with a handy bag that has a handle if you'd like to store it when not in use. The poles are wood... a pine I believe... very sturdy. I would recommend this teepee... I always update if there are any issues that may be helpful.
3/25/2016 UPDATE:...so I just finished deconstructing the teepee and felt an undate with tips might be helpful... first... you will never get the canvas teepee back into the canvas bag provided... it's like folding/rolling a really thick fitted sheet and trying to get into a tube sock.... BUT the wooden poles fit nicely into the canvas bag along with the plastic connector pieces... it would have been nice if the connectors gripped the poles better and stayed connected during the deconstruct phase... however... I just removed all the holed top pieces and then turned the teepee upside down and shook it sort of like a pillow case... the lower pieces eventually come out... I just rolled the teepee up, put all the poles and connector pieces in the bag and set in a large drawer I have. I would have lowered my rating one star for the deconstruct hassle, but honestly, my grandsons love it so much I just can't. The quality is such that this is going to last for many years if we take care of it. It's just a matter of learning how to use it in an efficient manner. Also... I have hard wood floors, so I went to a local carpet store and purchased some carpet padding. I cut into a circle and place it under the teepee when I have it set up... I worry less about bonked heads that way - grandsons 5 years and 2 years. Ok! Hope this is indeed helpful info!

title: Video Makes All the Difference (new rating, new reasons)
abstract:
I love my Echo Dot 'Alexa'. She turns on and off my lights, reminds me to take my meds, and plays any song I request on my Prime music list. That said... When my daughter moved to Fl. and video chatting was all we have, I decided to get the Echo Show 5. The sound of the Echo Show is far richer than the Dot. At first, I did not like the fact that Alexa's voice was now muted by bass. I solved the problem with the Amazon Alexa app, where I was able to go to audio settings and adjust the bass and treble.
Any music played on the Echo Show is far superior to that of the Dot (no offense to my Echo Dot, I still love it).
REVISION: I'm 'old school' and believe in 'manuals, paper manuals' for guided instructions. I had to 'Google' how to change the settings on the Echo Show so I could access options on what would be appearing on the screen. This was after I complained to Amazon and they said they would forward my complaint about too many ads appearing. They never told me to check my settings and I had no manual to guide me. So I think I have now gotten rid of 'cooking recipes' and movie suggestions for little children. I LOVE TECHNOLOGY, but please, give accompanying manuals.

title: Waterproof for snorkeling
abstract: Took this case with my ContourHD for Snorkeling in Hawaii. Not sure I agree with the postings that say you do NOT have to have switch in "ON/REC" position BEFORE you place in housing. Mine would not record with magnetic switch of waterproof housing UNLESS camera was first in REC mode before placing inside case. Stayed completely dry on 2 of 3 adventures where it was continuously submerged for 30 mins each time. On the 3rd trip I accidentally snagged part of the mask strap when I closed the case. 30 secs later the case leaked...Contour let out a continuous high pitched tone and would not turn off... Battery shorted... camera dead... card ok. Not wanting to spoil my trip I could only find a GoPro Hero cam as replacement... Not even close to the underwater shots available with the Contour. No way to mount a Hero on the side of your head (Mask) without a helmet! Used a wrist strap with Hero...very awkward as arms move more than heads... Contour captures what you look at naturally with less vertigo from watching the video. For diving or snorkel I would always opt for the Contour and this case (less that 10 Meters of course)

title: Way better than the useless bumpers supplied with bidet!
abstract:
*final update 12/31/22: one split after 16 months but I was already planning on replacing our toilet seats as the Mr's soft close stopped soft closing and I'm tired of the bang. But in a nutshell, I'd definitely still recommend these. I might even buy them once again if the new seats need the bumpers, too.*update 10 months later* 5/22 Yes, these are still holding strong, and I think you ought to know.
7/21 The bolts kept popping off making my seat dangerous, since the bidet bumpers included never worked at all. The bidet manufacturer suggested finding longer bolt or other bumpers. I was skeptical about whether or not these would work for my American Standard toilet seat since it's not flat underneath. That's where I've had problems before with bumpers not working. I applied these a few days ago, with the additional riser included. Then noticed the next day that only two front bumpers were touching the toilet rim. Taking them apart by hand wasn't possible for me before application so I wondered if I tried after application if I'd ruin the adhesive altogether. I held the larger side of the "toilet lego" with one hand and pried the shorter side off with a pair if needle-nose pliers. This didn't harm the adhesive. So far so good. So the back two I kept at double pieces, and the front two at the single piece height. I like them. So far the bolts haven't popped off again so it looks like these bumpers have taken the pressure off that was causing the problem in the first place. Five ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ better than the bidet manufacturer's included bumpers. One star off because they're difficult to take the pieces apart. I'll update if anything changes.

title: Well-Made, Long-Lasting Coffeemaker With All the Right Features
abstract:
This HAMILTON BEACH 12-CUP PROGRAMMABLE COFFEE MAKER (46201, Stainless Steel) is my all-time favorite--and I've tried lots of coffeemakers (e.g., Target generic, Braun, Mr. Coffee, Black & Decker). It has a swing-out coffee basket (easy to fill, no "showerhead" spewing steam in your face when you want to make a second pot right away). It has a "sneak-a-cup" feature (pour a cup during brewing). It has a carafe that pours without dripping (just don't try to pour too much, too fast). It has a keep-warm hot plate (turns off automatically after 2 hours). It has a removeable tank, marked with water levels for desired number of cups, for kitchen-faucet filling (easy to remove and replace). It has little rollers for easy shifting on a kitchen countertop (very helpful in a big coffeemaker). It's got 4-to-12-cup coffeemaking capacity, with adjustable brew strength (brew strength feature really works). And it's programmable (have your coffee ready when you get up in the morning).

Best of all, this is an extremely well-made, reliable, and durable coffeemaker. My Hamilton Beach Model 46201 coffeemaker--purchased in April 2015, and used daily to brew 1-2 pots--is still going strong! This is already longer than my other coffeemakers have lasted, so I ordered a second one to keep in reserve while the same model is still available. Coffeemakers with swing-out baskets are now nearly impossible to find, and it's good to have a backup coffeemaker around when your household consumes as much coffee as ours does.

title: What amazing sound coming from a compact speaker!
abstract:
Wow, wow, wow, I cant believe how compact this little speaker is and the sound wave coming out it is absolutely and truely amazing. I compared the sound with another portable 2-speaker ipod dock (ihome iH16GX), which also has an amazing sound: they were both about the same. But this little speaker wins it hands down for being so compact. I am looking forward to throwing this speaker into my bag and listening to it at work. I also loved this speaker as it allows me to use my shuffle, nano or classic (which the ihome only allows for the bottom insert to be used) whereas the x-mini uses the earphone port (more universal for the different ipod models).

I also like this speaker as it uses the universal USB port to charge the chargeable battery in the speakers. I hope these rechargeable batteries last a long time! I dont think they are replaceable looking at the build of the speaker.

For the price,this is a great little speaker and so easy to carry around. I just ordered two more for family members. I noticed the x-mini max is about to be released (two speakers) and ~$30 more expensive, but I think this one is so more fun!

title: What is up with this = it's been two months and I don't have it.
abstract: they admittedly are "running" behind. How do you run behind sending a piece of paper in the mail?
