title: Whoever invented SmartKey deserves a Nobel Peace Prize
abstract:
SmartKey allows you to rekey your new door lock to an existing key and it is SO EASY!!!!! I didn't read the directions, instead watched the video Kwikset has on YouTube. Word of advice, gentlemen and ladies and gentlemen again: Watch the very short video, without distraction, at least once before you just cue up the video with your nerves already tweaked from installing the door lock. Here's why...

Replacing my existing entry door lock/installing this new Kwikset Juno Wntry Lock was a more than a little exasperating. Replacing door locks is always at best an annoyance to me because twisting those screws that are just behind the roundish door knob is a serious PITA (pain in the...). Forget doing it with a standard Phillips head bit unless you're okay with your door handle being jacked up. (I mean, in hindsight it could've helped to use masking or painters tape a good 2 layers on the knob, but that thought just hit me as I type this). So you just about need a manual Phillips screwdriver. And keeping those screws in place without them falling through AND hitting those holes on the inside of the outdoor side is AAAAAAAAAGGGGGHHHHHH. Of course, if you haven't figured this out, I'm a high strung, low patience girl - hahaha. Rekeying was the easiest part of the process of installing this new door lock, I'll put it like that. Is it worth hiring a locksmith or handyman - uh, not even a little bit. Anywayssss... this door lock is great! Low cost, relatively easy installation, and BRILLIANT rekeying DIY capability.

title: Wish I'd known about this gadget sooner. Highly recommend. Could have save me
abstract:
A year ago I received an $8,000 water/sewer bill. My normal bill was running under $200.00 every quarter and I got hit with an $8,000 by the City of Ithaca,NY. This was a nightmare I wouldn't wish on anyone else because it turned out that my t year old toilet was running continually ( but not enough to hear it). The City has NO Plan for waiving excessive charges even if you immediately correct the problem ( replaced the toilet). I am a retiree on a fixed income and this was a huge hardship for me. Because I had signed up for Direct Pay they already took the money out of my bank account.
So..someone told me about this little Alert you install on the side of the toilet. It flashes only if water is running.Green lights for a few seconds then it stops. It's working now for a year and I highly recommend That every homeowner install one. Less than $40 can save you THOUSANDS.

Addendum: needed help to replace battery after 14 months and I called the manufacturer for help. They are a small US company and 'Ernie" walked us through the process of resetting device.
I'm so pleased with this LEAK ALERTOR for my toilet and HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
BUY one for Peace of mind. You don't want an $8000 water bill like mine!

title: Wonderful Lap table!!!
abstract:
I have been through MANY of lap desks and This desk is by far thee most comfortable on the lap. It has a handle for carrying and also inclines too making it easier to see the laptop screen and write on it. I use it in my recliner and in my bed. My 15inch Mac fits wonderfully on top and doesnt slide down at all. I think because there is a coating that grips everything. I have the black one. Anyway, there is a long plush wrist rest (couldnt think of what to call it) that blocks anything from falling off and comfy on the wrists as well. It also has a long mouse "pad"/"Table" built inside the table that slides either left or right. Both sides of it has a phone holder so that you can place your phone in it. It has room enough for my Iphone 8plus with a case. Its stands right up.

Another neat factor is it has a lil pouch with velcro cover on the front end of it for the detachable light. It slides in and out and can be plugged into what looks like a usb port. There is a switch on the desktop for on/off and it takes 4 double A batteries hidden inside the desk. I am tempted to see if the USB port will recharge my phone too. It may say something in the description about it but i am in the middle of writing this and do not feel like looking it up. Lol

I cannot say enough good things about this lap table. Quality is great! I will have to post a follow- up review in a couple of months. You know how some things start off great but then go bad over time? I hope this is not the case! I hope my review helps!!!

title: Wonderful for LCG.
abstract:
I ordered this deck box for the sole purpose of carrying my LCG decks. I currently play The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game, and wanted a large enough deck box to hold two player decks and the encounter deck. The current quest I'm playing is the final of the Core Set. This deck box holds all the decks and tokens wonderfully.

The two player decks comprise about 100 cards, which I have double-sleeved using Dragon Shield Perfect Fit and Dragon Shield Matte sleeves. One player deck and half of the other fits completely in one card tray. The other card tray houses the other half of the second player deck, the encounter deck, the threat dials, a handful of Ultimate Guard card dividers, a Fisher Space pen and a few sheets of paper I use for various purposes. The token tray houses normal-sized d10 and d20, as well as a small dice bag filled with Chessex stones and 10mm dice. The petrol color is awesome and my favorite of the Twin Flip'n'Tray options.

Though I keep the deck box at home, I imagine it will be sturdy on the move. I was worried about the magnets inadvertently loosening, but they are snappy and secure. The Professor knows what he's talking about. However, after watching some of The Professor's reviews on Gamegenic current offerings, I'm very intrigued. I don't have complaints with Ultimate Guard's non-removable flaps; I never even considered a company would make them removable.

title: Woodtsock Fantasy Guitar: No Casualties.....Yet
abstract:
Woodstock Percussion Kid's Fantasy Guitar is a small, six- string guitar designed to entertain youngsters as they exercise their creative abilities. It is a good starting guitar for youngsters and it includes a few extras, such as a pick, additional string, and instruction booklet.

This children's guitar is manufactured for young musicians in the making. It is small in size and easily fits in the hands of children. It is also very light weight so that children can easily hold it in place and play it without strain. It provides a means to make a little noise and create songs, making it a good choice as a creative outlet.

Like I said, this guitar is very light weight in construction. It is so light, in fact, that I immediately began to question the guitar's durability. The construction is comprised of very thin pieces of wood and other materials and while nothing has happened since I purchased this guitar a few months ago, it seems like only a matter of time until something breaks.

As for making music, this product does have some good things to offer. It creates a pleasant sound and kids will enjoy strumming the strings as they make up songs. Another nice factor is that the sound isn't very loud. One potential problem for some parents is that the strings cannot be tuned to the proper pitch. This instrument has the standard six strings, frets, and tuning knobs, etc., just like those of a standard guitar, but the strings can only be made to approximate the proper pitch. This won't matter to the vast majority of parents and I would say it is safe to assume that kids will not care either. But serious parental musicians may not like this.

Of all the features of this guitar, the one that annoys me the most is the tendency of the strings to loosen. With ordinary usage, the strings slowly loosen up, regardless of whether or not the knobs have been touched. At first, I thought my girls were playing around with the knobs, but quick observation proved this was not the case. The strings just naturally loosen up, with regular usage.

So, how does this children's guitar measure up overall? Well, it seems sufficient for its intended use and children will find it entertaining. On the other hand, its construction isn't very solid and the strings gradually loosen, even after a few minutes of use. Thus, considering all pros and cons, I'm going to give it an average rating overall. It hasn't broken or failed us yet, but it seems like a matter of time before it self- destructs and the field of pros and cons are basically equal.

title: Worked Great, I May Order More
abstract:
This accessory is perfect. I ordered it thinking that I may end up returning it, there were no instructions online and no good pictures, so I couldn't tell how it attaches and I wasn't sure if I could install it correctly. My board was already mounted, and there was no way I was removing it to install this. Turns out that it has a hole that spils over the bolt in the wall behind the glass. I removed one screw and was able to pull the glass out just enough to slide this in. There's no issue with it being installed after the fact. My board is about 2' by 4', a smaller board may have less play, so YMMV. I was also worried that one sided attachment would make it move around, but that isn't happening. It's in there snugly. And regarding what markers fit, the skinny ones and the fat ones both fit, but I have a set of double sided fat ones with magnets in the caps and those do not.

Two downsides: First, they should offer more sizes. At most I can get 4 of these, which holds 16 markers. And that would be very good because 8 of them would be very high up, this board is mounted such that my eye level is half way up the 4 foot high board. If they had one that held 12 markers, it would easily fit and I could do one or two of those on each side. I'm thinking about buying more now that I know they work, but trying to glue the next one to the wall behind the board to see if I can make my own mount instead of relying on the built in bolts. That may solve my problem.

Second downside is the price, this cost you like 50 cents to make. What ever happened to knock off companies coming along and making cheap copies? $12 each isn't cheap, especially when I would love to get 6 or 8 of them!

But overall it works well. Really I just wrote this review so that other people searching for "install" with the hope of finding out if they can slip it behind an already mounted board won't hit the same black hole that I did!

title: Works Great with Alexa
abstract:
I just bought a house with a very old garage door opener. It is so old it wouldn't sync up with the garage door opener button on my car. I called the car company and then the Home Link people and after trying several things, they concluded I couldn't link it and I'd have to either buy a new garage door opener or spend $80 on a "conversion kit". I started looking at the smart garage door openers and they were about $200 or more and so I looked some more and found Garadget.
I read the reviews and then looked at other types of add on's that would allow me to use both my phone and Alexa and the only one that seemed to fit the bill was Garadget, so I ordered it. The concept is great, it uses the same connections as the door opener button so it doesn't have to deal with any remote codes. It connects to the Wifi and then emits a laser light that reflects off a small round reflector you place on the inside of the door. If it sees the reflector, then the door is closed. If it doesn't see the reflector then the door is open. It is simple and elegant and the thing worked right away. It took me about 30 minutes to program it to connect to my WiFi, and attach it to my opener. Now I have the oldest and smartest garage door opener in the neighborhood.
I connected it with Alexa and found out that there are two skills for Garadget. The one that uses Garadget as the key word doesn't work, but the one that uses Smart Garage as the keyword works great. The only issue I had is with the app, which is pretty straightforward, but it was a problem to change the name. I couldn't see any way to save the name change or any other change I made and it was hit or miss whether it would take it. I still can't get the location alert to do anything If I enable it, I get the option for Door Radius (and I don't know what that means). It has 15 meters listed and if I try to change that, it won't take, then I can't save it. Again, I don't know what it does, maybe automatically opens the door when my phone is 15 meters away?
Bottom line, the thing is fantastic and being able to open and close the door with my phone or Alexa is a great benefit. I assume the app will be upgraded soon and even now it works fine to open and close the door. I would definitely recommend this product to anyone wanting to make their garage door smarter

title: Works excellently and as promised
abstract:
We love this shower head. We were looking for something with mid-range quality without breaking the bank. All of our hardware is brushed nickel so we wanted our shower head to match. I also did a lot of research for a more eco-friendly shower head with less water consumption. The pause function was essential and the light rainfall setting on this is fairly conservative with the water pressure. This was the best option we could find to fit the bill.

We have been using this for several months and we really like it. It has been functioning perfectly. Very easy to use. We love that we can toggle between the multiple settings and also use either the head, the hand spout, or both at once. When my hub and I need to shower at the same time, we use both the showerhead and handheld so that we aren't taking turns. The pause mode is great for not wasting water for in-shower beauty routines, like leaving face and hair masks on for several minutes at a time.

Overall this device has made our bathroom look so much better and I think we'll have an easier time selling our home when we're ready in a few years because of it. Love this this was such a high impact, low-cost upgrade.

title: Works for a bathroom - needed stronger model for bedroom
abstract: We needed a dehumidifer for our bedroom on the bottom floor of our split-level. The room was getting very, very moist in one corner of our room where small pools of water sometimes collected on the ground at the crack where the foundation met the floor, 3 feet below ground level. We thought this model might work because the air was not crazy humid but the pooling was occurring only in one part of the room. Our bedroom is about 8x10 ft with 7 ft high ceilings and we keep the door closed. We put the dehumidifier right next to the pool of water. After running 24/7 for 3 weeks, the floor was still getting very moist. It was a job too big for this little guy. It was taking in a lot of water but just wasn't doing the job. Now we've moved him into our bathroom on the same level, about 5x8', and we run it during and after showers. It is pretty effective there; with the door open during showers, the dehumidifier takes water off the ground within a few hours rather than 6+ like before it was in there. We got a bigger boy for the bedroom. Hope this gives everyone a better idea about the strength and appropriate room size!

title: Works great and does a great job
abstract:
Just received mine yesterday.
Great product as I put it together in about an hour, could have been less. (See below)
I did both front and back yards. I had lost part of my backyard grass and a lot of thatch had gather there. After running it over the whole yard, it really picked up most thatch.
I had to adjust it several times to get the right height, but was very easy to do.

Ok, while putting it together, I ran into a problem with the right handle. I could not tell if the handle was inserted far enough to get the screw to screw into the handle. That took up most of the hour to put it together. I got it in the best I could, but the screw did not fit. The photo above shows how far the screw went. I went ahead and left it as is and had no problems using it.

Again, I did my whole yard about 10,000 sq ft and had no problems. Begin electric, I did not want to run non-stop, so I would run for a bit, stop for about 5 minutes, then start again.
Over all an excellent product and I would recommend to anyone.

title: Works like a charm and a lot less expensive than apple charger
abstract: I had been struggling with the original charger for my Macbook Air 13" for at least 6 months. I had to wiggle the charger, try to hold it in, so it would charge - was a real pain. Finally my charger stopped charging. I was afraid it was the the laptop, not the charger. So I I used my husband's charger for a while and it charged fine. I decided to replace the charger after reading that the apple chargers last about 2 years. I was tempted to bite the bullet and buy the apple charger at $79. SO glad I did NOT do that. This charger at $20 works like a charm. I've been using it for a week now without any problems. The apple charger lost it magnetic ability and would not charge at all. This is really a good charger and at a really good price. Reviews say it fits a Macbook Air 11" and 13". If in doubt that this charger will work with your Mac, look at the details on the Apple charger to make sure it is compatible. This is not a 2-piece charger - it is one piece. No need to buy an expense proprietary charger when you can get this one that works as well as an Apple charger.

title: Works okay, horizontal footprint, very little memory, grunts a lot
abstract:
I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.

title: Works perfectly in my Note II
abstract:
Like others I opted for this more expensive card because I wanted peace of mind that it would work without problems with my Note II. I literally popped this in and it was immediately recognized and works like a charm.

I upgraded from a 32GB card that I managed to outgrow in six months (music junkie). Transfer from my old card to this one was simple. I used the following steps:

(1) Removed the old card from my Note II and placed it into the USB adapter which came with it.

(2) Plugged the USB adapter into my Windows XP laptop and mounted it as a drive. Marked the drive as sharable on my WiFi network.

(3) Inserted the new card into the Note II - it was recognized with no need to format.

(4) Connected to the shared drive (old card connected to my laptop) over WiFi and copied the contents to the new card.

For some reason I lost my playlists, but all of my music and other media came over perfectly. It's as though my storage magically doubled.

One thing I noticed is unlike my older card that heated up when i did the same procedure moving up from 16GB to 32GB is this one runs cool. The older card was a Sandisk, which was otherwise flawless and reliable. I just did not want to push the envelope with a 64GB card buy using anything but a genuine Samsung card because I heard there could be issues with cards in that capacity range. To me it was worth the extra bucks to be safe.

As for speed, I am going to take the lower numbers reported by others at face value. Assuming that this card is nowhere near as fast as Samsung claims, it's still fast enough for me.

If you have a Note II I highly recommend this card if you need the extra storage on your phone. It's a safe choice and works perfectly out of the box.

title: Works.. but not Great with my somewhat Older TV..
abstract:
I recently purchased this item (an BLK HDMI Composite​ Adapter by Audiovox) hoping that I could use it to connect my new Nintendo Switch Video Gaming Console (using the Switch's Dock) up to an somewhat older composite TV.

The television set in question does not have any HDMI inputs on it at all.

The adapter worked.. but not very well.

The picture displayed on the TV ended up being in black and white. And it was in fairly low resolution (of course I expected the resolution to be low).

Although I do think poor image quality probably results probably has more to do with the fact that the television itself is a bit older technology wise.. and less to do with the adapter.

So.. In the end, I will probably end up just getting myself a newer HDMI display/television of some sort to use with my Nintendo Switch. Because the results that I got using this adapter are not very suitable.

Something that I was a bit worried about.. going into this anyway.

Again, the poor results probably have more to do with the TV set is simply older technology.. and less to do with the adapter itself.

So I am only giving this product two stars.

EDIT: But again I am stressing that I believe my poor results where do to my TV being too old. I think this adapter probably works just fine.. and the TV in question just was too old and wouldn't work very well with any adapter.. due to it being older technology.

title: World Domination Becomes a Sport
abstract:
I have lost many a Sunday afternoon to Settlers. Do you know why I purchased Settlers? Because each of my friends has purchased our own set... we do not want to find ourselves at each others house and wanting to play but not have a board to set up. We have taken turns hosting and every time it has been fun.

It is a game of strategy, in my opinion a slightly more complicated/sophisticated version of Monopoly (although my friends vehemently disagree). Instead of building houses and hotels you build towns and cities, instead of collecting rent, you collect resources, and instead of chance cards you have victory cards... but somehow it seems more fun. There is an element of Chess- because you do have to build roads to tie your cities together, and to do that you have to have foresight and plan ahead.

This is a game of champions- and voted best Table Game by folks who vote on those things- be warned that once you start playing it may become addictive. Be prepared to be suckered into the sport for years to come.

I am reviewing this product in an effort to help other Amazon customers through relaying my experience with the product and providing any insight I garnered. Had I not liked this product, I would state so here in my review. I would really appreciate that if you found my review helpful, that you would please indicate so below by clicking the YES button below.

title: Wow! No more, "What'd they say?"
abstract:
Thank you to all you wonderful Amazon reviewers. I'd never purchased a Bose product before, with the exception of possibly headphones at some point in time. We know the Bose sound is legendary, but I never really needed a Bose radio or CD player. The Solo caught my eye because I love my flat screen TV, but the speakers are only so-so at best. Like many other reviewers, I have trouble understanding some dialogue on TV. It's fine as long as there is someone around to annoy endlessly by asking "what did they say," but watching TV alone, I miss big chunks of the story & plot. The doctor says it's just "one of the vestiges of old age." Oh. Another one of those. Thanks, doc.

So, I wondered if the Solo speaker might help, and thanks to all my hard-of-hearing contemporaries here (or should I say THANK YOU), I saw all the reviews promising that I wouldn't have to ask "what?" every 2 minutes any more. I could jump for joy after hooking up the speaker and giving it a listen, although my doctor would probably advise against it. On my TV, unlike some others mentioned here, the TV speakers work along with the Solo speaker, so it's easy to mute the Solo and hear the difference between it and the TV speakers. It's amazing. The sound is rich, and big, and crisp in a way that my surround-sound system isn't. Most importantly, in answer to my wildest hopes, I can understand every single word of dialogue, even Christian Bale mumbling behind his Batman mask. No kidding. The Bose speaker took 20 years off my age, and reduced my waist by four inches. Ok, I am kidding about that.

As if all that isn't reason enough to get one of these gems, it has to be the simplest piece of electronics to hook up, set up & operate. It's simply two cords, one to the power outlet, and the other to the TV. They include all the cables in the box: digital optical, HDMI & RCA. Plug, plug, power. That's all. The remote is four buttons: power, mute, up & down volume. It's hard to believe that such intricate, complex sound can come from such a simple device. Thank you, Mr. Bose, wherever you are. Not only would I highly recommend this to my friends, I think everyone with a flat-screen TV owes it to themselves to get one. Seriously. This is the audio-visual experience I thought I was already having with 5.1 surround system.

title: Yes, it is waterproof with some cameras and the right cables
abstract:
2022-01-29: Added photos showing waterproof connections and waterproof camera case for GoPro Hero 5 thru 7 black. Also, I don't attach the camera buckle to the battery, but use a dual mount to mount both camera and battery. It's easier to change batteries in my application with this setup. If your battery or case doesn't come with the correct cables, send a message to the seller and they'll send them to you. They've informed me that they'll be including that cable with both the case and battery.

Original: Before you buy this, you need to familiarize yourself with Suptig's waterproof cases, mainly for GoPro Hero Black cameras, and a few others. If you don't find a Suptig charge case that fits your camera, this isn't waterproof. I've used Suptig products for a few years to protect and power my GoPro cameras when mounted on the outside of whatever truck I'm driving... Peterbilt, Freightliner, Kenworth etc. in all kinds of weather. There's isn't a case for GoPro Hero 8 Black that I can find. There are cases for the 3, 4, 5-7 Black, and the 9 and 10 Black. I believe there are cases for some other brands. Only a charge case specifically made to connect to this or the previous battery using a cable with waterproof connections will be waterproof. It's not rocket surgery, but it isn't explained well in the product description. Lastly, you may have to message the seller to get the right cables. They're really good about sending out the correct cables for the application.

title: You Get What You Pay For...
abstract:
...and I paid.04 for this lens cap (+ $2.98 shipping!) I guess if your lens or camera didn't come with a cap or you lost yours this wouldn't be horrible. The lanyard is NOT attached as the photos imply it's just a 21" long piece of cheap nylon string. The cap has a single (why?!) hole to thread the line through to attach the lanyard line. The distance between the back of the hole and the inner wall of the cap is literally 2mm. I tried for over half an hour and could not for the life of me thread the lanyard onto the cap. If I safety line the cap to the camera I really have no use for the product. I had been told this held a little better than the stock lens cap that came with the Panasonic Lumix FZ70 that I just purchased but I didn't see that it had any more holding power on the 55mm Sigma UV filter I have mounted on my camera than the factory lens (which came with an easily attached lanyard). The stock cap is somewhat lower in profile than this.

Since the shipping was a several hundred times the cost of the item there's no sense or reason to return this. I guess I'll throw it in my 'spare and old gear' bag and if I somehow lose the Lumix cap that came with and is safely attached by a lanyard to my camera I'll have a spare.

Color me completely unimpressed.

title: You can shut off water to swap attachments without returning to the faucet!
abstract: This is exactly what I was looking for! I have a fairly large yard and have just done some patching in several areas with new grass seed. These need a gentle sprinkling from the hose spray nozzle. I also have 2 areas with sprinkler issues, and am just waiting for the sprinkler repair guys. In the meantime, I need to manually water those areas, and I like to use a standard garden sprinkler. For some of the trees and larger shrubs, I like to just use the hose. So I was frequently switching back and forth from the hose to the spray nozzle to the garden sprinkler - and each time, I needed to walk back to the house, turn off the water, return to the hose, remove the spray nozzle - attach the sprinkler, then return one more time to turn the water back on. Now - this handy little shut-off valve saves a bunch of trips back and forth. I attached it to the end of the hose, the lever lets you completely shut off the water. With the water cut off, it's easy to switch from spray nozzle to sprinkler and back again. And you can do all these things standing in the middle of the garden, no need to return to the faucet.

title: You need this deck!!
abstract:
I love love love this deck!! Worth every penny and more!
From the thoughtful quality packaging to the incredibly well appointed (and information packed!) guidebook, this indie deck is absolutely stunning. But even without the aforementioned things... This deck is lush and rich with symbolism and meaning that allow both beginner and seasoned readers a wide range of enjoyable, informative experiences when working with this intuitive, beautiful tarot.
The engaging art is stylistically consistent, the nod to the RWS makes it easy to work with, but the way it relates to current day and relationships is just wonderful. Empowering the reader with so much more than just a simple layout experience, it plays out relational storylines and navigates real-time issues that weave in and out of each Querant's individual needs.
Now, as to the feel... in hand, the deck is smooth, not slippery, and moves/shuffles beautifully. The weight of the individual cards is balanced, the thickness is just right... and had no "paper cut" edge issues that have been present in other decks. This one feels so natural and is a pleasure in working with it.. the gilded edges just add to its beauty, and is of the highest quality.
I adore and HIGHLY recommend this poignant, dynamic deck!

title: You really need this remote
abstract:
Like so many others with multiple remotes, I view this unit as a very attractive alternative to a sixpack of remotes. A single button turns on (in sequence) my Sony HDTV, Yamaha receiver, and FIOS DVR/receiver. Or, alternatively, the Sony, receiver, and Sony DVD - depending on the selection. It even switches the input on the receiver appropriately. A single button turns off whatever units are "on". And one of the best features is the ability to re-program the remote via the Logitech website if/when something is upgraded or replaced.

The only downside is that (obviously) a "universal" remote can't select EVERY option that may be available with the manufacturer's OEM unit. But those options tend to be little used ones. Another peeve is that sometimes I must shake the unit to get the display to light up. Otherwise, I don't see how most folks can get along without one. I really like mine.

UPDATE (4/3/2013) I don't know if anyone will be interested due to the original date of this review, BUT just to show the utility of this remote, I thought I'd post this update. I recently replaced the previously mentioned Yamaha receiver with a new Denon unit and the Sony DVD was replaced by a Sony Blu-ray AND I added a Roku streaming box. I went to the Logitech site and created new profiles using the new equipment and now I control all of the new units just as well as it had controlled the original units. So, the point is - the remote can grow with your system when you change or add new equipment. Pretty great, huh?

title: You won't regret buying this printer.
abstract: My husband bought this printer for work. He works from home, so I've been able to use it frequently as well and so far I'm loving it. I will say that setting it up was a nightmare. I'm far from technical guru, but do have moderate experience with computers and have set up several printers over the years. The main issue was getting the software on his work computer that does not have a CD drive. You can download the software from the Epson website, but for some reason it was extremely difficult to do. After downloading I would get an error message saying it was unsuccessful. After fighting with it for 3 days I finally got it setup, and I honestly have no idea how I did it so I cannot give any tips for others in a similar situation. After the initial headache though, it's been smooth sailing. I love the borderless printing option, it really does print all the way to the edge of the paper with excellent quality. The ink is super easy to load, and will save us a bundle of money over the life of the printer. You get a LOT of ink! The scanner on our last printer was awful. The picture quality was pathetic. This scanner is crazy good! We were both impressed with how well and clear the scanned images are. Same with the copier. I have no complaints whatsoever about this product and would absolutely recommend it without hesitation, although it'll be a lot easier to install if you have a CD drive to install the software. Once you have it set up, everything is very easy to use. The printer basically walks you through everything. If you can read, you can use this printer. The only thing my husband doesn't like is that you can only scan one page at a time and you have to place each page individually on the scanner/copier. He has to scan dozens of pages at a time, and he is used to putting a stack of pages in the printer all at once (the way you put blank paper in for printing). That's our fault though for not completely reading the product description before purchasing, so I certainly can't take away any stars for our own error. Overall, you really can't go wrong with this printer. I've been at my parents house over 100 miles away and can print things as if I were at home where the printer is. My only regret is not buying it 3 years ago.

title: You'll need to get creative with this one
abstract: The kit isn't so bad as is, I bought it to use with my angle grinder, the problem is that the drive wheel adapter thingy that they sent with the kit does not fit any of my angle grinders, it's a 3/8"-16 and all of the shafts on my angle grinders are 1/2"-13, so I had to get a little creative and temporarily installed a treadmill motor and had to make a drive wheel for that. I will eventually make a drive wheel adapter for my angle grinders but this will work for now. The belts they supply are just junk, they are probably best for use on balsa wood, I would not recommend these belts for metal applications. Nonetheless, I am partially satisfied with my purchase, my temporary set up worked out as I had anticipated, however, I am disappointed that this is not a plug and play device and that I wasn't able to just mount my angle grinders. Had there been options to receive the correct size drive wheel then it would have worked out better, but there aren't any options for choosing which drive wheel adapter size you need and in my book that's a failing grade. Cheers!

title: Your basic line troops for the Daughters of Khaine
abstract:
This box can make 10 witch aelves or 10 sisters of slaughter. The supplied instructions shows with pieces fit together to make either as you assemble the figures. It's a lot of information, but the sprues do have identification numbers imprinted to make it easier to figure out which pieces go together.

The box also includes a sheet of transfers you can add to things like the battle standard to give your army a bit of detail. Its simple, but nice to see..

The big issue most will have is the price. This is 10 figures and the MSRP makes it so its $6.00 per plastic figurine, and that's without paint, glue or the time involved in assembly. But these are your basic line troops for the Daughters, and you will need them to assemble most armies of this faction. (You can have an army general allowing medusae to be your line troops, but they are even more expensive.)

Then again, no one ever said Warhammer was an inexpensive hobby. If you like the army, go for it. I'd just recommend at least reviewing the army codex first so you have an idea what you are getting into, or if your local game shop has resumed holding matches, go and talk to players to get an idea of what faction might be right for you.

title: a good option
abstract:
I really like these... the flat wires DO help them not to tangle... Has a "universal" tip as most things do this day and age... worked with my brand new LG G4 cell, my old rotary dial IPOD and my Kindle 8" HDX. It comes with 4 (2 sets) of extra ear cushions. I feel that I have smallerish ears and I have a hard time finding earpods that are comfortable and will stay in. These work great. Comfortable and they have stayed in. Mind you, I am NOT jogging with them in. I only wish they'd come with a zipper case to hold them in for convenience. At the price point, you'd think they would. It does also have a microphone and I have "tested" that... worked. It has a little attachable pinch clip to keep in place as you move around. The foam tips are sort of like memory foam, but almost a bit softer really. I think this both helps them stay in AND retain comfort. The sound is very clean and clear - for an adult anyway. The tips are cornflower blue if that matters to anyone... I think the pic is very clear and representative. I will update if there are any issues.
UPDATE: 6/29/2015 I have used these earbuds a number of times... one of the issues I have had in the past is that this "shape" of earbud doesn't want to stay in my ear... (tiny ears?) but these DO stay in.. I think it's the type of foam tip... seems to grip a bit better? To be fair, again, I am not jogging with them in... I am mostly in a sitting position using them. The "flat" wires really do help them not get all tangled... having stay that.. they also resist "wrapping" a bit too. This is probably good. Otherwise you'd break the wires inside. The kiss of death to any wired accessory. Also, I've been informed that these are going to start coming with carry cases!! Yup. That would make them 5 star in my humble opinion and I'm keeping them in my "save" pile for a possible second order.
UPDATE 7/26/2015... Still happy with my purchase. I am informed by the seller that they are now including a case. This makes it definitely a 5-star value and worthy of a purchase. Will update if there any use/wear issues to report

title: beautiful puzzle - now a priced piece on the wall in the living room.
abstract:
we just completed this puzzle the day before yesterday and couldn't be happier! We opted to assemble it inside a frame [[ASIN:B01N39WPJS Black Poster Frame 29x40 Inches, 1.25" SnapeZo Profile, Front Loading Quick Poster Change, Wall Mounted, Professional Series]] which was rather spendy but it's beautiful and the frame actually has hinged sides so you just snap them down once the puzzle's glued together and hang it.

The puzzle itself it large and took up more room than we had on the table (hence the need for a frame to build it on) but we had so much fun putting it together. My son is autistic so it was overwhelming for him at first but we worked on the borders between the scenes and had different bins for the various scenes so once we found pieces and knew where they belonged we'd put them in their designated baggie. He really got into it once we started seeing the scenes come together - and loved it when I was stumped by various pieces and he was able to find them. Honestly - it's a great puzzle for the entire family!

On a side note, while we were not missing any pieces there is a flyer in the box letting you know that if you are missing a piece you can note on the flyer where the piece is and send the paper to the company and they will get the missing piece to you. I'm soooo impressed with that I just had to mention it! Top notch company

title: bed tent pirate
abstract: Pirate bed tent. The upside, comes in a nylon bag with good handles and zippered. The tent is made of a stiff, nylon material. Comes with printed instructions and is put together like a pup tent with stringed poles. Really need 2 people in order not to get too frustrated. Took longer than you would hope. Sigh. In the ad they note they are including a cute flashlight that also functions sort of like the old toys you inserted photo wheels into (view master) - comes with 8 little wheels. They also note you'll need to provide the batteries. But. What they don't mention is you will will need watch batteries! 1.55v little coins (surprisingly they are not all the same size either - some are tiny). I don't keep those on hand. Good thing my grandson hasn't arrived yet. I've got time to purchase them. I just assumed it would a AAA or AA. Eh. The flashlight is really low quality junk. But you have to have the batteries to try it! Over all, 3 stars is fair. But they do need to include specifics on the batteries or include them. Oh. I bought 2. The pirate and space ship version. They are both 'ok.'

title: bedding storage bags
abstract: I love love love these storage bags. I just replaced a MOUNTAIN of plastic storage tubs with just a few of these. The first pic I have provided has ONE king size quilt (NOT comforter) in it. PLENTY of extra room for pillow shams.. matching sheets, etc. The second is of the zipper pulls and you can see the zipper track... cute hearts - they may be cute BUT they are also very functional. That wider heart shape is easy to grab/pinch. when zipping. They also have very securely sewn nylon web handles. - see pic 3. The last pic is of a twin size comforter, fluffy blanket, standard size pillow, sham and sheets! Comforters take up more room than quilts but clearly there is still room in even this storage bag. I have a number of quilts - seasonal prints, etc.. and of course matching shams. So I put each quilt in their own storage bag and then stacked them in my linen closet. The outer material is very light in weight.. but a though nylon or nylon like material. There is a really useful clear window in the front so you can view your bedding or other item(s). The side handles are so very useful when moving them or stacking them as I did. Now, having said that, if you put 200lbs in these bags, the handles probably would tear out.. They are not meant for storing super heavy, sharp things. You could easily put 2 or 3 quilts and shams in one bag with no handle problem. I also store my full height shearling boots in one bag - I have 3 pairs. It's nice to put them away in a safe, insect free storage bag and have them so easy to retrieve when I want them. The plastic tubs I was using took up a HUGE amount of space in my linen area and because they are hard plastic, they were unyielding. These bags easily stack and conform in size and space - making them great space savers - compared to the plastic tubs. The gray color is a light to medium gray (depending on your opinion) as you can see in the photos. At this point I have nothing but positive things to report... however, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. And I truly hope that this info was helpful to you!

title: black and decker toaster oven
abstract:
Daughter lives in Arizona and needed a new toaster oven. She chose this one for it's size. She reports that it arrived quickly and in good condition (I have prime). She reports that she likes it because it is deep (will take a 9x13 pan), but doesn't take up a lot of counter space. She also specifically wanted one with little "electronics".... she prefers "dials" as they don't break as often in her mind. (I have an "electronic" toaster oven I've had for nearly 5 years - so to each his own!)... It is simple to use and looks nice with her new stainless appliances. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info be helpful. Further, I do NOT receive compensation of ANY kind for my honest reviews.
UPDATE.... 8/7/2016.... Wow. This toaster oven is HUGE. My daughter cooks full size pans and meals in this oven. The "up" side is that in Arizona, this toaster oven heats up the kitchen way less than the regular size gas oven. Trade off - it takes up some counter real estate and that's no lie. All that being said, my daughter says it is her favorite toaster oven yet. She is a very picky customer. I would add that for the price this toaster oven is really a bargain. Again, I do NOT receive compensation for my reviews of ANY kind.

title: black and white photo props
abstract:
Geez. The photo of these shows GLITTER - or the appearance of GLITTER. But if you don't carefully read the WAY too long description which says NO GLITTER - you'll be disappointed. It is nice they are already assembled - so they get 3 stars... but they get ZERO stars for their misleading photos of the props.. Not only is there NO sparkle of any kind.. they are literally just black and white. So.. I briefly considered applying some glitter glue... but then... they landed in the garbage can.. Not worth the effort to return. Just flat out disappointed in the seller's photos of the props to sell them. Because if you were to see what they look like in person, you wouldn't buy them!! Stinks. Meh.
UPDATE: 1/7/2019 Because I do my best to be fair and honest... I received an email from the seller.. they are trying a glitter cover to the photo area that appears to be glitter already. They included a photo of what they are trying.. for me... it appears to be a thin cover of tiny glitter flakes over the area that looks like it has glitter.. and because the props are literally black and white - I think the cover appears a bit yellowish... for me, I wanted the big chunky glitter so I wouldn't really have worked for me.. but that is just my personal opinion. They also generously provided me a refund. I did improve my rating by one star because the seller is really trying to make this product better in my opinion.

title: blink add on
abstract: After spending MANY times more than what you can buy a three camera Blink system for, we are THRILLED with our Blink systems. We have two- each with 5 cameras - so we "added" on cameras. They work seamlessly... effortlessly. They COME WITH lithium batteries. Honestly, if my husband and I can figure this out.. ANYONE can. I love that we don't have to "buy" anything else... cloud space.. or monthly rental fee of any kind. As long as you have wifi... it works. One way sound - (so no two way talking - but we find we don't need that) - cameras are night vision at night and are perfectly clear. The system we paid so much more for doesn't work even 1/2 as well. *sigh* Live and learn. Just wish we would have had Blink first. Note: we have our wifi system on a battery back up to help with power outs.. but if your wifi goes down, so do your cameras.. just want to be fair and honest... So far, that has not been an issue. They just work flawlessly. Could not be happier with how they work or how easy they are to set up and install. Also Note: We purchased the upgraded mount - it is worth the few extra dollars to get the most out of your camera position. Having said all that... I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. And I really hope my review was helpful to you some way!

title: chair leg covers
abstract: We just installed a bunch of new vinyl flooring where carpet had been. So, instead of the plastic nubs that help you slide on carpet, you need to switch to the felt based tips. We've been through a whole passel of felt squares - our chairs have 1 1/4" square legs. The felts with the stickers just slide off and never stay in place. I never tried the "tack" on or screw on types for fear of harming my floor - and then we found these! These are a really good design. They are different than other silicone sleeve with the felt squares only at the bottom... those slip and tear the silicone, eventually coming off. SO FAR - these have stayed in place perfectly, without slipping. Key is that the felt square rounds UP the side of silicone sock. Slides A LOT better across the floor as you're sitting on the chair than any of the other stick on felts. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. Time will tell if these are as good as they seem to be. We have four chairs so we used 16 tips and you get 24. So there are replacements should they become necessary. I think it's important that they fit snugly on the chair feet so measuring is important. If you're tired of changing your chair foot felts, I say give this one a try. They have multiple colors to choose from too.

title: coin counter
abstract:
UPDATE BELOW....I ordered this just to keep track of the loose change in my bowl. It is a fully plastic item and lightweight... but if it were any heavier you wouldn't be able to lift it when full of coins. The plastic bottle, while lightweight, appears to be pretty sturdy. Time will tell. The pics I have included show around $45.00 in change so I estimate the jar will hold around $200+ in change if I keep around the same mix of coins shown....It will obviously depend on what coins you are dropping in. There are two "pinches" on the side of jar, but they are pretty useless unless the jar is empty. When it has change in the jar, it's too heavy for the side pinches to be useful. The opening of the jar is about 2 1/2". And adult cannot put a hand inside the jar, so you will have to pour the contents out. The jar is about 10 or so inches tall... eye balling it. The top (counter part) requires 2 AAA batteries (not included) AND a tiny screwdriver to open the battery compartment. Upon opening and inserting batteries, I put in a counted number of coins.. $1.67 for a test. The lid immediately failed after 3 coins and just stopped adding or reading denominations at all. I read the directions and inserted a pen into the "reset" hole on the underside of the lid (to the top right area of the battery compartment). It reset and I tried again. It worked. And continued working through the rest of the coin drops. The screen read stays on a few minutes (haven't timed it yet) and then blacks out. It re-awakens when you drop another coin in. With each coin dropped the screen flashed the denomination of the coin 3x and then shows the total. Normally I just throw my coins into a big bowl. When it gets full I load up into a ziplock and take it to my bank. Back in the day they wanted the coin rolled... now, no bank will take rolled coins. Thus the ziplock bag. The counter will take some of the guess work out of the total.. IF it continues to work... but I am ok with a "close" total. It's amazing how fast it adds up. I am disappointed it failed right out of the gate. PLUS. I HATE it when you have to use a tiny screwdriver to get into the battery compartment!! I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE 2/14/2017.... the seller contacted me immediately and offered a replacement top, stating that the top should not have failed even with a restart. Currently the original top is still working. I will keep the second as a back up. It is rare to come in contact with such a responsible seller. I added one star to the rating for this response and hope the jar will keep working. It's not a high quality electronic instrument - I understand that - but I do really appreciate the effort by the seller.

title: creamer jar
abstract: I purchased a plant based milk maker and I needed a creamer when I make plant based creamer. This jar is nice. It pour nicely and washes in the dishwasher. The body is glass, the tops is mostly plastic. This works great.  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. All of my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different. I am not influenced by any outside source. I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers- ever. For some reason our shopper ranks are no longer visible - so, to give you a little more info about me, I am a top 50 reviewer (#30 the highest rank achieved). Those numbers used to fluctuate over time - up and down but I noticed that they stopped updating regularly - perhaps to phase them out. It's a shame because it did help you see who has been around the longest and who is a trustworthy reviewer.  I've been doing reviews for over 25 years with Amazon - over 6,000 reviews posted, those reviews have been viewed well over 50,000 times, including over 24,000 likes. Bottom line, I pay for all my stuff, just like you do.

title: died 8 months later
abstract:
Update 9/24/2020 - died today - system freezes after one minute and goes to black screen. HP product support unable to help, I tried their online chat and they are unable to help. I put in my serial# and product code to no avail. super depressed - this plus covid plus wildfires - HP you really let me down.

Arrived today (1/8/2020) I ordered it after much research and perusal of reviews. It arrived and the first thought out of the box "huh, PLASTIC" says it has a plastic frame so it feels cheap. Opened it up and it is dead, needed to be charged so I waited 4 hours while it charged. Fully charged it searched for updates and downloaded for over 10 minutes. Next was quick and easy, loaded my google/chrome profile from my gmail sign in, and then it went black - no warning and stayed black while I tried everything to figure out why it was not turning on. Finally came back on. Then I noticed as it started to get super hot that THERE ARE NO VENTS. Well that explains the heat. On the plus side the keyboard is super. Still I am wondering if this was a bad purchase and knowing I have a short window to return it I am holding onto the boxes and packaging it came in.

Update Day 3: no more overheating, I am chalking it up to setup overload. This a a huge improvement of my awesome first chromebook 5 years ago. This one debuted June 2019 and currently Google has the OS set to expire summer of 2026 which for $210 is a great deal. I have 6-7 tabs running at anyone time without a slow down. A True HD picture. Super fast page load and a nice size screen. PLUS no worry about viruses - Priceless. LIG.

Day 8: Still going good. I will note the the battery life is 5 hours with the light on full bright. No more over heating.

title: double rod garment rack
abstract: I have a closet with a REALLY tall bar... I needed a second bar and didn't want to loose all the storage in my closet lower area. This seemed like a good idea. I put it together, by myself in about 20 minutes. I am going to say that I could not install the wheels, they just would not screw in - 3 of the 4 would not. It's like the screw holes were crooked or something... but as it turned out, it fit better without the wheels and since I don't plan on moving it and out.. it was ok not to have the wheels on. I would say that someone stronger might have been able to force screw the wheels in, just not an option for me. The measurements given were accurate. I didn't realize that it was black with the silver hanging rods... (thought it was all silver) but again, that really didn't matter to me. You've gotta watch what you're buying for color! In any case, the price was right. FYI... I do NOT receive compensation of ANY kind for my reviews... my purchases are VERIFIED, full price, fully independent purchases. 100% As are my reviews! I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and always try to respond to questions and comments. Happy Shopping!

title: dumpling kit
abstract: Well. I was hoping for a bit more quality - but you get what you pay for... the rounds are VERY flimsy. The handled rolling cutter is about the most sturdy thing in the kit - the two spreader/filler spatulas are pretty good. The two wonton/dumpling presses are really flimsy and loose. I hope they will get through the mini project I have. They say they are stainless... but if they are, it's the thinnest stainless I have ever seen. The super thin inner box they came was open (sticker closure was sliced through) so someone else looked, passed and returned this set. I hate that. It should NOT have been resold. Included with the order was a card the says "congrats, you won the prize" There is a qrl square and a scratch off box that reveals "first prize"... when you go to the website it is a mag subscription (I don't remember what - but nothing good), a whole 6 month warranty, or a $2 "cash" card on your next amazon order. You will need your order number to obtain this info - but then, I've just shared it. All in all this is a very cheap, light weight set. If you make wontons/dumplings a lot - you'll want a much better set. However, for my use - maybe once? I might be ok.

title: exactly as pictured, basic short knap carpet for my office room, add rug pad for more loft
abstract:
I chose this for strictly indoor use, and it is exactly what I needed. In looking at it, I dont think it would work for outdoor use. Not sure how it would drain as the backing appears solid. But the knap is super short, so it could work for protected outdoor spaces (just broom off debris).

The backing has a light nub texture to help keep it in place on the floor, the seams are well stitched, and I dont notice any off coloring or cut. I placed it directly on top of another 5'x7' carpet of same size (style, and feel), and it all lines up perfectly. Size is exactly as expected. That being said, keep in mind that they include this in the description:

"Due to the detailed construction of our rugs, both handmade and machine-made, sizes may vary by up to three inches in width or length." and,

"Rug pad recommended"

The coloring is exactly what I wanted. I have an old house that hasn't been updated since probably the 70s. My office room has this chartreuse green wallpaper that I am rather in love with. The room used to have cream carpeting, but after some failed attempts to clean it, I eventually tore it out and put down an extra area rug until I found a more coordinating color. I found that in this green color. It is a celery green, and it works well with my other greens in the room.

I am giving it a generous 5 stars because it is exactly as expected, and it appears the same as it does in the picture. It meets my needs, and I would consider this brand again. However, if wallyworld had theirs in a color I needed, I would have gone with that for half the price. This is prettier though.

I bought it when this was $52. It was more than I wanted to spend for a lightweight carpet, but the coloring was important to me. I dont rate on price anyway as we all have different budgets and needs. I focus more on quality, how an item matches product description, and how it works for my needs. For that, I say it all lines up, hence the 5 stars (4.5 if I could).

PS. It came well wrapped. I was able to roll it out onto the floor and it took no time to lay flat. Looks great! If I see anything else, or if anything goes bad, I will be back to update.

title: external hard drive
abstract: I purchased this to save my recorded programs/movies from my Dishnet Hopper 3. Worked great. I wasn't clear if it came with a usb or not, so I purchased one... DON'T.... It comes with one that works perfectly. I keep it hooked up to the hopper, so the nice short cord is useful... (about 1 ft). If you need a longer one, then perhaps you'll want to purchase one - but not necessary otherwise. It was super easy - plugged it in, a box came up on my TV that asked if I wanted to update and format - I clicked yes and that was it. It was ready for transfer of saved material. The drive itself is approx 5:x4"x 3/4". It is black and has a little flashing light when it's being used. I had things sorted on my Hopper in "files". So far, I cannot figure out how to make folders on the hard drive, so everything is just mixed on the hard drive - that means looking thru about 200 titles - Eh - but the point of the hard drive for us is to save the content if we have to replace the Hopper at some point. It is easy to move the files back and forth.. And you can play the movies from the hard drive. It did take quite a while to transfer, we had about 50% of our Hopper memory - a number of hours. But no biggee to me. So far, I am happy with my purchase, however, time will tell. Having said that, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: extra large jaw loppers cut through thicker, stubborn branches with ease
abstract:
So far so good!

These have some heft, but aren't too heavy. The beak/jaw is strong, and quite large. PERFECT for larger branches that smaller loppers can't grab onto. This set comes with extra blade, and a pair of pruners. I like the handles- they have a comfortable grip that allows me to exert the pressure needed to cut easily through stubborn branches.

I acquired these to use alongside my smaller jaw loppers. I have several Hemlock trees that need a bunch of dead branches cut out. Many can be cut using the regular sized loppers, but there are still many that are too big for those. I considered getting out my mini chain saw, but I really preferred to just lop them off. These large jawed loppers were exactly what I needed!! I am still working on the trees, and I can say having these loppers have been a joy to use. I even used them in a landscaping/yard clean up job I had to go to. These large loppers work on smaller stuff, but I prefer my smaller jawed loppers for smaller branches, and for the most part I only really need regular sized smaller loppers. But when a bigger cut is needed, gotta use the larger loppers like these. Use the correct tool for the job!

All looks good, no issues. If they fall apart I will be back to update

title: faux fur white/ivory blanket
abstract: This blanket is not a "throw"... it is a full size blanket.... which I like. When I get cozy with a blanket for a quick nap or for comfort, I want it to cover me... including toes - so this is good for me. But to be fair, it is in no way a "throw" size at 90"x90". It fits on my queen size bed easily as a full blanket. It is 100% polyester. It machine washed and dried nicely and I don't have a fancy washing machine and dryer. To me, the "sherpa" side is actually a lot softer than the "fur" side. I have included a couple of pictures... it is a light, soft ivory color in my opinion, no yellow tones - but not fully white. I took a pic with my quilt which has white in it so you can kind of compare the color. It is what I would consider a medium weight when on you.. not super thick, but plenty warm and cozy. Having said that, it is quite heavy holding it all in one arm full. I prefer the "sherpa" size to my skin. The "fur" side does have a slight "swirl" effect in pattern. It is my opinion that you will want to carefully care for this blanket so you don't have to wash it too many times...I think the sherpa side may become lumpy and pilly... time will tell. I always try to answer all questions and comments...further, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful in any way.

title: floor lamp
abstract:
It comes disassembled. It took me about 20 minutes to twist all the segments together. The lamp I received is a matte black. The tubing is metal. The lamp is LED. There is a spot on the main tube of the lamp that is supposed to allow you to turn on the lamp and dim - it does not work. If you use the remote, you can use the toggle on the main tube to dim either the large or the mini lamp - but it will NOT turn the lamp on or off. The remote uses a really small barrel shaped battery (came with it) but looks like it will be hard to find. Eh. But the remote turns on and off both lights, dims them and changes the light from a blue or "warm" color light. The mini light has a goose neck that you can manipulate. The large light has two options, straight up and flat (pointing directly at the ceiling) or at a tilt (which I prefer for dust). I like the light, but disappointed that the main tube of the lamp doesn't work - not that I am terribly surprised it doesn't. It says to light tape the toggle - big nothing. You can tap, gently hold or bang it - NOTHING happens. Thus the 3 stars. TIP NOTE: because the tube is metal, and you have to twist the segments together, be SUPER careful to get them twisting correctly so you don't strip them or get them stuck at the wrong angle.
PROS: LED, doesn't flicker.
You can change the light from a white/blue to a warmer yellower light.
Dimmer option.
The mini light is nice if you read in bed or at the sofa.
CONS: You cannot turn the lamp on or off without the remote - even though you are supposed to be able to. Bad battery size - will be a pain to find replacement.
If I loose the remote, I will not be able to use the lamp. Eh.

title: foil and cling wrap dispenser
abstract: A couple of things... We installed this on the wall in the kitchen. You should know that this dispenser is ONLY for regular sized rolls (not the big box store rolls you purchase). That's one thing. But even when you have the regular sized rolls in - there are some issues. The most frustrating is that the rolls - particularly the foil doesn't stay lined up with the dispenser slot - so it 'rolls' on the edges and tears. GRRRR. I struggle with the cling wrap because it too doesn't like staying in place/line with the slots. If you put something at the ends of each roll to fill the blank area on each end - the roll doesn't roll properly. Eh. I was really hopeful for this to make things neater and tidier. Unfortunately it just makes things more frustrating. The box is heavy bamboo or bamboo like material. The slider cutters usually work - but if the material (foil/plastic wrap) aren't exactly flat under the cutter, it rolls up too. Could this work better in a drawer application - maybe - but I don't think so. The fact that it doesn't deal with the roll moving from side to side inside the dispenser - is still an issue. title: good mouse that doesn't quite fit my hand - yet
abstract:
howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee

title: goose neck cell phone/device holder
abstract:
I was really hoping to love love this... and I do like it..
PROS
- Like having a third arm/hand
- holds in place you choose
- black or white color options (I purchased black for husband and white for me)
- table clamp is easy to attach if you have a perfectly flat table (top and bottom) up to 2" thick or so - using twisting tube attached to the base. -NOTE: There is a "con" to this as well.
- The coil is very, very difficult to manipulate. BUT it once you get it there, it stays exactly where you place it.
CONS
- the clamp is really really stiff and difficult to stretch enough to hold your phone or device. If you have any strength issues, this might not be the best choice. Also, they edges will pinch you if you accidentally get your fingers in the way of the spring loaded clips.
- The table clamp only works with tables that are flat on top and bottom. The place I wanted to clamp on has a groove underneath and my husband had to make a wooden block of sorts for the table clamp to work.

Overall, I like the stand - but the engineering that is required to make a strong, stable holder, also makes it difficult to use. Just sayin.

title: keep looking for a different keyboard
abstract:
It was hard for me to pick a keyboard but I'm generally happy with it thus far! I like that it's wireless. I don't need any more wires on my desk. Rechargeable is also great. Working from home I have to buy my own batteries so forget that. I love the keys on this! It feels great to type on.

My only complaint is I can't charge this if my laptop is sleeping. I had been charging it via usb on my laptop and it wasn't working out well. To solve this, I had to use a much longer usb cable to connect to the power strip on the floor... it works. Overall, I'm happy with it.

Edit 1/21/21: I've been using this keyboard for 5 months now and the battery doesn't last as long as I would like. It doesn't last the full work week. Working Monday-Friday, it starts to die by Thursday. I've had it go out while typing sometimes but it does turn back on after a few seconds. I usually can make it until end of day Thursday. It takes many hours to charge as well. I plug it in 4pm and it's still charging when I check it one last time at 9pm.

title: longtime kindle owner
abstract: I am a longtime kindle owner. I read constantly. I have eye implants after cataract removal so I, personally, own a kindle keyboard with the black ink display which is less likely to irritate and tire my eyes than backlit screens. plus me and touch screens, not too compatible. I bought this for my daughter who reads a lot, too, and is pretty conservative moneywise. I got this so she could stick it in her purse and read on the bus going back and forth to work, afterall I have 1500 books she can load and read with no cost involved. I just would like to say, this kindle fire hd was amazingly easy to set up for her. I downloaded some books, some videos, some music, some apps, since my daughter in law has a kindle fire hd on my account and all of these things are available from our cloud. this is a wonderful thing. I told my daughter it is Christmas/birthday this year, maybe next year, too, since she had a "cow" about the money. I consider it one of the best investments I have made for a long time. only the cost of the kindle, a cover, and a fast charge socket were involved. and I was surprised to find how easy it was to set up, touch screen fears are quite eased now. if you have a family member who does not have a kindle, just get one for them. you will feel really good, I promise!!!!!

title: mason jar lights
abstract:
These are just the lids and lights... NO JARS. I knew this going in, so I purchased my own jars and some polished rocks to use as weights - we have rambunctious ground squirrels. I also purchased, separately, "stainless steel" handles as we live on the ocean front in Oregon. The handles were a bit of trick to get on the jar - it works best if you "screw" them on, like a lid sort of. I sort of twirled the lights so they hung down as a swirl down the center of the jar and then screwed the lids onto the jars. They charge in the day, come on at dusk and mostly stay on all night long. A couple I notice don't.. but I was only hoping for a few hours - so I'm good with this. They are not really bright enough to use a path way light - but they are bright enough to be a very pretty decoration. I ordered a dozen, but went back for a third set as my very determined squirrels did manage to shatter one by knocking it off even with rocks for weights! My Mom loved them, so I let her take three of them. She has them in her window sill, inside. They work nicely there too. As long as they get sun to charge, it's good. Now, I will say, that the rings have become to rust. I haven't tried to pop out the light portion and put a new ring on, but I may try this after the summer season is over. All work. I had NO failures. Some don't last through the night, even though they have exactly the same sun exposure - but still, last for hours. I do recommend putting something in the jars for weights even if you don't have sassy squirrels like we do as they will likely stay put better...As I said I used polished rocks.. but you could use glass beads or marbles or shells that heavy or packaged sand (because its dry - don't get it off the beach) really anything that would provide weight and you can fit into the canning jar. All in all, I really like these lights... just wish the rings were more resistant to rust! They would make beautiful wedding decor, or other party decor or individually as gifts with special inserts (weights). My Mom adores hers. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. If I decided to try and replace the rings I will post how that went. And I hope this info was helpful to you in some way.
UPDATE 8/14/2018.... I have added some photos that might be helpful - while the outer rings have rusted... eh... they are outside.. we are oceanfront (although they would rust outdoors anywhere) - I consider the rust "patina"... I may not attempt to replace the rings until they are not functional anymore - a couple seasons?? I DO recommend the separate purchase of the handles. They make the jars a lot easier to move around. Hope this is helpful to you!

title: meh
abstract: Keep in mind: this is a $40 device. If you're looking for reliable home surveillance, probably best to skip this one, and maybe D-Link altogether. That having been said, I found it fairly easy to setup. Video streaming to mydlink.com is at best undependable, however, so I wasn't sure at the time if setup was working or not. After messing with it for about an hour I had to leave and wasn't able to access the video stream. I checked in later and it had magically started working on its own. Go figure. You can access the camera directly via IP address or via their freebie app locally, but remote is a crapshoot. Resolution is low quality (320x240). Night mode is okay close up. I'm unable to access mydlink.com on my Mac - apparently there's no support for the current MacOS (Sierra). I emailed D-Link support with questions but received a generic "this is how to reinstall the camera" response, so I don't know if they eventually plan to support Sierra. It seems possible that this device has been orphaned in favor of newer models. The camera is small and light and the base is quite adjustable to allow easy positioning. (note: indoor use only) I bought it to enable watching for animal activity in my wooded back yard - I haven't managed to get it set up to email me activity alerts yet but it's (barely) adequate for that purpose.
