title: microwave bacon cooker
abstract: My microwave is an over the stove - and it is narrow - not as tall as some microwaves inside. In the beginning of my search I was looking into the stand up versions - but they would not fit in my narrow height microwave. So, I began looking at flat cookers. I landed on this one. I liked that it had a lid. One of my top reasons to find one that worked was to minimize the mess in cooking it. This one worked great. Even though it notes that it is dishwasher safe, I do hand wash it, hoping to extend it's life. I use the blue pre cleaning spray - works like a dream. I put 5 pieces of regular thickness bacon (not thick and not extra thin). 4 minutes cooked the strips to my liking - cooked but not crispy. On that note, I would not try to "crisp" bacon in the microwave - microwaves really aren't designed to crisp anything. But if you like normal cooked bacon this will work. One helpful hint I would share is to drain the oil in the bottom of the cooker while it is liquid. Don't let it set - it is way too much work to scrape it out. I do recommend hand washing. And I really like that I am not cleaning up bacon splatter for days and my bacon is tasty. I would recommend this cooker - but having said that I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

abstract: We have a semi tiny house... and this table is actually better than you would think. It folds flat with all the accessories, including legs completely flat and compact. title: portable power station
abstract: I purchased this to help with little short power outages we get from time to time. It will allow me to charge my phone and even run a coffee pot and/or a small (very small) hot plate to heat something. Most of our outages are less than a few hours. This would never replace a generator, but it could make life a bit less stressful in the event of a short outage. It is mostly a blue with black case. The plug in's are easy to see in the front. The back is a big light. I haven't actually used it just yet, but I did charge it up in case. The cord has a type of transformer on it with a fan and it is quite noisy when charging - I put it in the laundry on a shelf I plan to store in on for charging. Worked great. I never heard in there. Just a note here - it' doesn't auto stop the charge apparently, so the transformer fan just keeps running until you unplug it. For now it is fully charged and ready for a short outage. I can see where this could useful camping too. There are solar panels (additional purchase) but I did not purchase those. It also came with a nice collection of various cords. You can even charge it from inside your car at the cigarette lighter - nice. It's heavy - as you would expect but still compact in size for easy storage. Also has a nice carrying handle and a sturdy charging cord. I believe it's going to work just exactly as I need it to. As I use it I definitely update my review should new info seem useful.

title: rechargable salt and pepper shakers, blue light
abstract: I purchased these rechargable salt and pepper shakers because they came with a charging pad and LED lights. I have 2 rechargable shakers now that I must plug into a USB cord every few weeks - but no light. The problem with these is that the light is BLUE. It's almost worse than NO light because the blue light is so blue you can't see where or what you are grinding! The charge pad is handy, but you'll be constantly cleaning it because your shakers sit on the charger base - at the bottoms where the salt and pepper exit. Also, you must press the button to grind - my current shakers turn on when you flip them - there is a button but no one uses it. Additionally, the reservoirs for the peppercorns and salt crystals are VERY small. Eh. Minus 2 stars for the horrible blue light and another star dock for the way they are designed with the grinder opening on the charger base. I am searching for a better set, at the very least with a white light. I cannot recommend this set. Not sure what I will do with them, probably donate them. Honestly, one of the most disappointing purchase I have made in a long time. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. title: rechargeable grinders
abstract:
UPDATE of original review at bottom.... I purchased 2, one for salt and one for pepper. They charged up fully in about 1 hour. There is an adjustable grind dial on the top. Comes with a brush for cleaning and charging cords that are quite short. You can use any regular USB cord you have and I did for the initial charge. The base is clear glass. There is a rubber (or like) nub that you press "on" and it will grind until you stop it. No more twisting your wrist while you try to hold onto the grinder. As I have gotten older, it's less comfortable. Now, I have just begun using these and I hope that they will retain a charge for a reasonable time. Also, I did have to put a plug extender on my kitchen counter that also included USB ports. I didn't want to have to take them to my bedroom to charge when they needed it. They are fairly heavy - partly because of the glass bottoms. They recommend not filling more than 80% to make sure they grind properly. I followed that advice. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE: 2/20/2021... Just a quick note. I have found that when you turn over the grinders, they start. Initially they did not. Why, I am not sure. But when you tip them they grind and continue to grind until you right them... Most of the time anyway. There is a button to press on/off. Which is good because they don't always grind when turned. Hmmm. One less star for the reliability not really being 5 star. But I still consider it at least a 4.

title: silicone egg poacher cups
abstract: Silicone egg poaching cups - you get 4, multi color cups. They are flimsy - they are silicone and thin so that your eggs can poach in a reasonable time! I used my small sauce pan - so it sort of helped keep the cups upright, put a tiny cube of butter in each cup (my preference, great for taste and helps with the cleaning too) and then added about 1 1/2" water into the pan. The cups floated a tiny bit - but are held pretty well by the size of sauce pan. You MUST use a lid. I don't do super juicy eggs - so in about 5 minutes I had 'gel' yolk eggs - PERFECT - to me. Win! I read a review that mentioned you don't want to wash in the dishwasher as they absorb the soap flavor, so I hand wash them - which was easy. Honestly this cooked a perfect poached egg for me. I would recommend them. It does come with a cheapy oil brush - but my husband loves to 'brush pans' with a little oil when he cooks, so it'll last a little while I'm sure - it's just small and flimsy.

title: so convenience of finding these on my doorstep was so GREAT. so
abstract:
so, my story started with a subtle smell, which I thought was natural gas leak in my house.

so being just a whiff, and no recent gas line work/changes in 10 yrs, I was concerned.

I ordered 2 of these highly regarded Kiddie units and mounted them high, so it would sense the natural gas (aka: methane). ordered yesterday morning and god bless Amazon, were delivered same day for free, but with a $3 tax. HD had them at the same price, so convenience of finding these on my doorstep was so GREAT.

so, long story short. they are AC powered and have a 9volt battery back up. well, here's where my experience with this proven design went south. I plugged the AC adapter into a power strip, which wasnt turned on. so it went to the DC battery. d'oh! came home today to this thing chriping away, and not knowing what the hell was going on, except that I could smell something fishy, I called the Fire Department!

turns out, the beeping was because this unit MUST have AC power, and a good 9volt battery. it doesn't work without the battery. so in my panic, I took out the battery. but alas, then it was beeping still, since there was no battery at all.

I called 911 and out came the fire truck. being new to this device, they told me how it worked, AC and backup "good" battery MUST be installed. anyway, so all is well. the gas company also came out and confirmed with all appliances off, there is no leak as they saw zero flow at the exterior meter, meaning all internal gas connections were NOT leaking. good to know. I learned something.

so to end this "review" it works well....just don't have two week old salmon in your kitchen can...else it will fool you because it smells like a gas leak! lesson learned...don't buy fresh salmon flanks at Costco and never cook them! d'oh!

these units are working fine with batteries installed and power from the DC transformer. BUT...fyi, you MUST have both. should have read the instructions...but alas, I had not.

I would buy these again, and did...sending one to my sister with explicit instructions to NOT do what I did!

title: so far so good! Makes grilling veg so much easier
abstract:
So far so good. I only saw some of the bad reviews after buying and trying this. I can say that so far my bags are holding up well. Been doing a lot of outdoor cooking so we dont heat up the house any more than necessary on hot and humid days.

 I was getting tired of having my vegetables (and occasional fruit) fall apart or fall through grill grates. I dont care for silicone grill mats. I wanted something that will allow the flame to lick through. I was about to buy a steel basket when I saw these bags. Instantly intrigued! I grabbed them on a whim, and I glad I did. The reason I like them so much is because I can FLIP MY VEGGIES with ease.

Be sure to coat the bags with some oil. And so far I have only used medium to medium high heat. Not scorching flame. This is more off to the side as I use the higher heat and flame to take care of thicker proteins. So maybe just be mindful of that. I find these are making my life easier. I can do tomatoes, zucchini, asparagus, onions, green peppers, peaches, apples, nectarines, pineapple, oh and sliced potatoes with ease. I slide them in, snap the bags closed, toss on grill, turn a few times while they cook.

I have used it on Propane grill and a charcoal grill. No problems with structural integrity, yay!

All good! Used these several times this week already. If they break down I will let you know. But so far so good!

title: storage chest
abstract: I purchased this for a tiny room. It functions as a seating area (like to pull up your socks or put on your shoes) and to store spare bedding - and it is set at the end of twin size bed. It fits perfectly there.. It is black. The legs are wooden (or wooden like). It has 2 hinges that hold the lid open. It is sturdy. The top is buttoned and cushy. The inside is roomy for it's size and holds the spare sheets easily and has room for a small quilt too. It is a leather like material and is made in China. It arrived fully assembled and nicely packed with a custom made cover, lightweight cloth cover - that was cinched at the bottom. I have included some pics... if they make it past the Amazon photo trolls - I do really try to provide as many as possible of pics I would like to see if I were looking myself. I like this chest and think it will last as long as I would like it to - time will tell of course. I think it looks better than the price paid in my personal opinion. I never hesitate to update my review should new info seem useful.

title: super
abstract:
Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.

title: sweet spot for price and wattage, output power of 500W and peak 600W
abstract:
lithium ion battery. Good size for charging up small wattage stuff. Tablets, phones, laptops, mini portable fans, camp fan, rechargeable flashlights and lightbulbs, radio, even TVs and DVD player. Will need to go double or more to run a basic coffee maker.

---AC port: supports appliances with voltage of 110, frequency 60hz/50hz, and rated power of no more than 500w. Pure sine wave 110V AC output ports (2) with a rated output power of 500W and peak 600W

---DC Output port: 12v & maximum of 5A; max output power 60w

---Car cig lighter port: DC output w/ rated voltage of 12v & max current of 10A; max output 120w

---USB-C port: fast charging w/ max output of 60w

---USB-A port: fast charging with max output of 18W

Nice digital display. Can see how much power it has stored up, remaining time of power stored, temperature, output power, input power, AC frequency.

Power on/off. Will also auto power down after X amount of time to save power. Has 2, USB-A ports, 1 USB-C, 1 car charge port, DC port, and 2 AC outlets. Also includes a "flashlight" with typical levels of brightness and a flashing option.

Included AC adapter and charging cable (25V 5.5A), car charging cable (cig lighter to DC5525), solar charge cables (MC4 to DC5525 port). Panels not included.

Instruction manual is simple and easy to understand.

Good weight. Feels powerful and sturdy, yet isnt too large, clunky, or heavy. Easy to hold handle.

I have wanted to add some power banks to my household emergency supplies. Good to figure out what you really want it for, then make purchase (or purchases) from there. Ultimately I want to be able to charge up some basic items, and I would like to have some entertainment such as TV & DVD player. I just kind of imagined what I would like for when power goes out for any long length of time. This is a good size for smaller stuff, nice to use separately from a much larger power generator. Which I will eventually get for larger appliance needs, like running a coffee pot, hot pot, skillet. Since those items aren't as "vital", I didnt want to spend $1500-3000 (yet). Since 500W (or 700W) takes care of a lot of smaller gadgets and daily use items, I figured the pricing for that was in a sweet spot. Functional. Typically I figure about $1 per watt, less the larger the unit. This 500W at current price is budget friendly, especially if first trying out an item like this.

I'm pleased. It will stay in a spot in the house with easy access to charge up on occasion, and for of course if/when we need it.

title: topical phrasing- trash pands, doggo, etc. Looks fun; nice looking game
abstract:
Looks like a fun game for kids and adults. It is for 2-4 players, ages 8 and up. I bought it as a gift. I don't know if it is complicated or not, but it looked appealing and out of all the other games on here I looked at, I chose this one. I think with games you have to be one to want to learn and play them (I don't) and/or know who you will be playing with- are they patient, receptive to learning, etc.

 I bought it as part of a gift for a family with 4 kids of various ages. I bought a few games and this was one of them. I didn't want to spend more than $10 per game, and this fit the bill. Seeing the topical use of "trash pands" and "doggo" make me laugh, so I thought the older kids would like it too. Who knows how relevant it will be in a few years. I do not know if they ever played it or if it is collecting dust somewhere. I thought a couple of the older ones would like the name of the game. I am not into buying toys for kids, usually it is books, games, or project/activities. They seemed to be curious about it and had mentioned that they were getting into playing games like this, so hopefully they have enjoyed it.

I give it a 4 for simply being intriguing looking, sounding fun, well packaged, attractive, current, and seemingly quality game. I figure anything like this is a chance

title: underbed storage
abstract:
UPDATE BELOW: I purchased these to put my grandsons clothes - under the cots I have put up. Works really great - I like that there is a handle on the front and at the both ends. The zipper top is clear so you can see what is in there. And the clear vinyl keeps dust off and clothes clean. I like them. The fold up pretty small and square too. There is a bottom stiffener to help keep it useful. The dividers are a little less wonderful - but work. You press velcro on the side to get them in - they sort of work. The handles are a nylon strapping - about 1 1/2" wide and sewn on. I like them. I think I'll be able to use them for a while - we'll see. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
6/17/2020... After having loaded up my grandsons clothing and attempting to use the zippers - MEH. Really disappointing. SIGH. I hate the updates that aren't stellar... The zippers just don't want to make the corners... so we end up only opening just to the corner - makes it a bit more challenging to access all the clothing - but they fit perfectly under their cots. Zippers need a better frame possibly? Not sure - but they are a design flaw. If you don't have to get in and out of them very often - or fully open the top - maybe they're ok.

title: unsatisfactory-ness of life, book holders
abstract:
Four stars is probably the highest rating available for a book holder until consumer priorities change and it makes sense for companies to dump money into R&D.

This one is clever and offers a lot that others don't. It is by far the best i've used for small paperbacks, but book holders are really more handy for things that are unwieldy to hand hold - art books, anthologies, etc.

So, yeah - this is the best of its kind, which isn't saying much. It feels cheap and slightly fragile, though less so than any other I've tried, excepting a stainless steel holder my wife found at a kitchen store (not that it's a good holder - just _sturdy_).

For me the best combo available in 2021 is this book stand, plus any of the big, wooden ones with rubber-tipped, spring steel arms to hold the book open. That duo covers my needs closer to satisfactorily than anything else I've tried.

Maybe it would be useful to say something about why am I still messing with paper codices when I have extremely convenient alternatives in the digital realm, e.g. Zotero + PDF.

I haven't reasoned it all out, but I can say for sure that paper is durable in a way that digital stuff won't be any time soon - maybe they will invent durable digital media, maybe if Wall Street or the military wants it? Anyway, if someone 100 years from now is in the right place - a used bookstore, an estate sale, a thrift store - they might find the very books that I'm reading today. The Kindle books I "bought" 2 years ago have already evaporated and it would take some work on my end to find them again.

So that's a big part of it. I like to think I'm making a teensy contribution to the preservation of the printed word during a time when the idea of its unimportance is spreading like a gasoline fire - the way bad ideas do...

Also my experience of reading a physical book is different. Aesthetically, sure, but there's more to it than that. Like I said, I haven't thought this through, but there's something there. Nostalgia, sure. Maybe just that it's not a video screen, which maybe is permanently tainted ignoble in my mind - by association with entertainment and "social" media?

IDK the text is never the dream, and the medium is never the text. I just feel like more of it remains on a beautifully set paper page than on an imperceptibly flickering screen.

title: very good value
abstract:
i would first off like to address some previous reviewers that have stated that they had a low humming or buzzing noise. i believe this was caused by these people not having a adequate subwoofer cable to shield against EMI and RFI. i have a very nice ATLONA subwoofer cable that is; double shielded, has oxygen free copper conductor and 24k gold connectors. i have had no humm or buzz.

here is my review of the polk audio psw10

Pros:
 low cost, easy to install, aesthetically pleasing(looks very nice), porting, made from composite material that will last a long time, auto shut off feature when not in use, very good sound quality, nice and crisp not "boomy" bass, very good owners manual and customer support/service from polk audio.

Cons:
 Low wattage, no cables included, not down firing port and no low-frequency effect (LFE)support.

conclusion:
 I am very pleased with this subwoofer. It has a dynamic power rating of 100W but it sounds like more. the quality of the sound coming out is very good. I actually had to turn it down because it was so loud when i was first was setting it up and testing it( I have worked with Jet engines that require double hearing protection for years). I don't know how loud some people watch their TVs or movies but, this is way more than loud enough.It shakes my house.
 I really like the way this thing looks. this subwoofer also complements my sound bar very well.
 I have; watched movies, TV and listened to music. all sound superb to me.I highly recommend if you buy any subwoofer you buy a quality subwoofer cable.
 I highly recommend buying this subwoofer if you are looking for a good value or "best bang for the buck".

title: very sturdy
abstract: I bought this rack for a couple of reasons... I liked that it folds flat for storage and that it seemed to be very strong. I was very happy when it arrived initially because it is mostly assembled and very easy to understand as to how the rest assembles. I would have given it 5 stars but I ended up having some missing screws and had to deal with the sellers "customer service." A very, very disappointing experience. After doing everything but stand on my head, they agreed to send the two screws that were missing from the box. (The screws were to attach the the clips which keep the top rack piece all together with the base when not in use). Further, the seller uses F E D E X to ship... so the box was really beat up and had a 4x4" hole in it. The rack was not padded in the box in any way, but managed to arrive undamaged, except for the warehouse forgetting to include the screws. If you don't have to deal with the seller for some reason, you will be very pleased with the rack I believe. It is very sturdy. Folds up so nicely and conveniently. You should know the wheels do NOT have locks on them. The wheels are very sturdy as well, industrial almost. This rack is built to last for some time. You'll spend a bit more, but honestly, you get what you pay for. I plan to try it out at my Mom's garage sale in a few weeks. That should be a good test of it's ability. I will also update IF the screws ever arrive. I have my doubts. Bottom line: Great quality, sturdy, commercial rack. I would buy this brand again but would consider other sellers.

title: waterfall faucet
abstract:
[[VIDEOID:a9acf5d63a0f761d3938fa7867aec297]] UPDATE BELOW
I just put in a vessel type sink in my bathroom and had chosen a more spout pour faucet. The problem was the water would splash over the front edge of the sink. When we tried to reduce the pressure of the water, it wasn't enough pressure to rinse. So, I purchased this style. The waterfall effect "fans" the water so there is less of a "hose" stream of water and while we did slightly lower the pressure, the water now stays in the sink. In addition, the faucet is quite lovely. I was worried it was a bit too modern, but it looks very nice with the brushed satin texture and the oval shape that matches my vessel sink and the beveled edge mirror above it. It's actually quite a nice look. Also the faucet itself is quite weighty - I hope this equates with quality. The previous faucet was super loud too - like a jet plane taking off... this one is quite pleasant, sounds like water, not a jet plane. Those are all the pros... there were a couple of "cons" I've noticed so far... the water doesn't stop immediately... it's sort of slowly stops pouring. I didn't see any where to adjust for this so I am hoping it won't end up a dripper or leaker. The other is that the hoses that were included with faucet were WAY too short. Fortunately the hoses from the other faucet we were replacing fit. Lucky shot. Time will tell and I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
UPDATE: 1/13/2021 I am concerned about the slow stop on turning off the faucet. There isn't anyway to adjust the stop. In all honesty, I love the look and the feel of the faucet but I am looking at other options.

title: window candles
abstract:

title: works fine in Windows not so much linux - extremely light weight
abstract:
I needed something to burn CDs on a laptop where I removed the DVD burner in order to put in a second harddrive to more easily dual boot windows/linux. It is always a pain to put the DVD burner back in so figured I would pick up an external. I rarely burn so I didn't want to spend a lot. I have found LG products to be low priced and usually functional so I went with this model (the one with 50 in the model number). Linux had a little trouble recognizing so I just booted into Windows instead. Worked fine in windows. I am not sure why linux had trouble recognizing it, since I have the option to dual boot Windows it was not a deal killer and I didn't bother tearing my hair out to get it going in PCLinuxOS. Those of you who run linux are probably familiar with hair tearing. Sometimes it is just easier to go over to the dark side and boot windows.

One thing about this item, it is SO lightweight that the usb cable which is a bit stiff can actually flip it all over. You have to get the USB cable to lie nice in order to have the unit sit flush.
